ST_File.F_NPC023_013:
"I've got something to take care of today, so I won't make it to rehearsal."
Akane frowned slightly as she read the message Suzuha had sent to her phone. This was the third time this week Suzuha had sent her a message saying she couldn't make it to band practice. Akane turned around and met Aurelia's worried gaze. They both looked toward Suzuha, but Suzuha merely lowered her head, packed up her schoolbag, and hurried out of the classroom.
In the rehearsal room, Aurelia's drumsticks tapped the drumhead at irregular intervals. Thump, thump, thump—like the jumble of thoughts in her mind.
Akane missed another beat. She turned off the metronome, took several deep breaths, and set down her guitar.
"Rin…"
"Let's call it a day."
Aurelia came over and sat beside Akane. After a moment's hesitation, she asked, "Do you think something's been going on with Suzuha lately?"
"Why won't she say anything?" Akane couldn't understand. Weren't they best friends? Was there really anything they couldn't talk about and face together?
"That's just how Suzuha is. Don't worry. I'll ask her about it tomorrow."
Aurelia offered a few words of reassurance, and rehearsal was quickly put on hold.
The next day, Akane caught Aurelia talking with Suzuha out of the corner of her eye. Their gazes kept drifting toward her, only to dart away again. Akane pretended not to notice.
Yet things didn't improve. Suzuha continued to miss rehearsals, and sometimes Aurelia disappeared along with her too. Akane wanted to ask, but didn't know where to begin. A secret she couldn't be part of had split "Lines" into two unequal halves.
Akane stood alone in the rehearsal room. It was so quiet that the only thing that could be heard was her own breathing. As usual, she switched on the power and plugged in her guitar. But without the drums and bass, her fingers seemed unable even to press down on the strings. Akane lowered her head and looked at her hands. Suddenly, a white star flew from her fingertip, followed by a second, then a third… They landed on the black-and-white keys, the drums, and the cymbals. These shimmering stars lit up Akane's eyes. She gently plucked one string after another, completing a song entirely by herself.
The strings eventually fell silent, but her heart was still pounding. Akane ran out of the rehearsal room. The wind swept past her, but she still sought an answer.
"Are you okay?"
"It's just a minor injury. Don't tell Akane."
Suzuha sat casually on a bench, her arm wrapped in bandages. Aurelia sighed softly as she watched the sun dip towards the horizon. "Are we really going to keep this from Rin?"
"Keep what from me?"
Akane appeared beside them. Suzuha immediately pulled down her sleeve to hide the bandages. "Don't worry about it."
The tension hung in the air. Finally, Aurelia stood up and explained that she and Suzuha had been disappearing lately because they were working as Anomaly Hunters, taking on commissions to earn money.
"That's dangerous…" Akane said with a frown.
"I knew you'd say that." Suzuha pouted.
Being in a band was expensive, and Suzuha's family wasn't very supportive of her passion for music, which meant she'd have to work a myriad of odd jobs for several more months to afford a better bass. Becoming an Anomaly Hunter, however, made things much easier.
"Why didn't you tell me?" Akane pressed on. "Aren't we friends?"
"What would it change if we told you? You're not an Esper."
The moment Suzuha said it, she realized she'd misspoken and hurried to explain further, "That's not what I meant."
"Without an Esper Ability to help us, Anomalies are far too dangerous for high school students like us to confront." Aurelia shook her head quickly.
Akane pressed her lips together and raised a hand. A white star fell onto Suzuha's head. Suzuha reached out and caught it, staring blankly. The star dissolved into specks of light in her palm and disappeared.
"Is that… your Esper Ability? Since when?!" Suzuha suddenly leaned in, examining their band captain from head to toe, as if observing a microorganism. She was close enough to touch, so—
Akane raised her hand and flicked Suzuha hard on the forehead. "If you'd told me, I could've helped you, idiot."
"Ow! That hurt, Akane!"
"Hmph. Let that be a lesson. Next time something happens, tell your Captain first."
"Yes ma'am, Captain."
They laughed and huddled together as stars rose in the sky behind them.
When Akane thought back on that day later, she wondered if Suzuha had been right. What difference would it have made if she'd told her? She wouldn't have been able to change anything regardless.
ST_File.F_NPC021_015:
"I'm Lavinia. Dispatched by Yggash Court, I'll be your guardian from today on."
I can still remember the morning Lavinia first arrived. I had just pulled an all-nighter and was forced out of bed, so I listened in silence, exhausted, as she read off those long, tedious terms: "I'll come by at eight every morning, and during working hours I'll stay in the office until seven in the evening. Miss Blackbird—if I may call you that—please don't mind me. If you need anything, just let me know." With that, she gave me a stiff bow, as dull and severe as she was. "How did they describe me to you, Lavinia?" "Miss Blackbird, I trust only what I see with my own eyes." The woman in front of me bowed again, then started to sweep through The Witch's House like a lioness patrolling her territory. "It's a necessary part of my work," she explained, "but I won't enter your private space without permission." She kept her word. For years after that, she never once set foot in my attic. Even when I blasted movies at a ridiculous volume, she never complained. I have to admit, I was quite happy with that.
It took us several years to get even a little familiar with each other. I didn't have much need for conversation, and she mostly kept herself shut in the office during working hours. She seemed to treat me more like a coworker than someone she was monitoring. The dining room became the place where we talked the most. "Miss Blackbird, please sit in the chair, not on the table." "Miss Blackbird, don't forget to take your medicine after purifying an Oracle Stone." "Miss Blackbird, there's a document I'll need you to look over later." "Lavinia, if your words were as tasty as your cooking, that'd be great." "Miss Blackbird, I put careful thought into everything I say to you, just as I do with everything I make for you."
Every week or two, she'd report my condition to Yggash Court. The Witch's House is a cage, though warm and comfortable… Please don't misunderstand. I have no issue with Lavinia herself or with Yggash Court. They have provided me with everything I could ever need. Until the job was done, they were probably afraid I'd fall ill again like before, or disappear one day without warning. I can understand why they went to such lengths to assign a so-called "guardian" to keep tabs on me. Even going out requires a guardian's permission or escort. But sometimes I think they're a little too cautious. Usually, only supermarket sales can push me to go outside. Still, every so often Lavinia would take me out for a walk—either to the Bureau to file documents, or to handle some other procedure. I wanted to drive, but she never let me.
Lavinia and I lived together peacefully like that for a long time. Compared with when she first arrived, our relationship had come a long way—or at least, I think so. She no longer called me "Miss Blackbird," and now and then she'd even strike up casual conversation on her own. She still kept her distance, but I could feel her slowly beginning to treat me like a "real" person. And honestly, I think I'm starting to enjoy being "real."
ST_File.F_NPC027_012:
"My mom and dad are both Espers."
The first time Linko talked about her family, she scared the Bureau's archivist half to death, because they'd already checked—her parents were perfectly normal—or at least, in Hethereau, normal people with no Esper abilities.
But then she further explained that her "Dad's Esper Ability is sitting perfectly still through more than a dozen movies in a row," and her "Mom's Esper Ability is walking more than a dozen street blocks without stopping," causing everyone to let out a sigh of relief. Afterwards, they immediately started gossiping about how such amazing people could've ended up together.
Linko's mother was an urban exploration blogger—an endlessly energetic go-getter who believed in ghosts, urban legends, UFOs, aliens, and just about every other paranormal thing you could think of. Every day she'd trawl forum posts for leads, and the moment she thought, "This might be a real one!" she'd set off to investigate… Of course, most of the time her impulsiveness got her fooled by those half-baked posts and she'd end up empty-handed, but she never let such things discourage her. Eventually, she really did stumble into a legitimate spooky spot… and subsequently fell into an Anomalous Realm. There, she met another unlucky soul: a film nerd obsessed with supernatural movies, stuck in a creative rut, who'd shut himself away for days to research new creative ideas before deciding on that spot to shoot his new project.
And so, a very Hethereau kind of love story began. Two young people whose personalities were complete opposites met in the Anomalous Realm. At first, they couldn't stand each other, but then later helped each other, stayed together, escaped danger alongside each other, kept thinking about each other, and finally, the next time they ran into each other, confessed their feelings. Linko has heard that story from them both many-a-time, along with plenty of conflicting versions—but the one thing that never changed was their continual adoration for each other.
After Linko was born, those two young Hethereau parents poured all their love into her, and thus she inherited their quirks, too. The first time their daughter crawled into the bedroom with a pacifier in her mouth, Dad generously shared one of his treasured finds—his carefully edited, age-appropriate supernatural movies… And just like that, before she had even outgrown her bottle, Linko could watch horror flicks with her father without batting an eye. Not long after she learned to walk, Mom would take her out to practice, only to get distracted by some shop she'd never been to before and somehow end up walking up and down the entire city block… Strange as all that sounds, whenever Linko talks about her mom and dad, she wears the same happy smile they do.
In any case, little Linko grew up bathed in love.

ST_File.F_NPC030_012:
"I was just on the phone with you, and now you're here!" Around Elyms, that hardly counts as coincidence or fate.
Elyms explains that when someone calls her, she can send a projection of herself along the established connection and materialize wherever that friend is, ready to help with whatever they need.
"That's so convenient~!" "Right~?"
People tend to focus on how quickly she can travel by phone and overlook the part about providing help. Few stop to wonder why that help comes in so many forms, almost as though her abilities can change to suit the person calling.
Those extra thoughtful touches only work while the call is connected, though. Maybe the line doesn't just connect to Elyms's phone. Maybe it also connects to a digital storage space, allowing her to bring whatever the caller needs and materialize it along with her.

So far, all of that could still be explained as part of a phone-based ability. But a few questions remain.
How can she slip into computers and manipulate files?
How can she roam the vast ocean of networks, bypassing every block?
How can she pull magical equipment straight out of video games and use it?
Of course, these abilities are incredibly useful in investigations and combat. No one's complaining about that. But… what do any of them have to do with phones? Elyms has never offered an explanation. She simply uses them as naturally as breathing, moving through the digital world as though this, too, were something she'd always been able to do.

ST_File.F_NPC021_017:
"The Witch's House is a shell that keeps time sealed inside forever."
Unlike the old things in my collection room, I'm an "old thing" that's quite happy to embrace new things. Yggash Court periodically sends over supplies they think are necessary, and that includes the phone I use now.
I have to admit, it's hard to believe how much the world changed during the century I spent shut away inside. After I learned to use this device, Yggash Court no longer had to keep watch on me all the time, and Lavinia gradually realized her real job was to make sure I actually got back to work. I once set a record by watching horror movies for 58 consecutive hours. If Lavinia hadn't finally lost it and cut the internet, I probably could've gone another 20.
I don't think spending so much time on my phone is a bad thing. With this little box, I can stay in sync with the outside world without even leaving the house. I've also learned a lot of new things, like how to drive a car. By the way, I've set and still hold the fastest completion times in several racing games.
More than that, I've never slacked off because I was having too much fun—quite the opposite, in fact—I've actually gotten busier. I created an account on Bagel and tried running an online business, and to my surprise, it turned out pretty well. Thanks to where I live and my own mysterious nature, "the Witch who lives in The Witch's House" gradually became known to more and more people. Oh, and "Witch" and "The Witch's House" are the names my friends on Bagel came up with for me and my home. They also made up tons of urban legends about me, and honestly, those rumors are more interesting than my actual life story.
The busier my online business got, the more income The Witch's House brought in, and I had more pocket money to grab discounted items on sale days… Don't worry—anything I couldn't finish or use up didn't go to waste. Every so often, I'd box up the leftovers and send them to the orphanage. Even though Lavinia already warned me not to throw things over the wall anymore, I still think it's a pretty efficient method of getting rid of stuff. The only real risk is being mistaken for someone up to no good… But as long as I head out at night and turn into a blackbird in time, almost no one notices me.
In any case, compared to the days when I wandered the wilds, I'm satisfied with the peaceful life I have now. If I could, I'd even like to stay in The Witch's House forever… Still, one day the prophecy will be made clear, and the bird that's only been roosting here for a while will spread its wings and take flight again. No matter what fate has in store for me, I will accept it gladly.
ST_File.F_NPC021_013:
"Birds in the sky never know they are the stars of the day."
Long, long ago, I too was once one of those stars.
My earliest memory begins with a spark. I remember the sun being so close that everything around me was perpetually burning. Countless birds like me were fleeing in desperation. I heard someone's voice, but I did not dare to look back. I don't know how long I flew. Only when the last flame on my feathers was snuffed out by the wind did I come to rest by a lake, where I saw a patch of black in the water blinking back at me.
"Blackbird" became my name.
I flew through the sky, yet the birds never saw me as one of their own, never joined me in flight. I walked the earth, yet people saw me as an outsider. They either drove me from their lands or treated me as a divine envoy of portent—because my innate ability to know nearly everything was, to people then and now, both terrifying and irresistible.
But I cannot divine my own fate. I can see the past and future of others, yet I do not know where I was born or where I'm meant to go. So I simply followed the wind. I saw countless living beings, and I saw their fates shining beneath the stars. I envied them. They had homes, memories, and somewhere to return to. Their lives were brief, yet straightforward and complete. Birds or humans—everyone needs a reason to exist. So what about me? What was the meaning of my coming into this world? I spent a hundred years flying in the sky, and another hundred walking the earth, yet no matter how I searched, I never found an answer.
As time goes on, it slowly wears away many things, including the passion to search for my memories. I have grown tired of this fruitless search. I am weary. I want to fold my wings and stop—maybe even find some place to lie down and sleep, with birdsong and the swaying leaves around me. Sometimes, I wonder if the real me perhaps died long ago, and what now wanders the world is nothing more than a lone spirit.

ST_File.F_NPC015_013:
A violet-blue rose.
Its color falls somewhere between deep purple and ashen blue, and its petals curl slightly at the edges, shimmering with a cold, metallic luster in the light. It sits in a plain white porcelain vase, kept fresh in clear water, stem standing straight, clearly well-tended. Yet the petals near the base have begun to wither and gray, as if some of its life force has been quietly siphoned away, leaving it barely holding its form.

Beside the vase stand several other gifts from the past:
A dark red rose, petals brittle as paper. It was once offered by a smiling guest during a toast, though the poison in his glass nearly spilled over as their hands touched.
A gold-edged rose, petal tips singed with scorch marks. It came from a murmured ritual, its giver claiming to be a devotee, though the flames spiraled out of control the moment the prayer was spoken.
A rose faded almost to pale gray, personally presented by a client as a token of sincerity, though beneath its petals lay a web of carefully crafted lies…

Each of these flowers marks the beginning of an encounter, a testament to a confrontation. The intel, the energy, the killing intent hidden within them… she refines it all into bullets, then traces the arc of the moment they were given, and silently returns them to the ones who offered them.

ST_File.F_NPC1029_013:
Aurelia became friends with Akane and Suzuha on a springtime school trip. She was totally entranced by the jellyfish at the aquarium and, before she knew it, drifted away from the rest of her class's group. Just when she began to panic because she couldn't find a familiar face in the crowd, Akane and Suzuha spotted her. Each of them took one of her hands and led her back to the class rendezvous point, then sat on either side of her on the bus ride home.
From that embarrassing moment onwards, Akane and Suzuha became Aurelia's best friends. 

On the birthday that followed, Aurelia's living room wasn't empty anymore. In front of the incredible gift pile, two girls who'd never seen anything like it merely stared, wide-eyed. "What are you two doing, hiding over there?" The moment they heard Aurelia's voice, Akane immediately tried to shove the tiny present in her hands behind her back. But Aurelia, sharp-eyed as ever, caught her in the act.
"Is that for me? It has to be for me, right?!" Aurelia darted over, making an effort to grab the little box.
"You already have so many presents! T-this one really isn't anything special…"
"That doesn't matter!" Aurelia shouted, full of indignation. She finally managed to get a hold of the gift, hugging it to her chest. "This is my first-ever birthday present from a friend. It's mine, no takebacks!"
"Really… it's nothing…" Akane's voice grew quiet. 
Before she could finish, Aurelia had already ripped the wrapping paper to shreds. Out of the palm-sized box rolled out a few shiny little pins: souvenirs from that same aquarium where they'd first met. The tiny jellyfish mascot wore a cutesy, pitiful expression that, funnily enough, looked like Aurelia when she couldn't stop crying that day. 
Aurelia stared, unblinking, at the pins that had rolled onto the table. Beside her, Akane was so embarrassed she couldn't bear to stay a second longer. She grabbed Suzuha's hand and began to make a move for the door—but before they could even take a step, Aurelia barreled into both of them and wrapped them in a tight hug. The little crybaby was sobbing like the mascot on that pin again. "T-this is perfect… the best thing in the entire world!" She could barely get the words out between her tears.

Even though her parents still couldn't be there for that birthday in particular, Aurelia no longer felt lonely. Suzuha lit the cake candles for her, and Akane set a party hat on her head. The birthday song they sang for her became the most beautiful melody Aurelia had ever heard.
When she blew out the candles, she prayed with all her might that she'd be with these friends of hers forever.

To master anime culture, Hathor approached it with the spirit of tackling a difficult challenge: learning from Haniel and diving into "Gen Z."

Instead, during planned time periods, she pulled out a 1,000-page notebook to record various questions that arose while watching, and after finishing each episode, she wrote a review analyzing plot highlights, viewer comment dynamics, character relationships, and more. She never skipped episodes or watched in double speed, and she categorized and filed the personal styles of the main creative team's directors, scriptwriters, and animation staff.

ST_File.F_NPC015_014:
It took Jiuyuan a lot of effort to retrieve Hathor after she was taken by the Bureau for losing control of her Esper Abilities. The loss of control itself wasn't the issue. What mattered was how Hathor handled the aftermath, and this was the first lesson Jiuyuan, as Hathor's mentor, needed to teach.
From that day on, Hathor doubled her training regimen on her own. Her movements grew faster and her decisions sharper as she shed off exhaustion for stability. Her expression remained calm, but her rhythm had become erratic. Jiuyuan knew this state all too well: the more one rushes to control one's powers, the easier it becomes for the powers to control them. She didn't stop Hathor’s training, nor did she warn her about overdoing it. Some students tend to mistake reminders for warnings or interpret concern as mentors thinking they aren’t trying hard enough. Rather than have Hathor quietly use such warnings as a new benchmark to push even harder, Jiuyuan thought it was better to let her train where she could watch. By keeping an eye on things, nothing would go wrong.
But the nature of Sterry's work meant Jiuyuan couldn't have Hathor's back forever. How could she pave the way before letting go? What she hadn't expected was that the solution would find its way to her. Haniel, who had stumbled onto the scene when Hathor lost control, unexpectedly had the ability to calm her. And as luck would have it, the girl was also interested in courier work…
Things just fell into place.

Hathor's execution and combat abilities were impeccable, but interacting with others left her at a loss. When the two little owlets first arrived, Hathor faced them like someone flipping through a book with no instructions: cautious, yet clueless about where to begin. The awkwardness in the shop didn't elude Jiuyuan. In a rare move, she gave Hathor a special commission: make an effort to understand today's youth and assimilate.
Imagining the ever-methodical Hathor carrying out this commission, Jiuyuan, who was usually so adept at controlling her emotions, couldn't suppress a smile—her first one.
What Jiuyuan had always known, but Hathor had yet to realize: that stubborn, almost clumsy honesty of hers, was exactly what she needed to connect with those two little owlets.

Changes began to occur in Hathor’s daily life: popular comics started appearing on her desk, and on days off, she would go to livehouses with Haniel and Illica instead of staying alone in the training room. Occasionally, new words she'd never used before would slip into her conversations.
Though Hathor still worried about losing control, much of her tension had vanished amidst the laughter and playfulness of everyday life at Sterry. After one Esper control lesson, Jenson, who had been watching, teased, "You've been mentoring her for so long, and now she's getting more popular thanks to being 'led astray' by those two little owlets. How does that feel?"
"I thought you only cared about fishing. Seems you haven't completely lost your sense as a spy."
Hathor's tone was as flat as ever: "Would you like me to conduct another loss-of-control test right now?"
Jiuyuan glanced at Jenson, who was silently calculating the renovation costs if Hathor decided to lose control on purpose. Jiuyuan couldn't help but smile. "No need. Things are just fine the way they are."
There's no need to mold a student to fit some standard. She can find her own answer.

ST_File.F_NPC027_015:
Humans and Anomalies can't ever truly understand each other's feelings. Or rather, a human can never really understand an Anomaly.
A group of bored children came across a lone Fluffy in the grass. The kid leading the group got a bright idea: he wanted to see what the Fluffy looked like after it transformed, and the others quickly agreed. Treating it like a toy, their poking and teasing gradually transformed into bullying. There is a natural divide between humans and Anomalies; therefore, it is only natural for children not to empathize with an Anomaly. But Linko stood there in silence, unsure how to speak up. Little by little, she began to pick up Fluffy's frequency as it shifted from hurt and confusion into anger.
"St… stop! It's… really sad right now, and if you guys keep going… it'll be dangerous…"
For the first time in her life, Linko shouted at her "friends."
But what came next, whether it was the frequency she felt or the voices she heard, crushed her hopes.
"It's just an Anomaly. Why are you trying so hard to play the saint…?"
"You care so much about what it feels like, but you don't care about how we feel?"
"What a buzzkill freak…"
More than hurt, what filled Linko's heart was disappointment. She and the Fluffy stayed in that grassy field, silent for a long, long time.
Do people boxed in by common sense or prejudice really understand each other? Can they even understand each other at all? Maybe "fitting in" itself is just an illusion; people imprisoned by judgment can never truly understand one another, and all efforts to fit in will only end in a futile tug-of-war.
"We all live in our own frequencies, sending signals into the universe that go unanswered."
That night, Linko wrote in her diary.
Humans can't understand each other either. One person can never really understand how another feels.
Like stars in the night sky, like islands in the sea, gazing at one another across an abyss…
Linko no longer wanted friends.

ST_File.F_NPC027_011:
Humans, Anomalies, and everything else all possess a singular, universal truth—a drive to be perceived; like flocks of birds flashing their feathers, flowers giving off aromas, whales singing into the deep… But beyond that, there's something at our core, something even more uniquely our own, spreading outward from body and mind, crossing the thickest barriers and the deepest voids, ceaselessly proving our existence and uniqueness to the universe.
"Like… a 'frequency,' only tuned differently."
When Linko was having her Esper ability information registered, nearly everyone who dealt with her was left more confused than they started. Nothing the girl described could be verified by any device or theory, and yet they all stated at some point that they could clearly feel—if only for a moment—that they were being connected with, as if resonating on the same frequency as something else… Until Linko would say something she really shouldn't in that innocent, caring, faintly sympathetic voice of hers, and they would hurriedly put their dependable adult masks back on.
"Work's really rough, huh… Why not just jump ship?"
"Cough, cough! No, I can't. And I wasn't even thinking about such things. Next question—"

In the early days after her Esper ability awakened, Linko would often be left dizzy after syncing up with too many frequencies at once—causing her to send the noise flooding into her mind back out again unconsciously, disrupting nearby equipment and people. As a result, the Bureau custom-built a head-mounted device for her to help block out interference and to help her focus. Most people her age might have found its design a little intimidating, but Linko loved it. After her ability awakened, the things she liked—and the reasons she liked them or was drawn to them—only became harder for others to understand, which made it even harder for her to fit in. Fortunately, for a loner like Linko, "not being understood" was never a problem that needed solving.
And yet, one accident long ago introduced her to a new companion, and one act of courage landed her a new responsibility. After facing off against the gloomy, taciturn ETD-6 captain, Linko was approved to become the Guarantor for the Oddity Xiaozhen and was brought into ETD-6 as its youngest member due to a special exception. Exe's judgment was spot-on: Linko's Esper Ability made it far easier for ETD-6 to track down and capture Anomaly-related criminals. Whether it was truly frequencies guiding her, or merely the universe putting her on the right path, Linko's uncanny intuition was vital to cracking major cases regardless. Even so, even after a year in ETD, many people still can't help but worry about her wildly offbeat way of doing things.
"…Um, Linko, aren't we a little too far from the main group?"

ST_File.F_NPC003_015:

ST_File.F_NPC028_017:
What makes a human human?

Before waking up, Iroi had a long, strange dream. It started in the pitch-black depths of the sea, slowly rising up, then stepping onto land, running like mad through a barren jungle just to avoid being eaten.
I heard everyone has a dream like this while they're still in the womb. You watch yourself crawl from the water onto land, slowly evolving into a human, and finally wake up naturally, right as you're being born.
But in that dream, Iroi wasn't born as a primate. Instead, she was sent on a different evolutionary path, becoming one of the Caprinae.
This should never have happened, and her human nature forced her to wake up from that dream. And so, she woke up in her mother's womb way too early.
Fetuses wake up, but Iroi's case was different. She woke up with complete consciousness. She touched around, felt the warmth around her, and caught the occasional glimpse of faint light. It was dim, warm, comfortable, with a pulse beating in rhythm with her own. So this is the "world," so this was what it felt like to be "alive."
She was taken away as her world opened up.
After living in the womb, the real world overflowed with light and empty space. It was terrifying. Her mind was shocked, and she no longer wanted to live. As a result, Iroi lost consciousness, and her body shut down. That's the beginning of her sicknesses.

At first, the Iroi created from her powers only knew that she must live.
When she was hungry or was in pain, she voiced her needs to attract attention.
Then she noticed that people made all kinds of sounds to express their thoughts. She slowly started to understand the sounds, then tried making them herself—and that, is how she learned to speak.
Just saying something out loud isn't always enough to make people believe it, so she learned all the right expressions.
Knowing what to say, to whom, and in what context, that's something she also had to pick up, however slowly…

Having grown up this way, how exactly is she any different from any authentic human being?

—Humans usually do not question whether they are humans or not. She does. That's about it.

After retiring from her previous job, Jiuyuan settled into a fairly relaxed life at Sterry.
The day-to-day tasks aren't complicated: sending and receiving packages, checking receipts, and passing around clipboards for signatures… As long as the process is clear and the staff reliable, none of the tasks pose much of a challenge. The real headaches come from commissions that can't be handled through any standard procedures: those involving intel, Anomalies, and the Anomaly Hunters who handle them. Clients with hidden agendas tapping their fingers on the counter, buyers using Anomalies as cover for covert handoffs, clients falsifying danger levels to drag Sterry into their schemes, not to mention the tangled web of factions at play… These may not seem a big deal, yet calculated troubles are far more vexing than any package delivery.

Still, Jiuyuan handles them all with ease.
One moment she's making small talk with a contact at a banquet hall, and the next she's at the scene of a target's transaction, tidying up the mess. She never breaks a sweat, and leaves only the cool scent of roses in her wake. With her intel and finesse, she has quietly woven a web across the fabric of this city. Most ripples, no matter how faint, inevitably land in it.

Though, what she excels at most is reading people.
Hathor, earnest to the point of stubbornness, is assigned to critical operations, handling high-risk Anomalies or missions where failure isn't an option.
Haniel and Illica, lively and quick on their feet, are better suited for dealing with people or coming up with a spark of brilliance when situations go sideways.
As for Manager Jenson and what he's been up to lately…
He really should find a better hiding spot for that fishing rod.

There are currently no late-night chat sessions happening between antiques in Eibon… probably. After all, not many of them can talk. This doesn't stop the Temporal Globe from rolling around when bored, surveying the other items in the shop and letting its imagination run wild.
(Hey, newcomer, where are you from?)
(I used to sleep in a dirty street until someone took a liking to me and bought me. The cost of my freedom was 998 Fons. Does that put me at the bottom of the hierarchy in this shop?)
(There are plenty who don't even know their own worth. Like me, I stayed in a dark, cramped place for ages and ages… so long that the little crack I had grew bigger and successfully merged with the original carved patterns… until… light came in. That woman appeared, gently lifted me out, and smiled.)
(Was it one of those scheming, triumphant smirks?)
(No. It was a completely confident smile, like she was certain I'd be there. But for some reason, that smile made her seem somewhat… regretful?)

ST_File.F_NPC013_011:
The bodyguard at Eibon Antique Shop does not say much, always standing quietly beside everyone else. She seems to have a nickname, "Daff," which Hotori occasionally calls her. Whenever Hotori calls her that, Daffodill looks away, her ears turning completely red. As for the others… if they want to be cut to pieces, they are welcome to try using that name.

Daffodill owns many eyepatches. Though she wears them less now, she still keeps up her collecting habit. Nobody can tell the difference between those eyepatches, but she firmly believes in her taste. Leather ones, patterned ones, ones with especially neat stitching… she carefully sorts them by category and places them in her small collection box.

Daffodill was not born with poor vision; rather, it was the price of her Esper Ability. At nineteen, cruel truth burst into her eyes like a kaleidoscope, and since then she could see through anomalies to perceive layers of essence across time and space. Sometimes, glimpsing the truth is not a good thing. She learned about her parents' cause of death, about her own wishful emotional attachments, about needing and being needed… and lost the faith she had relied on for survival. The red-cloaked hero in the picture book silently turned her blade toward Mother, toward that hateful, beating heart that had once falsely given her warmth. If the goddess of vengeance wanted to punish her for this… then so be it.

Daff longed for a happy, beautiful place, and so accidentally embarked on a journey full of metaphors.
So then, what about the ending of the story?
Her life until now was one monopolized by lies. It was a life in which no one needed her… there was no point in continuing. That was what Daffodill had been thinking when she met that slightly tipsy woman. The woman talked about a daffodil growing in the center of the lake, proud and aloof, seemingly impossible for anyone to pick. She naturally needed that flower too, but would not pick it.
A strange woman and a strange flower. What reason did that daffodil have for growing alone there? It must depend on something. Surely it grew that way because it was rooted in others' need for it. When the wind rose, Daffodill heard a different sound of rustling leaves than before.

Why not follow the woman and seek answers in the life ahead?

ST_File.F_NPC030_016:
Hey there, friend! If you've made it this far, you must be pretty patient~
I don't know when you first found out about us or read those stories, or how much outside information had been released by then. Hmm… Anyway, there's something pretty interesting I can tell you about "information."
Have you ever thought about how the amount of information you had about all this before opening this save file, the order in which you encountered it, and your own subjective interpretation of it all can dramatically affect "the reality you perceive"?
That might sound a little abstract, so let me give you a couple of simpler examples.

For instance, when Exe first joined the Bureau, people in other departments were scared of him and kept their distance because of the look on his face. They immediately labeled him hard to get along with and started gossiping, each trying to avoid being the first to deal with him. So I selectively edited his full reason for joining, leaving out the context, and spread the message that he was "working to see that the criminal who killed his close friend was punished."
Think about it. When most people hear that, they naturally assume it means "he's working to secure the killer's apprehension," right? So they mistake him for someone who's cold on the outside but warm inside, with a strong sense of justice—even though they don't know him at all. Once I'd changed their impression of him, people in the other departments stopped making so many negative comments. Their attitudes improved, and they became much more willing to put up with his little lapses in social grace.
There wasn't even 0.01% of a lie in it, you know. They simply didn't guess what the sentence really meant.
It really does save a lot of unnecessary effort. Even Exe picked up the trick and started using it himself, grumbling all the while~ Now you know.

Here's another example. Do you have a sense of how the order in which you receive information can affect things? Let's say you encounter it in this order: first you get to know "this me," then you see what little "Y" looks like.
Without any further explanation, wouldn't you be more inclined to assume that "little 'Y' is me as a child" rather than "I'm using the likeness of little 'Y'"? After all, "this image is me" has already taken hold in your mind.
If simply switching the order can have that kind of effect, just imagine the potential of using more advanced, more precise methods.
If you can grasp even a little of that power, perhaps you'll understand how information tech can be used as a weapon to kill someone who once existed—or as a forbidden spell that creates life from nothing, making someone who never existed real.

After all the information you've received along the way, you probably have some thoughts of your own by now.
But even those thoughts might be the result of carefully crafting, adjusting, and controlling the information you've been given to steer them in another direction.
—Even so, do you still believe in "the reality you perceive"?

ST_File.F_NPC016_012:
In Sterry's early days, there were only three people. Though few in number, they had clear divisions of labor. The Mentor, well-versed in human weaknesses, frequently moved in social circles, while Jenson, with his proper speech and meticulous attention to protocol and rules, could break through negotiation deadlocks with just a few words, making him better suited for business cooperation discussions. However, from beginning to end, Hathor always maintained some reservations toward Jenson. Her sharp instincts for danger, honed through long training, whispered warnings that this man wasn't as rule-abiding as he appeared, though the Mentor's good working relationship with him indicated that Jenson could currently be trusted. As for the heavy responsibility of package delivery, it naturally fell to Hathor, who joined last.
Sterry's Elite Courier, the tough biker chick of few words, first choice for urgent delivery quests. Regular items, fragile goods, anomaly packages—all reached their destinations accurately, safely, and intact to the roar of her motorcycle. Some statistics claimed that her single-day record was 200 regular deliveries and 11 anomaly containers, all completed while assisting as an Anomaly Hunter contain two Class III anomalies. She was truly a tireless delivery machine: cold, ruthless, efficient.
Hathor herself hadn't noticed that such a pace was too demanding and had gone on too long. It wasn't until she returned one day to the shop, seeing her Mentor smiling and introducing Sterry's new members, that Hathor truly realized how exhuasted from work she was.

ST_File.F_NPC027_016:
When Linko was ten, she would often follow frequencies and wander all over the city by herself. Feeling out unknown frequencies and exploring wherever they led became her own private, joyful way of passing the time—even if her adventures usually only turned up strange little things, and sometimes even led her to dangerous Anomalies, Linko never got tired of it.
One afternoon, Linko sensed a warm, welcoming frequency, full of an energetic, life-filled energy. She followed its direction, passing through streets and alleys, turning several corners, and even climbing a big tree, all under the frequency's guidance.
She was small, however, and the trunk was huge. She ran out of strength halfway up the tree. Stuck there with nowhere to go, she could only curl up and think of a way out of her situation. Suddenly, a girl in a Clement Academy uniform jumped down from a higher branch and helped her down, all while saying things like, "What were you thinking, climbing a tree this high all by yourself?"
"I'm playing Tamachi GO. I thought I could catch a Rare Tamachi up in the tree, but instead… I only caught you! Here, let me show you my Tamachi Index…"
"Huh?! That really is a Rare Tamachi! You must be a genius at this sort of thing!"
A gentle, kind frequency came from the girl. Like a sunflower basking in the sun. Linko brightened up too.
After that, Linko often went exploring all over the city with her newfound sister-figure, and she started collecting her own Tamachi Index too. She always searched for Tamachi purely by instinct. Even though it got her into plenty of trouble from time to time, the joy of pet-hunting outweighed it all. Still, her Index never quite caught up to her sister's.
Two years later, her sister became busy with school and handed her beloved console and handwritten strategy notes over to Linko, asking her to inherit her Tamachi Index and become a Tamachi Master for the both of them.
"Linko is the best guide in all of Hethereau. Believe in yourself—your path is the right path!"
That was what Linko's sister had said to her the last time they met.
After that, Linko kept exploring the city, squeezing into every nook and cranny to catch Tamachi. She still got lost often, but in the end, she always found her way back home. Every time she caught a new Tamachi, she compared her own Index with her sister's, only to find that her sister had already collected it. Nevertheless, Linko didn't lose heart. She just kept searching, believing that one day her Index would catch up to her sister's and even surpass it.
But from then on, every time she caught a Tamachi, Linko never again felt that same warm, lively frequency.
"So the source of that frequency was my sister all along…"

ST_File.F_NPC027_017:
After starting middle school, Linko still often strolled around Hethereau, following the guidance of all kinds of strange frequencies. One day, she went in through the back door of a building and accidentally stumbled into an Anomalous Realm. It was a room with walls that were lined with old TVs, most of them with broken screens that no longer turned on. Following a faint but warm frequency, she searched through the pile of battered old TVs and found one that was very, very small.
Driven by a sudden instinct, Linko pressed the power switch. After a burst of static, a little ghost suddenly popped out.
"Wah!! You unlucky little imp, how dare you disturb this evil spirit's rest! As compensation, starting today, you belong to this evil spirit as its servant! Heh heh heh—mmph—"
Having seen plenty of horror movies, Linko wasn't scared in the slightest. She simply scooped up the little ghost like she was catching a stray cat on any normal day.
"So you were fine, after all. Just a minute ago, your frequency almost disappeared."
"Huh? Frequency? Gone? What kind of nonsense are you spewing? I was just taking a little nap in the TV!"
"You live in a TV… Tamachi live in a screen too, so you're basically like a Tamachi—oh! So you're an electronic pet!"
"Huh? What the hell is that supposed to mean? Who are you calling a pet!? Believe it or not, this evil spirit will mmmph—"
"Yes. From now on, I'll call you Xiaozhen."
After that baffling negotiation, Linko took the little ghost Xiaozhen away… along with her TV.
But when they left the Anomalous Realm, a group of people in Bureau uniforms were already waiting at the entrance for them.
What Linko didn't know at the time was that Xiaozhen had long existed as an Anomaly inside the office building. She could slip into all kinds of TVs and would occasionally pop out to scare employees working late. But on that day, an Esper criminal broke into the building with hopes to cause harm. Just as he was about to attack an innocent employee, they were suddenly dragged into the Anomalous Realm. According to the people who experienced it firsthand, it was a labyrinth made from countless piled-up TVs. They were sealed away in a safe room, while the criminal was confronted by ghostly fire spilling out from countless TV screens, and by a massive ghost formed from those coalescing flames. The battle in the Anomalous Realm lasted for what felt like hours. The ghost's strength was nearly exhausted, and was almost nullified. However, Xiaozhen used the last of her strength to fling the criminal out of the Anomalous Realm. After that, she found the last intact TV and went into a deep slumber… until Linko suddenly woke her again.
In the end, ETD-6 arrested the injured Esper criminal in the empty building. Not long afterward, Linko and the office workers reappeared inside. Fortunately, there were no casualties. Linko and Xiaozhen were investigated by the Bureau following the whole debacle. Linko met a grim-faced young man, and the uniformed personnel seemed to treat him with considerable deference.
"The Celaeno Compound is interested in that ghost."
Linko didn't know what kind of place that was, but her instincts told her it couldn't mean anything good for Xiaozhen. She could vaguely sense that even within the deathly-still frequency of the man before her, there might be a weak point she could utilize…
"Xiaozhen isn't a malicious spirit. I'm not handing her over to you, because…"
Firm and unflinching, Linko clutched the TV with Xiaozhen inside tightly to her chest.
"—she's my friend. I don't want to be separated from her."
"…"
The young man said nothing more. Not long after, Linko received a document. An ETD captain secured the decision that allowed her to keep Xiaozhen. On the condition that she accept ETD oversight and arrangements, she would be permitted to become Xiaozhen's Guarantor.
"Xiaozhen, Xiaozhen! I'm your official Guarantor now!"
"Guarantor? What does that mean?"
"It's not a master and not a servant… um… whatever. The point is, you get to stay with me!"
"…Heh heh heh~ Then this evil spirit shall graciously look after you, little frequency imp!"

Haniel's books are always filled with bookmarks, each stamped with little animal paw prints. Whenever Haniel befriends small animals in the park, she makes a special bookmark for them, stamping their paws as keepsakes. These little travelers are always on the move. Who knows when they'll meet again?

It still sleeps peacefully on the same little hillside. Haniel sometimes goes there to play guitar, even though she sounds terrible.

ST_File.F_NPC014_011:
Haniel. Public Bagel Account: @Haniel_SterryExpress. Private Account: @genesectparanormaldeptace. Current main alt: @fancontentmaster. The public account is for plugging Sterry Express and managing the brand image of Sterry Express—"If the money's good, we deliver anything!" (Jiuyuan's words). The private account is Haniel's main social hub: fics, art, music, cosplay sets… In the scene, she's a god-tier creator with an endless output. Her only flaw? Her posting schedule is a disaster! Her fans live in permanent agony, screaming: "It's so good, I'll take whatever crumbs I can get!" As for the alt, on days she's too lazy to post, Haniel just surfs Bagel incognito on various throwaway accounts. The second her cover is blown, she jumps ship to the next. She's sworn to defend the sacred right to consume fan content in peace.

Ever delivered a package before? Every Sterry Express courier has their own delivery ritual. For Haniel, the moment she gets the delivery slip, it's like a quest notification has dropped straight into her hands——
Today's Quest: Deliver Package (0/1)
Package Integrity: 100%
Time Left: 00:59:59
3-Star Rating:
No-Damage Delivery (0/1)
On-Time Delivery (0/1)
Service with a Smile (0/1)

When Haniel was little, she had a ton of so-called "hobbies": violin, horseback riding, chess… Just like every other kid in her circle, she went through the usual "elite education" routine. She didn't hate any of it, but that didn't mean she liked it either. It all felt like a drizzly, soggy day where the world's colors are washed out and even birds feathers get stuck together.
Haniel likes sunny days better. So, before her nightly bedtime story, little Haniel sat down with her mother for a real conversation on equal footing. She laid out what she wanted and what confused her, asking the person closest to her for help. Her mom gently stroked her hair and apologized, saying she'd failed to notice Haniel's feelings in time.
Finding your true "hobby," the thing that's really yours, is hard. Luckily, Haniel was one of the fortunate ones.

ST_File.F_NPC005_012:
At Leon International, Skia embodied the role of a regular office worker and was naturally suited for that kind of life.
In modern civilized society, the fact that awakening Esper Abilities could change physical appearance was already common knowledge. His transformation was indeed dramatic, and just one look gave him a worse shock than any he'd experienced in five years of work… but once he calmed down, there was nothing he couldn't rationalize. After all, it wasn't a job that depended on looks, so it shouldn't break his routine…
The truth was, his routine wasn't determined by his own mindset.
Back then, he'd stood up in the meeting room, unable to bear it any longer, forcing himself to remain polite as he asked why the projects he'd always handled weren't even going through him for reports anymore.
Sitting among the well-dressed elites around him, someone wrinkled their eyes forcefully. Skia later realized it was the kind of motion… like trying to squeeze out some murky substance that had fallen into their eye.
As the meeting adjourned, Skia raised his gaze, looking past the cracks in his self-imposed mask that he was forced to reexamine, his eyes meeting the massive silhouette in the center of the projection screen that rose with his standing figure.
Does he look like a monster to others?
Well, at least the price of gaining the Esper Ability's wasn't too high. Now he was a regular office worker in every way except appearance.

ST_File.F_NPC023_012:
While the other children were still busy slobbering all over their recorders, Akane could cover the holes with her little fingers and play a complete melody. Besides the recorder, she was interested in anything that could produce beautiful sounds: the harmonica, piano, violin, and even the simple triangle.
Akane could play the theme song from Kokoro Rider, but she didn't understand what her classmates meant when they talked about "heroes." It didn't matter. She could still make beautiful music, even if she was the only one listening.
One day, Akane went into town with her parents and saw a young band performing beside a busy street. Even though only a few people stopped to listen, they kept singing and playing. The passion in their music drew Akane in.
Was being in a band different?
Akane found the acoustic guitar her father had once used and gently plucked the strings, imitating the guitarist she saw earlier. But the guitar was far too old and terribly out of tune. Her parents saw it all, however. At her elementary school graduation ceremony, Akane received her first guitar.
Akane joined many bands over the years, but often left them soon afterward. Bands broke up for all kinds of reasons: moving away, pursuing further education, creative differences, among other reasons. Yet Akane was desperately searching for that electrifying feeling she had felt when she first heard that band perform. Akane looked at the band posters on the wall—HTRE. The young musicians who had once performed on street corners were now taking the stage at Imaginist, while Akane could only watch from the audience.
So when Aurelia asked if she wanted to start a band, Akane accepted almost without hesitation.
—A band that belonged to them, and to Akane herself.
Now Akane was standing onstage too. The blinding lights made it impossible to see the audience, but she could hear their cheers pulsing in her ears.
At that moment, Akane's heart beat only for one song—her own.

ST_File.F_NPC022_015:
Among all her sisters, only one made Zankou limit her abilities when they locked eyes.
Her soul was a pure, translucent flame, as clear as the first light of dawn. As if beholding a wondrous sight, she blurted out at their very first meeting…
"What a beautiful color…"
But the white-clad girl named Daffodill didn't understand. She simply obeyed her adoptive mother's orders, walked to the car door, bowed, and reached out to welcome her new little sister.
"Welcome home, little sister."
Zankou reached out toward her, obsession and curiosity gathering in her eyes. Unknowingly, a feral smile nearly surfaced on the girl's face. As if snatching something away, she suddenly clutched that girl's hand tightly, pulling her closer, as if wanting to bathe herself in that hallowed flame…
After that unconventional greeting, they were eventually ordered to become partners, sisters—family.
Zankou knew she and her sister were not the same, but so what? Two complete opposites—conjoined in their fate. In the Scarlet Letter Garden, countless vines would wind around and bind them, till death did them part. They would step into the same mire, share the same flower bed, walk onto the same battlefield, and return to the same grave. They were as close as family could be.
Day after day, she watched Daffodill through her "special" eye. As the first daughter adopted by Inanna, Daffodill was steadfast and immovable, rigid—no matter how harsh the mission, she would always surpass Mother's expectations. When it came to eliminating a target, she was even unfeeling… Yet that very same sister would tenderly heal her wounds after every mission or punishment.
…But later, for some undiscernable reason, Daffodill changed. That decisiveness and indifference became hesitation, along with growing melancholy and confusion. From then on, that white, steady flame would occasionally flutter.
"So she has a side like that too, then."
Zankou continued to observe Daffodill, as though watching a bud begin to blossom. If her sister became weak, before Mother destroyed and discarded her, she would transform her into her most prized possession. With a heavy heart, Zankou looked forward to that day.

ST_File.F_NPC026_013:
In an age when digital payments are everywhere, Chiichan still insists on withdrawing her salary from the bank each month, exchanging it for cash, and dividing it into a thin stack and a thick stack. She picks up the thin stack and counts it carefully. Once, twice, three times. Then she takes a few bills from it and adds them to the thick stack before tucking it all into a sturdy envelope.
"This address…" she says. "We don't have direct delivery there." The post office clerk looks at the destination with some difficulty.
"Th-That's okay."
"There's a good chance it could get lost with that many transfers, you know?"
"…Yes, I know."
Chiichan hands the envelope to the clerk. The envelope is stamped; she receives a mailing receipt in return. Walking home with the receipt, a map slowly unfolds in her mind. Chiichan has looked at many maps. On them, the place where she was born is just a tiny dot. If she left from Hethereau, she would have to take a very, very long boat ride to reach a new city, then transfer to a train and ride for a very, very long time to yet another city… If she chose to fly partway, she would have to take a very, very long bus ride… But even once she's figured out the route home, she has to think about the travel costs, and the savings needed so her family could live happily together without ever having to hunt Apocha again. She calculates how much she can save each month, how long it will take… By the time she's done with all the calculations, she's arrived.
Chiichan stands in front of the mailbox by her door, breathing deeply. Whenever she moves somewhere new, the first thing she does is send her new address back home. Then she waits. Maybe today will bring a letter…
"Knock knock." Chiichan taps lightly on the mailbox. "Knock knock." Two more taps.
This is a secret code between the siblings: it means "I found you." When they couldn't speak, they would answer each other with soft knocks instead.
Chiichan opens the mailbox. Inside is nothing but dust. So it is, every month.
Chiichan closes the mailbox and goes home with another mailing receipt. There are a dozen identical ones in her bedside drawer. So it is, every month.
Chiichan doesn't know when she will receive a letter from home. Maybe tomorrow. Maybe next month. Maybe never.

ST_File.F_NPC023_015:
One of the accounts Akane follows on Bagel is the official "Tamamochi Street Life" account. Its profile is frequently updated with news about events on Tamamochi Street, and from time to time, a figure riding a jellyfish appears in their posts.
Hethereau is a city both big and small. It's big enough that people living in the same city can go years without crossing paths, yet small enough that you might spot an old acquaintance just by scrolling through Bagel's local feed—or learn how someone's doing without ever actually seeing them in person.
Akane knew that, even after everything Aurelia had been through, she was still as cheerful and optimistic as ever. But the more Aurelia seemed like her old self, the less Akane knew how to face her. That day, pain spread silently through the corridor outside the ward, oppressively subduing her until it was too hard to breathe. Faced with Aurelia's parents' accusations and tears, Suzuha fled in a panic, while Akane could say nothing but, "I'm sorry." In the end, she chose to run away too.
The only reply beneath that Bagel post sat there alone for two years. She had hesitated, and ultimately missed her chance. After that, she could never bring herself to speak.
It was Night of Moondog again, tonight. This time, though, one of them was still onstage, one was in the audience, and the other was in a distant city. Only after the stage lights went out and her phone screen lit up did a new message finally appear in their long-abandoned Bagel chat.
If Aurelia, who could barely walk, could finally take that first step, then Akane should be able to as well. Akane replied to Aurelia's message, then finally worked up the courage to open her other friend's profile. A guitarist who could handle the most complicated songs kept hitting the wrong keys while typing out her message. After several attempts, however, she finally managed to send a proper message: "How have you been?"
Akane turned off her screen as soon as she sent it. A reply didn't come until the next day.
"So-so."
Akane smiled faintly when she saw it. This was much simpler than she'd imagined. The quiet group chat for the three of them finally resurrected. They sometimes shared bits of everyday life, but the days when they could talk about anything were over. Now they chatted carefully, steering clear of painful subjects—including the music they had once loved most.
Then one day, Akane saw a post on Bagel about Clement's Centennial School Alumni Reunion and finally took the step she should have taken long ago—
"@Suzuha @Aurelia, are you coming to the reunion?"
ST_File.F_NPC030_011:
Whenever someone new joins the much-feared ETD, Bureau employees can't help wondering: Is another terrifying or high-maintenance weirdo joining up?
The only exception seems to be the lieutenant of ETD-6, who won everyone's trust and affection with ease from the moment she showed up. She fit right in, as if she'd always been there!
The creation of ETD-6 had been a sudden, somewhat experimental decision. Rumors had only just begun circulating that the director had personally promoted a young man with a strategically valuable Esper Ability and tasked him with forming a squad. No one had even seen him yet. Yet the "lieutenant" had already made herself at home, moving from office to office and building relationships throughout the Bureau. She helped the new squad establish smooth communication and cooperation with the other departments.
Even though there were fewer rumors about her past before joining than there were about the reclusive captain's… everyone still accepted her in no time.

Elyms is known for her kindness, wit, and knack for looking after people's feelings. Even strangers quickly feel like old friends around her and find themselves opening up. She makes friends with all kinds of people in no time. As the officer responsible for ETD-6's internal and external communications and information flow, she also seems to have an extensive network both inside and outside the Bureau, which is invaluable when investigating Anomaly Crimes.
In her free time, you can often find her on the phone, browsing Bagel, or chatting with online friends. And she never lets social media distract her from her real-life friends. It's hard to imagine how much social energy it takes to make sure no one who talks to her ever feels ignored.
She has another curious habit: she effortlessly adjusts her way of speaking to suit whoever she's talking to. Maybe that's why people's impressions of Elyms can differ slightly in the details, but everyone agrees she's cheerful, friendly, and incredibly easy to get along with. She's a real social butterfly.

"You always reply so fast! I just sent you a message, and you already answered!"
"Haha~ If I know what I want to say, I just go ahead and send it!"
"But you're always chatting with so many friends at once. How do you manage to reply to so many people?"
"I'm a really, really fast typist! Whoosh—whoosh! Want to see? Oh, and I have more than one device. I can type with both hands flying, and there's voice input too~!"
"Why do I always feel like I know you? Like we were really close a long time ago."
"I've actually felt that way too. So… do you remember anything more specific?"
"Let me think… Hmm, before… where were you? What did you do?"
"Well, maybe I was… someone you could vent to online? Customer support for a platform? A counselor? Something like that~" she replied with a half-joking air.

Before entering Ghroth Island, Chaos was an Anomaly Hunter on a small island, where he went by his old name, Conrak. Eventually, he would abandon the name he received from his parents like a sunken boat in the sea.

Conrak once got into a shipwreck with another 11 crewmates. They found themselves in an ocean isolated from the world.
There was an archipelago in the ocean, which didn't even have internet access. Conrak and his crewmates settled on one of the islands but never stopped wanting to go back. Unfortunately, no islander was willing to leave their home to ferry them across unknown waters, and no outside vessels passed through the islands. The group decided to build a ship and sail home by themselves. They named the ship "the Boulder."
Once they built the Boulder, the group began to save up supplies for their return trip. For two years, the group navigated the Boulder around the islands to transport goods for funds. Since the group members were also Anomaly Hunters, they often took commissions, solving many issues that plagued the islanders. Gradually the "Boulder Hunters" became known local heroes.
In the end, because the group lived peacefully on the islands and was praised as heroes, some of them no longer wished to risk another adventure to return. Only five of them decided to go back.

However, on its return journey, the Boulder went through a storm. Conrak fell into the sea, and his companions weren't able to find him.
Luckily, Conrak fell into the sea near Ghroth Island and was saved by an Undertaker from the Island.
Once he formally joined Ghroth Island, Conrak changed his name to Chaos.

ST_File.F_NPC012_013:
A child prodigy; the "golden kid;" "the boy kissed by the god of wisdom."

The day Edgar came back from Twinkle School of Espers, aunts, uncles, neighbors, and their children all swarmed in droves to congratulate him, nearly trampling down his family's doorstep. Whether they came out of curiosity to see what made this so-called "neighbor's kid you should learn from" so special, or were reluctant children dragged along by parents demanding they "learn from his example," they all reached the same conclusion:
He really didn't look like anything special.

Meanwhile, Edgar found himself surrounded by adults, completely overwhelmed. He just couldn't keep up with their overlapping chatter. As they talked over each other, Edgar's future became crystal clear in their minds: he'd immediately become a star researcher at Zerogon Laboratory, the rising star of Yggash Court, the new director of the Bureau of Anomaly Control. Pink Paws Bank's job offer was worth considering too. With Edgar's abilities, why would't he become a board member at PPB? Of course, when the time came, he shouldn't forget to give a helping hand to that kid living diagonally across from him whose grades barely scraped by in every subject…

The adults listing out and arranging all these bright futures for him had become completely lost in their own fantasies. It was as if Edgar were their own child, fulfilling all the dreams they, themselves, couldn't…

Edgar looked around helplessly, unable to join any conversation. He was so nervous he pulled his scarf up high, wishing he could hide completely inside it. Luckily, at that very moment, his father squeezed through the crowd and patted his shoulder: "What do you want to be when you grow up, Edgar?"

Encouraged by his father's gaze, Edgar said softly:
"I… I just want to be Edgar."

She had never known that a daffodil grew in the center of the lake. She had never seen it as a child. Had it grown after Ms. T took her away?
The woman smiled and raised her wine bottle, inviting her to toast. Daffodill looked at her swaying, carefree manner and felt inexplicably angry.
"I have already lost everything. What exactly am I supposed to toast to?"
"Do toasts need reasons? Well… then… to the despair of having nothing, to skies never witnessed. And to the one and only daffodil in the center of this lake."
"…Do you want to pick that flower too?"
"Mmm… I need that flower. But I will not pick it."
Meeting Daffodill's look that clearly said this was contradictory, the woman tapped her forehead with the wet tip of her umbrella.
"Who decided that needing something means you must take it? I only need it to exist, so I can drink something fine while admiring it like this. That is enough for me."
When the wind rose, she heard a different sound of rustling leaves than before.
Perhaps… there really was a daffodil growing in the center of the lake.

At that moment, a pair of hands wearing red gloves covered her eyes.
Ms. T, who happened to be visiting, witnessed the tragedy of her parents alongside her. In her heartbreak, she offered to adopt Daffodill as her daughter. The beautiful girl had lost both parents, and no other relatives would risk being implicated by taking in a child of misfortune… She had always been the one who was not needed. Only Ms. T reached out her hand to her, so she gratefully took her place by Ms. T's side.
ST_File.NPC022_about_001: She has a pure soul, like a steady white flame that never burns out even in the midst of blood and violence. We were partners for years, and I never tasted a negative emotion from her. Then one day, standing over an enemy who was pleading, she hesitated. That night, the girl who never spoke about anything came to me for a talk. I thought she was growing weak, and while I was concerned for her change, another part of me wanted her to rely on me more… Then came the betrayal. I'll never forget the storm that day, the look on her face as she escaped, and the color burning in her soul… A color I'd never seen before.

Well then, you could probably take the grand prize in a "How Well Do You Know Miss Blackbird?" contest by now. I've rambled on quite a bit—I hope you haven't gotten tired of it yet.
I'm honestly surprised that anyone would be so deeply interested in my story, and it's left me a little flustered… Truth be told, I hadn't planned to write this much. My past has been long and rather dull, like a tedious, predictable movie with no climax worth waiting for. If I were to record every story from those hundreds of years, it might take about the same amount of time all over again. So I picked out just a small part to write down, and I hope I didn't bore you to death.
In the life I've lived, I've seen countless meetings and farewells. To me, people and birds are much the same—both only rest on a branch for a mere moment before quickly leaping into the boundless sky. I never expected to meet you, but I've already prepared myself for any parting the future may bring… Ah, please don't misunderstand. That's just the usual way a diviner thinks. One day, you'll go where you need to go, and meet all the people you need to meet. Our paths have crossed for only a moment, but being able to open my heart to you like this means more than I can say.
I can't see your past, but I can see that your road ahead will shine bright like the stars. No matter where fate leads us from here, I sincerely wish you happiness.
In any case, since our fates have already been decided, please don't worry too much about what I've said. At least in this moment, as you read these lines, I'll be by your side, sharing these feelings with you.

ST_File.F_NPC026_015:
After completing basic employee training, Chiz's first task at Pink Paws Bank was to get a customer to sign up for a card.
"It's easy," said Mayu, her mentor, patting her on the shoulder. "Our bank has the best benefits in all of Hethereau. You've got this."
"Sorry, I don't need one."
"No thank you."
"Uh-huh, okay, okay, uh-huh, okay, I understand, okay, okay."
Chiz collected dozens of polite refusals and cold shoulders. The air conditioning blasted in the bank lobby; Chiz felt cold inside, too. She huddled in a corner, wondering about resigning. Maybe she wasn't cut out for this job. She was always bad at so many things. She didn't even know how to write a resignation letter.
Chiz would probably remember the day she met Kolinsna forever, with her beautiful golden hair and dazzling red dress. Chiz felt like she was looking at Fons herself walking among mortals. She remembered how Mayu had described it: "Someone who looks like they'd definitely sign up for a card." Chiz really wanted to stay. She just had to try a little harder. So she gathered her courage and walked up. "H-Hello!" she started, "Welcome to Pink Paws Bank… Would you like to sign up for a card?"
The girl with the golden hair and red dress seemed startled by her. She stared at Chiz for a good while, then spoke. Her voice was lovely… until she proceeded to point out Chiz's every flaw; from the way she talked, to her outfit and appearance, to her posture and the angle she was standing at. Chiz felt stares coming from every direction. Tears were already welling up in her eyes. She really wasn't suited for this job after all…
"I'll sign up for a card."
Would Mayu teach her how to write a resignation letter…?
"Hey, don't you even know how to process a card?"
"S-sorry!" Chiz apologized on reflex, then kept responding yes, over and over. Before her brain could catch up, she was already standing in front of the machine. Somehow, despite her fumbling, she managed to successfully issue a card.
"Th-thank you for coming." She didn't know why things had turned out this way, but the result was delightful. After seeing off the young noblewoman, Mayu finally found her chance to approach. She looked at Chiz, who was especially happy about successfully signing up her first customer, with an indescribable expression. "Chiz, do you know who that was?"
"She was… That lady just now?"
"She's the Dvořák family's young lady."
Chiz's smile slowly faded. Pink Paws Bank belonged to the Dvořáks.
Under Mayu's pitying gaze, Chiz choked out: "M-Mayu, do you know how to write a resignation letter?"

ST_File.F_NPC028_012:
For most people, dreams are unstable and ephemeral. Iroi's Esper Ability stabalizes dreams, making them constants that do not cease to exist when impacted by external factors.
Iroi can send her dreams into the consciousness of other living beings. The number of beings she can affect at the same time varies, depending on the targets' mental strengths. If the target's mental strength is too high, she may not be able to break in at all. She also can't affect beings without sentience.

Two gates exist at the entrance of Iroi's dream world, a Horned Gate and an Ivory Gate. Sometimes she conceals one of them when necessary.
If one enters the Ivory Gate, they are forced to experience a long and bizarre dream of creatures fighting and devouring each other. No one knows why this is the case.
If one enters the Horned Gate, they reach Iroi's true dream world and can have a nice dream. The real Iroi is hiding somewhere in the corner of this world.

In other words, the "Iroi" people see on the outside is not her true self.
The Iroi people see is nothing but an illusion created by her powers. The external Iroi, after taking over the original, is in essence a non-human consciousness that mimics human beings.
Don't be afraid. The external Iroi has posed as a human for about twenty years. She's not that different from a genuine human. She won't bite.
No need to panic.

ST_File.F_NPC022_012:
When it comes to the unknown, human beings have always shared the same curiosity and arrogance. From awe to fear, from scrutinizing to touching, until the spark of "conquest" fully ignited the fuse of greed… such was the attitude some held toward the existence known as "Espers".
Cults, circles, private research institutes, secret societies… those driven by greed and pride gathered like hyenas, desperate for a morsel of flesh. They would pay any price, ignore every restriction and taboo, and thirst for the miracles an Esper Ability could bring… or perhaps, for the ability itself.
On a remote island, there was a secret society deemed "Eyepecker." Its members believed in a heresy: Esper Abilities were a gift from a mysterious unknown, and that gift would bless the fortunate ones born with special "eyes". They went about collecting those who were described as such, regarding them as "vessels" for the awakening of Esper Abilities, imprisoning them in dark, dank dungeons and burning their eyes every day with a searing mixture. They firmly believed this would awaken abilities—and that by transplanting those eyes into themselves, they could seize that power for their own.
Zankou's earliest memory began in that cruel jail.
The girl had a pair of gem-like eyes. She could not understand why, her vision deprived of color, she could only see a gray-white blur. What she understood even less was how far a human's greed could push them to do the unspeakable. Ever since Eyepecker had abducted her, the meaning of her existence had been reduced to being completely bound every day, having her eyelids pried open, and trembling as the scalding, acrid, murky liquid dripped onto her eyeballs.
The voracious, intoxicated by their own delusions, carried out their devilish deeds day after day, heedless of its absurdity. Yet, ironically, Zankou really did awaken the Esper Ability dwelling in her eyes under that inhuman torture. When she was brought to the eye-extraction ritual, the society's members were already arguing over who the eyes would belong to, each one revealing the hidden identity they had been concealing all along: the powerful, the wealthy, or some illustrious family… Their voices grew into a raucous uproar, and in the haze of anesthesia, Zankou saw the first color beyond black and white. It was warm and blinding, burning brightly among the embers of countless souls, spraying from wounds opened in slaughter, weaving into a scarlet maelstrom that encircled her…
That day, the Eye of Delusion shrouded the entire island, and the lowlifes who competed with one another instead butchered each other to death, drowning within the hallucination, until no one was left alive.
ST_File.F_NPC032_015:
For Shinku, the challenge of transferring to CSU-2 was more about getting along with the two new teammates than about getting used to a new place.

Whether Shinku puts on a resting drake face or makes up an excuse, Mint just brushes it off and keeps approaching her. "Resting drake face? Aww, why so grumpy, who made Taya angry this time? Or did you fail an exam?" "Busy? Sure, let's do it another time then! How about after work tomorrow?"
Mint does not know when to back off. She's just there because she wants to be. It's a hassle, really… but Shinku doesn't hate it—who hates a friendly kitty anyway?
As for the other teammate…
Oneiroi. After Shinku's first mission with her, she understood exactly why she'd been transferred to Unit 2. This one had the ability to prevent her from going berserk. This should have been good news for Shinku, because she'd finally stop worrying about hurting teammates. But she couldn't bring herself to accept Oneiroi the way she accepted Mint.
Iroi was hiding herself. She wasn't showing her true self…
And that was what Shinku was exactly doing.
