ST_File.F_NPC026_016:
Chiz is terrified of loud noises. She's been afraid of thunder since she was little, but it got so much worse after she became an Esper. This is the price she pays for her powers. The sound of popcorn machines, fireworks going off, even karaoke—any overly-noisy environment makes her heart race. Only her soundproof home soothes her. Because of this, Chiz never attends gatherings.
"Chiz, want to grab dinner together this weekend?"
Mayu was inviting her again. Chiz did want to go. She was so grateful to Mayu, the first person to show her kindness after she joined Pink Paws Bank. And it wasn't just Mayu; there was Haruna, Grace… All her coworkers were wonderful people. Chiz had always wanted to treat them to a meal and properly express her thanks. But someone like her…
"I should probably…"
"How about coming to my place? I'll show you my cooking. Come on, Chiz, come on."
If it was at someone's home, it probably wouldn't be too loud…
Chiz finally accepted. She stayed up all night reading posts on Bagel to learn how to be a polite houseguest. If she never got another chance, she had to make this one count.
"Welcome! You didn't have to bring anything!"
"Chiz's here? Come in, come in!"
"Um… H-Hello, everyone…"
The house was warm. There was the smell of home cooking and the chatter of coworkers. So this is what a gathering was like. How nice. Just as Chiz was secretly feeling happy, Grace handed her a box.
"F-for me?"
"Of course! Open it, quick." Haruna leaned in close to Chiz, urging her to open it.
Chiz untied the ribbon. Inside the box was a pair of noise-canceling earplugs. They were beautiful. And pink.
"Pretty, right? We all picked them out together."
"Other than being cute, they're almost completely useless. The noise-canceling is extremely average."
"But they're perfect for our Chiz, right?"
Yes, the noise-canceling was perfectly average… Just enough for Chiz to hear the sound of fireworks blooming in the sky without being so scared that she had to cover her ears and run away.
ST_File.F_NPC026_014:
Chiz keeps a diary. She hasn't stopped writing since receiving her first journal. She writes down everything worth remembering, so that when she sees her family again someday, she can tell them everything. Then, she'll finally say the words she's been preparing for so long: "Yes, I've been doing well out here."
But her diary isn't just words: there are rice ball wrapper labels, flower petals that landed on her shoulder, and stickers from coworkers. They're all proof that she's doing well. Chiz feels that only by recording things this way can she truly feel like she's not just stumbling through a pleasant dream.
At first, Chiz's diary entries were very short.
"M: XX, D: XX. Food was good."
"M: XX, D: XX. Clothes were pretty."
"M: XX, D: XX. Flowers smelled nice."
She didn't know what else to write, so she just honestly recorded how she felt. Once, a friend found out and suggested, "If you don't know what to write, why not try drawing?" But Chiz didn't think her drawings were all that good, either. She was still troubled.
One day, Chiz ate a delicious candy. She couldn't bear to throw away even the crinkled wrapper, so she put it in her diary. The candy was delicious, and her problem was solved. She's continued to this day.
"Ahhh, how is it this late already? I have work tomorrow!"
Chiz hurriedly closes her diary. Her entries have been longer and longer, lately. There's more and more worth recording. That tasty milk tea has to be written down. Getting praised by her manager has to be written down. The first sunny day of spring, the first sunny day of summer, the first sunny day of fall, and the first snowfall of winter all have to be properly recorded. Chiz doesn't like rainy days. She only likes sunny days, because on rainy days, food is hard to find.
But Chiz really likes snowy days in Hethereau. Snow is clean and white.
ST_File.F_NPC026_011:
Chiz stands, professionally dressed, in the gleaming lobby of a bank.
Chiz walks the corners where the streetlights don't reach, sewage pooling under the cracks in the pavement.
"Chiz, Chiz, where are you going?"

Once Chiz learned to run without stumbling, she had to leave home and help her older siblings find food outside. Shiny bread wrapped in plastic… Chiz only saw that once. Most of the time, all she could find were wild vegetables and mushrooms. When even those were gone, they had no choice but to hunt "Apocha." That's what they called the edible Anomalies. But Apocha were dangerous; it was common to get hurt, and medicine was even harder to find than food. And then there was that saying: "Eat too many Apocha, and you'll become an Esper." Espers, like Anomalies, were outsiders to be driven away; because, just like Anomalies, Espers attack. After dinner, Chiz watched her mother cradle her newborn baby sister; patting her, soothing her, singing to her. Chiz remembered when she was little, so little that the whole world was no bigger than her mother's embrace, her mother would gently pat her, soothe her, and sing to her.
"Chiz, Chiz, grow up quick."

Faster, faster. Chiz pressed her palm against the bleeding wound on her neck, glancing back at the Apocha that was closely tailing her. She ran as hard as she could, away from home. Farther, farther—until she couldn't run anymore. Chiz tripped on a rock and fell hard to the ground. The Apocha had vanished somewhere along the way. She didn't have the strength to stand, so she just lay there, nibbling at the food she'd found. She could only eat a little. She had to bring the rest home. Her family was waiting for her. She had to get home… Chiz couldn't remember how she found her way back. But somehow, she made it home with the food… and a new Ability. Maybe, just like the stories said, she had eaten too many Apocha. On her last night home, she used her new Esper Ability to put on a little fireworks show for her younger siblings. She remembered their eyes shining bright, their soft gasps; fighting over who got to play with their magical big sister.
The next day, her mother brought Chiz to the shore. A boat would take her away from home, carry her to a new world. Even after her mother's silhouette had completely disappeared from sight, Chiz could still hear someone calling out in the salty sea breeze.
"Chiz, Chiz, you must…"

Chiz now lives in the heart of Hethereau. Even at night, the whole New Herland District blazes with lights. Chiz often turns off all her lights indoors and leans against the window, watching the flow of cars outside. Back in her homeland, nights were deathly silent. Light didn't mean streetlamps or the moon; light meant danger. It could be an Anomaly's lure. It could be dangerous Espers and their weapons.
Chiz sits in the darkness of her room, while a glittering world sparkles outside her window. She hugs herself, imitating her mother from memory, softly humming a melody still warm with feeling.
"Chiz, Chiz, you must be happy."

ST_File.F_NPC021_014:
Long ago, Yggash Court noticed this weary old bird—or, more precisely, her unusual foresight. So, when Blackbird was unsure where to rest, Yggash Court extended an olive branch: if she was willing to help them with one task, they would provide her with a safe place to stay, ample food and water, and anything else she needed.
Almost without a second thought, she accepted their suspiciously generous offer. Blackbird had never heard of this so-called Yggash Court before, yet she didn't care. All they wanted was for her to unravel a prophecy's hidden meaning, and solving riddles was what she did best. Yggash Court hadn't lied to her, either. After signing the contract, they led Blackbird to her new home. The moment she stepped inside, Blackbird knew she would spend the next one hundred years there. As if by design, every decoration had been arranged to her liking. Even the chairs were of perfect height. Standing in the room, Blackbird felt, for the first time in her life, like she had finally returned home.
Perhaps she had wandered for too long, or perhaps she had grown too attached to the idea of a "home," but after that Blackbird rarely left. She read, wrote, stargazed, and organized her collections. Blackbird liked anything that took a very long time to finish. Time wasn't worth cherishing. That might sound harsh to others, but to Blackbird, life was the only thing she could afford to spend so freely.
Perhaps she had been too confident in her own abilities; when Blackbird realized she couldn't finish the work assigned to her so easily, she felt an unprecedented sadness. But only a few days later, she pulled herself together again—she had thought of the possible link between this prophecy and her own fate, and the idea nearly made her tremble. If she could uncover her missing memories, if she could see her destiny clearly… even if the odds were only one in a million, it was a sign of something she had never experienced before. Blackbird then decided to see this humble job through to the end.
As for how long it would take to unravel that obscure prophecy, Blackbird was unsure. Yggash Court's terms never specified a deadline. Maybe a hundred years, or two hundred—perhaps even longer. Blackbird always reminded herself, though: "No matter how long it takes, I will finish it."

Just like most people can't remember their earliest days as an infant, Lacrimosa can't recall anything from before she became "Lacrimosa."
Based on a line of text carved on the coffin where she woke up, Lacrimosa decided on her own name. Why don't other people get to decide their own? Don't adults always tell her that she should choose the kind of person she wants to become?
However, names she didn't choose like "Mosa" or "Lacrimosa Senpai" also seem to be calling her. If she had chosen a different name, would she have become a different person? …Lacrimosa can't answer such complex questions yet.
She only knows that her teammates taught her to respond seriously when her name is called. Lacrimosa has kept those words close to her heart.

Thus, her popularity among citizens rose a bit more.

There was an Esper who went by the name of Icaria on the Boulder. She was short and had a pair of wings, which saved her when the smuggler's ship sank. She usually enjoys zipping around, often joking that she never grew taller because her feet never touched the ground. Conrak called her "Shorty."
Icaria didn't have any parents. She just had an older brother, who liked to make a big deal about working hard to raise her. The brother, however, never cared about her. That's why Icaria decided to stay on the island, though she was capable of flying home herself.
Icaria died when the crew fought an anomaly known as the Kraken. Her wings were not made from feathers, but from some material that melted in high heat. During the fight, she tried to make the anomaly focus on her, but her wings melted when she flew too high and fell right into the Kraken.

After that, Conrak was frustrated about the limitations of his abilities. He tried to experiment with what kind of shapes his smoke could form. Just before a battle, a bird flew past him. He thought that if he could shape his smoke into a bird, he could take to the sky.
This idea didn't come at a good time: he couldn't apply it to the battle at hand, but it was enough to make him regretful… If only he had thought of it sooner, he could have saved Icaria.
Nonetheless, the idea wouldn't have helped even if he had it earlier. 

Chaos is still trying to create flying birds with his smoke. Even after years of practice, he is still only able to create a few small birds that could fly a few meters, unable to even carry the tiniest speck of dust.

The year-end shopping list was, as always, Jiuyuan's responsibility. But this year, when it came to what to buy, things were a little different from before. The moment Haniel and Illica, who had just recently joined, heard about the year-end shopping, they immediately insisted on adding a celebration party that wasn't part of the original plan. And so, what was once a neat and simple list turned into an outing for all five of them.
"Jiuyuan! We need flowers, balloons, spotlights… and cake!"
"And a standee!"
"…What's a standee?"
"You know, one of those poster things with your photo on it that you put by the entrance. Hathor, wanna try it?"
"That won't be necessary… Master."

"What about presents? There should at least be presents!"
"Of course, everyone gets one."
"Hehe, Jiuyuan's the best!"
"What about Jenson? Did he get us presents?"
"Today's bill is going under his name."
"Jenson's so generous!"
"Then I'm adding a few new comics!"
"And the CD I didn't get last time!"
"…Fine, get it all."

The list was checked, revised, and added to over and over again.
As the two little owlets eagerly confirmed every checkmark with Jenson, Jiuyuan stood off to the side and let out a soft sigh.
A little noisy, a little chaotic.
But in moments like these, the accounts can wait, and the plans can be pushed back a bit.
Times like this… aren't so bad.

ST_File.F_NPC003_011:
One of the Bureau of Anomaly Control's ETD-4 members, and once a criminal.
As for what crime got her thrown onto the legendary Ghroth Island… nothing too serious. It was just an innocent little gesture that put some people to sleep forever.
"Endless rebirth and reincarnation all lead back to the black hole of nothingness."
Twirling her hair around her finger, she smiled with sparkling eyes.
"I simply followed their wishes, sending those party people to the paradise they'd been craving their whole lives."

As a pardoned prisoner, she isn't treated any differently than any other Squad 4 member.
Except by that dog-faced guy with calm but wary eyes. Maybe because a few months ago they were escort officer and wanted criminal?
Well, overall, she thinks her new job is pretty good. Fighting to her heart's content, letting danger excite her mind, letting pain make her body tremble… violence comes from life's excess. How could anyone not be addicted to tasting it?
She doesn't know why that strange woman brought her back from the island, but whatever. She had nowhere else to go anyway. The place where she once knelt and prayed devoutly, entrusting her faith, has long been sealed off. Anyone who sees that ruined wasteland would laugh! Only a pair of familiar silver eyes still gaze at her, merciful, generous, full of desire… she can feel it.

"Go raise some hell, Fadia. I'm sure you'll find something interesting."
A pretender, a dog, and a brat?
Fadia narrowed her eyes.
Well then… let's find that "something interesting."
ST_File.F_NPC006_011:
Captain of ETD-4 at the Bureau of Anomaly Control. Baicang—carefree, irreverant, blunt to a fault, master of dodging work, and a walking troublemaker.
In a certain hidden internal Bagel forum in the Bureau, a heated discussion unfolds: "Who's the least captain-like captain among ETD?"
"Am I the only one who thinks Captain Baicang from Squad 4 has a twisted sense of humor???"
"You're not alone. Every night, before I fall alseep, I realize the pranks he pulled on me at work. You have no idea how much that disrupts my sleep."
"Same here. And when you confront him about it, he just gives you this smiling face… ugh, makes me want to clench my fists even tighter."
…
It's actually pretty funny.
With zero remorse for his antics, Baicang swoops in to gleefully like and save every comment.

Rumors about Squad 4's captain are mixed.
For instance, "Watch out for that long silver-white braid, for it's the Reaper's banner." "He seems to like hiding behind his team members and playing weak, but he's actually analyzing his opponents' strength and countermeasures." "He's reliable when it counts, very capable, and doesn't abuse his power." "He loves all kinds of pasta, especially Italian, but when he cooks it himself he breaks the noodles in half before putting them in the pot (absolutely tasteless)." All these rumors are basically true, confirmed with love from his closest team members.

Beyond that, things lurk in his past that they cannot see.

From an unwanted branch family child to voluntarily entering the main house for Esper Ability development, the young man gradually slipped toward what he thought was a beautiful "abyss." He learned early the weight of life: Light as a feather. Something he could blow away just by speaking. For a long time he stopped saying anything at all, perhaps to atone, perhaps simply from fear. He was like a lone young leaf that had lost its way, spinning as it fell, until finally caught by someone important… that was when he found his home.

Are words curses or prayers? He can easily extinguish life, yet cannot preserve anything. Thus, he can only keep moving forward.
From summer to winter, from spring to fall, the veins of fall leaves turn yellow, still clinging to the branches before finally falling.
In the system of the Five Colors, white is associated with Gui Cang and the season of autumn, giving rise to the name White Cang or Baicang.

The Bureau of Anomaly Control and the charity house have entirely different vibes. Still, Iroi was able to get used to the different pace, and she got along with her new teammates, Mint and Shinku.

Shinku mistakenly assumed that the external Iroi had taken over the real one, and disgusted by what she thought was happening, she held a grudge against the external Iroi.
After that, Mint worked hard to convince Shinku and Iroi to clear up the misunderstanding. Once Shinku learned the truth about the Iroi in the dream world, she realized she assumed wrongly and apologized to Iroi.

"You saw that pitiful being in a dream and threw out everything to stand up for her—what a hotheaded dragon who doesn't think things through!"
"Arrgh, why are you still so mean after I said sorry? You… Ramtenna!"
"Okie-dokie, problem solved! Let's get along with each other like this!"

That's how Mint earned a lavish meal from Shinku and Iroi.

ST_File.F_NPC021_012:
When the first tongue of flame leapt up from beneath her feet, even Merula's lips would not stop trembling.
Her naive heroism vanished without a trace in the face of the fate closing in on her. Merula fought back the urge to run, but when the sweltering pain rose through her calves, she truly understood how terrifying death could be.
It hurts… it hurts…
Her whole body erupted in a raging inferno. Merula wept and screamed. The pain was countless times worse than she had imagined, and all she could do was beg helplessly for help. Her faint voice was drowned out by the song of the surrounding crowd, that mournful singing growing louder and louder, like a tempest.
The figures in the crowd, including the Inquisitor, wavered in the shimmering heat. In her haze, Merula saw the Devil leering at her.
…I want to become… a real… Witch…
Merula pleaded in despair. If there was no escaping this fate no matter what, then if she became a Witch, could this absurd slaughter finally cease?
At least… I could save everyone…
Merula dimly remembered the Devil agreeing to her bargain, the price being half her soul in exchange. In the next instant, a spark tore free from her chest, now blackened like charcoal. The spark circled in the air, then soared further and further away. Merula forgot everything. Though the surging flames blocked her sight, she remained steadfast, staring blankly in the direction that singular spark had gone.
Live on…
Once its presence disappeared into the flock of birds and could no longer be found, boundless fear and loneliness replaced her resolve and swallowed her whole. She felt pain again. She did not want to die. She did not want to suffer. She wished to call out for that spark, to beg it to take her away. A tear fell from her empty eyes, then more followed, dripping to the ground and gathering into a river of sorrow.
The Inquisitor's laughter stopped. The burning agony subsided. A strange silence fell over everyone. Merula stood dazed at the stake and saw the frightened looks on everyone's faces, and the Inquisitor's face twisted with rage.
"Merula… Merula is a Witch…!"
It was as if she was a million miles away, the voices barely noticeable. However, it was that distant, far-off line that she would hear again and again for the next several hundred years. A pain unlike fire swept through her body and soul. With great effort, she raised her head and saw a gigantic "cage," vast as the sky, gradually taking shape. Centered on Merula, it fed on her blood and flesh and spread outward without end, as if it meant to shroud the entire world.
"The witch hunt" was then brought to a halt, just like that.
The furious Inquisitor roared, threatening Merula and ordering her to withdraw this bizarre "cage," but Merula could hear nothing anymore. Her body gradually grew smaller, from a girl into a child, and from a child into an infant. At last, she vanished, leaving not even a drop of blood behind.
Driven by the maddened Inquisitor, the deadly blaze burned within the cage for many days and nights. By the time Merula was finally able to completely control her new body, she brought down a rain of blood to extinguish the flames. The town from her memory had long since turned to ash. Across the ground where everyone had once stood lay countless black Oracle Stones. She heard the wailing of souls. She heard the Inquisitor's shrill laughter. It's all right, though. They can never escape again. Merula could only comfort her heart, overflowing with terror and remorse, using those words. No one would die because of the Devil ever again. The Devil that brought calamity would never be able to do evil again.
We have no reason to blame a girl so kind, yet so foolish. Poor Merula desperately tried to make up for the disaster she had caused. For hundreds of years, she remained vigilant, guarding against any possible sign of the Devil. She would ensure that people elsewhere would never suffer the same misfortune, that their tears of despair would no longer fall, and for the sake of that pure and naive wish—to become a true savior for all.
But where was her savior?
Outside the cage, the birds flew for one hundred years, then another hundred. All things slept in the night, and then were awakened by dawn. Only the first second of eternity had passed, and the starry sky still remained the same.

ST_File.F_NPC016_011:
After a busy day, Hathor returned to Sterry. The chatter and cheer inside was somewhat inviting. The Mentor warmly introduced two new members of Sterry: Haniel and Illica. Hathor didn't have any particular thoughts about their arrival and simply nodded in acknowledgment. Following the Mentor's arrangements was something she was used to. If Hathor were to recall her feelings from meeting with Haniel and Illica, she'd probably say: Very energetic, great couriers.

However, while interacting with them over the following few days, Hathor gradually realized that the relationships between the five of them weren't as smooth as expected. The Mentor and Jenson, who were familiar with her, could sense her true thoughts from her expressions and actions even when she said nothing, and knew she wasn't intentionally cold. The two new members didn't seem to understand, though. Perhaps due to her icy exterior, they always showed some instinctive wariness, completely different from how lively they were when facing the Mentor. Just as Hathor was repeatedly pondering how to explain to them that she simply wasn't good at socializing, a conversation with the Mentor changed everything. She was given a unique commission: spend time with Haniel and Illica, and understand the lives of modern youngsters. This was a task with a clear directive, so she didn't hesitate.

However, when actually facing the two, taking the initiative to speak proved much more difficult than expected. Hathor had mentally rehearsed scenarios for initial conversations many times and had even prepared several backup plans for dealing with awkward silences. So, during a rare chat session, she tentatively asked about their daily hobbies. The following responses completely deviated from her expectations:
"Of course it's watching the greatest manga of this century, 'Gen Z'!"
"Buying merch, going to events, analyzing the lore with fellow fans on Bagel, conventions, live events, and wotagei!"
"Seasonal anime previews, fan arts, weekly new episodes… we never miss a single one!"
Faced with Haniel's enthusiastic string of recommendations, Hathor showed visible confusion: What is wotagei? What is an "anime"?
Just as Hathor was about to interrupt and give her brain some time to process, she caught sight of Illica, who was eagerly waiting with excitement to join the conversation. She fell silent for a moment and held herself back from speaking. If they'd really like to talk about it… then listening for a while longer wouldn't hurt.

ST_File.F_NPC012_011:
Of the "Eibon Anomaly Detectives," most say he looks the most befitting of the 'detective' mantle. Edgar neither denies nor confirms this… Probably because explaining it would be really, really troublesome.
After all, his other titles include "Eibon Ace Trio," "Hyelp's Most Promising Rising Star," "Bridge Crossings' Top 3 Anomaly Hunter," and countless other impressive-sounding nicknames that Nanally, Sakiri, and Taygedo (and sometimes Kiroumaru too) casually make up.

Despite still being a baby-faced boy, he's remarkably mature for his age; almost old-fashioned, likely because the other two are so impulsive that Edgar is always the one left bowing and thanking people. More often than not, he's the one apologizing and paying the bills.
Of course, Edgar's main responsibilities are gathering intel and planning operations. As for how many times those plans have been followed… well, as long as the results are good, who cares? Edgar has come to fully embrace this philosophy; though it doesn't stop him from carefully preparing each time and having a Plan B ready for any unexpected situations that might (or rather, definitely will) occur.
Taygedo often watches the three young Hunters head out and sighs with mock profundity: "Future Edgar will be just like Adler!"

The path to becoming an Elite Courier isn't always smooth sailing.
During her 16th delivery quest, Haniel accidentally lost a package. Even though it was found three hours later and Owner Jiuyuan didn't blame her for anything, Haniel still felt really guilty. Not wanting to worry her family too much, Haniel acted normal at the dinner table, casually chatting about all sorts of topics she was interested in. Of course, brave Haniel wouldn't let negative feelings bother her for long. After a good night's sleep, she was back to her usual self… but before leaving the house, Haniel received a gift. The headset she had mentioned at dinner the night before was now sitting quietly by her bedroom door.
"Haniel will definitely become the best courier ever," read the note on the gift box.

ST_File.CA_NPC030_02: I close, I close, I close again!
ST_File.NPC009_Chitchat_003: I just saw Kiroumaru sneaking food in the kitchen.
ST_File.NPC009_weather_001: I'm not like those kids with endless energy to burn, running around every day. I'll wait for a nice, shady day before I go out again.

ST_File.NPC027_self_002:

But sometimes, I wonder if Fons are really that important… I mean, once I save up enough to move back home, maybe they won't matter so much. Still, that's an enormous amount of Fons. I'd probably have to work at Pink Paws Bank until I retire.
ST_File.NPC024_talk_003: I spent a few years in a place far from the city, where people lived by the "will of God." The will of God was always right, because people could always find a way to interpret it as right. Prophecies are much the same. If you find a good interpretation, then believe in it.
ST_File.NPC015_chat_003: I'm in special deliveries for Sterry. The content… depends on the client. Different people have different needs.
ST_File.NPC014_about_004: I really wanna try Hathor's motorcycle. Must feel amazing to ride! People say she seems cold—but that's only 'cause they don't know her. With me around, even Esper Ability blowups are no big deal! Go Haniel! No fear!
ST_File.NPC030_self_003: Do I exist? You see the character model, interfaces, text, you hear this voice clip, and you know that it's all just ones and zeros—illusions put together from numbers and signals. So I guess that for you, the moment all this stops meaning anything, I might as well have never existed! As for meaning, that has to come from "why" you exist—the question of "why (Y)." ST_File.NPC027_hobby_001:

ST_File.NPC013_gift_001: I don't think I've told you, but I… like it a lot. Thank you.
ST_File.NPC028_about_006: I really liked Sunward. Textbooks would never have taught me the things I learned there. But after I left, I didn't know why my friends there stopped contacting me. Isn't that what friends do, stay in touch? Or maybe they never really thought of me as a friend…?
ST_File.NPC1029_chat_002: I like going out at night. There aren't a lot of people on the streets, so I don't have to worry about bumping into anyone. Though if they saw me floating on the road that late, they might get spooked…
ST_File.NPC021_chat_002: I love collecting all sorts of antiques. The stranger the design, the more I like them… My collection? I have more than what you usually see. I had a whole room built to store them. If you're interested, come by and take a look sometime.
ST_File.NPC023_self_002: I'm no astronomy geek but I love looking at stars. I like quietly watching them fill up the night sky. When my mind's a mess, I look up at the open sky… and knowing all that starlight traveled unimaginable distances just to reach us, that thought calms me down every time.
ST_File.NPC012_gift_002: I like it a lot. Thanks for all the effort!
ST_File.NPC027_gift_002: I like this a lot. Thank you, Appraiser… I knew we were in sync.

ST_File.NPC021_gift_004: I love it. You really thought a lot about this.
ST_File.NPC029_weather_001: I stay indoors all the time, so I don't get any sun. On days like this, Chaos would likely go out for a jog.

ST_File.NPC008_Chitchat_001: Why do I feel like this shop is making more money than Eibon?
ST_File.NPC010_self_002: It would be difficult for me to have a truly neutral stance on Esper abilities or anomalies, as I undoubtedly have vested interests with them… Most people are puzzled when they first meet me, wondering how a blind man can perceive the world around him with such clarity. ST_File.NPC008_weather_003: I won't dress like an ugly yarn ball… Ah, achoo!
ST_File.NPC1029_self_003: There are many great eateries along Tamamochi Street where I work. ST_File.NPC006_weather_003: I proposed introducing "days off for cold weather" for my squad. Which passed unanimously… except for Skia's vote. Then, our dear Director rejected it. Ah well, if you've got any "cold weather days off" or "winter breaks" where you're from, do enjoy them on my behalf.

ST_File.F_NPC028_015:
At first, Iroi's dream world was just a hazy, chaotic mess. As she grew up and experienced more of the world, three little kids, Morpheus, Icelos, and Phantasos, started trying to fill her dream world with color and life. The three kids worked together. Morpheus created passers by, Icelos created birds and beasts, and Phantasos created scenery that weren't based on living beings. Through their collective efforts, Iroi's dream world became a tiny world that rivaled reality itself.
As for when the three kids first appeared, neither Iroi remembers clearly—did they show up when her powers awakened? The real Iroi claims to have seen them since the moment she was born.
Morpheus likes to act cool and calls himself the boss, but he's actually the one who usually gets picked on. Icelos is cute and shy, but has a bit of a mischievous streak. Phantasos is a total airhead, always flying around aimlessly while blowing a little trumpet. For young Iroi, who spent so much of her time alone in hospitals and at home, they were her best friends.

"Iroi has new friends now. Is it time for us to leave?"
"No way, I don't want to leave her!"
"She's there… we're there… must not part…"
ST_File.F_NPC027_014:
At first, Linko desperately sought friends.
The flocks of pigeons at dawn, the comets at midnight, the ducks by the river, the shells on the beach, the interesting little shop her mother found, the new game her father recommended—and all those countless frequencies from the infinite beyond reaching into her little head… Linko wished to speak about it to a true friend.
Despite this, she was always alone. Maybe because of her parents, Linko was more tolerant and curious than other kids her age. Whether it was Anomalies, insects, ghost stories, or urban legends, Linko was always full of curiosity. After her Esper Ability awakened, her ability to sense frequencies made the way she perceived the world around her unlike anyone else. Because of that, she had a very difficult time making friends. Even when she joined after-school group activities, she would just stand quietly in the corner.
"Everyone has their own channel. If I try tuning in to their frequency first… could I become friends with them?"
After her Esper Ability awakened, Linko could receive and discern other people's frequencies. If she spent some time tuning to the same frequency as someone else, she could even begin to experience that person's emotions… Were such a thing to come to pass, as long as she kept paying attention to how they felt, she should slowly but surely figure out what would make them happy. At least, that's what Linko thought.
So, the lonely girl began trying to approach other children her age. She was a little stiff and awkward, but it eventually started to work. At last, though she was merely the quietest little tagalong in the bunch, she had finally found the "friends" she had always wanted.
Anyhow, that was what she believed before the split.

ST_File.F_NPC009_015:
The Tsukinoki family's courtyard pairs perfectly with fallen snow. The snow gives it an added sense of historical elegance, like covering displayed antiques with a blanket of dust—except this dust is pure white and pristine.
Unfortunately, year after year, such scenery passes by in the blink of an eye. Hotori has always felt this way.
Even at a young age, she was already deeply melancholic about the changing seasons and passing years. This was because she feared that the ever-changing outside world would bring unwanted changes to this reclusive family. How wonderful it would be if everything could freeze like a still life at its most perfect moment.
"The best time to appreciate snow is when it's melting. For that… you need to be in motion, don't you?"
Many years later, when she truly could make snowy scenes stand still, one early spring she encountered—not by chance—an old guest who had once stayed at their family estate for a time. Now an elderly man in his twilight years, he took a sip from his wine cup after every sentence during their casual conversation.
Hotori realized this would be their final meeting. She poured the wine and waited with rare solemnity to hear his next heartfelt words.
"What's most precious isn't what remains unchanged and eternal. It's the things that break… the things that are breaking right now."

ST_File.F_NPC023_011:
A rumor has been making the rounds among the bands who've performed at StarSign: "If something goes horribly wrong before a show and you can't fix the problem yourself, try asking the person at the bar. You know—the one with the totally blank expression."
Akane Rin, a live house staff member, is nothing short of a professional. She can handle all kinds of instruments and is even happy to pass on some seriously advanced techniques. But recently, maybe too many people have been coming to her for help, because the blonde girl is finally starting to lose patience. Now, anyone who wants to ask her anything has to order a drink first—only then is her advice free. Even so, the musicians aren't backing down. Just like in an anime, the idea that "that totally unremarkable staff member is secretly a former member of a super band?!" is way too tempting to ignore—
"What is Akane like onstage?"

"Did she really give up on being in a band?" Plenty of people have wondered.
In a quiet room, Akane stares at the guitar in front of her, its string snapped, and asks herself the same thing: "Did I really give up, just like that?"
But if she doesn't give up, what else can she do? Can a one-person band really count as a band?
Akane sits in a corner of the bar, watching bands come and go onstage. Most only perform a few times before moving on. Akane barely even remembers their faces—only the songs they played. As time passed, even those melodies began to slowly fade from her memory, until they were gone for good.
Every band is like "LINES."

To Akane, "LINES" represents her past—a time with its share of regrets, but one that was beautiful all the same. "THE WHOOTS!!!!" is a culmination of her noisy, lively present. As for the future…
Who knows?
Akane only knows she'll keep playing. Forever and ever, the score that belongs to her will never end.

ST_File.F_NPC022_017:
Zankou and Daffodill were once Scarlet Letter's sharpest daggers. The sins that stained them were as dark as the hollowness in their heart.
Trial after trial, mission after mission, they enacted Mother's bidding. Zankou didn't care for her life as a blade; rather, she only desired to watch Daffodill.
As an assassin, she knew of every obstacle Mother needed removed. But as a person, she knew only Daffodill
Daffodill always stood before the mirror after finishing a mission, contemplating in silence as she bandaged her wounds. And every time, Zankou would quietly savor that weary, melancholic back—beautiful even when riddled with scars—and, as always, use her Esper Ability and a tender hug to dispel her sister's doubts.
Finally, those doubts bore fruit.
On one mission, when it was time to bring the blade down on a target, Daffodill listened to the target's pleas for mercy—and stilled her hand. Zankou witnessed her hand trembling, yet also noticed the bloodthirstiness shrouded in those cries for mercy. At that moment, a treacherous idea took root in her mind.
In the blink of an eye, the cold gleam of a hidden weapon flashed toward her sister. Zankou deliberately stepped in front of the blade, taking the blow. In this moment, Zankou also struck back against the assailant, killing them.
Blood poured from her wound—pain she would willingly endure. Breathing hard, Zankou gazed upwards. She saw Daffodill's trembling hand loosen around the knife, and heard hurried footsteps and an apology laden with fright.
"At last, you've become as weak as they are."
Zankou watched, enraptured by the violently wavering flame before her.
She had imagined it countless times: no longer restraining her Esper Ability, Zankou using her eyes to see through everything, then pulling her into an illusion meant only for the two of them. Twisting her likes and dislikes, manipulating her memories—until, before she could completely devolve into a sentimental, uninteresting commoner, she would become Zankou's plaything.
However, in those final moments, Zankou had relented.
Even softened and shaken, that white flame still fascinated her. She no longer desired to snuff it out.
ST_File.F_NPC022_013:
Zankou saw a shockingly pleasing red in the pool of blood.
The owner such red strut towards her, her high heels echoing throughout the empty dungeon's walls. Then the clacking stopped, giving way to velveteen words:
"Let me see your face, my poor little petal.
From today on, Scarlet Letter is your home."
Home… what was that?
The woman before her promised the girl something she couldn't comprehend: a "home." Though the girl couldn't understand the meaning of the woman's words, she could feel that her voice and touch were gentler than anything she had ever experienced.
"You may call me… Mother."
Zankou looked warily at the tall, thin woman before her. Beneath her gentle gaze lurked an indecipherable smile. The blaze of her soul was as vermilion and resplendent as the clothes she wore, and its greedy flames danced and flared before the girl's eyes, almost burning her alive.
Yet, she still willingly replied with one word only:
"Mother."
ST_File.F_NPC022_018:
Zankou could recall when her sister changed, and how trusting, careless, and foolish she had been before.
It was at one of Inanna's auction events. Daffodill, who was in charge of security, had acted out of turn and returned after a brief disappearance looking a bit haggard. She covered her left eye and brushed the whole incident off, referring to it as an "accident." Seeing her sister's face wounded to such an extent caused Zankou to fly into a rage, so much so that in the next few missions, her methods were far more brutal than usual. For months after, Daffodill wore an eye patch. To comfort her sister, Zankou even had one made for herself—completely useless, of course—and when she took it out to show off, her sister could only respond with a startled laugh.
Zankou never once wondered what exactly that eye patch of Daffodill's was hiding.
On one rainy night, she witnessed Inanna lying in a pool of blood, and Daffodill—the Esper who had taken off her eye patch and was holding a blade. Mother's blood had stained her sister's collar a glaring crimson. And that flame… that pure white flame was entirely extinguished. It had become something utterly unlike anything before, unlike anyone else—a color of sublime purity Zankou had never perceived in her life.
Zankou attempted to make sense of the chaos before her. Too many questions crashed together in her mind. She didn't understand why her sister had betrayed them, didn't understand where her sister's Esper Ability had come from, and didn't understand what that odd flame even meant. As for Daffodill… she merely stood there, unmoving, like a child frozen in fear, strangled by shame.
Her sister fled in silence, that streak of light vanishing beyond the hedges of the Scarlet Letter Garden.
Zankou struggled to call out for her, their mother still lying off to the wayside, forgotten in a pool of blood. All Zankou's thoughts—and her gaze—incessantly followed her sister's departing figure. An unknown amount of time had passed before she finally uttered a few words, those same words she had said to her sister countless times before:
"What a beautiful color…"
ST_File.F_NPC022_011:
Zankou rarely speaks of the days that came before she joined The Scarlet Letter. To her, such dark times were not worth remembering.
It all began with a careless, secret experiment. A solitary, unknown girl was treated as a vessel for cultivating Esper Ability, and the researchers, along with those greedy, gluttonous elites, considered her a worthless sacrifice on the path to greatness. Unbelievable pain, solitude, mutilation, rebirth… these grotesque, repulsive torments were daily occurrences. Time and again, she would inch towards the edge of death, only to be dragged back to the world of the living.
Until, in a bitter irony, a miracle truly came to pass: her Esper Ability burst forth, turning that sinful dungeon into an ocean of blood. No one survived but her.
A noble, pure-hearted philanthropist was the first to discover her amidst the ruins. She brought that girl back to the gardens, as if transporting a feral wildflower. To her delight, that wildflower, born in the filth and muck, was already tempered completely—exactly to her liking.
Thus, the flower known as "Red Nightshade" took root in the soil of Scarlet Letter, and Inanna gained her loyal adopted daughter—her sharpest dagger.
Yet, Inanna was unaware that the "leash" on her daughter frayed at the edges. Zankou kept quiet about her own Esper Ability, and only opened that uncanny eye of hers from the shadows, hoping to peer into her new family's hearts. Those who tried to bully her, curry favor, or befriend, were merely ignored—and instead swept into a sinking mire, where reality and illusion blurred. They began to doubt what was real or false, slowly transforming into soulless husks—playthings to be puppeteered by Zankou.
"Everyone has a flame burning in their heart."
To Zankou, people's faces were merely monochrome, but the bright red flames of their souls never ceased to burn.
Each person's fire was different—some fierce, some dim, some dark, some crimson… In her eyes, most were utterly mundane; the few that were worth a second glance could only serve as brief playthings. It was only when she watched those flames burn themselves out on the brink of collapse, exhaling flake after flake of hopeless ash, that she showed a hint of delight, as if at last admiring a masterpiece.
But in this cold, monotonous world, dotted with countless dreary flickers, there was always one different soul… At first, it was a blinding white; later, it became a hue she had yet to see anywhere else—an indescribable color.
"How beautiful… I'm unable to look away."
ST_File.NPC022_talk_001: When Mother was in a bad mood, she loved to use "training" as an excuse to punish us physically. After she punished us, she'd start crying those fake tears while saying things like "Mother forgives you." That was her way of raising us. But for the four of us… Daffodill was made of iron. The whip could come down on her and she wouldn't even blink. I could see straight through Mother's intentions, so of course I wasn't affected. As for Poinsette… her fake tears were more convincing than Inanna's. Watching the two of them put on their mother-and-daughter act was one of my favorite ways to pass the time.
ST_File.F_NPC022_019:
Mother survived Daffodill's attempt on her life. She woke, recovered from her injuries, and maintained her usual image as if nothing had occurred. Zankou was unsurprised. Daffodill had mastered the art of assassination, but someone like Mother was not to be trifled with. She still performed her role as that poised, luxurious philanthropist—as if entirely unphased by Daffodill's betrayal.
Zankou could see the subtle change, however.
In the past, Mother's emotions had always been stable and cold, even going so far as to be utterly arrogant. Following the assassination attempt, though, she became distrustful, constantly carrying the unease often found in those in positions of power…
The scarlet tower in her memory had already collapsed, but Zankou no longer cared about such frivolous things.
Right now, her only desire was to drag that woman who had slipped through her fingers back by the neck…
Mother brought another "Little Sister" back home, eventually. She had begun to favor the children whose vulnerability made her feel powerful in turn—and the girl named Poinsette was one of them. At first, Zankou only considered her another flower among the field. Unexpectedly, though, she discovered an interesting side to the newly introduced bud. Precocious and gifted, that little bud wouldn't let Mother's favoritism or torment transform her into a wilting flower. Instead, she became a resilient weed, seeking any way of escape from Scarlet Letter's garden. Seeing through her act, Zankou became even more curious and took the initiative to entice Mother into promoting Poinsette, so that she would serve at Inanna's side from then on. That little bud, now a weed, noticed Zankou's intentions, and could only obediently play along…
Though the song and dance between the two amused Zankou for a while, it couldn't fill the void left by Daffodill's absence. Zankou never encountered anyone whose soul could compare to hers, and thus her longing grew day by day…
At last, after a long and thorough investigation, she caught wind of Daffodil's trail—a rundown antique shop in Hethereau, a shanty utterly unfit for her.
Fortunately, Inanna's next target was also in Hethereau, so Zankou gladly undertook the mission and went to investigate. Daily, she disguised herself as various passersby, passing by Eibon's door countless times, until she had finally come upon the face she had waited so long to see.
Suppressing a smile, she slipped into a dark alley, pressed a hand to her chest, and felt her heartbeat pounding wildly like a drum.
"This time, you'll never escape from me again, Sister."

ST_File.F_NPC016_016:
One day after finishing her delivery quests, Hathor was riding her motorcycle as usual, speeding away down the road. Perhaps because she'd been watching too much anime lately, the massive billboard advertisement for "Gen Z" unusually caught Hathor's attention. The limited venue merchandise shown in the promotional image was a term Hathor had been hearing frequently recently, and it looked familiar. The items could only be purchased through limited offline channels, like exclusive conventions, shops, or cafes. As it happened, there was a shop nearby that Haniel had been talking about for ages, and somehow, Hathor felt like trying her luck.
The phrase "trying her luck" shouldn't appear in the vocabulary of someone accustomed to precision operations. Since getting into anime culture, Hathor had gradually begun accepting things in life that carried "randomness": the randomness of gacha pulls, daily fragmented discussions about new anime with her two fellow fans, the randomness of new terms popping up unexpectedly, the "pseudo-randomness" of whether limited venue merchandise could be obtained, and so on…
Today also brought a random event: the spontaneous decision to detour to a limited merchandise shop after finishing deliveries. Next she would "try her luck" on limited goods, and then give an unexpected gift to the two little owls… Hathor habitually kept herself wound tight, perhaps due to muscle memory from early high-intensity deliveries, or the professional discipline of strictly following plans, plus the careful caution she'd always maintained toward her Esper after losing control.
But since she'd begun learning about "modern youngster life" from those two, something called "randomness" had started taking root in her body. Like noticing the billboard advertisement today, like suddenly detouring to a merchandise shop, like putting a gift that wasn't on her quest list into her pouch. She had never so clearly realized that she had been wound too tight for too long, so long that she'd forgotten she actually lived in a city full of human warmth and life.

ST_File.F_NPC1029_012:
Aurelia was born into a stable, happy family. Her parents loved each other very much, and the household was often peaceful. She was the little sweetheart her parents had prayed and prayed for. Their gentle, lovely little plum blossom. The only flaw in this picture-perfect family was… her parents' work schedule. As she grew older, both of her parents advanced their careers. The time they could spend with Aurelia grew less and less. Aurelia understood that her parents were working incredibly hard to give her a better life, so she knew not to throw tantrums or act overly spoiled.
But, now and again, when she saw kids her age walking down the street hand in hand with their parents, Aurelia couldn't help but stare. She knew the thing weighing her down was a "First World Problem"—she never had to worry about her next meal or a new pair of shoes. She got any toy she wanted right away, and even if she was picky about her food or stayed up too late, she never got punished. Wasn't that enough? Compared to her classmates whose parents were strict or distant, she already had so much. She shouldn't be greedy for more.
So, she'd only stare for a moment before looking away quickly and obediently heading toward her empty home. At an age when she didn't fully understand the meaning of "lonely," Aurelia had already seemed to experience "loneliness." 

She got used to not expecting her parents to be around. However, on her birthday, she couldn't help but hope it might be different. Colorful presents, a huge teddy bear, and a triple-tier birthday cake kept her company while she waited. She continued waiting as the sun went down, the sky turning from blue to pink to violet. Soon enough, the moon climbed high into the sky, and the hands of the clock continued to tick inch by inch.
Eventually, Aurelia gave up. She lit the candle that was nearly sinking into the buttercream, sang "Happy Birthday" to herself, and then gently blew it out. For an instant, the room flared with a brilliant, bright glow before slipping back into darkness.
It seems that, even if you make a wish, nothing guarantees it coming true.
"Just once would be enough," She thought. I wish Mom and Dad could come home.
ST_File.F_NPC1029_014:
Aurelia's Esper ability awakened when she was fourteen. She couldn't remember exactly what was going on at the time, except that one time, when she was writing in class, her pen ran out of ink. Just as she gave her pen a shake, an entire school of jellyfish suddenly appeared. Both the teachers and students lost their trains of thought completely upon seeing this, their eyes wide and jaws to the floor. 
In the middle of the crowd, Aurelia was the most confused of all. "I just… did this?"
She tried shaking her hand again. The jellyfish mimicked her hand movements perfectly. Her classmates shouted in excitement, "Aurelia! Are you, like… did you just become…"
"You're an Esper!"

After many tests, it was officially confirmed that Aurelia was indeed an Esper now. But, aside from registering her status at the Bureau of Anomaly Control, her life didn't seem to change at all—until she realized the price she had to pay for it.
Losing her sense of direction turned Aurelia into a stranger in her own hometown. Though she walked the same route to and from school every day, she would forget where she was at any point again and again. The shops along the road all looked familiar, but when it came time to cross the street or turn a corner, her mind drew a complete blank. From then on, no matter where she had to go, Aurelia had to look up the route in advance and memorize every detail. 
Initially, everyone at her school thought Espers were super powerful and cool. They looked at Aurelia with envy and awe. But it turned out that Aurelia's Esper ability was pretty underwhelming. What situation would ever occur where someone needed to summon and control jellyfish? It was entirely useless. It didn't take long for their excitement about her being an Esper to die down, and instead, focus on her daily navigation disasters. Even though the classmates who knew about her condition did their best to look out for her on campus, the moment a shop changed its sign or some road got closed down for construction, Aurelia would end up scrambling around, asking anyone and everyone for directions. In the end, Akane and Suzuha got into the habit of going out of their way to pick Aurelia up and drop her off every day, terrified of her wandering around in the streets in the middle of the night. 
"I don't want to keep bothering you with stuff like this…" Aurelia muttered, her head hanging low. Suzuha held Aurelia's hand, giving it a little tug, signaling that they needed to turn left at the intersection. Walking alongside them, Akane let out a sigh. She lifted her hand and flicked Aurelia on the forehead. Aurelia shrank back, exclaiming, "Ow! That hurt, you know!"
"You became an Esper, that's all. You haven't changed as a person. You've always been a hassle, even since you were little!"
Suzuha burst out laughing next to them. Aurelia puffed out her cheeks in protest, "Akane! You're so mean…"
"Am I wrong? H-Hey! Stay back!"

Warmed by her friends' laughter, Aurelia let the topic go. However, though she stayed sunny and optimistic on the surface, a tiny bit of unease had gripped her heart.
Am I truly the same as before? Can things really stay the same between us?
ST_File.F_NPC1029_011:
Aurelia's life has been anything but boring: she sang in a choir, started a band, worked as an Anomaly Hunter, and now she's a diligent salarywoman. With a resume that impressive, some might consider her life a bit too "maxed out" for someone her age—at least, that's what the regulars on Tamamochi Street often gossip to each other. 

Of course, her colorful background never prevented her from diving headfirst into whatever job she takes on. These days, as the street manager of Tamamochi Street, Aurelia can easily name every resident and recall their likes and dislikes—no matter how old or young. She's always the first to offer a helping hand to solve whatever daily problems the residents run into. Her dedication to her job often makes people wonder: just how much does the City Hall pay her? 

After work, Aurelia will sometimes be spotted wandering the streets alone. If you were to walk up and talk to her, nine times out of ten you'll find she's completely lost (and she'll be very grateful to any good samaritan that'd point her in the right direction)… Sometimes, though, Aurelia will pretend to know where she's going, though no one truly believes her. In the end, everyone on Tamamochi Street is Aurelia's friend. However, it seems that there isn't anyone who genuinely understands her.

As for the places she wishes to go but, for some reason or another, can't, and the words she wants to say but swallows them down every time… maybe only someone who stays by her side for a long, long time will ever be allowed to know. Then again, everyone keeps a few secrets locked away in their heart, right? Today, Aurelia is once again smiling, her head held high as she rides her beloved jellyfish down the street, cheerfully greeting everyone she meets. This is the life she chose, no matter what.
ST_File.F_NPC1029_015:
Aurelia's chances of recovering the use of her legs were slim, but the doctor gently suggested that it wasn't entirely impossible. If more advanced medical technology emerged in the future, or if she encountered an Esper with profound healing powers…. Regardless, the possibility wasn't zero. 
During the breaks in her rehab, she often opened Bagel and stared at the little group chat with her, Akane, and Suzuha. Neither of them had sent a message to the other in a long, long time. Many times, Aurelia had typed out a message, only to delete it. What was she supposed to say to them?
After countless bouts of agonizing over her phone, Aurelia made up her mind: once she recovered a bit more, to the point where she could be discharged from the hospital and take care of herself, she would go see her friends in person and surprise them. She had endless amounts of things she wanted to tell them about. 

However, even after some time had passed, there was still no improvement in her legs. She had learned to stop treating "recovery" as her only hope. Still, with the help of her Esper Ability, her life gradually returned to some semblance of normalcy. Though she couldn't play the drums like before, Aurelia thought nothing of it. With just a bit more effort, the day of her reunion with Akane and Suzuha wouldn't be far off.
Suddenly, her phone buzzed with a special tone—the one she had set for Akane's messages specifically. Aurelia rushed to grab her phone, nearly fumbling it out of her hands in the process. But, the words that met her eyes once she opened the chat window were ones she never could have imagined: "Suzuha is leaving. By the time she messaged me, her car had already driven off…"
…Huh? 
For a moment, Aurelia couldn't comprehend the meaning of those words, as if they were nothing more than a string of meaningless symbols. What did Akane mean by "leaving"? Why would she say that? Her fingers trembled so much she could barely type out a reply, and a flood of questions sat heavy on the tip of her tongue. 
"Where's Suzuha going?"
She was going somewhere without them. Suzuha wouldn't be staying with them anymore. Aurelia… understood. Suzuha was a sensitive and thoughtful girl. If she kept living in Hethereau, a city filled with memories of their friendship, she would only tear open closed wounds. Aurelia knew this, so there was no need to ask. 
"What about LINES?"
She, deep down, knew the answer to that, too. Even if Suzuha stayed, without Aurelia as their drummer, the band would only have two paths going forward: going on a hiatus or disbanding. Of course, she could recommend something like "find a new drummer," but she couldn't bring herself to say that. "LINES" was born from Aurelia's selfish wish, and it existed for the three of them. If one of them left, what meaning was there in the empty shell left behind? 
"What about you?"

Even through her shaking fingers, she typed out those three words. 
In the chat window, the "someone is typing…" bubble flickered for a long, long time. Akane, who always spoke her mind, must have been desperately searching for words to say, just like Aurelia had done prior. Akane, so straightforward and outspoken, had been pushed beyond her limits.
If it weren't for the fact that Aurelia feared being looked down upon or abandoned, if it weren't for her lack of courage… If it weren't for her…
It felt as though thousands of years had passed before a new message had finally appeared on the screen: "I don't know. I'm sorry."
Aurelia felt herself begin to tremble. The words before her dissolved like paint in water. 
Why? 
Don't disband. 
Weren't we supposed to be together forever? 
Akane loves singing so much—she should always be on stage. 
There was so much Aurelia wanted to say, but she no longer felt she had the right to say it. The one who brought "LINES" to an end, the one who forced Suzuha to leave her hometown, the one who made it so Akane could never sing again… it wasn't fate. It was herself. 
And yet, even so, there was still one thing she wanted to convey. Even if the damage had already been done, even if it was far too late… 

"I love your music, Akane. Please, even if you feel like stopping now, continue it in the future."
"I promise you, I'll definitely be waiting for you wherever you go."

ST_File.F_NPC027_013:
Linko's Esper Abilities awakened at the young age of seven.
It was an utterly ordinary evening. Linko's mother had taken her along on a stroll through the supermarket, picking up holiday snacks and decorations while they were out. Linko followed her mother, yet her gaze drifted to a peculiar shop down the street. When she snapped back into reality, her mother had vanished entirely. The crowd was gone too, along with the surrounding noise, leaving her alone in an empty mall. At the time, she was too young to understand what an Anomalous Realm was. Initially, Linko had only wanted to escape that strange maze so that she could find her mother. The space itself was seemingly infinite, however. Linko called out in a faint little voice and cried, with no idea where to go. Hours later, exhausted, she fell to the floor, with almost nothing left but a plea on her lips…
"If only I could find Mom and Dad."
As if answering that wish, all at once, countless loud "voices" surged in from beyond, flooding the empty mall, then spiraling inward like a vortex and forcing their way into her mind: confused, wary, uncertain, worried, lonely, sirens, barking dogs, singing, ragged breathing… and her mother.
Driven by instinct, her young, exhausted body pushed itself back to its feet. Among the countless invisible threads of sounds, she followed the warmest, most familiar one and continued walking.
Farther. Just a little farther.
The "voices" grew louder and louder, and more and more noises poured into her mind. She could no longer think straight. She could only continue to walk—
Linko could barely remember how she escaped. She only knew that when she opened her eyes again, her tearful parents were holding her tight, and the unfamiliar people in uniforms nearby sighed in relief.
Linko later learned that after she was drawn into an Anomalous Realm, the Bureau dispatched the Containment Units to intervene and rescue her. What she didn't know was that as soon as search personnel confirmed the exit, everyone present suddenly felt as if they were hearing an imaginary, chaotic uproar. Electronic communications briefly went down, and some people even claimed they were seeing double, or that they heard the same voice from multiple directions at once. The incident itself severely disrupted the rescue operation. The Bureau had even suspected that an Esper was the cause, and had already prepared to send in ETD for investigation. But then, all of a sudden, Linko stepped out of the Anomalous Realm on her own. The instant she heard her mother calling out to her, she froze, and the noise disturbing everyone else stopped immediately. The Bureau members on site glanced at one another.
"The trapped citizen is safe and rescued. Victim is a suspected Esper. As for the target Anomaly… Nullification confirmed."

Standing on the bustling street corner, Edgar had no idea where he was supposed to go. Though he thought for a long, long time, he remained just as lost, just as confused.
He gave up on route planning, maps, and navigation. Following his mother's advice, he was now "letting the wind guide him" through Hethereau. According to her, encounters with destiny often arrive when you least expect them.
With no destination and no clue which direction to take, could he really find his "destiny" this way? Edgar couldn't fathom such an unplanned approach; the indecision paralyzed him. Instead, he bought a small bag of feed from a street vendor and crouched by the fountain to feed the pigeons.

Later, when Edgar looked back on that day, he felt he'd begun to dimly understand what his mother meant by "fate."
As he felt the pigeons pecking at his palm, watching the sky gradually turn a warm orange as golden clouds drifted toward the still-blue horizon, a sudden gust of wind smacked him right in the face. Along with it came a recruitment poster with crooked handwriting and a drawing of some TV-headed creature.

"Eibon Antique Shop."
He stood up, looked around, and followed the street signs to Hankaku Street.

ST_File.F_NPC022_014:
The Scarlet Letter Garden nurtured many flowers. The loving Inanna tended to them, raining down sweet dew and pruning their branches. The flowers that pleased her most were even granted new names—"Red Nightshade" was one of the many.
Yet, Zankou knew that Mother did not love her flowers; she simply enjoyed standing at the center of the garden and admiring her hard work.
Within the Scarlet Letter's estate walls, Inanna no longer needed to hide her true nature. The generous, sentimental philanthropist was merely a public performance. In the confines of her heart, there was only a businesswoman's austere coldness and greed, along with the arrogance that developed unceasingly once she had entered "high society". Like a towering crimson spire, she cast a chilling shadow, looming endlessly over her Garden.
She always mixed rewards with punishment when dealing with her daughters. Zankou was subjected to the harshest training. Zankou didn't care; her time in the dungeon had long since numbed her to pain. Even after enduring such torment at the hands of Mother, Zankou still dedicated complete loyalty to her, and carried out every task she was given. As she watched her other sisters have their emotions and fates toyed with, however, Zankou found that she, too, could find a little amusement in the Garden.
The Eye of Delusion could perceive emotions—and taste them, too. The rotten sweetness of fear, the bitterness of despair, and the sharp bite of hatred… her fellow flowers' feelings became nourishment for Zankou… And Zankou came to fully understand Mother's hobby.
Her aberrant eye was always on the prowl for vivid colors, as if admiring a field for its beautiful blooms, only to pluck the finest flowers. Whenever a lovely sobbing rang out through the estate at night, and the tiny glows of the soul twinkled, Zankou would gladly bring comfort to that fragile bud, then later control it, toy with it, to then ultimately cast it aside. Under her words and gaze, those unsettled little buds bloomed.
Such pleasure never lasted long. The girls' minds were rapidly frayed from gazing into the Eye of Delusion, becoming husks at Zankou's mercy, and the color of their souls faded, withering and unwatered.
It never mattered, though. The Scarlet Letter's Garden was vast; even if one blossom withered, there would always be another waiting to sprout.

ST_File.F_NPC032_011:
There's a distance in Shinku's politeness. As a new CSU member transferred to the BAC's HQ at Hethereau, Shinku didn't exactly make a great first impression on colleagues. Shinku maintained a deliberate distance and kept people at their "right places"—with the exception of that star employee who is known for lacking common sense.
It's not just at work, Shinku practices the same thing in her daily life too. She'll show up in the crowd rushing towards DSD to grab the latest Mystery Box or sit in the packed stands at the finals of the anomaly trading card championship, chatting with fellow fans about her collection. But once the crowds clear out, it's always Shinku going home by herself. Living in a bustling city, she's never refused to contact anyone, but she's also never let anyone into her "territory" either.
Shinku's definitely sparked some criticism and caused misunderstandings, but she firmly believes she's making the right calls. Ever since that heavy rain, she's grown used to being on her own.

There was a time when Shinku believed she wasn't different from kids her age, until that heavy rain made her understand what the power she'd been born with actually implied. Since then, her life has been completely different.
When Shinku first left Hethereau to train under her mentor at CSU-9, she wondered what would've happened if the incident had never ever occurred. But soon, she set that unanswerable question aside and found what she thought was the best way to keep the same tragedy from happening again—she just kept everyone at a distance.
And so, the determined dragonling began to grow.
She started bearing every burden on her own. With the help of her senior colleagues, she grew capable enough to handle things solo and even protect others. Her lone-wolf style meant that even if she lost control, the impact could be kept to a minimum. Everything seemed to be falling into place, until the day her mentor handed her the transfer papers, and the chance to see whether she'd truly moved past that rainy night finally arrived.

The past is the sharpest hunter, striking its killing blow the moment its prey lets its guard down.
But apparently, a maturing dragon isn't that kind of prey.

- Point Two: Edgar's mind is reasonably sharp

Therefore, Edgar is well-suited to work at Yggash Court's archives like his parents, organizing documents and studying Anomaly-related topics until the day he dies.

Edgar's mother had to work very hard to suppress her laughter at her son's reasoning; not because the conclusion was absurd or ridiculous—quite the opposite, actually. The logic was clear and the reasoning sound, leaving almost no room for refusal.
But having Edgar move into Yggash Court's tree hollow, put on thick beer-bottle glasses, and bury himself in stacks of files was still a bit… premature. ST_File.F_NPC021_011:
At first, the bird flew through the sky, not knowing where it had been born or where it was headed.
Whenever Blackbird tried to reflect on her past, her memory always came to an abrupt halt at a certain point, as though she had only been born to assume the form of a bird. Yet she could still sense her past that lay before that specific memory: a hidden history, forever burning in her mind.
Her mission had her retrace her steps, all the way back to the beginning.
Blackbird questioned the birds, but they merely chirped back; she questioned people, but they glanced at one another, unable to make sense of her words; she questioned the starry sky, yet the stars remained silent. So she wandered the world aimlessly for four hundred years, flying to the farthest reaches of the horizon and walking every inch of the earth—yet she still failed to find even the slightest clue about her past. In the end, she decided to stop the journey that had long since exhausted her.
"I'm tired. I want to rest," Blackbird thought.
So she accepted Yggash Court's invitation and entered into a contract: Blackbird would use her divination abilities to decipher an ancient, profound prophecy for Yggash Court, and in return, Yggash Court would provide everything she needed.
And so Blackbird moved into what is now known as The Witch's House. After wandering for so long, she finally had a place she could call home. Perhaps that old way of life had drained her too deeply, since for the next one hundred years, she shut herself away in a small, enclosed space and seldom stepped outside again.
Just when she thought her days would go on like that forever, something shattered the status quo. On an otherwise ordinary day, she reached for an Oracle Stone to purify it, as per usual. The moment her fingers touched it, however, a pain unlike any other overwhelmed her. Yet Blackbird did not give up. Even when the pain made her faint countless times, she kept trying again and again, striving to purify the soul attached to it—not only out of compassion, but also out of a stubborn need to prove her own existence. By the time the pain almost reached its zenith, Yggash Court sent many doctors to examine her, yet none could determine the cause of her illness. From then on, she was left with a lingering condition that she would have to endure forevermore.
Even now, whenever Blackbird touches an Oracle Stone, she still feels that searing pain. But unlike before, she has fully accepted it, and perceives it as some revelation. Yggash Court no longer needs to worry over it, either—Lavinia, the specialist ostensibly assigned to help with Blackbird's daily needs, is watching over her and reporting her movements back to them. Blackbird has never voiced any objection to this. Until the work is finished, Yggash Court naturally does not want her falling ill again or leaving, and Blackbird understands completely.
Now, Blackbird's life has settled back into peace. With the help of Yggash Court and Lavinia, she has come into contact with many new things she had never seen or heard of before. She tried starting an online divination business, and her work only grew busier from there. It was around that time that the title "Witch" began to spread on Bagel. More and more customers came to her for divinations, and she was happy to use her crystal ball to help people sort out their worries. Seeing her customers smile and hearing their thanks, Blackbird felt a deep sense of fulfillment from the bottom of her heart.
Later, a bird came to rest on a branch. The shadows over its fate were scattered by starlight, and it rested there in a calm stillness, waiting for its next journey.

ST_File.F_NPC005_011:
Skia's name had once been praised by his old colleagues as having "quite the martial artist's spirit." Skia didn't care much for the supposed depth of his name. But he found quiet satisfaction in the act of writing it—each letter placed with purpose, each curve and line falling into place. It was neat, orderly, and well arranged. Just the way he liked.
However, whenever he signed his name with too much force, that scene would always reappear in his mind… That day when he signed his employment contract at his ex-company.
For that job, he completely embraced all the workplace etiquette his colleagues believed in as "standard practice," never questioning any of it. This included things like specialized signature training to leave clients with an elite impression.
It made perfect sense, really—if all it took to preserve one's dignity was to follow a visible, rigid set of rules, then the cost was laughably low for the rewards.

As for his current signature… the overall form remained rigorous, but a closer look revealed slightly hurried connecting strokes.
Had he stopped caring about these surface details? Had taking too much time off made him sloppy? Or perhaps it was the pressure from too many emergency missions piling up with all the cleanup…

Things weren't done the way he wanted. He felt he was the only one willing to maintain the system. Well… there was nothing he could do about that.
Despite that, he gradually got used to working at the BAC. And… how should he put it? He didn't mind the sincere jokes of his teammates.

On the other hand, there was a new cafeteria lady at the Bureau who was particularly enthusiastic about Skia.
When serving him food, though Skia hadn't said anything, she would ladle several extra bone-in ribs, then casually speak to another female staff member about how her son also likes chewing on those ribs.
The other woman lowered her voice, sounding embarrassed. "He… he's not an Oddity! He's the lieutenant from ETD-4!"
Skia quietly stared at the perfectly balanced, almost strict meal composition, topped with those extra bone-in ribs… then picked up his tray and walked away. In the end, he never asked about the "breed" of the lady's son.
