ST_GameplayDec.DiyBoss_Dec:
<title>Hunter's Crucible Rules</>
1. In Hunter's Crucible, you can choose how difficult the enemies are. Higher difficulty awards a higher score.
2. You can also add modifiers to make enemies stronger and earn extra score.
3. Each stage's rewards are unlocked based on your highest score for that stage.
ST_GameplayDec.GingerbreadDuel_Desc:
<title>Snap! Golden Crackshot</>
Snap! Golden Crackshot is a <red>1v1 shooting duel</>. Players take turns as the <red>Shooter</> and <red>Dodger</>, battling with precise aim, evasive movement, and cover. Participating in matches rewards <red>Caramel Tumbleweed</>, which can be exchanged for event rewards.

<title>Matchmaking Rules</>
1. The system prioritizes matching you with opponents of a <red>similar rank</> based on Rank Points.
2. You can cancel matchmaking while waiting. Once a match is found, it <red>cannot be canceled</>.
3. Before the match begins, the system will <red>randomly select one Pukaboo</> for each player to use as their character.
4. After entering the match, the maximum wait time for the opponent is <red>30s</>. If the opponent fails to enter before time expires, you win.

<title>Shooting Rules</>
1. At the start of the match, the Dodger can adjust their hiding position. During the preparation period, fog blocks the Shooter's vision, and the Shooter <red>cannot fire</>.
2. During the shooting phase, the Shooter enters <red>Aiming Mode</>. Each shooting round lasts <red>60s</>, and the Shooter can fire up to <red>3 times</>.
3. Hits to different body parts deal different amounts of damage: <red>Torso: 10</>, <red>Limbs: 20</>, <red>Weak Point: 30</>.
4. If the Shooter <red>hits the opponent</>, <red>runs out of bullets</>, or the <red>countdown ends</>, the players immediately <red>swap roles</> if the match has not ended.
5. Each Pukaboo's <red>weak point locations</> can be viewed by selecting View Profile on the matchmaking screen. Choose where to aim carefully, and protect your own weak points.

<title>Dodging Rules</>
1. The Dodger can only <red>move left and right</> within the designated area and cannot move forward or backward.
2. Use <red>Switch Actions</> to change your posture and use cover to hide exposed body parts.
3. The Dodger can see the opponent's <red>red aiming laser</>, allowing them to determine the opponent's aim direction and dodge in time.

<title>Cover Rules</>
1. Shooting can destroy cover in the arena, revealing the area behind it.
2. Destroyed cover will <red>remain destroyed until the match ends</> and will not be restored when the Shooter and Dodger switch roles.

<title>Match Results</>
1. Reduce the opponent's HP to <red>0</> to win. The match ends immediately.
2. Each match lasts up to <red>10 rounds</>. Once the round limit is reached, the match ends and results are calculated.
3. At the end of Round 10, the player with <red>more remaining HP</> wins. If both players have <red>the same remaining HP</>, the <red>second player</> wins and the <red>first player</> loses.
4. The first player and second player are determined by each player's role at the start of the match: the player who starts as the Shooter is the <red>first player</>, while the player who starts as the Dodger is the <red>second player</>. This does not change when the roles switch.
5. Victories grant <red>Rank Points</>, while defeats deduct Rank Points. The points gained or lost after each match are dynamically adjusted based on your current rank and the difference in Rank Points between you and your opponent.

<title>Caramel Tumbleweed</>
1. After the match, you will receive the event currency Caramel Tumbleweed regardless of the outcome.
2. The more <red>HP</> you <red>deplete</> from your opponent, the more rewards you earn. Defeating your opponent grants even greater rewards.
3. During the event, Caramel Tumbleweeds have a cumulative acquisition limit. The limit starts at 600 on the first day and <red>increases by 300</> each day.
4. Spend Caramel Tumbleweeds at the Caramel Trading Post to redeem rewards.
ST_GameplayDec.PropHunt:
<title>Shadow-n-Seek Rules</>
Shadow-n-Seek is a new multiplayer asymmetric party mode. In each match, players are randomly assigned to either the <orange>Hider</> side or the <orange>Hunter</> side, then thrown into a lively game of pursuit, disguise, and deception within a limited stage. One of the three maps will be selected randomly for each match: the School, Photo Studio, or Hospital.

<title>1. Team Assignment</>
When the match begins, all players are split into two sides: <orange>Hiders</> and <orange>Hunters</>. Hiders must use objects in the stage to <orange>disguise themselves</> and avoid the Hunters' search. Hunters must find and <orange>capture all Hiders</> within the time limit.

<title>2. Hider Rules</>
At the start of the match, Hiders have a short <orange>preparation period</> to freely explore the stage and choose an object to disguise themselves as. Once transformed, their appearance will match ordinary objects in the stage, making them difficult for Hunters to identify at a glance. <orange>Hiders also move much faster during the preparation period.</>
Hiders <orange>cannot attack</> during the match. They can only move and reposition themselves to avoid being captured.

<title>3. Hunter Rules</>
Hunters have <orange>2 minutes and 20 seconds, including Berserk Mode</>, to find and capture every Hider. Hunters can use <orange>Scan</> to detect whether any Hiders are nearby. Scan has a cooldown.
Shoot a Hider to <orange>capture</> them and eliminate them from the match.
Hunters have a maximum of 40 HP. Missing a shot costs 1 HP.
The final 20 seconds are <orange>Berserk Mode</>. During Berserk Mode, Hunters <orange>no longer lose HP</> when they miss a shot.

<title>4. Win Conditions</>
Match results are determined in one of the following 2 ways:
<orange>Hiders Win</>: If at least <orange>1 Hider remains alive</> when the timer ends, the entire Hider side wins. They also win immediately if the Hunter runs out of HP.
<orange>Hunters Win</>: The Hunters win by <orange>capturing every Hider</> within 2 minutes and 20 seconds, including Berserk Mode.

<title>5. Scoring Rules</>
At the end of each match, players earn points based on their side's result and their personal performance:
<orange>Team Victory</>: All surviving/participating players on the winning side receive <orange>Team Points</>.
<orange>Personal Score</>: Hiders earn Survival Points based on <orange>survival time</>. Hunters earn Capture Points based on the <orange>number of Hiders captured</>.
<orange>Total Score</>: Total Score = Survival/Capture Points + Team Points.

<title>6. Results and Rewards</>
When the match ends, players are ranked by their total score and the results screen is displayed. <orange>City Stamina</> is then consumed based on your score, and you receive a corresponding amount of <orange>Fons</>.
You can still play <orange>without City Stamina</>, but you won't earn any <orange>Fons</>.
ST_GameplayDec.GameplayDesc_PrisonFight_Content:
<title>Fight Club Rules</>
Fight Club is a no-holds-barred brawl hosted by the new Tornado. Anyone can enter, everyone fights fair, and respect is earned with your fists.

<title>Rules</>
Four fighters enter the arena and battle until time runs out. Final rankings are based on elimination order.
If no champion is crowned before the timer ends, rankings are based on each fighter's DMG dealt.
Depending on your final rank and damage dealt, City Stamina will be consumed, granting different amounts of Fons and Strong Painkillers.
A participant who deals no damage during the match is considered passive and can rank no higher than 4th place.
You can still enter with no City Stamina. You will still earn Strong Painkillers based on your rank and damage dealt.
Your Stamina cap in Fight Club matches your open-world Stamina cap.

<title>Combat Mechanics</>
Weapons are banned in Fight Club. This is a bare-knuckle brawl.
If a participant goes too long without dealing damage, spectators outside the ring will throw Soap at them.

<orange>Basic Attack</>
Launches a series of quick strikes that can break an opponent's Block.
<orange>Heavy Attack</>
After a string of Basic Attacks, the final hit becomes a <orange>red-glowing</> Heavy Attack that deals heavy damage and inflicts Stun.
Heavy Attacks can interrupt an opponent's Basic Attack.
Hold Basic Attack to unleash a Heavy Attack right away.
<orange>Block</>
Consumes Stamina to perform a <orange>blue-glowing</> Block.
Block at the right moment to counter an opponent's Heavy Attack, dealing damage and inflicting Stun.
<orange>Grapple Throw</>
Builds energy when Basic Attacks, Heavy Attacks, or Blocks deal damage. Once your energy is full, you can use Grapple Throw on an opponent who is Staggered, dealing massive damage.
<orange>Elimination Recovery</>
Restores HP once whenever you eliminate an opponent.
<orange>Stagger</>
Fighters become Staggered and cannot move after taking damage from a Heavy Attack, a well-timed Block, Soap, or a Pinecone Bomb explosion.
<orange>Soap</>
Soap appears at random during the match. Pick it up and throw it to Stagger an opponent.
<orange>Pinecone Bomb</>
If no fighters have been eliminated, a Pinecone Bomb will periodically appear above each fighter's head. When the countdown ends, it explodes, dealing heavy area damage.
Hit another fighter with a Heavy Attack to pass your Pinecone Bomb to them and reset its countdown. Each fighter can only have 1 Pinecone Bomb above them at a time.
ST_GameplayDec.LogisticsCenter_Desc:
<title>Logistics Hub Overview</>
Kool Express's Logistics Hub handles cargo sorting, fleet dispatch, and business strategy. Its goal? To dominate Hethereau's logistics industry!
Recruit drivers and earn rewards by running the Logistics Hub.

<title>1. Recruitment & Driver Management</>
Recruit the right drivers for the job. As you level up the Logistics Hub, you'll be able to find even more skilled drivers around the city.

<title>2. Logistics Strategy</>
Earn Kool Resources by dispatching drivers to complete orders. Level up the Logistics Hub and spend Kool Resources to upgrade your Logistics Strategy, and get more powerful bonuses

<title>3. Driver Dispatch</>
Send drivers out to complete a variety of orders and earn rewards. You can only dispatch a limited number of drivers at a time.

<title>4. Relationship Network</>
Unlock more connections as the Logistics Hub levels up, allowing you to accept orders from new organizations.
Completing certain orders affects your Official Reputation and Underground Reputation, which determine the types of orders available in the daily refresh.

<title>5. Earning Rewards</>
There are caps on the Kool Resources and Kool Tokens you can earn from the Logistics Hub. Once you reach a cap, you won't earn any more of that resource. In this version, you can earn up to 15,455 Kool Resources and 57,220 Kool Tokens.
ST_GameplayDec.DarkRacing:
<title>Underground Circuit Event Rules</>
Underground Circuit is a new 6-player Vehicle Brawl. Players <orange>do not</> need to bring their own Vehicles. During the match, they will battle using Vehicles and Vehicle weapons that <orange>spawn randomly</> across the track. Racers can choose to <orange>go solo</> and fight to cross the Finish Line first, or <orange>ride together</> in the same Vehicle and work as a team to claim victory.

<title> 1. Obtaining a Vehicle</>
At the start of the match, all players are unable to attack and can only move within the prep area. Once the countdown ends, players must rush out immediately, choose a Vehicle, and take a seat. Players may choose either the <orange>Driver Seat</> or the <orange>Passenger Seat</>.

<title> 2. Starting Traps</>
Various traps are scattered at random across the first 100 meters of track beyond the starting area. They activate as soon as they are touched. Use them wisely, and you may reach your preferred Vehicle before anyone else. Trap types are listed below: 
<orange>·Taygedo's Hammer</>: Smashes a random nearby target and knocks them down.
<orange>·Gigafluff</>: Charges straight ahead at targets in front, including the user.
<orange>·Paper Squadron</>: Whirls around nearby targets and throws off their direction.
<orange>·Ghostly Kite</>: Launches the user forward with a glider, granting a short burst of flight that can cross obstacles.
<orange>·Imaginadough</>: Creates a slowing field behind the character.
<orange>·Weird Bandage</>: Chases a random target ahead and wraps them up upon contact.

<title> 3. Vehicle Rules</>
Multiple Vehicles spawn at random across the track, and each comes equipped with a basic weapon. Vehicles are available on a first-come, first-served basis. During the race, players may enter and exit Vehicles freely, but they cannot summon Vehicles on their own.

<title> 4. Obtaining Weapons and Attacking</>
Various <orange>Weapon Crates</> appear along the track. Touch a Weapon Crate to obtain its item. Switch to <orange>Aiming Mode</> to attack with it. Drivers and passengers share any weapon item picked up by either rider.
Weapons can damage enemy Vehicles. Once a Vehicle has taken enough damage, it will be destroyed, and its riders will lose it.

<title> 5. Weapon Types</>
<orange>·Pistol</>: Fires single shots as the Vehicle's default weapon.
<orange>·Shotgun</>: Plants traps on the ground. Any Vehicle that drives over them will have its tires blown out, including your own.
<orange>·Frost Gun</>: Covers the target Vehicle's riders' screens with frost, blocking their vision.
<orange>·Gatling</>: Unleashes rapid suppressive fire, dealing heavy damage to target Vehicles.
<orange>·RPG Launcher</>: Fires a powerful rocket that poses a major threat to target Vehicles.
<orange>·Call Support</>: Triggers automatically after pickup and calls in 1 precision strike on the player currently in first place. If you are already in first place, it targets the player in second place instead.

<title> 6. Victory and Rankings</>
The first player to reach the Finish Line wins, triggering a 30-second countdown. Once the countdown ends, the race is over, and rankings are determined by each player's <orange>Total Completion Progress</>.
Players riding in the same Vehicle with the <orange>same progress</> receive the <orange>same rank</>. If players in the same Vehicle have <orange>different progress</>, their ranks are calculated separately based on their individual race progress.

<title> 7. Blacksteel Bolts</>
After each match, all participants receive Blacksteel Bolts, which can be exchanged for desired Items in the Bolt Shop.
Blacksteel Bolts have a <orange>daily acquisition limit</>, and this limit will <orange>increase over time</>.
ST_GameplayDec.Mahjong_des:
1. <title>Basic Rules</>
Sequence: 3 consecutive suited tiles of the same suit.
Triplet/Kong: 3 or 4 identical tiles.
Pair: 2 identical tiles.
Winning Hand: To win, use the tiles in your hand plus 1 drawn or discarded tile to form 0–4 sets, each made up of a Sequence or Triplet/Kong, plus 1 Pair.
For example: With 1 Character, 2 Character, 3 Character, 4 Bamboo, 5 Bamboo, 6 Bamboo, 7 Dot, 7 Dot, 7 Dot, and 9 Dot in your hand, you can win by drawing or claiming a discarded 8 Dot or 9 Dot.

<title>Special Rules</>
1. When a player wins (either by discard or self-draw), the game does not end. The winner draws a replacement card from the end of the wall and continues playing and staying in a ready hand. They can win multiple times (or deal into others' wins) until the wall is exhausted. This is the key difference from "Last Man Standing" (where winners exit after winning).

2. After receiving the initial hand, each player must select three tiles of the same suit to exchange with another player in the direction specified by the system. This is a crucial first step for adjusting your hand and building toward bigger wins.

3. Before play begins, you must designate one of the three suits (Dots, Bamboo, or Characters) as your "Void Suit" and prioritize discarding all tiles of that suit during play. When winning, your hand cannot contain any tiles of this suit.

4. Players who are not in ready hands (waiting to win) must pay compensation based on the highest possible multiplier of other players who are in ready.

5. Flower Pig: If a player still has tiles from all three suits at the end of the round, meaning they failed to fully discard their missing suit, they become a Flower Pig. A Flower Pig must pay a higher penalty to all players who are already in Tenpai (Ready Hand), or one tile away from winning.

<title>Scoring Patterns and Multipliers</>
Pong — 0×. When another player discards a tile that matches a Pair in your hand, you may claim it to form a Triplet.
Kong — 1×. When another player discards a tile and you already have 3 identical tiles, you may claim it to form a Kong.
Added Kong — 1×. If you draw a tile that matches a Triplet you previously formed with Pong, you may upgrade it into an Added Kong.
Concealed Kong — 2×. If you draw and hold 4 identical tiles in your hand, you may declare a Concealed Kong.
Common Hand — 1×. Wins with a standard hand made of Sequences and/or Triplets/Kongs, plus 1 Pair. Triplets/Kongs are not required.
All Simples — 2×. Wins with a hand that contains no terminal tiles: 1 Character, 9 Character, 1 Bamboo, 9 Bamboo, 1 Dot, or 9 Dot.
All Pungs — 2×. Wins with a hand made only of Triplets/Kongs.
Pure All Pungs — 8×. Wins with a hand made only of Triplets/Kongs and 1 Pair, with all tiles from the same suit: Characters, Bamboos, or Dots.
Seven Pairs — 4×. Wins with 7 Pairs.
Pure Seven Pairs — 16×. Wins with 7 Pairs, with all tiles from the same suit: Characters, Bamboos, or Dots.
Jiang Seven Pairs — 16×. Wins with 7 Pairs made only of 2s, 5s, and 8s from the Character, Bamboo, and Dot suits.
Straight Seven Pairs — 8×. Wins with 7 Pairs, including 1 set of 4 identical tiles.
Pure Straight Seven Pairs — 32×. Wins with 7 Pairs, including 1 set of 4 identical tiles, with all tiles from the same suit: Characters, Bamboos, or Dots.
Double-Straight Seven Pairs — 16×. Wins with 7 Pairs, including 2 sets of 4 identical tiles.
Triple-Straight Seven Pairs — 32×. Wins with 7 Pairs, including 3 sets of 4 identical tiles.
Jiang Double-Straight Seven Pairs — 64×. Wins with 7 Pairs, including 2 sets of 4 identical tiles, with all tiles made only of 2s, 5s, and 8s from the Character, Bamboo, and Dot suits.
Jiang Triple-Straight Seven Pairs — 128×. Wins with 7 Pairs, including 3 sets of 4 identical tiles, with all tiles made only of 2s, 5s, and 8s.
Four Kongs — 64×. Wins after declaring 4 Kongs and/or Concealed Kongs.
Pure Four Kongs — 256×. Wins after declaring 4 Kongs and/or Concealed Kongs, with all tiles from the same suit: Characters, Bamboos, or Dots.
Terminals in Every Set (All Terminals) — 4×. Wins with a hand where every Sequence, Triplet/Kong, and Pair contains at least one terminal tile: 1 Character, 9 Character, 1 Bamboo, 9 Bamboo, 1 Dot, or 9 Dot.
Pure Terminals (Pure All Terminals) — 16×. Wins with a hand made only of terminal tiles: 1 Character, 9 Character, 1 Bamboo, 9 Bamboo, 1 Dot, and 9 Dot.
Pure One-Suit — 4×. Wins with a hand made entirely of one suit: Characters, Bamboos, or Dots.
Golden Hook — 4×. Wins after using Pong, Kong, and/or Concealed Kong until only 1 tile remains in your hand.
Pure Golden Hook — 16×. Wins with a Golden Hook hand made entirely of one suit: Characters, Bamboos, or Dots.
Robbing the Kong — 2×. Wins by claiming the tile another player tries to use for an Added Kong.
Kong Discard Penalty (Kong Discard Loss) — 2×. Applies when a player declares a Kong, draws a replacement tile, then discards a tile that allows another player to win.
Kong-Draw Win — 2×. Wins by drawing a winning tile from the replacement draw after declaring a Kong.
Win on Last Tile — 2×. Wins by self-draw on the final tile of the round.
Earthly Hand — 32×. A non-dealer wins during the first turn cycle of the round.
Heavenly Hand — 32×. The dealer wins immediately with their starting 14-tile hand.

<title>Scoring Rules</>
1. Each player starts every round with 10,000 points. Points are reset at the end of each round.

2. When a player wins, the final Multiplier is calculated by multiplying all applicable Scoring Pattern multipliers together. Stacking several smaller patterns can lead to a much higher total score.

3. Kong tiles score instantly: When a Revealed Kong or Concealed Kong is declared, points are immediately collected from the other three players, providing ongoing scoring opportunities throughout the game.

4. After the game ends, rankings are determined by each player's final point total.

5. Special settlement: If three players all reach 0 points, the game ends early and rankings are settled.

<title>Ranking Rewards</>
The mode currency, Chirpy Sparrow Balls, is calculated as: Fixed Ranking Reward + Bonus Points Reward, where Bonus Points Reward = (player's final points − 10,000) ×5, and any negative value counts as 0.

2. Based on ranking order, you can spend 25, 20, 15, or 10 City Stamina to obtain Fons, with bonuses applied based on your Tycoon Level.

No rewards are granted for table games played using furniture inside houses.
ST_GameplayDec.Mahjonglizhi_des:
<title>Basic Rules</>
1. Wind Tiles: East (東, ton), South (南, nan), West (西, shaa), and North (北, pei).
2. Dragon Tiles: White Dragon (白, haku), Green Dragon (發, hatsu), and Red Dragon (中, chun).
3. Dora: Bonus tiles that add extra han after the hand already has at least one Yaku(valid scoring condition). Dora are determined by the Dora Indicator. The Dora is usually the next tile after the indicator, not the indicator itself.
4. Red Dora: Special red 5 tiles, usually one red 5 Character, one red 5 Bamboo, and one red 5 Dot. Each red Dora adds 1 han.
5. Sequence: 3 consecutive numbered tiles of the same suit, such as 2-3-4 Character.
6. Triplet (Koutsu): 3 identical tiles. Quad: 4 identical tiles. A quad is treated as one meld when forming a winning hand.
7. Pair: 2 identical tiles.
8. Winning Hand: A standard winning hand is made of 4 melds and 1 pair. In notation, this can be written as [n*AAA + m*ABC + DD, where n + m = 4] (it excludes special hands like Seven Pairs and Thirteen Orphans). AAA means a triplet or quad, ABC means a sequence, and DD means a pair.
Example: Suppose your hand contains 1 Character, 2 Character, 3 Character; 4 Bamboo, 5 Bamboo, 6 Bamboo; 2 Dot, 3 Dot, 4 Dot; 7 Dot, 7 Dot, 7 Dot; and 9 Dot. You can win by drawing or claiming either 8 Dot or 9 Dot.


<title>Winning Hands in Riichi Mahjong (Japanese ready-hand mahjong): In Riichi Mahjong (Japanese ready-hand mahjong), a hand cannot win unless it has at least one Yaku. Yaku are the scoring conditions or hand patterns that make a completed hand legally valid. Beginners can start by learning Tanyao (All Simples) and Riichi (ready-hand declaration).Yaku (valid scoring conditions) and Bonus Han (bonus scoring units)</>

1-Han Yaku (valid scoring conditions worth one Han)
Riichi (ready-hand declaration): Declare Riichi when your closed hand is in Tenpai (ready to win). A closed hand means you have not made any open calls.
Tanyao (All Simples): Your hand contains no Yaochuuhai (terminal or honor tiles). Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tiles) are the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits, plus the honor tiles: East, South, West, North, White Dragon, Green Dragon, and Red Dragon.
Menzen Tsumo (closed-hand self-draw): Win by Tsumo (self-draw) with a closed hand.
Yakuhai (value tiles) - Seat Wind: Your hand contains a triplet or Kan (quad) of your Seat Wind.
Yakuhai (value tiles) - Round Wind: Your hand contains a triplet or Kan (quad) of the Round Wind.
Yakuhai (value tiles) - Dragon Tiles: Your hand contains a triplet or Kan (quad) of White Dragon, Green Dragon, or Red Dragon tiles.
Pinfu (all-sequences hand): With a closed hand, your completed hand contains four sequences and one pair. The pair must not be a value pair, meaning it cannot be a Dragon pair, Seat Wind pair, or Round Wind pair. The winning wait must be a two-sided sequence wait.
Iipeikou (pure double sequence): With a closed hand, your hand contains two identical sequences in the same suit.
Chankan (robbing a Kan): Win by claiming the tile another player adds to an open triplet to declare a Kan (quad).
Rinshan Kaihou (after a Kan): Win by drawing the replacement tile after declaring a Kan (quad).
Haitei (last tile draw): Win by Tsumo (self-draw) on the last drawable tile from the live wall.
Houtei (last discard): Win by Ron (discard win) on the last discard of the hand.
Ippatsu (one-shot): After declaring Riichi (ready-hand declaration), win by Ron (discard win) or Tsumo (self-draw) before your next discard, with no calls or Kan (quad) declarations interrupting the turn order.
Open Chanta (outside hand, open version): With an open hand, every set and the pair must contain a Yaochuuhai (terminal or honor tile). The hand must also include at least one sequence and at least one honor tile.
Open Ittsu (pure straight, open version): With an open hand, your hand contains the 123, 456, and 789 sequences in the same suit.
Open Sanshoku Doujun (mixed triple sequence, open version): With an open hand, your hand contains the same numbered sequence in each of the three suits: Characters, Dots, and Bamboo.
Bonus Han (bonus scoring units)
Dora (bonus tile): A Dora Indicator (bonus-tile indicator) shows which tile is Dora. Normally, the Dora is the next tile after the indicator in the tile order. Each Dora adds 1 Han (scoring unit), but Dora is not a Yaku (valid scoring condition) and cannot make a hand valid by itself.
Ura-Dora (hidden bonus tile): If you win after declaring Riichi (ready-hand declaration), the hidden Dora Indicators (bonus-tile indicators) are revealed. The tiles indicated by them are Ura-Dora, and each Ura-Dora adds 1 Han (scoring unit). Ura-Dora is not a Yaku (valid scoring condition).
Red Dora (red bonus tile): Special red 5 tiles. Each Red Dora adds 1 Han (scoring unit), but Red Dora is not a Yaku (valid scoring condition).
2-Han Yaku (valid scoring conditions worth two Han)
Double Riichi (first-turn ready-hand declaration): Declare Riichi (ready-hand declaration) on your first uninterrupted turn at the start of the hand, before any player calls a tile or declares a Kan (quad).
Sanshoku Doukou (three-color triplets): Your hand contains the same numbered triplet or Kan (quad) in each of the three suits: Characters, Dots, and Bamboo.
San Kantsu (three Kans): Your hand contains three Kans (quads), open or closed.
Toitoi (all triplets): Your hand contains four triplets or Kans (quads) plus one pair.
San Ankou (three concealed triplets): Your hand contains three concealed triplets or concealed Kans (quads). A triplet completed by Ron (discard win) does not count as concealed.
Shousangen (little three dragons): Your hand contains triplets or Kans (quads) of two Dragon tiles, plus a pair of the third Dragon tile.
Honroutou (all terminals and honors): Your hand contains only Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tiles): the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits, plus East, South, West, North, White Dragon, Green Dragon, and Red Dragon. This hand contains no sequences.
Chiitoitsu (seven pairs): Your hand contains seven different pairs, 14 tiles total. This Yaku (valid scoring condition) requires a closed hand.
Chanta (outside hand): With a closed hand, every set and the pair must contain a Yaochuuhai (terminal or honor tile). The hand must also include at least one sequence and at least one honor tile.
Ittsuu: (pure straight): With a closed hand, your hand contains the 123, 456, and 789 sequences in the same suit.
Sanshoku Doukou: (mixed triple sequence): With a closed hand, your hand contains the same numbered sequence in each of the three suits: Characters, Dots, and Bamboo.
Open Junchan (pure outside hand, open version): With an open hand, every set and the pair contains a terminal number tile. Terminal number tiles are the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits. This hand contains no honor tiles and must include at least one sequence.
Open Honitsu (half flush, open version): With an open hand, your hand consists of one suit plus honor tiles.
3-Han Yaku (valid scoring conditions worth three Han)
Ryanpeikou (twice pure double sequence): Closed hand only. Your hand contains two separate pairs of identical sequences. This does not also count as Iipeikou (pure double sequence).
Junchan (pure outside hand): With a closed hand, every set and the pair contains a terminal number tile. Terminal number tiles are the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits. This hand contains no honor tiles and must include at least one sequence.
Honitsu (half flush): With a closed hand, your hand consists of one suit plus honor tiles.
5-Han Yaku (valid scoring conditions worth five Han)
Open Chinitsu (full flush, open version): With an open hand, your hand consists only of one suit and contains no honor tiles.
6-Han Yaku (valid scoring conditions worth six Han)
Chinitsu (full flush): With a closed hand, your hand consists only of one suit and contains no honor tiles.
Mangan (limit hand)
Nagashi Mangan (mangan at exhaustive draw): At an exhaustive draw, all of your discards are Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tiles), and none of those discards were called by another player. Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tiles) are the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits, plus East, South, West, North, White Dragon, Green Dragon, and Red Dragon.
Yakuman (limit hands)
Tenhou (blessing of heaven): The dealer wins with the initial 14-tile hand before making the first discard.
Chiihou (blessing of earth): A non-dealer wins by Tsumo (self-draw) on their first turn, before any calls are made.
Daisangen (big three dragons): Your hand contains triplets or Kans (quads) of White Dragon, Green Dragon, and Red Dragon.
Suu Ankou (four concealed triplets): Your hand contains four concealed triplets or concealed Kans (quads). A triplet completed by Ron (discard win) does not count as concealed.
Tsuuiisou (all honors): Your hand consists entirely of honor tiles: East, South, West, North, White Dragon, Green Dragon, and Red Dragon.
Ryuuiisou (all green): Your hand consists only of green tiles: 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 Bamboo, and Green Dragon.
Chinroutou (all terminals): Your hand consists entirely of terminal number tiles and contains no honor tiles. Terminal number tiles are the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits.
Kokushi Musou (thirteen orphans): Your hand contains all 13 types of Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tiles), plus one duplicate Yaochuuhai (terminal or honor tile), for 14 tiles total. Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tiles) are the 1 and 9 tiles in the Characters, Dots, and Bamboo suits, plus East, South, West, North, White Dragon, Green Dragon, and Red Dragon.
Shousuushii (little four winds): Your hand contains triplets or Kans (quads) of three of the four Wind tiles, plus a pair of the fourth Wind tile.
Suukantsu (four Kans): Your hand contains four Kans (quads), whether open or closed.
Chuuren Poutou (nine gates): Closed hand only. Your hand contains 1112345678999 plus one extra tile, all in the same suit.
Double Yakuman (double limit hands)
Suuankou Tanki (four concealed triplets with a single-tile pair wait): Your hand satisfies Suu Ankou (four concealed triplets) and wins on a single-tile wait for the pair.
Kokushi Musou 13-Sided Wait (thirteen orphans with a 13-sided wait): Your hand satisfies Kokushi Musou (thirteen orphans) by waiting on any one of the 13 Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tile) types.
Junsei Chuuren Poutou (true nine gates): Your hand has the pure Chuuren Poutou (nine gates) shape, waiting on any tile from 1 to 9 in that same suit.
Daisuushii (big four winds): Your hand contains triplets or Kans (quads) of East, South, West, and North.

<title>Abortive Draws</>
Four Wind Discards: Before any calls are made, all four players discard the same Wind tile on their first discard.
Four Kans Abortive Draw: The hand ends in an abortive draw when two or more players have declared a total of four Kans (quads). If all four Kans (quads) are declared by the same player, this abortive draw does not occur.
Nine Terminals and Honors: Before making your first discard and before any calls are made, you may declare an abortive draw if your hand contains nine or more different Yaochuuhai (terminal and honor tile) types.
Four Riichi (four ready-hand declarations): The hand ends in an abortive draw after all four players successfully declare Riichi (ready-hand declaration).

<title>Multiple Ron (Atamahane)</>
If multiple players declare Ron on the same discard, the winner is determined by turn order. Only the player with the highest priority wins; multiple Ron is not permitted.

<title>Ranking Rewards</>
1. The mode currency, Chirpy Sparrow Balls, is calculated as: Fixed Ranking Reward + Bonus Points Reward, where Bonus Points Reward = (player's final points − 25,000) ×2.5, and any negative value counts as 0.

2. Based on ranking order, you can spend 65, 60, 55, or 30 City Stamina to obtain Fons, with bonuses applied based on your Tycoon Level.

3. No rewards are granted for table games played using furniture inside houses.

<title>How to Manage The Cafe by Origen</>
1. Once an item is listed and stocked in your shop, it will gradually earn Fons over time, up to a maximum of 72 hours.

ST_GameplayDec.MahjongRoomDescription:
<title>Special Rules</>
1. When a player wins (either by discard or self-draw), the game does not end. The winner draws a replacement card from the end of the wall and continues playing and staying in a ready hand. They can win multiple times (or deal into others' wins) until the wall is exhausted. This is the key difference from "Last Man Standing" (where winners exit after winning).

2. After receiving the initial hand, each player must select three tiles of the same suit to exchange with another player in the direction specified by the system. This is a crucial first step for adjusting your hand and building toward bigger wins.

3. Before play begins, you must designate one of the three suits (Dots, Bamboo, or Characters) as your "Void Suit" and prioritize discarding all tiles of that suit during play. When winning, your hand cannot contain any tiles of this suit.

4. Players who are not in ready hands (waiting to win) must pay compensation based on the highest possible multiplier of other players who are in ready.

5. Flower Pig: If a player's hand still contains all three suits at the end (meaning they failed to clear their Void Suit), they are considered a Flower Pig and must pay a higher compensation multiplier to all players in ready hands.

<title>Scoring Rules</>
1. Each player starts with 10,000 points. Points reset after each round.

2. When winning, the total multiplier is calculated by multiplying all applicable scoring patterns together. Strategically, small hands can build into big wins.

3. Kong tiles score instantly: When a Revealed Kong or Concealed Kong is declared, points are immediately collected from the other three players, providing ongoing scoring opportunities throughout the game.

4. After the game ends, rankings are determined by each player's final point total.

5. Special settlement: If three players all reach 0 points, the game ends early and rankings are settled.
ST_GameplayDec.RobbankGameplay_Dec:
<title>Mode Rules</>
 1. Collect as many Collectibles as possible on the map before time runs out. Evacuate to convert your earnings into Fons. Rewards will no longer accumulate once the cap is reached.
 2. ReroRero Phone Booths appear on the map. Evacuate through any activated booth before time runs out. If all characters are down or time expires, all earnings are lost.
 3. Taking damage may cause you to lose earnings. Plan your route and watch your characters' status.
 4. The map contains valuable Collectibles as well as functional items like Access Cards and Vault Keycards. They don't give earnings directly, but can unlock rooms with lots of Collectibles or be carried for use in future runs.
 5. In Multiplayer, rewards scale dynamically with party size. As more players join, defeated targets drop better loot, high-rarity Collectibles appear more frequently, Paw-Paw Coin gains are improved, and rewards from defeating Mammon are increased.

<title>Special Notes</>
 1. Earnings from this mode are capped per update cycle (2 weeks). Once the cap is reached, Fons can no longer be earned, but the mode remains playable.
 2. This mode uses a special <red>Character Balance Mode</>. All deployed characters use fixed stats regardless of progression, while Awakening effects remain active.
 3. Certain skills and Awakening effects are adjusted in Character Balance Mode:
 3.1. Baicang's Ultimate: Executes the target instantly when their HP falls below 5% (2.5% for Bosses).
3.2. Sakiri's Awakening Effect: Disables Gluttonous Dissolution.
ST_GameplayDec.OpActFriendlyCitizen_Dec:

 3. You can earn up to 150 points per day. Once the daily limit is reached, no further points can be obtained that day.

ST_GameplayDec.Endlesstrial_Des:
<title>Mode Rules</>
Terminal Depths is a limited-time challenge mode. Clear stages quickly and complete stage objectives to earn rewards.

<title>Roster Setup</>
1. Stages in Terminal Depths are divided into <orange>Stage Groups</>. You can only <orange>set your roster before entering the first stage of each Stage Group</>.
2. The number of characters you can add to your roster <orange>increases as you reach higher floors</>.
3. Once your roster is set, you can freely choose which characters to deploy <orange>in any stage within the current Stage Group</>.
4. Characters in your roster <orange>retain their current HP between stages within a Stage Group</>, so manage their HP carefully as you progress.

<title>Stage Group Reset</>
1. To replay a completed stage, select it, reset its Stage Group, and restart from the first stage in that group.

<title>Attributes & Cards</>
1. Each stage features enemies with different <orange>Esper Ability Resistances and Weaknesses</>.
2. On every 10th stage, you can set <orange>cards to Upright or Reversed</> to apply Positive or Negative effects in that stage.
3. The <orange>number of cards you can set to Upright</> increases when you <orange>earn an S Rating on specific stages</> in the current Stage Group.

<title>Score & Rating</>
1. Clearing a stage grants a stage score based on <orange>the challenge objectives you complete and your clear time</>.
2. Each stage has 3 challenge objectives. Completing them grants additional score, but <orange>the score obtainable from challenge objectives is capped</>.
3. The faster you clear a stage, the more score you earn from clear time, up to <orange>300 points</>.
4. Ratings are based on score: <orange>S requires 200 points, A requires 100, B requires 50, and lower scores receive C</>.
5. To <orange>rechallenge a completed stage</>, select it, reset its Stage Group, and restart from <orange>the first stage in that group</>.
6. Repeated challenges retain your <orange>highest score and best rating</>.

<title>Rewards</>
1. For the <orange>first 50 stages</>, each stage grants a <orange>first-clear reward</>.
2. Clearing designated stages grants <orange>title rewards</>, while <orange>clearing higher floors upgrades the title effect</>.
3. The title displays your <orange>total score in this mode</>.
ST_GameplayDec.GamePlayDec_CombatAwards_Content:
<title>Circle Bounty</>
Circle Bounty are issued by the Anomaly Hunter Guild. Appraisers can obtain substantial reward after completing Circle Quests.
When each Circle Bounty season begins, Standard Hunter Supply is unlocked by default.
You can purchase Elite Hunter Supplies or Honor Hunter Supplies for more generous rewards.

<title>Circle Quest Info</>
Appraisers can complete Circle Quests to earn Experience Points, increase Circle Bounty levels, and claim seasonal rewards.
Circle Quests are divided into three categories: Daily Quests, Weekly Quests, and Seasonal Quests.
Daily Quests reset at <orange>05:00 daily</> (Server Time).
Weekly Quests reset at <orange>05:00 every Monday</> (Server Time).
Experience Points have a weekly earning limit. Experience Points obtained from Seasonal Quests are excluded from this limit.
After Circle Bounty reaches its level limit, completing Circle Quests will no longer increase its level.

<title>Special Notes</>
If, due to special circumstances, Elite Hunter Supplies or Honor Hunter Supplies is unlocked more than once, or an already-unlocked Elite Hunter Supplies is upgraded to Honor Hunter Supplies, Experience Points will not stack. The corresponding purchase will be refunded in Riftcrystals.
At the end of a Circle Bounty season, any unclaimed level rewards will be sent via Mail.
ST_GameplayDec.RoomPreviewIconInvite:
<title>Character Invitation Guide</>
1. After owning a house, you can invite different characters to move in via the invitation interface.
2. Once a character is invited to move in, they will reside permanently in the designated house.
3. Characters will act autonomously after moving in, such as reading books, wandering around, etc.
4. Each action's <orange>first</> interaction with a resident character will increase Affection.
5. Invited characters of opposite genders cannot share the same house.
6. Each property can accommodate different numbers of invited characters.
Wiener Apartments can accommodate <orange>1</> character.
Eden Apartments can accommodate <orange>2</> characters.
Skyview Halls can accommodate <orange>2</> characters.
Golden Capital can accommodate <orange>3</> characters.
Stillmeadow House can accommodate <orange>4</> characters.
Pegasus Residence can accommodate <orange>5</> characters.
Fenglin Villa can accommodate <orange>5</> characters.

<title>Invitation Interaction Guide</>
1. Invitation interactions are divided into Solo Actions and Interactive Actions.
Both action types require reaching the corresponding <orange>Bond Level</> or placing the corresponding <orange>furniture</> to unlock.
2. Obtaining Character Interactions: When a character's Bond Level reaches <orange>Lvl 4</> and <orange>Lvl 6</>, you can obtain the Bond Items <orange>Familiar</> and <orange>Close Friends</>. Upon obtaining them, some of that character's actions will be automatically unlocked.
ST_GameplayDec.GamePlayDesc_Abyss_Content:
<title>Beyond the Rails</>
Beyond the Rails puts your skills to the test with <red>high-difficulty</> challenge stages. Complete stage objectives to earn <red>Platform Seals</>, which can be exchanged for rewards once enough are collected.
Each station hosts unique <red>Anomalies</> that reveal Esper Ability <red>weaknesses</> and <red>resistances</>. Check station details and plan your <red>Companions</> carefully to tackle them efficiently.

<title>Train Routes</>
There are two route types in Beyond the Rails:
 1. <red>All-Day Routes</>: Permanently available. Rewards can be claimed <red>once</> per completion.
 2. <red>Special Routes</>: Rotates periodically with tougher stages, updated content, and exclusive rewards. Unlock it by completing the All-Day Route first.

<title>Otherworld Resonance</>
Every route comes with a unique <red>Resonance Effect</> that applies to all stations along it. Learning how to use this effect can give you a big edge in completing challenge objectives.

<title>Otherworld Supply Stop</>
 1. Unlocking a route grants <red>Shadowquills</>.
 2. Spend Shadowquills at the Otherworld Supply Stop to obtain <red>Miss Levi's Gift</>, which grants powerful skill effects.
 3. Miss Levi's Gift works only at the current station and cannot be carried forward. Resetting a station lets you choose a new one for it to take effect.
 4. Note: Shadowquills and Miss Levi's Gifts are route-specific and cannot be shared.

<title>Route Updates</>
Special Routes typically reset <red>every 14 days</>. When that happens: a) All Platform Seals are cleared. b) Otherworld Resonance and station Anomalies change. c) Challenges in progress during a reset automatically fail.

<title>Fast Travel</>
After a Special Route resets, your total Platform Seals from the previous route determine how far you <red>auto-progress</> in the new route. Stations cleared automatically retain the Companion setup from the previous run in your Otherworld Travel Log.

 18–20 Seals: Auto-complete Station 1, jump to Station 2.
21–23 Seals: Auto-complete Stations 1–2, jump to Station 3.
24–26 Seals: Auto-complete Stations 1–3, jump to Station 4.
27–29 Seals: Auto-complete Stations 1–4, jump to Station 5.
30–32 Seals: Auto-complete Stations 1–5, jump to Station 6.
33–35 Seals: Auto-complete Stations 1–6, jump to Station 7.
36 Seals: Auto-complete Stations 1–7, jump to Station 8.
ST_GameplayDec.fishtank_Des:
<title>Fish Tank Setup Guide</>

Auto-Feeding
Different fish species require different kinds of fish food. Once you have purchased the right food, you can enable auto-feeding.
The more fish you raise and the heavier they are, the more Fish Food they consume.
When Basic Fish Food is insufficient, Premium Fish Food is consumed instead.
Auto-Feeding is triggered automatically once per hour. If there is sufficient fish food in reserve, a single feeding will fill up the Hunger Bar.

Water Temperature
Each fish species has its own ideal water temperature. The more species you keep in the same tank, the stricter the temperature requirements become.
Water temperature directly affects fish health. You can enable automatic temperature control to keep the water temperature within the ideal range for all fish in the Fish Tank.

pH Value
Each fish species has its own suitable pH range. The more species you keep together, the narrower the compatible pH range becomes.
The Fish Tank's pH value changes over time and affects fish health, so adjust the water quality regularly.

Fish Density
Different Fish Tank sizes can hold different maximum numbers of fish.

Health
If fish are hungry, the water temperature is abnormal, or the pH value is unsuitable, their health will continue to decline. If conditions are not improved for a long time, fish may be lost.
Keeping fish well-fed and maintaining a suitable, stable water temperature and pH value will gradually restore their health.

Fish Weight
For fish caught while fishing, heavier fish are larger in size.
ST_GameplayDec.BidkingCabinet_Dec:
<title>Collection Showcase Overview</>

1. The Collection Showcase has display slots of different sizes where you can store and display high-quality collectibles.
2. Collect the required number of certain collectibles to exchange them for exclusive furniture for your home.
3. Furniture exchanges are limited each month.
4. Certain Special Life Skills change the requirements for furniture exchanges.
5. Spend Gold Shell to upgrade the Collection Showcase and enhance its displays.
ST_GameplayDec.Volleyball_Dec:
<title>Mode Overview</>
1. Volley Star is a 2v2 competitive volleyball mode.
2. Complete the training quest Let Your Summer Spirit Soar! under coach Uncle Loong's guidance to officially register as a Volleyball Challenger.
3. Work with your teammate and use actions such as <orange>Serve</>, <orange>Receive</>, <orange>Set</>, <orange>Spike</>, and <orange>Block</> to outplay your opponents and rise as the next Volley Star.

<title>Match Victory Conditions</>
1. Matches are played in <orange>2v2 Competitive Mode</>.
2. Both teams attack and defend by returning the ball over the net and looking for openings to score.
3. The first team to <orange>reach 7 points</> with a <orange>2-point lead</> wins. If neither team meets both conditions, play continues.

<title>Serve Rules</>
1. At the start of the match and after each point, the next rally begins with a serve.
2. Players can choose between two types of serves:
<orange>- Underhand Serve</>: A stable and reliable basic serve that always clears the net. Recommended for beginners and players with lower Serve Aptitude.
<orange>- Jump Serve</>: A more aggressive advanced serve. Its chance of clearing the net depends on the player's <orange>Serve Aptitude</>. If Serve Aptitude is too low, the serve may fail. Recommended once Serve Aptitude reaches 100 or higher.

<title>Touch Rules</>
1. Watch the ball's trajectory and time your touches carefully to return it to the opponent's side or set it up for your teammate.
2. Each team may touch the ball up to <orange>3 times</> before returning it.
3. On the 3rd touch, the ball will be sent back to the opponent's side regardless of the action used.

<title>Spike Rules</>
1. Spiking is the main offensive option in a match.
2. After your teammate sets the ball on the <orange>second touch</>, you can spike.
3. A successful spike sends the ball rapidly toward the opponent's side, putting heavy pressure on their defense.
4. When you trigger a spike, your character runs up and <orange>leaps into the air</>. During the brief airborne window, you can choose between a Short Tip and a Deep Power Spike.
<orange>- Short Tip</>: Drops the ball into the frontcourt and always succeeds. Recommended early on when Spike Aptitude is still low.
<orange>- Deep Power Spike</>: Slams the ball into the opponent's backcourt. Its chance of clearing the net depends on Spike Aptitude. With proper timing, you can perform a Perfect Spike, which always clears the net.
5. Auto-Spike is enabled by default. When a spike becomes available, your character will automatically jump, and you only need to time your Short Tip or Deep Power Spike. If Auto-Spike is disabled, you must press jump yourself to initiate the spike.
6. Use <orange>Receive</>, <orange>Set</>, and <orange>Spike</> in sequence to create stronger scoring opportunities.

<title>Block Rules</>
1. Blocking is an important defensive option for stopping an opponent's attack.
2. Once the opposing team <orange>sets the ball</>, move near the net to block the incoming attack. A successful block can shut down their offense.


<title>Rookie Series</>
1. Rookie Series is a PvE challenge mode where you can take on stages to recruit more players and build your ideal volleyball team.
2. Clear each stage in order to hone your volleyball skills and earn rewards.
3. Rookie Series consists of 4 stages:
<orange>- Warm-Up</>: A basic stage designed for players experiencing volleyball mode for the first time.
<orange>- First Serve</>: The difficulty gradually increases, testing your basic controls and team coordination.
<orange>- Finding Form</>: Face stronger opponents and put your offensive and defensive skills to the test.
<orange>- Pro Arena</>: The most difficult stage, where you face off against powerful volleyball players.
4. After clearing a stage, you earn <orange>Star Power</> based on your performance.
5. Accumulate enough <orange>Star Power Ratings</> to claim <orange>Star Rewards</>.
6. Each Rookie Series match consumes <orange>City Stamina</> and rewards <orange>Fons</>.

<title>Weekly Match</>
1. Weekly Match is a weekly competitive mode where you battle through a series of matches for the championship.
2. Clear Rookie Series <orange>Warm-Up 10</> to unlock Weekly Match.
3. Weekly Match consists of two phases:
<orange>- Group Stage</>
<orange>- Finals</>
4. Group Stage: Complete <orange>2 matches</>. Rankings are determined by match results, and the top 2 advance to the Finals.
5. Finals: Qualified players must complete <orange>3 matches</>. The champion receives the highest-tier rewards.
6. During the Finals, losing a match will <orange>immediately end your run and settle your results</>.
7. Each Weekly Match consumes <orange>City Stamina</> and rewards <orange>Fons</>.
8. Based on your final Weekly Match result, you will receive the corresponding amount from the <orange>Tycoon Incentive Fund</>:
<orange>- Champion</>: 500,000 Fons
<orange>- Runner-Up</>: 400,000 Fons
<orange>- Top 4</>: 300,000 Fons
<orange>- Top 8</>: 200,000 Fons
<orange>- Eliminated in Group Stage</>: 50,000 Fons
9. Participating in Weekly Match also earns <orange>World Ranking Points</> based on your final result, allowing you to compete for a place on the World Ranking.
10. The first time you reach a specified placement on the World Ranking, you can receive a <orange>permanent exclusive title</>.

<title>Player Aptitude</>
1. Each player has 6 core Aptitudes:
<orange>Serve</>, <orange>Spike</>, <orange>Set</>, <orange>Receive</>, <orange>Dig</>, and <orange>Block</>.
2. Raise a player's Aptitudes to improve their performance in matches.

<title>Serve</>
Affects a player's serving ability:
<orange>- Jump Serve Success Rate</>: The higher the stat, the greater the chance a Jump Serve will clear the net.
<orange>- Serve Speed</>: The higher the stat, the faster the serve travels.
<orange>- Serve Direction</>: During the serve animation, you can choose <orange>Serve Left</> or <orange>Serve Right</>.
<orange>- Serve Power</>: Reduces the opponent's chance of successfully receiving the serve.

<title>Spike</>
Affects a player's offensive ability:
<orange>- Perfect Spike Timing Window</>: Widens the timing window for a Perfect Spike, making it easier to perform.
<orange>- Perfect Spike Chance</>: Increases the chance of triggering a Perfect Spike.
<orange>- Spike Success Rate</>: Increases the chance that a Deep Power Spike will clear the net. Short Tips always clear the net.

<title>Set</>
Affects a player's setting ability:
<orange>- Set Accuracy</>: Reduces deviation from the intended set location.
<orange>- Ball Contact Range</>: Expands the range within which the player can make contact with the ball.

<title>Receive</>
Affects a player's defensive ability:
<orange>- Defensive Range</>: Expands the area in which the player can receive the ball.
<orange>- Attack Resistance</>: Increases resistance against opposing serves and spikes.

<title>Dig</>
Affects a player's ability to make difficult saves:
<orange>- Defensive Range</>: Expands the range for diving saves.
<orange>- Attack Resistance</>: Increases resistance against powerful serves and spikes.

<title>Block</>
Affects a player's blocking ability:
<orange>- Block Hang Time</>: Increases airtime while blocking.
<orange>- Block Range</>: Expands the area the player can cover while blocking.
<orange>- Attack Resistance</>: Increases resistance against opposing serves and spikes.

<title>Aptitude Training</>
1. Use <orange>Talent Bread</> to improve a player's growth potential.
2. Using <orange>Talent Bread</> increases the stat gains the player receives when leveling up.
3. Each stat can be trained with Talent Bread up to <orange>3 times</>.
4. Each stat can gain up to <orange>12 additional points</> through Aptitude Training.

ST_IntroduceMsg_World.Hospital_AnomalyCanIntro_Jigsaw:
Jigsaw (Type ?) 
This experimental subject's body can be artificially divided into at least four or more sections. It is generally used as a Bio-lock space requiring high levels of security to access; the sample itself must be fully recombined with its other fragments, or "pieces," before a specific space can be opened.
It holds significant medical research value and may be combined with █████████; investigation is still ongoing.

ST_Item.Furniture_draw_0014_desc:
"Flowers: Dream Path" by Bichir Whites, and an anonymous contributor.
Whites mentioned multiple times in his diary that he met a close friend during his travels, and they would often meet to discuss art. They even slept side-by-side in the studio, painting through the night. The "Flowers" series was created during this period. Perhaps influenced by this friend, Whites' paintings from this time used lighter, fresher colors and focused mainly on depicting the concrete forms of objects.
"Dream Path" is the first painting in this series, created by Whites based on his friend's description of a pathway from a dream.
ST_Item.Furniture_draw_0015_desc:
"Flowers: Butterflies to Flowers" by Bichir Whites, and an anonymous contributor.
Whites mentioned multiple times in his diary that he met a close friend during his travels, and they would often meet to discuss art. They even slept side-by-side in the studio, painting through the night. The "Flowers" series was created during this period. Perhaps influenced by this friend, Whites' paintings from this time used lighter, fresher colors and focused mainly on depicting the concrete forms of objects.
"Butterflies to Flowers" is the third painting in this series, created by Whites after hearing a tragic local love story. The other person wrote a poem for this artwork.
"The butterfly messenger seeks branches where buds first bloom, half-rolled rouge petals, shy of the eastern wind's gaze."

ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1021_desc:
Edgar's namecard as a staff member of Eibon Antique Shop.
The photo is from Edgar's personal resume. Edgar went all out preparing to apply for a position at Eibon Antique Shop… but in the end, none of it was actually necessary.
Still, Taygedo, whom Edgar respectfully treated as the "interviewer," got a real kick out of it.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1010_desc:
Nanally's namecard as a staff member of Eibon Antique Shop.
The textured watermark patterns on the paper (crumpled from sleeping on it), the understated luxury color scheme (ran out of budget for color printing), the faintly visible decorative lines (hand slipped while drawing)… Every detail speaks to the mysterious and noble identity of the card's owner. She calls this "boss vibes." Surely someone out there gets it.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1003_desc:
Sakiri's namecard as a staff member of Eibon Antique Shop.
"What do you mean you don't have a namecard? How can a member of The Coluccis not have a namecard? Go get one made right now!" This namecard was born from that exact demand. It's unclear how Sakiri actually feels about it, but at least Nanally is satisfied.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1005_desc:
Daffodill's namecard as a staff member of Eibon Antique Shop.
What does it mean for a person to have a namecard? Is it like a dog having a tag with its name on it? She doesn't quite understand the significance yet. But one thing she knows for certain: before, she always used different codenames for different missions. Now, she just needs to be Daffodill.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1029_desc:
Hotori's namecard as the Owner of Eibon Antique Shop.
Almost every antique acquisition deal that ends with the buyer being duped by fakes or inferior goods somehow traces back to Hotori through this card. So every now and then, she takes it out for a good look, wondering if there's something wrong with the placement of the photo and text in the layout… from a feng shui perspective.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1033_desc:
The official namecard of the Butler of Eibon Antique Shop.
Present this card at the shop to receive personal service from the Eibon Butler, along with a special discount! But for Adler himself, the very existence of this card signifies something more: a wanderer who drifted through half a lifetime has finally found a place to call home.

ST_Item.EquipmentUpMaterial_lv1_desc: "Take me along? Sure, why not—it's not like I have anything better to do."
ST_Item.PortableVision_BlueDrawing_desc: "Architecture is the art of combining planes and space… If it's hard to understand, why not try looking at it from a different angle?"
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1075_desc:
Namecard of Oneiroi, a member of the Bureau of Anomaly Control's CSU-2.
A photograph, and a name. It is the name her parents gave her at birth—and in some distant legend, it also seems to belong to a god who rules over dreams. The name clings to her like an incantation. Was her Esper Ability granted because of it? Or had that god already foreseen the miracle that would be bestowed upon her, quietly planting this name in her parents' minds before they chose it? Tangled, disordered questions drift through her thoughts, bump against her forehead, and fall to the floor—without echo, without answer.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1076_desc:
Namecard of Shinku, a member of the Bureau of Anomaly Control's CSU-2.
Most Anomalies handled by the Containment Units each day are not exactly known for their reading skills, and the work rarely places them in ETD's awkward position of handing out namecards while apologizing to affected civilians. So when would these little printed slips ever prove useful? One can only guess—but perhaps someone within the Bureau collects them like trading cards…
ST_Item.BusinessCard_1090_des:
A Namecard for Elyms, a lieutenant in the Bureau's ETD-6.
As ETD-6's communications officer, Elyms deals with people from all walks of life, so the card has a clean, attractive design and was printed in large quantities. Oddly, the name and photo look a little blurry, but the phone number is crystal clear…
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1072_desc:
Namecard of Linko, a member of ETD-6 in the Bureau of Anomaly Control.
Linko often wonders whether her dreams are completely out of her reach, like frequencies playing endlessly, only to never be picked up—slipping past towering high-rises, treetops, and antennas alike. If, one day, you see a photo, hear a name, or catch a signal from somewhere you can't quite place, it might just be her, sending out a long-lost "hello".
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1071_desc:
A namecard belonging to Chaos, a member of ETD-6.
One of the few copies still intact. Half of the original batch became Tindalos's toys—dogs are born to destroy things, after all. The other half were scattered across the city and somehow turned into telemarketing calls to Chaos's phone. Good thing Bureau of Anomaly Control employee namecards are free.
ST_Item.BusinessCard_1074_des:
A Namecard for Exe, captain of the Bureau's ETD-6.
The only name printed on it is his "online handle," with a small note underneath explaining that it's pronounced like the letter "X." Is he keeping his real identity under wraps, or is he just used to going by that alias? Maybe there's more to the name than its obvious connection to the .exe file extension…
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1008_desc:
Skia's namecard as Lieutenant of ETD-4.
A namecard should include essential information such as the holder's name, title, full company name, detailed address, and valid contact methods like phone number, email, Bagel account, and Sesame Codes, ensuring that clients and partners can easily get in touch. However, this card, produced in a standardized format, seems to fall short on information. Skia is not amused.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1004_desc:
Lacrimosa's… namecard? As a member of ETD-4.
"Just hand this card to someone, and they'll know who you are without any introductions." Sounded convenient enough, so Lacrimosa decided to make one herself… The photo might not be the most professional, but it certainly leaves an impression.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1039_desc:
Fadia's namecard as a member of ETD-4.
When a bold and provocative lipstick mark is printed on a namecard, the recipient tends to have an interesting reaction. A secret thrill from mistaking it for an invitation, perhaps. The awkwardness of something beyond normal social norms. A fleeting flash of disdain… In truth, it's all just a little test. She uses it to catch a glimpse of their true colors, and she never gets tired of it.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1023_desc:
Baicang's namecard as the Captain of ETD-4.
Concise wording, clean layout, and so professional that it doesn't seem like Baicang's card at all. Of course, that's because he didn't actually make it himself. All credit goes to his dependable Lieutenant. As for Baicang's take on it… well, how could a little piece of paper ever define a living, complex person?
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1019_desc:
Mint's namecard as a member of CSU-2.
Does seeing this card make you think of Mint? Then open up Bagel and chat with her right away! Mint's always got endless topics to talk about, and she'll absolutely reply in a flash! Well, except when she's on duty, of course.
ST_Item.Dicelimite_lacrimosa_desc: A serene dream upon a quiet pillow, accompanied by a lingering song.
ST_Item.BandageClue_1_des: "The patient exhibited significant anxiety and abnormal behavior, insisting on tightly binding the affected areas with bandages and refusing to remove them. Patient also shows extreme sensitivity to visual and auditory stimuli."
ST_Item.item_quest_K110358_usedesc: "We! Are! One! —Conscientious Giant Pup!" Quest Item
ST_Item.Dicelimite_blackbird_des: "Perhaps fate is simply that which we cannot escape."
ST_Item.WeaponGacha_Nanally_desc: "Leave everything to the one and only Ichi-daime!"

ST_Item.Frame_MangHe_005_ly: Obtained from the Open Roads Ahead Mystery Box.

ST_Item.Dicelimite_zankou_desc: "Hopelessly devoted, and happy to stay that way."
ST_Item.food_059_desc:
Seize the day. 
Fill a large mug from the barrel's spout with frothy, deep golden Heitwein. Raise it high with friends, or even strangers! Laugh heartily, and relieve all unhappiness! Immerse yourself in the satisfaction of the moment!
ST_Item.MysteriousVisitorClue_4_des: "After the Nursing Department's emergency response team intervened, all escaped test subjects were contained by 02:10."
ST_Item.Furniture_Ornament_005_desc:
"They say if you play this violin at dusk, you might glimpse the future."
The previous owner tried it. It's fake.
Regardless, this is still a finely crafted violin. Despite having only four strings, the melodies that flow from them can captivate any listener's heart.
"The performance may seem plain, but paired with youthful melodies, perhaps you'll see a future full of hope." That's what was written inside this violin's case.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1014_desc:
Jiuyuan's namecard as the acting owner of Sterry Express.
The card was produced by Sterry in a standardized format, with the photo being a fixed element. The moment it's placed in your hands, a transaction has already quietly begun. It's just that most people don't realize what they've actually agreed to until much, much later.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1020_desc:
Haniel's namecard as an Elite Courier of Sterry Express.
The card was produced by Sterry in a standardized format, but Haniel clearly added a little personal touch during the photoshoot. Apparently, when handing over the card, she's supposed to say: "When the cherry blossoms fall like rain, will we meet again?"
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1025_desc:
Hathor's namecard as an Elite Courier of Sterry Express.
This card was produced by Sterry in a standardized format, but the photo on it was not chosen at random. It doesn't promise any guarantees, yet it carries a silent message: at the very least, someone has already thought through your worst possible situations in advance.
ST_Item.item_CharacterUpMaterial_lv1_desc:
"Notes from a Rising Hunter: Your Guide to Promotion!"
—This is a hunter's guide that garnered 999+ Sesame ratings on Bagel. A rookie who had just received their hunter's license tried to put the book into practice, leaving only one comment: Be… ware… of… Anomalies!
ST_Item.RobBankItem_027_desc: The latest phone released by Cubox Technologies features significant improvements over previous models. The side effect of these upgrades is being even more addictive.
ST_Item.BandageClue_2_des: "Since you're handling the patient, you'll represent our department this time, V."
ST_Item.WeaponGacha_Jin_desc: "Time flows like a river, winding ever upward."
ST_Item.SpecialGift_letter_des:
"It's the sunlight streaming through the window into the room, The first breath of air when you open the door. The music drifting from the street corner. Even the rain falling on your hair, the wind passing through your fingers—I want to share it all with you in that very moment."
"This letter is too short, but there's so much I want to say. If this letter could convey even one ten-thousandth of how much I miss you… If when you read this, you happen to hear that music from the street corner too…"
…
Is this too over the top?

ST_Item.WishingItem_01_desc: "Deep roots bring lasting peace to the home."
ST_Item.PortableVision_Anomaly_010_desc: Fluffy is a docile Anomaly creature that resembles a white rabbit in appearance. It survives by feeding on cotton textiles and makes "fluff fluff" sounds, often appearing in groups during sunny afternoons. Blankets "processed" by Fluffy become exceptionally soft and warm, providing deep, restful sleep. Under normal circumstances, Fluffy poses no threat. However, it is extremely sensitive to flames. Once exposed to burning, it triggers a "rage mode" where its originally gentle appearance completely breaks down in fury, replaced by endless anger and iron fists.
ST_Item.SpecialGift_elyms2_des: "A little gift for every good friend. Why not share one with yours, too?"
ST_Item.Prison_Paralyser_usedesc: A paralytic drug specially made by Living Fossil. After injection, it induces a deep coma with a cause that's nearly impossible to determine.
ST_Item.Birthday_cake_des: A full team effort went into this anniversary celebration: Hotori funded it, Taygedo did the shopping, Edgar designed the cake, and Daffodill brought it to life. Sakiri and Nanally handled the decorations, while Adler crafted the sponge, cream, jam, frosting, and even tiny fondant figures of every Eibon member.  The preparations are complete… now all that's left is someone to blow out the candles.
ST_Item.abysspoint_usedesc: Miss Levi spends her days traveling through the Anomalous Realms, so she's bound to drop a few precious feathers along the way. If you can collect these feathers and return them to her, you'll receive a thank-you gift in return. However, when returning them, whatever you do, don't ask whether losing so many feathers affects her plumage… even if you mean well.
ST_Item.DefendTowerCoin_usedesc: A currency used in Coal Lump's Treasure to obtain various items from the Sweetbloom Sweets.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1057_desc:
The namecard of Akane Rin, guitarist for "THE WHOOTS!!!!"
She picked up her father's broken wooden guitar and gently strummed the strings. Amid the harsh, dissonant noise, she found her own melody—and a new path forward. Guitar after guitar, instrument after instrument, her band formed, broke up, and formed again. No matter how much she endured, the girl always looked towards tomorrow, hoping to pursue her dreams and transform into a bright, shining star every time she took the stage.
ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1070_desc:
The namecard of Aurelia, the administrator of the Tamamochi Street.
Everyone on Tamamochi Street knows about her. When newcomers arrive, she usually drags them around to every shop in town before they even have a chance to ask her for her name. No wonder the box full of namecards that she printed when she took the job remains untouched.

ST_Item.PortableVision_Anomaly_041_desc: Cheese looks just like a camera, but when you press the shutter, it instantly freezes all living beings within the shooting range in a state of time suspension. Their bodies cannot move and their consciousness falls silent, as if trapped within a single frozen frame. Cheese is a one-time-use Anomaly that immediately disappears after use. Ordinary people are severely affected by Cheese, with freeze duration lasting up to dozens of hours, and they completely lose their memory afterward, only vaguely recalling a blinding flash. Some Espers are only frozen for a few minutes and can clearly recall all details before the shot, including the identity of the camera holder. Due to its potential uses including assassination, escape, and hostage situations, ordinary people have no access to it, and it currently circulates mainly in underground market bounty trades.

ST_Item.Universal_BusinessCard_1042_desc:
The namecard of Blackbird, proprietor of The Witch's House.
No matter how hard Blackbird tries, the crystal ball—so willing to reveal everything—always falls silent when she asks about her own fate. On each attempt, she stares at the mist swirling inside the ball, lost in thought, imagining where she was born, where she grew up, and where she'll be laid to rest. As her mind wanders, she drifts into a deep slumber, unaware that a peculiar dream is awaiting her: she's a bird with black feathers, soaring over people's heads, with centuries trailing behind her, as though scattering her song across the earth as she flies on endlessly through the many cycles of the world's seasons.
ST_Item.food_019_desc: Uncle Bob's orange-flavored juice. A great source of everyday vitamin C. Each gulp contains fresh orange pulp!
ST_Item.food_043_desc: Uncle Bob's orange-flavored juice. A source of everyday vitamin C. Each gulp contains fresh orange pulp!

ST_Item.Prison_walkman_usedesc: A Portable Player loaded with popular hits and classic oldies. Some inmates might be willing to trade their treasured belongings for one.
ST_Item.Universal_frame_1023_desc: As one leaf withers, another is born.

ST_Item.HospitalJigsawFake_2_desc: A "Jigsaw" piece created by a Mysty. Collecting other piece might unlock a space somewhere…
ST_Item.BussinessExp_desc: A good apple a day brings Fons my way… hmm, that doesn't really roll off the tongue, does it?

ST_Item.item_WeaponBreakMaterial_02_lv2_desc: Unnamed music, like innocent emotions—indescribable but sincere.
ST_Item.ExperimentClue_3_usedesc: A hastily scrawled note tucked into someone's memo.
ST_Item.item_quest_007_desc: An ordinary membership card. The worn edges indicate frequent use, yet its surface remains pristine, showing how much the owner cherishes it.
ST_Item.Furniture_Bed_003_desc: A bed that can relieve fatigue. The light pink bedding brings you a clear dream.
ST_Item.Furniture_Bed_001_desc: A bed that can relieve fatigue. The lilac and amethyst bedding brings you sweet dreams.
ST_Item.Furniture_Bed_002_desc: A bed that can relieve fatigue. The ashen-blue bedding brings you a tranquil dream.
ST_Item.Prison_playboy_desc: In the monotony of unchanging days, everyone craves something new, whether inside or outside the cage. The only difference is that within these walls, a stack of glossy paper printed with the latest news takes on a value far beyond its cover price. Whoever has it holds the power to define the "free world." When everyone else knows nothing of the outside, only you stay informed. It might not help you in any practical way, but it's enough to create the illusion that the world hasn't forgotten you yet.
ST_Item.Scaled_Hacksaw_des: A common hacksaw, handy for woodworking.
ST_Item.RobBankItem_G002_desc: An unremarkable iron-gray key used to open the electrical panel.
ST_Item.Yahaha_Mu_Lamp01_Key_desc: A key that was left behind in a pile of clothes. It might be able to open something.
ST_Item.CabinetKey_desc: One key opens one locker compartment. With the key, you own the compartment.
ST_Item.Pukaland_atmosphere_ticket_01_des: A full day of nonstop wonder! Grants unlimited rides on the Puka Wonder Wheel for 24 hours after purchase.
ST_Item.Pukaland_atmosphere_ticket_02_des: A full day of dreams you never have to wake from. Grants unlimited access to Dreamland Tea Party for 24 hours after purchase.

A collection of cat trivia.
"If cats could dream, what would they dream of? Delicious cat food? Bugs chirping in the grass? Or maybe… me?"

ST_Item.ExperimentClue_6_usedesc: A torn experiment log, possibly once belonging to an assistant nurse at the hospital.
ST_Item.SpecialGift_Book3_des:
A travelogue exploring the customs and daily life of Hethereau. Written in an accessible, humorous style, it has become required reading for elementary and middle school students across the realm.
"Sunward Island"… Twisty, a short-limbed amphibian, likes cookie crumbs…
