ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_08:
"Preface"
The Hexenhammer was written together by Heinrich Kramer, Inquisitor of the Capital Tribunal, and Jacob Sprenger, High Confessor. Having received the King's approval and commendation, it was sent forth through all the kingdom as a guide unto the hunting of the Witch, that the Confessors of every parish and the faithful might learn to know and to judge the Witch.
The Witch was the first among hags to set her name within the Devil's book. She is the foremost of all witches, the Queen of the world below. Every wicked hag doth desire to become a witch, and every one of them fashioneth herself after the Witch. And thus are hag and witch alike the very talons of the Devil, a true and present scourge.
Insatiable desire driveth a soul to conspire with the Devil and so to fall, the soul offered up in exchange for magic. And a woman's soul is weaker still, for women know not how to reason or to judge, and thus doth desire take root in them easily, and they are the more readily worked upon by the Devil. They are the enemy of friendship, an inescapable punishment, a certain evil, a natural temptation, a beckoning calamity, a threat unto the household, a bewitching scourge. To stand against the power of the Devil, ye must all be the more careful in word and deed, holding fast unto virtue and guarding your good name. Any strange word or act, any failing in virtue, may be a sign that the Devil draweth quietly near. Watch thy woman neighbor, watch thy daughter, watch thy wife, watch every soul about thee, for any soul may fall beneath the Devil's hand and become a witch. And whosoever will not believe in the Devil and in the Witch, that one is the greatest heretic of all!
For the protection of the faithful, let all of ye read this book with care, that ye may learn how to tell a witch, how to know a soul fallen into corruption, how to discern heresy and sorcery. And shouldst thou fear that thou thyself art possessed or cursed, thou mayest learn from this book how to break such magic. Inquisitors and Confessors, too, may learn from it the means and the procedures for the judging of witches.
We pray devoutly to the Highest One that the knowledge in this book may spread among all the faithful. To fight against the cunning of the Devil, we will let slip no one who may be a witch! We will let slip no agent of the Devil! We will defend the glory of the Highest One without wavering!
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird01_NPC1065_004: You don't know who Merula is?
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_11:
"See Through the Disguise of the Witch!"
The witch who hath made her pact with the Devil will surely bear upon her body the Devil's mark. The Devil and the witch are cunning, and only by shaving away every hair upon the witch's body and searching inch by inch shall it be found. Oftentimes the Devil's mark disguiseth itself as a mole, a freckle, a birthmark, an insect's bite, or a scar, that the witch may argue her way free. Be ever watchful, and suffer not thyself to be deceived! Suffer it not!
"The Wicked Familiar of the Witch"
That she may the more easily lay her curses upon the faithful, the witch must hide her tracks, and so she loveth to keep a familiar, such as a wolf, a hare, a bird, a toad, a cat, a tortoise, a swine, a hedgehog, a sheep, and the like. Beware any woman who keepeth an animal!
"The Tears of the Witch"
A fallen soul can feel no sorrow, and so the witch cannot weep true tears. But the Devil hath taught them the sorcery of weeping, and so, when they are questioned and put to torture, they oftentimes feign tears by this sorcery. It is the Devil helping them to counterfeit their weeping, that they may cheat thee of thy pity. Take care thou art not deceived by them!
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird01_NPC1050_011: Oracle Stones are born of specific human activities.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_09:
"The Bargain Between Witch and Devil"
The Devil keeps a book bound in the hide of a black bear, its pages carrying a dark red sheen, wherein are set down his every sorcery and his true name. The Devil's servants pledge their souls, and with blood for ink they sign their names in the book, receiving in exchange the magic they have so long craved. Once the bargain is struck, the witches can never turn back, which means their souls can no longer be saved, and death alone can end the curse they bring upon the faithful.
At every full moon, the witches spread flying ointment upon their backs and ride their brooms to the mountaintop to join the Witches' Sabbath. They light black candles to summon the Devil, and the Devil appears in the shape of a black goat. The woods fill with their songs of praise to him and the sounds of their games. In the frenzy they roast the flesh of animals for their feast, and offer infants in sacrifice to the Devil, receiving in exchange great power to curse the souls of the good.
We pray devoutly unto the Highest One that the knowledge within this book may spread among all the faithful. To war against the cunning of the Devil, we will let slip no one who may be a witch! We will let slip no agent of the Devil! We will defend the glory of the Highest One without wavering!
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_14:
"The Trials of the Witch"
For the sake of the Highest One, for the sake of casting out the Devil, and for the sake of preventing calamities and plagues: under the guidance of the Papal Confessor, the King hath decreed the founding of the Holy Tribunal, and hath commanded that a hundred Inquisitors be trained to judge witches.
"The Mission of the Holy Tribunal"
The Inquisitors, once their training is done, will have mastered the greatest store of skills for the discerning of witches, and they will go in circuit through all the kingdom to seek out, so far as they may, every witch that lieth hidden.
At the same time, those witch-hunters approved by a Confessor likewise possess the power to discern witches, and should one hold proof enough, he may put witches to death first and thereafter bring his proof to claim bounty.
Should any village or town find the signs of a witch, or the traces of some other agent of the Devil, yet be unable to know them for certain, they may, under the guidance of their local Confessor, petition the nearest Holy Tribunal for an Inquisitor, and the Tribunal will send forth an Inquisitor with all haste to hold a witch trial in that place.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_12:
"The Bane of the Witch"
The Devil is the enemy of the Highest One. Both water and fire are His holy works, most fit to prove whether a soul hath fallen.
If she be a witch, then when cast into the water, the holy water will refuse to receive her fallen soul and will cast her out, and so the witch will float upon the surface. If the soul be devout enough, it will sink beneath the water. But take care, for the cunning witch may use her sorcery to feign sinking. Yet the holy water will wear her magic away, and so thou must wait a sufficient time at the water's edge before thou canst be certain whether a soul hath fallen. Whatever befalleth, have patience!
If she be a witch, then when she walketh across the iron plate made red by the holy fire, she will surely let forth a wail of anguish. After three days' waiting, the wound will show itself cleansed by the holy fire, and thus may the witch be known for certain.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_13:
"The Evil Deeds of the Witch"
The witch drowneth the bull in the water, and maketh the ox leap more than four feet from the ground. She casteth the long-handled pot into the fire, tippeth the hay out from the wagon, layeth her magic upon the ale, shattereth the pail and setteth the kettle to dancing. She hurleth through the air apples, chairs, ashes, candlesticks, and dung. She looseth forth wicked creatures without bodies: a man's head upon a white cat's tail, the trunk of them empty as air.
The witch can appear in two places at once, and can walk a wet stretch of road yet stay dry from head to foot. Even upon a loose and creaking floor she maketh not a sound. She can reach a place in all haste, divine the contents of an unopened letter, make cheese of an uncommon savor, know secrets not meant to be known, smell the figs within another's pocket, and fall from a rooftop yet take no hurt at all.
One upon whom the witch hath laid her curse may lose all sense, his limbs struck useless, his whole body seized with convulsions, his mouth locked fast. Some too will foam at the mouth, their teeth clenched tight, their bodies wracked with fits that will not cease.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_10:
"The Marks of a Witch"
The soul of a witch hath long since fallen, and so doth she often live an immoral life and stain her own good name. Shouldst thou meet a witch who seemeth devout and modest, it is likely her cunning at work, for she meaneth to deceive thee with a pretended piety and virtue, that she may escape suspicion.
Those witches who have but lately offered up their souls often keep some remnant of morality and conscience, and under questioning they show their fear, they are afraid, they despair, they hang their heads and fall silent, and this alone is proof enough that they have betrayed the Highest One and committed grievous sins.
If they claim to be innocent and stay calm, then plainly it is the Devil's sorcery that protecteth them from betraying themselves, and this is proof enough of their guilt.
As for seasoned witches, they are most skilled of all at lying and deceiving. They pour out wild falsehoods without restraint and argue back with all their strength. These are signs of possession, for the closer they are unto the Devil, the more easily are they possessed, and they must be guilty.
Let no faint trace escape thee. Those witches whose hands and feet are bound love above all to roll their eyes amid the torture, for they are using their gaze to send word unto the Devil. Take care, for by this they may hold out against the punishment a day longer, but so long as thou pressest on with the will of the Highest One, the Devil cannot help them forever.
Should a witch draw her last breath before confessing, fear not. Call at once for the aid of a Confessor, and hold the rite of exorcism, for that death was brought by the Devil. The witch wished to confess her sins unto the Highest One, but the Devil would not suffer her to speak more of the names and secrets. The executioner who feareth death will fall into corruption at this moment. Thou must keep thy courage and thy steadfast faith, trusting that the Highest One will protect thee, guarding thy soul with thy will and standing against the Devil with thy devotion.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird01_NPC13303_009: A doll that listens to stories… Isn't that a sign of the Witch's possession? Would you rather the Inquisitor turn our house upside down? I'm a constable now, I must set an example!
ST_Main_BlackBird.q110947_SumUp:
The Inquisitor told the townspeople that the Witch had finally descended upon St. Arbor. Billy volunteered to serve as the town's sheriff, and several other townspeople joined him. The magistrate called on the townspeople to return home and find anything that made them uneasy, to then burn it before the Sacred Tree the next day to test whether the witch's soul was attached to it.
After the crowd dispersed, you and Blackbird discussed what had occurred, but an ominous feeling lingered in you both. You vowed to learn as much as possible about the town and search for any Anomalies that might be lurking within it.

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_52:
Dear Diary:
Father is always criticizing Mr. Billy for not being virtuous enough, saying I should marry the manor's butler or one of the male servants. But he has no idea how hypocritical that sounds to me!
He thinks I don't know about that letter he hid in the table drawer! He used to have a lover at the manor, and I have an older half-brother from that affair!
I hate him, but I can't take revenge on him. Mother is in poor health and couldn't withstand such a shock!
Mr. Billy's household is looking for a maid. Maybe I could go there. Given my status, he wouldn't treat me too badly—he'd only give me easy work. Besides, he's handsome, charming, and good with money. He's infatuated with Annie right now, but that's only temporary, just like my father. If we got married, I'd never let him become the kind of man my father is!
Most importantly, I wouldn't have to keep facing my father and mother. Once I've figured out what to do, I can come back. They wouldn't really have the heart to hit me! It's decided, then. I'll take Father's hidden stash of silver coins and leave at first light tomorrow. Maybe I should go into the city first. I've never been there, so I'll take a look and come back! Especially since I've heard they hang people there every day. It must be exciting!
Once I take the silver coins, will he realize that I've read the letter? Perhaps that's for the best. He certainly wouldn't dare criticize me in front of Mother. Maybe he'd even treat her a little better!
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_41:
Dear Victor,
It's been long since we met, and I trust you fare well in our old home. I sought to have the Viscount Leon give Derrick a place, yet by no means would he agree to it. I asked of Lester, who serves still in the Manor, and it seems the good Lord Leon is hard pressed enough in his own affairs. Though the family keep up the airs of the nobility for all to see, they have been much diminished since the year of the plague.
And no wonder, for so many died in that time, and with the war besides, much of the land lies fallow, and the rents he gathers each year are fallen near by half.
I hear your life is now most prosperous, and I do rejoice for you with all my heart. Should you be able to find Derrick some work, that would be better still. If you are willing, I would have him come and see you. Some things, perhaps, are best said by one who is himself a father. I ask only that the boy might take heart and live rightly, and give himself no more to the gaming table and the cup.
Love,
Luna Cobblepot
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_07:
Dear Riley,
You were right to depart, I fear. The times grow less peaceful with each passing day. It is not the patrol constables alone. While I was out with the cattle, I beheld soldiers of the neighboring kingdom at the very edge of the moor. By the mercy of the Highest One, I am swift of foot, and they did not spy me. The tidings of the King's defeat are like enough to be true, and none can say whether they will press into Casco. The floods come ever more often, and I doubt not our neighbors suffer likewise, I am half afraid they will fall upon the village and take our grain.
How do you fare in your town to the south? Is it warmer there? Does the land more readily bear wheat? I have already begun to sell off what I own, and may come to cast my lot with you before long. If your own days are hard, I pray you do not fear to tell me the truth, for I can seek elsewhere. Should I find a better place to settle, I will send word. Either way, I am bound further south, to seek out warmer and richer land.
I have enclosed with this letter my latest divination. Perhaps it may…

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_49:
Once, there was a king. He ruled over a vast and fertile land.
There were golden wheat fields, hills lush with green, and rivers that never froze. Spring came early, and autumn always arrived late. People said it was due to the Highest One's continued vigilance over the land.
When the king was young, he was brave and victorious in battle. He led his armies to win one war after another. His lands spread farther, his castles grew taller, and more and more people bowed before him.
And so, the king gradually came to believe that all of this had been achieved through his own strength.
In time, he no longer looked upwards. He forgot who made the seeds sprout, the rivers thaw, and the livestock survive the winter in peace.
The Highest One therefore withdrew Its gaze.
And the Devil, who had been hiding among the shadows all the while, finally reached out its hand.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110924_SumUp:
You and Blackbird found yourselves in another layer of an Anomalous Realm, where you also unexpectedly encountered Valmona. However, the girl surprisingly didn't recognize either of you. She introduced herself as Annie, a herbalist from St. Arbor.
The girl, Annie, noticed that Blackbird was injured. Only after she mentioned it did you and Blackbird realize that a wound had somehow appeared on Blackbird's leg. Seeing that you had nowhere to go, Annie decided to take you both to her home to bandage Blackbird's injury.
ST_Main_BlackBird.q110934_SumUp: You and Blackbird arrived near the Sacred Tree, but noticed nothing out of the ordinary. You suggested that Blackbird try using her divination powers to determine how to nullify the Inquisitor.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110951_SumUp:
You and Blackbird returned to Annie's house and found Billy and Betty urging Annie to burn her herbs. Annie refused, but after a heated argument, they forcibly took them from her.
Back in the room with Blackbird, you reflected on the day's events and concluded that you were witnessing the birth of the Anomaly known as the "Inquisitor." The only mystery left was the identity of the golden-haired girl. Blackbird decided to perform another divination.
ST_Main_BlackBird.q110906_SumUp: You and Blackbird met at the agreed-upon port, ready to set out.
ST_Main_BlackBird.HM_01_SumUp: You formed a contract with Blackbird.
ST_Main_BlackBird.q110933_SumUp:
You and Blackbird were then brought to Annie's house. Annie bandaged the wound on Blackbird's leg and warned Blackbird not to tell anyone about her ability to perform divination, to avoid causing trouble. You cautiously asked Annie whether she knew anything about Valmona, but learned nothing.
After Annie left, you and Blackbird discussed the situation and decided to investigate the town's Sacred Tree.
ST_Main_BlackBird.HM_02a_SumUp:
You arrive at the fire trial site with Blackbird and she seems to remember something. The memory comes with great pain which you share immediately. 
You are shocked to find Fadia being executed right at the center of the billowing flames. Then the anomaly known as the "Inquisitor" appears and Skia arrives at the same time. You fight the Inquisitor alongside the ETD squad.
ST_Main_BlackBird.q110940_SumUp: You and Blackbird pass by the bakery, where you run into Annie and some of the other townsfolk. You ask around about Betty, and Annie tells you she might be at the mill with Billy.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110960_SumUp: Later, you and Blackbird came across Levis and his group discussing how to rescue Mary. You both joined the conversation and agreed to help with the rescue.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110967_SumUp:
When you both returned to Annie's house, Annie told you that Pickett and the others had been burned to death, leaving behind only a few odd stones that glowed with an ominous blood-red light.
After calming Annie, who was terrified, you and Blackbird realized that perhaps, no matter what the two of you did, the fate of the people here had been decided long ago. Blackbird refused to believe it, instead insisting on performing another divination.
ST_Main_BlackBird.q110969_SumUp: When the two of you returned to Annie's house, you both discovered that Billy had suddenly threatened to accuse Annie of witchcraft. Annie resolved to accuse Billy in turn and even considered using the townspeople's secrets to win more support. Blackbird wanted to help, so Annie asked her to persuade some of the townspeople. You were worried about Blackbird, but it seemed she hadn't forgotten who she was just yet. Blackbird believed she should do what Merula had done to find a way to break the Anomalous Realm and nullify the Inquisitor.

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_51:
The king knelt in the empty church, begging the Highest One to look upon his land once more.
But the Highest One told him, "I never left. It was you who gradually forgot where to go during the endless winter."
The king asked, "Then how can we drive out the Devil?"
The Highest One replied, "First, let the light return to your hearts."
So the king ordered the bells to ring once more. The people returned to the church, prayed again, and helped those who had lost their provisions and homes.
They no longer trusted the whispers in the darkness, nor followed those who promised them shortcuts. At last, they understood:
The Devil loves the cold above all. But, more frightening than the cold, is a heart that has grown accustomed to it.
So, child… be devout and faithful.
Do not be deceived by the voices in the darkness and do not believe those who would teach you to abandon your faith. So long as people still believe in the light and steadfastly walk toward it—
even an endless winter will one day come to an end.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110973_SumUp:
Annie was tormented by her failure to end the trials, so she decided to step forward tomorrow, admit that she was a witch, and put an end to everything. Blackbird offered to stand trial in Annie's place, and you realized that, at some point, Blackbird had come to completely see herself as Merula.
As you tried to bring Blackbird back to her senses, Annie suddenly spoke. Only then did you realize that Annie was, in fact, the real Merula. She had sent a letter to Blackbird and impersonated both "Valmona" and "Annie" in order to lure Blackbird and help her keep the Inquisitor imprisoned in this Anomalous Realm.
You gradually came to piece everything together. You told Merula that Hethereau no longer had the conditions for an Inquisitor Anomaly to survive. All she needed to do now was break the Anomalous Realm, carry out the Nullification of the Inquisitor, and set her own soul free.

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_40:
In the 262nd year after the town was founded, during the spring plowing, purchased Shweishate's oak woods and ten fields for Luna's son Derrick, eighteen silver coins. The postage and clerical fee was five copper coins. Additionally, they advanced eighteen silver coins from the Fran family's estate, to be repaid after the autumn harvest.
In the 264th year after the town was founded, during the thaw, they sold the birch woods north of the valley to Billy for twenty-two silver coins. The payment was received, and the deed was amended.
In the 265th year after the town was founded, before New Year's, they sold Billy the twenty fields beside the old well that Martha had brought into the family, for fifteen silver coins. The payment was received, and the deed was amended.
In the 265th year after the town was founded, before New Year's, purchased half a set of silver tableware with the names filed off from Dot for ten silver coins;
In the 266th year after the town was founded, after New Year's, returned the Fran family's estate to Annie, totaling eighty-five silver coins and half a set of silver tableware; all accounts settled.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_45:
Year 264 since the founding, at the time of the thaw.
Victor Parris, of his own will, sold the birch wood on the north side of his valley to Billy Putnam.
It was agreed between the parties that the price of the birch wood was twenty-two silver coins, to be paid in full by Billy Putnam in a single payment.
The bounds of the woodland are as follows:
from the hilltop on the north, running south to the edge of the meadow, ending ten paces from the river. All birch trees within these bounds, and the land on which they stand, shall belong to Billy Putnam from the day the silver is delivered.
Thereafter, Victor Parris and his family shall make no claim to this land by old bounds, old covenant, or any other cause.
Both parties confirmed this in each other's presence, and set down this deed as witness.
Seller: Victor Parris
Buyer: Billy Putnam
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_46:
Year 265 after the founding, before the New Year.
Victor Parris sold to Billy Putnam twenty strips of field, lying next to one another beside the old well.
It was agreed between the parties that the fields were priced at fifteen silver coins, to be paid in full by Billy Putnam in a single payment. From the day the silver is delivered, the twenty strips of field, the crops upon them, and the right to till them in the coming year shall all belong to Billy Putnam.
Victor Parris warrants that this land has not been mortgaged, pawned, or otherwise sold to another.
Both parties confirmed the same, and set down this deed as witness.
Seller: Victor Parris
Buyer: Billy Putnam
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_47:
Year 266 after the founding, on Michaelmas.
Giles Warren sold three of his own goats to Billy Putnam.
It was agreed between the parties that the three goats were priced together at three silver coins, to be paid in full by Billy Putnam in a single payment. The goats shall belong to Billy Putnam once the silver is delivered.
Giles Warren confirms that they have not been mortgaged or promised to another.
Set down as witness.
Seller: Giles Warren
Buyer: Billy Putnam

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_03:
On the second day after the new moon, Dorothy Osborne was accused of consorting with the Devil. I shaved every hair from her body and finally found three moles atop her head—three marks of sin, the Devil's own marks! She refused to confess, as was common with many servants of the Devil. Alas, that did not trouble me. I knew exactly how to make them bow their heads and confess!
After five consecutive days without sleep, she was too weak to keep up her denials. At last, her lies were exposed. She confessed to signing the Devil's black book in blood. She was a witch! She confessed that she had come to Casco to guide the enemy, allowing heretics to set foot upon this wasteland. She kept the frozen earth from thawing, unleashed pestilence, and left the Cascans starving. She used divination magic to twist the people's faith and lure them into depravity. She was a witch!

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_26:
Cause of Action: Clyde Williams was drowned in the doing of his lord's service, and his family seeketh confirmation of the land and standing they are to hold thereafter.
When the flood came, Clyde Williams, to safeguard the flock of his lord, Viscount Leon, drove the sheep across the river in the rain, and losing his footing unawares, fell into the river and was drowned.
His wife, Bonnie Williams, and his son, John Williams, were thus bereft of the head of their house. The Manor findeth that Clyde died in the doing of his lord's service, and that no other was at fault therein.
Verdict:
Viscount Leon commandeth that a parcel of land be bestowed upon the Williams family, as a solace and recompense. From this time forth, the Williams family are released from their bondage as serfs, and shall no longer bear the personal labor service formerly annexed unto the land.
This matter is entered into the Manor's land book and the roll of households.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_31:
Cause of Action: After the death of Rand Putnam, Billy and Faithful fell into dispute over the inheritance and the ownership of certain timber.
In high summer, Rand Putnam drowned in the flood. After the first frost, the Putnam family took count of the fields and other goods he had left behind.
Billy Putnam and Faithful Putnam fell to blows over the dividing of the inheritance. Faithful saith that Billy had secretly felled a stand of timber that ought to have come to him; Billy saith that the ownership of that wood had never been clearly parted in the first place.
Verdict:
Upon the urging of Confessor George and of their mother, Odette Putnam, the two brothers agreed to cease their quarrel. The parties took count of the inheritance anew, and for the time being divided their several portions according to the Manor's land book and the records of family estate.
The matter of the affray is pursued no further, and this case is closed by accord.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_29:
Cause of Action: Carter Ernst broke into the lord's dwelling to steal, and in his flight brought about the death of a manservant.
In high summer, whilst Viscount Leon was gone abroad with his household, Carter Ernst stole into the lord's dwelling and took away sundry jewels. Being spied in the act by a manservant of the house, Carter, to make his escape, fell to struggling with him, and brought about the manservant's death.
The Manor Court took Carter Ernst into custody, and delivered the case unto the Constable for hearing.
Verdict:
Upon hearing had, Carter Ernst was found guilty of theft and of manslaughter. The Constable, according to the law, sentenced Carter Ernst to be hanged.
The Manor Court entereth the outcome of this case into the roll of criminal causes.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_38:
Cause of Action: Giles Warren oweth a drink-debt unpaid, and the tavern seeketh to have the Manor recover it.
Giles Warren had long taken drink upon credit at the tavern, and having run up a debt, failed many times over to repay it. The keeper of the tavern thereupon prayed the Manor Court to recover the same.
Upon examination, it was found that Giles did indeed have a debt unpaid, and that he was unable to pay it out of hand.
Verdict:
The Manor commandeth Giles Warren to clear the debt within a set term. Forasmuch as he was unable to repay in ready silver, it is granted that he sell off some part of his cattle, and with the money so gotten make satisfaction of the debt.
The debt being cleared, Giles is set free.
The Manor Court giveth him warning that hereafter he shall not take drink upon credit against goods he is unable to pay.
The case is closed.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_23:
Cause of Action: A dispute between Will Parris and Cannon Putnam over the ownership of twenty strips of field.
At the winter solstice, Will Parris brought suit before the Manor Court against Cannon Putnam, that he had refused to return twenty strips of field. The two had beforehand entered into a covenant of mortgage upon a loan, wherein Will, putting up the twenty strips of field as pledge, borrowed silver coin of Cannon, and it was agreed that upon the clearing of the debt he should take back the land.
When the term was come, Will, though he was two days late in clearing the debt, did nonetheless demand the return of the pledged land. Cannon refused to return it, alleging that Will had broken the covenant.
Verdict:
Upon the hearing before Viscount Leon, the Manor findeth that Will Parris hath discharged the principal, and that the twenty strips of field remain in the holding of the Parris family. Yet because Will was late in his repayment, the Parris family must pay over unto the Putnam family one month's interest besides.
Hereafter neither party shall sue the other again for these twenty strips of field.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_39:
Cause of Action: Annie Fran, being come of age, prayeth to take back the inheritance kept in trust by Confessor George and Magistrate Victor.
After the New Year, Annie Fran came of age, and according to her parents' will sought to have the Manor Court restore the inheritance the goodman Fran and his wife left behind. Confessor George and Magistrate Victor rendered up the account books of the several years, for the Manor to examine.
Verdict:
Upon examination, the Manor confirmeth that Annie is now fit to inherit and to manage the family's goods in her own right.
Confessor George and Magistrate Victor must render back to Annie Fran the inheritance the goodman Fran and his wife had left, together with the account books thereto belonging. In token of her thanks, Annie promiseth to furnish herbs to Magistrate Victor's household free of charge for the next three years.
From this time forth, the goods of the Fran family are Annie's own to inherit and to manage. The case is closed.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_28:
Cause of Action: The widow Martha Garcia, having been remarried to Victor Parris, seeketh that the ownership of the land and goods held in her name be entered on record.
After the first rains of spring, the widow Martha Garcia was married to Victor Parris, and took the name Martha Parris. The land, cattle, and other goods held in her name before the marriage must all be entered anew by the Manor.
Verdict:
The Manor confirmeth the land and goods that Martha did lawfully inherit and hold before her marriage, and granteth that they be merged, after the marriage, into the name of the Parris family. The several fields, woods, cattle, and other goods shall also be entered into the book of family estate by the Manor clerk.
Hereafter, unless there be other testament or lawful disposition, this portion of goods shall be managed under the name of the Parris family.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_24:
Cause of Action: An affray between the Putnam family and the Parris family, arising from a quarrel at a betrothal feast.
At the New Year, Rand Putnam and Raven Parris were to be betrothed. At the feast held in the Putnam house, the elders of both families, by reason of an old dispute over land and the grudges laid up therefrom, fell once more to quarreling, and thereafter to blows.
Cannon Putnam saith that Will Parris did wound him in the fray, and did damage the tables and chairs of the house, and thereupon prayed the judgment of the Manor.
Verdict:
Upon examination, it is found that both parties were at fault. The betrothal of Rand Putnam and Raven Parris is therefore broken off. The Parris family must make recompense unto the Putnam family for the mending of the tables and chairs, and must bear besides the charges paid by Cannon Putnam for going to Fran's apothecary on account of the injury.
Hereafter neither party shall, by occasion of this affray, stir up again the old dispute over land.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_33:
Cause of Action: After the goodman Will Fran and his wife died of the plague, the guardianship of the inheritance and the disposal of the goods of their only daughter, Annie Fran.
When the sunflowers were in bloom, Rebecca Fran and her husband, Will Fran, died one after the other of the plague then in the town. After the death of the two, there remained only their daughter, Annie Fran.
Forasmuch as Annie was not yet come of age, and was unable of herself to inherit and to manage the land, cattle, and other goods of the Frans, according to the testament that the goodman Fran and his wife had left in their lifetime, the inheritance of the Frans shall, until Annie be come of age, be kept in the joint charge of Confessor George and Magistrate Victor.
It was further willed that the land held by the Frans, together with three head of cattle, be all sold unto Magistrate Victor, at the price of eighty silver coins, with half a set of silver tableware given besides as part of the bargain.
The rest of the estate and goods belonging to the Frans shall yet be kept in trust by Confessor George and Magistrate Victor. The two may not of their own accord sell off the chief estate of the Frans, and whatsoever gains arise therefrom in that time must be entered item by item into the account book, and, when Annie be come of age, rendered back to her in full.
And further, according to the will, Annie Fran shall hold, for the term of her life, the use of the apothecary that standeth in Magistrate Victor's name, together with its yard and its house.
Verdict:
The Manor Court confirmeth the will of the goodman Fran and his wife to be valid.
Confessor George and Magistrate Victor shall together serve as the guardians of the inheritance and the keepers of the goods of Annie Fran, and shall dispose of the land, cattle, and other goods of the Frans according to the testament.
The land of the Frans and three head of cattle shall belong to Magistrate Victor, at the price of eighty silver coins and half a set of silver tableware. This dealing in goods must be entered into the Manor's account book.
The rest of the inheritance, and whatsoever gains arise during the time of their trust, must be kept safe by Confessor George and Magistrate Victor and entered item by item. When Annie be come of age, the goods and gains that ought to be hers shall be rendered back to her together, according to the testament and to what is written in the account book.
The use that Annie Fran holdeth for the term of her life in the apothecary that standeth in Magistrate Victor's name, together with its yard and its house, is likewise entered and confirmed by the Manor Court.
This case is entered into the roll of inheritance and the land book.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_37:
Cause of Action: A maidservant in the house of Billy Putnam was killed by mishap whilst carrying firewood, and her kin seek recompense.
In deep winter, a maidservant in the house of Billy Putnam was set to carry firewood for winter. As she bore it along, the woodpile stacked in the yard toppled and struck her down, and the maidservant died upon the spot.
The kin of the dead came before the Manor Court and set forth that the maidservant was yet young in years, and that having long borne the drudgery of the house, she had come by a hurt to her back some while since. That same night she had moreover been punished for overturning a basin of water, and was bidden to go without her supper.
The kin say that Billy Putnam and the steward of the house, knowing well that the maidservant was hurt in body, and knowing too that she had not eaten that day, did nonetheless bid her carry the heavy wood alone, and set no other servant to help her. Therefore the kin of the dead seek that Billy Putnam make recompense.
The Manor Court sent men to view the place, and confirmed that the woodpile did indeed lean awry, and had toppled in the course of the carrying. Billy Putnam owned that the woodpile had been stacked by his own servants, but said that the punishment the maidservant had suffered that day bore no direct part in her death.
As for the maidservant's heavy daily labor, her back injury, and the punishment she suffered that night, the Court holdeth these to be the common lot of servants, not enough to lay blame upon the master. Therefore the Manor giveth judgment only touching the death caused by the toppling woodpile, and the responsibility Billy Putnam ought to bear therein.
Verdict:
Upon agreement between the parties, Billy Putnam is willing to pay the kin of the dead eight silver coins. The kin accept, and promise that hereafter they will not call Billy Putnam or his servants to answer again for the maidservant's death.
The Manor Court confirmeth the accord.
The case is closed.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_36:
Cause of Action: The tavern of the Walls, being suspected of receiving and selling stolen goods for thieves, was shut down by the Constable.
In high summer, the Constable received report that the tavern might be keeping and selling stolen goods on behalf of thieves passing through.
The Constable entered the tavern to search, and seized sundry goods of unknown origin. The tavern was thereupon shut down for a time, and Dot Wall, together with those who had charge of the keeping of the tavern, were brought to questioning.
Verdict:
By autumn harvest, he inquiry was ended. The Constable could not prove that the Walls knew the goods to have come from thieves and had willingly helped to sell them off, nor was any proof found that the Walls partook in the theft.
Therefore the Constable granted that the seal be lifted, and the tavern of the Walls returned to its trade.
The Manor Court set down the outcome of the inquiry, and this case is closed.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_35:
Cause of Action: Pickett Corey and Billy Putnam fell into dispute over the bounds of a plot of open ground by the river.
After the coming of spring, Pickett Corey fenced in a plot of open land by the river, and began to break the soil and sow wheat. Billy Putnam saith that the place belonged of old to land the Putnams once used, and that the bounds between the two had never been laid down anew.
Billy demanded that Pickett take down the fence and render back the land. Pickett saith that the place had lain untilled for many years, and that since taking on the lease of the mill he had kept charge of the riverbank thereabouts, and therefore had right to use it.
Verdict:
The Manor commandeth both parties for the time to cease from enlarging their tillage, and that neither destroy the boundary-marks and fences the other hath set up. The clerk must call up the old land book and the records of bounds, and, if need be, measure the ground anew.
Until the measuring be done, this case is left without final verdict for the time being.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_32:
Cause of Action: Pickett Corey seeketh to take on the lease of the mill belonging to the lord.
In spring, upon the surety of Magistrate Victor, Pickett Corey made suit unto Viscount Leon to take over the mill of the town. Upon inspection, the Manor confirmed that Pickett had aforetime mended the old water-wheel and had held the affairs of the mill for a season in another's stead, and that in that time there had been no great fault.
Verdict:
Viscount Leon granteth unto Pickett Corey the lease of the mill. It is agreed between them that Pickett must render up unto the lord four parts in ten of the mill's yearly income, and the rest he shall dispose of as he will.
Should there be any default in the rents and dues, any concealment of income, or any neglect of the needful repairs, the lord shall have right to take back the mill.
This covenant is entered into the Manor's account book, and taketh effect from this year forth.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_30:
Cause of Action: John Williams, putting up his right to use the meadow as pledge, borroweth of Billy Putnam.
John Williams saith that the land he worketh hath yielded poorly year upon year, so that he is unable of himself to maintain the living of his house, and therefore borroweth twenty silver coins of Billy Putnam. It is agreed between them that John Williams putteth up the south slope meadow he holdeth on lease as pledge, and shall repay the loan and the interest thereon out of the gains of his grazing.
Billy Putnam prayeth the Manor to confirm this covenant, that no dispute may arise hereafter.
Verdict:
The Manor granteth that this pledge be entered on record. Until the debt be discharged, John Williams may yet continue to use the meadow for grazing, but may not of his own will sublet, sell, or pledge it anew.
Should he fail to repay according to the covenant, Billy Putnam may, according to the judgment of the Manor Court, seek to dispose of the said right of use.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_27:
Cause of Action: John Williams seeketh the use of the hillside meadow south of the town for the term of his life.
John Williams made suit unto the lord to rent the hillside meadow south of the town, and prayed that the term be set for his lifetime. Upon inspection by the Manor steward, it was found that the meadow belongeth to the lord, and that in recent years none had held it on any long lease.
Verdict:
Viscount Leon granteth unto John Williams the use of the said meadow for the term of his life. John must render the rents and dues according to the covenant, and may not of his own will sublet, sell, or otherwise deliver the meadow unto another.
This right of use is entered into the Manor's land book.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_25:
Cause of Action: Victor Parris accuseth Cannon Putnam of the killing of his father, Will Parris.
After Michaelmas, Will Parris was drowned. Victor Parris, suspecting that his father's death was linked to Cannon Putnam, brought his accusation before the Manor Court.
Forasmuch as the matter touched a man's life, the Manor Court first took Cannon Putnam into custody, and delivered the case unto the Constable for further hearing.
Verdict:
Upon examination, no sure proof was found that Cannon Putnam had murdered Will Parris, and Cannon was set free.
The Manor Court pursueth the charge of killing no further, yet hath entered this case and the course of its hearing into the record, that it may be examined in days to come.
ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_34:
Cause of Action: Louis Wall accuseth Pickett Corey of hoarding flour in secret at the mill.
After the autumn harvest, Louis Wall, suspecting that flour was being hoarded in secret at the mill, brought accusation before the Manor Court against Pickett Corey, the keeper of the mill. Pickett denied the hoarding, saying that all the grain within the mill was set down in the accounts, and that some part of the loss was owing to the breaking of the water-wheel and the millstone.
Verdict:
Confessor George looked into the accounts of both parties, and questioned the mill workers and the farming folk who brought their grain, yet could find no sure proof that Pickett had hoarded flour in secret.
Upon the mediation of Confessor George, Louis withdrew his accusation, and Pickett declared that he would pursue the matter no further.
The two were reconciled before the Manor Court. This case is closed.

ST_Main_BlackBird.Blackbird_Bookcontent_50:
In the first year, winter came earlier than usual.
In the second year, spring was late.
The rivers froze, the pasture withered, and the wheat was beaten to the ground by frost and snow before it had ripened. The people began to starve.
They slaughtered their livestock, ate their stored grain, and then began eating the seeds meant to be saved for the following year.
But winter did not end.
The ice and snow grew thicker each year, while summer grew shorter. Some villages lost their roads beneath the blizzards. Some children died from cold and hunger before they even reached adulthood.
The people were terrified. They said the Devil had finally come.
The Devil hid in the long nights, in the hunger, and in people's hearts. It made them forget how to pray, doubt the Highest One, and lose faith in one another.
And so, the Devil's followers gradually grew in number. They mingled among the people, saying that winter would never end. They said the Highest One had abandoned them all. They also said that if people bowed their heads to the Devil, they could trade their submission for food, warmth, and a chance to survive.
At last, during yet another endless winter, the king lowered his proud head.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110968_SumUp:
The third trial arrived, and you and Blackbird realized that nothing had changed. Mary accused Lizzie of being a witch, while Abigail led the girls in turning against Lizzie, claiming that she had seen an evil spirit. Lizzie desperately pleaded her case, but the Inquisitor turned a deaf ear, sentencing her to burn at the stake.
Another oracle stone fell to the ground following the burning, and the Inquisitor announced that yet another witch was hiding among the crowd. You sensed that the Witch-Hunt Anomaly was about to manifest. Blackbird could no longer stand by and, at last, decided to end the farce once and for all.

ST_Main_BlackBird.q110952_SumUp:
The next day, the test in the Sacred Tree's fire revealed nothing. Billy pointed out that Mary had secretly hidden a talking doll, and Abigail backed him up. Mary's doll was eventually burned, but the witch's soul remained nowhere to be found. The Inquisitor nevertheless decided that Mary had been bewitched by the witch and ordered her to be imprisoned.
Everyone believed that the witch's soul could possess animals associated with demons. After some discussion, they decided to have Tommy, the black cat from Annie's house, undergo the test in the Sacred Tree's fire. Blackbird stepped forward to defend Annie, declaring that if they took the black cat, she'd take Billy's sheep too. While this was happening, you couldn't help but notice a change in Blackbird's demeanor.

Dear Blackbird,
Many souls here need your help. In all the world, you alone can save them. You must help them! The matter is tangled and grievous, more than I can say within a letter, but you need only come and look once to see how dire it is. I beg you, for the sake of all these many souls who wait upon you eagerly, take pity and help me! If you cannot come, I truly know not what I am to do next! I beg you, help me! Help me! I beg you, help!
Yours, Merula

ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_mainreview_001:
Edgar told you an urban legend about the "Invalid Number". Four years ago, many people dreamed that an old friend they'd lost touch with gave them an unreachable number. Every dream featured the same number, digit for digit. Curious, you dialed it too, but the call didn't go through. After falling asleep, you dreamed of an unfamiliar room. A phone on the floor rang, and when you answered it, Nitsa from ETD was on the line.
When you woke, you went to the Bureau to ask Nitsa about the call. She told you that ETD-6's captain and lieutenant had apparently left nearly two months earlier to handle a confidential case and had since gone missing. The only lead was the mysterious space you'd entered in your dream, where you'd found the lieutenant's phone. Worried about her friends' safety, you and Nitsa dialed the "Invalid Number" together—but only you entered the Anomalous Realm again.
There, you met Exe, ETD-6's captain. He explained that the high-level Meme Anomaly "Imaginary Old Friend" had evolved from the "Invalid Number" and was born from humanity's collective imagining of an ideal friend. It draws on the memories people share with old friends they hope to reconnect with, then creates "friends" tailored to their needs. These creations return to their users, gradually eroding and overwriting the place of their real friends in their memories.
Exe was hacking into Archive Units one by one to examine the fabricated "friends" and search for the Anomaly's core. You split up to explore and try to meet up with the lieutenant. In one Archive Unit, you found the lieutenant from Nitsa's photo: "Roxanne." Exe suddenly appeared and shot and killed her. Your consciousness then faded as if your connection had been severed.
When you woke again, you found yourself in a sunny meadow beneath a bright blue sky. There you met a peculiar girl who said her default name was "Elyms." By reverse-engineering the space, you realized it was a special Archive Unit belonging to Exe. Elyms was a counterpart of the "Imaginary Old Friend" and ETD-6's lieutenant. She explained her Anomaly abilities and how she had joined the Bureau as a person in her own right. Then you learned the shocking truth: this operation was Exe's reckless, single-minded plan to erase his own partner, Elyms.
Elyms told you a hazy, fairy-tale-like story whose truth could never be objectively verified: the story of "X," a brilliant but ill-tempered boy, and "Y," a mischievous, lonely computer spirit… from their innocent, carefree beginnings to their cruel, twisted end.
Exe refused to accept the "Invalid Number." He would rather keep reopening his own wounds and endure the pain as if it were new each day than lose the only proof that the "real Y" had existed: every memory in his mind, every vivid trace of his most precious treasure. He had cast himself as an antivirus program whose goal was to erase the "Imaginary Old Friend." After hearing all this, you began to understand why Elyms had brought you there. Torn by conflicting feelings, you decided to play a game, become Elyms's friend, and return to the Anomalous Realm.
At the end of that long journey, Exe compiled data on 316,650 friend-images, transferred it to a single storage medium, and released it all at once. With his complete understanding of the "Imaginary Old Friend," he gave the formless Meme Anomaly a "true form"—by hacking into his own brain and blasting it out. He trusted without a doubt that the Anomalous Realm's restoration mechanism would bring him back after death, just as the Anomaly believed that the version of itself known to this human was its own "true form."
…And so, he carried out this extraordinary crime.
You reached Exe just as he managed to erase the "Imaginary Old Friend," only to find him sinking into an even deeper void. You couldn't sway this clear-headed, frighteningly single-minded man who no longer cared about anything—unless there was still something in the world he had to care about, some "target." To fulfill Nitsa's request, preserve the new connections the "Imaginary Old Friend" had created, and stop Exe from destroying himself, you fought him to buy Elyms time. Though he should have been nearing his physical and mental limits, Exe showed no sign of stopping. He wrecked the arena, trapping you and leaving you behind.
Elyms raced through the shattered Anomalous Realm, making call after call to restore the genuine connections that had been severed between people and their "false friends," rebuilding her own code as she went. After sending you back to safety, she chose to face the pursuing Exe as the one "friend who would stand against him"—
"We're fighting with the very meaning of our existence on the line… and yet, doesn't it remind you of long ago, when we could forget the world and play together like the best of friends, carefree and thinking it would last forever?"
Days later, a return call brought news: both ETD-6's captain and lieutenant had made it back to Hethereau alive. After all that, it seemed Elyms had just barely won this round.
The latest showdown between "Boy X" and "Imaginary Y" was over for now, and its record was sealed in the "Imaginary Old Friend's" secret hideout. They had to face the future without answers and grow up even if they hated to leave. The two "ever-unchanging, elf-like children" couldn't stay in their vacation dreamland forever. For now, at least, it was time to switch back to "adult" mode… Pull yourself together, take responsibility, and get back to work.
—Until "tomorrow," when they meet again as enemies.

ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_084: Then I found these numbers: 316651… Though I'm not sure if they have another meaning.
ST_Main_Exe01.HM_U01C09_002_Sumup: Had he picked up the phone and accepted the "Imaginary Old Friend," this blood-soaked, brutal ending might have been covered and healed by a tender "reunion." Instead, Exe's answer was to rip the phone line in two. He kept the beautiful memories he cherished most alongside his crushing remorse. Only through enduring pain and self-hatred could he ensure that his "Y" would never disappear.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111029_01_Sumup: After answering the call, you found that you were the only one transported to the same place you'd been the night before. This, then, really was an Anomalous Realm. The lieutenant's phone was still lying there. You picked it up and began to explore the area.

ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC031_014: I was nervous last night, so I hung up. I thought I had the wrong number…

ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC030_011: Maybe something happened, maybe Y was hiding… But if Y didn't say anything about it, then whatever! What mattered was that they had fun together!
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC031_009: I see. Per the ETD office security code, I cannot yet open the door. May I ask you to state your business?
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_056: Is that so? I don't know her though. Does she even know me…?
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_118: Am I? I'm just replaying previous recordings…
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_059: Right, because the definitions carried by the earlier images lacked this one identity.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_045: Of course! Because it's also a true story… at least it is true beyond a doubt to the one who lived it.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_217: Yeah… what a fresh take, that a friend can be an enemy… everything just clicked.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC012_030: Right. The usual containment procedures or nullification methods don't work on meme anomalies, so people just saw it as some weird, unsolvable incident, and accepted it as is.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_018: This is a safe space. It's so safe, you can even stay here forever!
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_125: …it comes with what every anomaly carries: encroachment…
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC012_005: It's a friend from school. On Bagel, he scrolled past a topic we used to talk about, and he called since it reminded him of me.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_Meta_Npc_Dlg02_Mian03_02: This is all my fault… I should've kept a closer eye on them.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_058: It's me, the Appraiser from Eibon. We met during the Fogden incident.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_133: That's me. I guess I don't need to introduce myself.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC031_059: Someone's calling the work phone. Let me pick it up real quick.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_366: It's just a bit noisy. Anyway, call you back later, okay? No need to worry about me.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111029_Room1_08_QuestPanel: Is this a dead end? It doesn't seem like it.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_073: Correct. The thing is, the results of the investigation had to remain one of the Circle's secrets, not to be made public, because at that time, there were already more than 300,000 persons under my influence.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC00114_004: It's true! I also thought it was weird!
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC029_047: We're wrapping up, but it's not over yet, is it? You're rushing to hand out the consolation prize. You sure I won't find your true form? You're declaring yourself the winner ahead of time?
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC030_019: I meant your other train of thought. The one that isn't about offing me.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC012_037: Good night. You should get some sleep too.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe_HM01_NPC029_005: I'll log you out to somewhere safe for now.
ST_Main_Exe01.Meta_Bub_Mianrongrong_sleep_pre_03: So nice and warm… Getting sleepy…
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_281: Elyms isn't the old friend everyone used to have, but that doesn't mean she isn't a friend of theirs… That's how I see it.
ST_Main_Exe01.q1110671_01_Sumup: Elyms told you that you could wait for Exe to erase her, after which he would take you back to Hethereau. You were shocked to learn the truth behind the captain and lieutenant's mission: Exe had long planned to kill Elyms, his Anomaly partner, and had now put that plan into action. Using Nitsa as an example, Elyms explained how the "Imaginary Old Friend" overwrote people's perceptions and memories. Still, you couldn't understand why Exe would go to such extremes.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111087_QuestPanel: Elyms looks a little blurry. Let's hear what she has to say.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111087_01_Sumup: Elyms explained what happened afterward and thanked you. Before leaving, you asked the "Imaginary Old Friend" whether it would keep consuming people's real memories of their friends. The entity then shared its own perspective.

ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_des_11: A softer and cleaner carpet. You could tell how expensive it must have been.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_Player_041: Does filling the gap mean the avatar replaces the real friend in their heart?
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_068: At first, I deployed avatars in multitudes. I used different social identities to blend in, and approached users who dialed the Invalid Number, to help them reconcile with their old friends.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_277: In the end, your conversations stopped at that brutal fallout. You never apologized for the words that went too far. You never typed what you actually felt into that chat box—not a single word. You never knew, and now you never will, what Y meant to say that day.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC02114_005: How come you've been getting home so late these days? Have you been drinking too? I ran into one of your colleagues the other day.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC02114_007: I haven't seen you for a while.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_192: Lately, I've even started to feel some of those unnecessary emotions, like fear.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111006_QuestPanel: Someone called you while you were half-asleep. What happened?
ST_Main_Exe01.q111009_QuestPanel: Someone's calling the phone you just found. Their voice sounds familiar…
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC00114_002: What's so weird about that? I-I went there once too.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPCSub033_002: I am working on the report! By the way, why do I hear things crumbling down on your end?
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe_HM03_NPC030_005: Have you identified… the real me?
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_Meta_Npc030_026: Do you ever give your friends a ride?
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC00114_003: Got a work order once: grab a cafeteria meal, leave it outside the 17th-floor server room.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_Meta_Player_002: Can a bus actually do that?

Before this place became a battlefield, she insisted on getting you safely back to Hethereau. Exe agreed. The phone rang. On the other end of the line was a friend who cared about you…

ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC029_075: Just when I was about to win, Y would put up a wall to scare me and watch me smack right into it…
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC029_031: Mechanisms are there to be exploited. I knew your realm would reset me, because that's the kind of anomaly you are.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe_HM03_NPC029_003: There's more than I can ever remove.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC030_002: Antivirus, reformatting, reinstallation… He tried it all! Tell me, how do you do that to someone with a straight face?
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC030_006: The storage room was small, cramped, stuffy, and uncomfortable. But the flickering pixels on the screen were just so—much—fun!
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC029_070: Come at me. Let the countdown begin.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC02114_001: Come in. Please make yourself at home.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe_HM02_NPCA_005: I knew it. This never should've been a case. That kid just had to go do his own thing…
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_060: I knew it was more than just a dream. Is it possible to talk to you face-to-face?

ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_des_21: A few energy drinks are scattered on the desk. Beyond that, the desk shows almost no sign of use.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111011_QuestPanel: The caller in your dream sounded like Nitsa from the Bureau. Go ask her about it.
ST_Main_Exe01.q111023_01_Sumup: The phone in your dream belonged to one of Nitsa's close friends, ETD-6's lieutenant. The captain and lieutenant reportedly went to handle a confidential case and had been away for nearly two months. Nitsa has grown increasingly worried, and the space you stumbled into last night is the only lead you have.
ST_Main_Exe01.Meta_Album_Photo_Description_03: The Fluffies reuniting with their big bro finally. What a touching moment!
ST_Main_Exe01.Meta_Album_Photo_Description_08: The Fluffies keep Quietlight company while it recharges. With friends by your side, no challenge is too big.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_057: That's why "I" appear as an anime-style image, just like the kind someone sets in their chat interface.
ST_Main_Exe01.Meta_Album_Photo_Description_05: Tasty Tater giving out French fries. Sharing is the key to happiness.
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC029_038: What does it feel like to watch your data and the connections you built get torn apart, one by one?
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_249: The oddities are no big deal. It's more about the mental strain here… Dig too deep into the massive collective dream born from shared subconscious, and you're lucky if you get away unscathed.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC029_114: You died once and forgot how to work?
ST_Main_Exe01.TExe01_NPC029_025: Each block corresponds to one user's archive unit. Crack the storage medium, and the avatar data of that user's old friend will be rendered into a "person" and released.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe_HM03_NPC029_001: All your files are stored separately. The "person" I cracked is only one of your fragments.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_NPC030_087: Take this one, for example. It's still one of the forms others see me in, but at least it lets you recognize me.
ST_Main_Exe01.Exe01_Player_311: For example, there's one thing you can't give me… that feeling of waiting on a friend to call you.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_EC_NPC034A_001: (☆▽☆) Hey hey! Taygedo's family runs an Anomaly Hunter group, right?

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC01401_010: 60 million Fons! This beautiful lady's raised the stakes to 60 million!
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_Player_021: All 6 puppets have a similar aura. It should be from the same anomaly or the same type of anomaly, but it's very faint.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC00401_007: A 72-hour limit. After that, the replica disappears.
ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC005_Alphard_00001: Seven weeks ago, New Helios experienced a Class VII anomaly disaster, <blue>Hypervortex</>.
ST_MainDialogue.CS_BZ_003: Have we been here several times already?
ST_MainDialogue.CS_BZ_005: Perhaps we should go down and take a look.

ST_MainDialogue.CS_BZ_012: It seems these plants can respond to words.

ST_MainDialogue.CS_BZ_010: I wish I could climb up those vines.
ST_MainDialogue.CS_BZ_004: There's a door over there; let's look around the room for a key.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC017_062: <TypingTitle titlename="Alcohol Brand" titlecolor="grey_title" contextcolor="blue">Bacchus</> is a young brand, established after the eldest son of the <blue>Dvořák family</> bought a vineyard of the same name for his third wife.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC00201_006: Kenneth urged me, saying, <blue>"No pain, no gain,"</> so we pawned what we had at Pawn Moonlight to realize our dreams.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_Player_040: A place that <blue>makes all your wishes come true for you as long as you're willing to pay the price</>, huh…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC01401_031: <blue>Nightingale</> is always sharp. Overacting makes it easier for her to spot flaws.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC01401_002: <blue>"Dawn to dusk, scorched to gold, venom to sweetness, zealotry to determination."</>
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC007_005: You just need to follow the trail to find the nest.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1018_025: The Helm of Theseus… they took the helm… Uh, it hurts…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC024_009: Bingo. You're asking the right questions.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC009_012: Hmm… There are more and more divisions in the Enforcement Tactical Division nowadays!

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC011_010: We got you covered, Boss! JTF will be right here!

ST_MainDialogue.Main_Prologue_Alphard_00005: {Gender}|gender(He,She) has never worked in our organization before. Mint, make sure you explain everything carefully.

ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC003_Skia_00001: —The Wertheimer Index in the Halfport strongly fluctuates. Unit 6 won't last very long.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC00301_001: I don't know what happened. I just bumped into it like that!

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC011_095: "Ten years of one's sense of taste"… he knew the price very well.
ST_MainDialogue.MP00_00_Player_019: …Appraiser? I do have some perception of anomalies, but I'm not familiar with antiques…
ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC006_Alphard_00005: …the future of Code Zero… is beyond the reality of the Prophet…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC022_045: Everything… started because of you. My ignorant little sister.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_Player_015: Does it have to be chanted?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC012_008: Gave it all to you last week…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC012_043: No. Judging by our method of entry, our placement within the pawnshop appears to be randomized.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC022_030: And we… are the same way too.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_Player_011: You mean I don't have to go with you?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_092: And who are you…? Did you also enter here by mistake?

ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC003_Skia_00002: I'll go ahead. See you at the site.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1054_021: But if I was strong enough… Master wouldn't have been injured, and she wouldn't have left.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_NPC008_001: …Hey, dumb otter, where'd you fish that getup out of? The dumpster? Don't tell me you're planning to wear that on your date?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC027_008: Oh… right, the delivery! Thank you, Xiaozhen.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC012_014: Seems like she thinks we're her editors trying to chase her down for her manuscripts.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC009_019: Very well. I'm wait for your good news.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1013_010: Very well… I understand. You may leave. I'll take care of myself.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC010_014: The lady has always valued talent…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC011_057: Master…? Where have you been in the past few days? I sent you so many messages! How's your injury? Are you feeling better?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC012_001: That's a generous offer, with <TypingTitle titlename="Very Important Customer" titlecolor="grey_title" contextcolor="blue">VIC</> exclusive services.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC00113_001: In any case, we'd like you to come to BAC to assist with our investigation.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC017_094: Ebisu has a complex list of offerings. We didn't expect to contain anomalies other than the mission target…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1046_201: I forgot about the family… because I was escaping the past?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC014_047: We won't be so unlucky to face the tricky ones, right?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_051: I'll go check up on her…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC02501_017: I didn't mean that. If my words offended you before, I apologize. I was too anxious.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC022_075: Mother's wish was to have a harmonious family. We were all trying to fulfill that wish, trying not to ruin anything.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_NPC012_007: Well, if Mr. Adler says so…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_148: You're the one who created the other Nanally… Did you also create all of this?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC00201_002: Yes… I'm surprised you already figured that out…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC022_080: …The most unforgivable thing is: Mother, she who brought us into the world, was the one to pay the ultimate price.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1046_305: Isn't it better… to be alive?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC017_066: Hotori's way of striking back is indeed unique…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC017_007: Haha, gotta love your sense of humor, Hotori.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC017_067: Hotori, the client's target auction item hasn't come up yet, please be patient…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC010_001: Moby-Dick's clerk said the latest issue has arrived, so please handle it, Taygedo.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC02501_004: It's unclear if it's an anomaly… Our collaborating perfumer is missing…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC012_041: Looks like their route is different from ours—Chuppa?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC022_002: Threatened, you say? There seems to have some misunderstanding. My sister here is simply bored of playing house…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_NPC010_017: I apologize for the embarrassment. We've cleaned up the mess in the fitting room and returned the sample clothes we used for reference. We're sorry for any inconvenience caused.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_Player_074: …At last, we can get back on track with our original plans.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_Player_027: …Come to think of it, with Taygedo's ability, transforming something like graphite into actual diamonds… it doesn't seem impossible, does it?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_NPC010_058: This is a name Sir Taygedo gave <blue>Azure Vista</> when he invested in it.
ST_MainDialogue.MP00_00_NPC008_003: Spare me! My ears are already sore—
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1046_047: I'm sorry…! My bad! This isn't the time to be fooling around…!
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC01401_028: The Class V Anomaly… The Class V Anomaly was brought in by the villain who stole the auction piece… and Ebisu will not be held accountable…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_Player_152: Lady T… Is she the Mother Zankou spoke of? When she said "Mother" misses you too… could it be…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_120: "If you want to see the true nature of things, you need to look from different angles, as if using a kaleidoscope."
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC009_003: "Though silent, one's demeanor speaks," isn't that your industry's favorite saying?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC009_045: Pawn Moon's business is built on integrity. This chef must be hiding a lot of things.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_Player_058: "Operation Love Confession"… Is Taygedo really planning to confess here?
ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC005_Alphard_00005: "But it is the only Esper without detectable Wertheimer Index, the first in human society."
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC022_060: Because of our existence, the numbers on the registry representing your life are depleting. When the numbers reach zero, we will fall asleep with nothing left but gratitude.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_008: The "King's" body is in the midst of dead fish. Did the fish slay the king or the king slay the fish?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1018_012: This one is haunted by worries about the future, unable to let go of her obsession with protecting others, and has yet to face many heartbreaking farewells.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1046_285: Did the Mighty King die? He was still wiggling his whiskers around confidently yesterday.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1046_283: The Mighty King looks tired. He's not moving at all, and won't even sing anymore.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC022_019: Little Renee, what would you choose between "an eternity in solitude" or "a moment of happiness"?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1053_045: The "child" was born. He was sturdy yet nimble, and once his spring is sprung, he could run two laps in the royal city, with no one able to keep up! Everyone congratulated the old carpenter, but she shook her head and said: "No, this isn't a real child."
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1053_048: The "child" was born. His beauty caught everyone's eyes. The king invited him to dance at the palace for foreign guests. Everyone congratulated the old carpenter, but she shook her head and said: "No, this isn't a real child."
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC086A_006: The only thing "it" can do is to trap people in a day they cannot escape…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_254: "Being strong" is never what it seems. For me, the heart you got for your family is your greatest strength.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC015_073:
RTB Quest failed
The Scarlet Letter organization intervened and seized control
Motives unknown
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_Player_150: The Eternal Present probably requires the owner's verbal consent before it can detach itself…
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1054_007: I feel just as fake as the badge I made.
ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC005_Alphard_00009: After the Hypervortex incident, the Code Zero reappeared briefly.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC086A_005: Maybe "eternity" doesn't exist after all. Well, it's not like I didn't know that. Aside from my beauty, nothing in this world can last forever.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC013_058: The curse of eternal life, a fallen family, a blank tomorrow… hints about "time" are all over the place.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1055_004: Dreamwalker? I see, that's a fitting name.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_NPC034A_033: Azure Vista! I'm so glad we get to check this place off our list before leaving Hethereau!
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC011_005: "Mysterious Puppets in Hethereau: Performance Art or Terrible Omen?"
ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC005_Alphard_00004: "Tests show that all physiological indicators of Esper Zero are within the normal range. It has good language and cognitive abilities and highly developed social skills."
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC00806_001: The head chef at Delichemy? Kenneth, I believe his name was.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_02_NPC012_013: The "Damsel in Distress" scenario typically results in a quick increase in affection… The challenge lies in orchestrating a resolvable crisis at the right time and the right place.
ST_MainDialogue.MP00_00_NPC01001_027:
"Film Orbit Studio now back in business! New scenes for your latest photos!"
How's that for promotion?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC028_019: It'll make you want to say "Ayo, ayo, just let it go!"
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC02201_008: Cake Sweeper sensei! Are you home?

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_210: Of course they're allowed to run away. But that choice has to be made by themselves—
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_Player_197: The villagers from Elden Ville… Are they your family?
ST_MainDialogue.HM_Prologue_MainSQC005_Alphard_00008: Code Zero has something in common with you. With undetectable Wertheimer Indexes.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1055_013: That absolute, unkillable demon pursues me relentlessly… But I'm not going to make the same mistake and let her succeed.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC1013_021: A helm to keep everyone trapped in the past, full of beautiful dreams… how wasteful it would be to simply change course.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC00301_002: This young man at the door called the place Pawn Moonlight.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC014_012: In places where only Esper abilities work, only those I approve can see it, top-notch secrecy!
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_03_NPC009_056: Certain anomalies dictate that all is bound by cause and effect. Yet, some things evolve with time, allowing for new interpretations or transformations. Should we consider this mere intuition, or perhaps a revelation?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC1046_018: It's almost mealtime, Fuuka should be at Food First. Shall we?
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_01_NPC020_011: Otro gets terrible allergies every shedding season… Keep a close eye on this one. Don't let it run away and cause more trouble.

ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC010_025: It's not like Nanally to leave without telling anyone.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_04_NPC011_111: She's been gone this morning and hasn't come back.
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC011_064: She must be threatening Master. Appraiser, we have to save her!
ST_MainDialogue.MU01_05_NPC012_011: She must blame herself for not being able to protect her family.
