- When the Dimension Visitor is neither nullified nor contained, that is, when the Corridor exists, the Helm of Theseus cannot leave the Anomalous Space.
——Updated Records——
- Now that the Corridor has collapsed, the Helm of Theseus exists beyond the Corridor. Its functions are not clear at this moment.

Anomaly Nexus
High clearance required to access files.

Risk Assessment
Low risk.

Containment/Guarantor Status
The anomaly is not currently under containment.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2024_des:
"A dazzling key that unlocks the door of your mortal prison."

Anomaly Story:
The obsession with immortality seems baked into human nature. Out of fear of death, refusal to accept a short, fleeting life, or a desire for more, be it knowledge, money, or power, the hunger for youth and longer lifespans has never ceased. The Anomaly known as "Eternal Present" is that desire made manifest. Its origin has long since vanished from the written records, and most of its past beneficiaries remain shrouded in mystery. Yet, after millennia, Eternal Present still shines brightly.

The Anomaly itself presents as a brilliant, dazzling gem—but its true form is rarely seen. Only once it forges a contract with a host will it reveal itself. From then on, the Contract Bearer can no longer perceive the passage of time.
However, signing the contract poses a significant risk. Because the contract signer's perception of time is completely shattered, they eventually become numb and apathetic towards their existence.

Escaping Eternal Present is, in theory, very simple: as long as the Contract Bearer utters the words, "Free me of my immortal prison", Eternal Present will sever the contract and lie in wait for a new host. The previous host loses every privilege they once had and resumes life normally.

As of right now, the last Contract Bearer reported was Dolores Constantine. With Eternal Present, she attempted to revive the fading Constantine family. In the end, however, she abandoned the Anomaly and embraced her own mortality. After her passing, the Constantine name quickly sank into obscurity, and Eternal Present vanished without a trace.
(Record Update)
Dolores Constantine passed Eternal Present onto her "daughter"—a puppet she herself had given life to—in an attempt to dodge the pursuit of the Anomaly known as the "Debt Collector".

Characteristics:
· Appears as a dazzling gem.
· For any Contract Bearer of this Anomaly, the consequences of time decrease dramatically, granting them an immortal existence.
· Eventually, the Contract Bearer will begin to develop an apathetic worldview.
· To break free of this Anomaly, the signer must personally declare, "Free me of my immortal prison".

Anomaly Nexus:
When there's no one left to desire more time—or when time itself is swallowed into oblivion—Eternal Present will undergo nullification.

Risk Assessment:
Low Risk.

Containment Status:
Not Contained.

Containment Procedures:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1005_des:
"As ashes yearn for dying embers."

Anomaly Story
Throughout various Anomalous Realms, both Hunters and Bureau personnel have witnessed a cyan bird-like Anomaly. This Anomaly, which we call the Fire Phoenix, exhibits simple behavioral patterns with no intelligence, communication abilities, or aggression. It has virtually no notable characteristics and is even more docile than common birds.

The Fire Phoenix typically appears as a surge Anomaly within other Anomalies' Anomalous Realms, rarely manifesting independently. The Fire Phoenix instinctively seeks stable, secure Anomalous Realms or long-term Esper constructs as habitats. Once separated from these "habitable environments," the Fire Phoenix will naturally undergo Nullification over time. Unlike common birds, The Fire Phoenix does not seem to eat or digest, yet still instinctively avoids danger. Its flight capabilities match those of skilled flying birds. When entering Anomalous Realms or inhabiting Esper constructs, The Fire Phoenix briefly strips off its physical state and enters an energy form. This transformation is also used to evade danger, but when used under non-habitable conditions, it significantly reduces the Fire Phoenix's existence time before natural Nullification.
The Fire Phoenix's instinct to seek Anomalous Realms or Esper constructs can sometimes be used for guidance; but this makes them difficult to contain. Apart from the Bureau of Anomaly Control, civilian conditions suitable for long-term Fire Phoenix habitation are virtually nonexistent; but even with such conditions, maintenance costs are considerable, making the containment of a Fire Phoenix cost-prohibitive.
Some researchers theorize that the Fire Phoenix may be fundamentally connected to Anomaly genesis. If we compare an anomaly's birth in the real world to an explosion, the "ashes" stirred up by its aftershock become the Fire Phoenix. As ashes don't retain heat for long, the Fire Phoenix exists in a constant state of "decay" over time. If it can receive some form of "replenishment" from Anomalous Realms or Esper constructs, the Fire Phoenix can continue existing, which explains why they seek these habitable environments.

Anomaly Characteristics
• Instinctively seeks Anomalous Realms or Esper constructs as habitats.
• Transforms into energy form when entering habitats or evading danger.

Anomaly Nexus
Eliminate its physical form through attack, or allow natural Nullification over time under non-habitable conditions.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Due to the demanding conditions required for containing the Fire Phoenix, only the Celaeno Compound currently maintains a limited number in containment; civilian containment is virtually nonexistent.
Currently, this Anomaly cannot be guaranteed.

Containment Measures
Joint containment with Anomalies capable of forming stable, secure Anomalous Realms.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1028_des:
"Tread carefully at night."

Anomaly Story
There have only been a handful of direct sightings of a "Leech Spawn". The puzzle of this Anomaly can only be pieced together from blurry footage and fragmented witness accounts. Due to the nature of the "Leech Spawn", in that they often attach themselves to objects or lurk in the shadows, they're incredibly difficult to catch.
A "Leech Spawn" is a type of "Protocore" Anomaly, with no stable physical form, and is thus classified as low-level Oddities. Their overall shape resembles a dog, but their head looks like two fists fused. Their tail is similar, in that it has the streamlined structure of a hand. Leech Spawns are composed of a mist-like substance that radiates cold temperatures, causing anything it touches to go numb.
Leech Spawn display a quasi-biological habit of attaching themselves to objects to conceal themselves. Because of this, Leech Spawn are incredibly difficult to contain or nullify.
According to most witness accounts, Leech Spawns often attach themselves to streetlights and create the illusion of malfunctions to lure in maintenance workers. They can also potentially utilize shadows beneath streetlights to mimic human silhouettes, while repeatedly emitting sounds that are similar to a baby's cry for help. It should be noted that this Anomaly merely mimics noises, and does not have the proper vocal organs to speak.
Multiple related incidents have already become urban legends among the public, and are discussed across many sections of online forums. The source for Leech Spawn is no longer reliable.

Anomaly Characteristics
- Leech Spawns are hound-like Bio Anomaly and a branch of "Protocore";
- Their true bodies are made of a mist-like substance and have no stable form;
- They possess visual organs that appear iridescent under different lighting angles;
- Their bodies have sleek, hand-like structures, allowing for rapid movement;
- Their behavior patterns show deliberate imitation of intelligent life;
- They often attach themselves to objects to camouflage themselves;

Anomaly Nexus
Create bright light to disrupt the Oddity's habitat.

Risk Assessment
Potential threat.

Containment Status
Most have been nullified. A small number are contained at the Celaeno Compound.

Containment Measures
Illuminate with light sources, ensuring there are no blind spots present.

Experiment Log
Test Objective: Determine how light affects Leech Spawn behavior.
The test team consisted of C.S.U. members with specialized Anomaly-handling training. With adequate protective measures in place, there was no risk to life or any other safety issues.

Variable Control: Illumination level—controlled through adjusting the lighting equipment.

Results:
- At 100% illumination, Leech Spawn showed almost no behavior, only occasionally pacing slowly with no clear, identifiable purpose.
- At 60% illumination, Leech Spawn were capable of running and moving about. They showed no obvious aggression, but remained wary of approaching organisms.
- At 30% illumination, Leech Spawn displayed clear aggressive behavior, and their behavior patterns shifted from vigilance to active aggression.
- With no illumination, Leech Spawn reverted to their pre-containment behavior patterns and aggression, posing a safety threat. Testing was conducted using inanimate dummies.

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1027_des:
"Two eyes, one nose, one mouth… Mm-hmm. No doubt about it. I'm a genuine human!"

Anomaly Story
Many years ago, just as a special recruitment fair hosted by the Bureau of Anomaly Control was about to end, an octopus-like Anomaly wearing a paper-bag hood came wobbling over. It had clearly done its best to disguise itself, but everyone could tell at a glance that it was not human. Under countless watchful eyes, the mysterious Anomaly extended a long, agile black tentacle and submitted its resume, making its intention to join the Bureau perfectly clear.
The interviewers were baffled, but they still gave it a chance. Since this Anomaly had hidden its true face beneath a paper bag for reasons unknown, it was obviously impossible to judge it by ordinary human standards. The interviewers gave it a standard interview, followed by several improvised assessments tailored to its abilities. The results were surprisingly impressive. The Anomaly proved highly skilled at clerical work, with remarkably nimble "hands and feet." In the spirit of fairness and impartiality, the Bureau of Anomaly Control ultimately decided to hire it.
This is the U-7646[Or], now known as "Mr. Bag:" an Anomaly with no Guarantor who found employment entirely through its own efforts and now works under the Bureau of Anomaly Control. True to its name, it always wears a hood made from a paper bag, along with a "shirt" made from the same material. Beneath that shirt are several long, flexible, shadow-like tentacles. "If you ignore the hood, it is actually very cool," one employee once commented. When no one is watching, Mr. Bag secretly changes its paper bag and draws expressions on it to show how it feels at that moment. No one has ever seen its true face, and no one knows where it came from. "Mr. Bag" is the name registered on its employment documents, while "Mr." is a title it insisted on adding itself. Clearly, Mr. Bag very much hopes to be respected as a human being. Perhaps that is one reason it chose to disguise itself and enter human society.
Since taking office, Mr. Bag has handled the tedious work of organizing and distributing documents inside and outside the Bureau. To let it work to its full potential, the Bureau assigned Mr. Bag enormous personal workspace, allowing it to wave its tentacles freely in an open environment and process tasks efficiently on multiple fronts. Its dedicated space contains countless mailboxes. One end of each mailbox connects to its office, while the other connects to Bureau of Anomaly Control offices throughout Hethereau and to certain government departments. Mr. Bag knows the location and owner of every mailbox. During work hours, it can be seen swiftly waving its "shadow tentacles," collecting documents sent from various places through the mailboxes, then sorting and filing them away. At times, it also uses the mailboxes to distribute documents. People unfamiliar with the mailboxes are often startled by the tentacles suddenly emerge from inside, but Mr. Bag has long since grown used to such reactions. Sometimes, after sending or retrieving the necessary files, it even offers a little greeting gesture before vanishing with a whoosh, retracting its tentacle just as suddenly as it appeared and closing the mailbox behind it.
Outside of its primary duties, Mr. Bag also manages "Mr. Bag Tips," a public broadcast channel run by the Bureau of Anomaly Control for all citizens. The channel usually broadcasts content such as "Anomaly Basics," sends out low-level Anomaly alerts, and serves as one way for Anomaly Hunters to obtain Anomaly bounty information. Even while handling clerical work with astonishing efficiency, Mr. Bag has never missed a single broadcast. Such astonishing work capability may be rivaled only by the one known as "Agent.LUCK."
Thanks to its outstanding performance, Mr. Bag became the only employee in the history of the Bureau of Anomaly Control to win "Employee of the Month" for fourteen consecutive months. "So, just treat Mr. Bag like any other colleague and get along with it. I am sure that's what it wants, too," said the then-deputy captain of ETD-6. To this day, the kind people around it have never exposed Mr. Bag's clumsy disguise, and the innocent Anomaly has long since come to think of itself as a member of humanity. As long as its colleagues treat it as human, then perhaps, in practice, there is no real difference. For Mr. Bag, that is enough.

Characteristics
Mr. Bag is an octopus-like Anomaly who wears a paper-bag hood and a shirt made from the same material. Beneath the shirt are several long, flexible, shadow-like tentacles. When no one is around, it secretly changes its paper bag and draws expressions on it to show how it feels.
·It excels at processing documents efficiently on multiple fronts. Since taking office, it has been responsible for centrally organizing and distributing many documents inside and outside the Bureau.
It believes it is a member of humanity and deeply hopes to be respected and treated as human.

Anomaly Nexus
Insufficient clearance. Currently inaccessible.

Risk Assessment
Generally harmless. Mr. Bag is quite capable in a fight, but very friendly toward humans. That said, please do not provoke him on purpose.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly, guaranteed by the Bureau of Anomaly Control.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2010_des:
"No one may stop dancing until the star takes her final bow!"

Anomaly Story
In the era of the aristocracy, there were far fewer forms of entertainment than we have the luxury to enjoy today. Banquets, where hosts would flaunt wealth and status through material extravagance over glasses of wine, became one of the most common pastimes of high society. In that era, a rare and unique fabric material came into existence and, unsurprisingly, drew the eye of many looking to show off. Who would be the first to weave an unparalleled gown from this rare material? Two famous master tailors shared this honor, commissioned jointly to create an evening dress for a socialite. One was named Crouch, while the other's name has been lost to history. They were both collaborators and competitors, each striving to create the most dazzling design for the gown. As a result, the dress lived up to its makers' intentions, transforming the lady who wore it into a true "Prom Queen." As she danced, more and more guests joined the revelry, genuinely captivated.
However, such joy did not last long. As the ball continued, the expression of the "Prom Queen" in her magnificent evening gown became twisted, and the surrounding guests realized they could no longer stop dancing. An invisible force, like strings manipulating marionettes, binded their limbs, controlling their movements. Some nobles tried to intervene, but upon approaching, their own formal attire seemed to be afflicted, dragging them too into this mad dance. Fear spread, and those not yet controlled fled, while the affected nobles could only keep dancing until they collapsed from exhaustion.
When people returned to the devastated ballroom, the "Prom Queen" was still dancing alone, surrounded by fallen nobles. The "Prom Queen" bowed to the audience. Though she had long since perished, she still completed her curtain call under the dress's influence before finally collapsing. The dress was recovered, and both tailors were arrested. In the end, Crouch took his own life in prison out of guilt, but the nameless tailor mysteriously disappeared along with the evening gown.

R-4317(Ob), "The Never-ending Arachne," appears as a deep crimson women's evening gown. The fabric has a unique silky texture, extremely smooth to the touch. When in contact with skin, the fabric adheres and clings tightly, making it very difficult to remove. I certainly have never worn it, and I am not curious about how they came up with this description… But this description easily brings spider silk to mind, making one wonder about the material's origins.
As a Class V Anomaly, The Never-ending Arachne has surprisingly simple containment measures. It only needs to be folded like clothing and placed in a sealed container. However, anyone who witnesses The Never-ending Arachne will be amazed by its beauty and feel a strong urge to try it on. This urge gradually intensifies with viewing, suggesting a possible mind-affecting ability, but it is not permanent. Once the line of sight is broken, the urge to wear it quickly fades.
When The Never-ending Arachne has sufficient space to move (enough to accommodate an adult standing with arms outstretched), if a poor curious soul approaches the Anomaly, it will activate. The Anomaly will generate several Derivative Anomalies. Subsequently, anyone within its area of influence will feel their body being pulled as if by spider threads, wanting to join in this "dance." Once they join, they can only dance endlessly until exhaustion. If one refuses to dance with it, or if the "performance" offered is not enough to please it, The Never-ending Arachne will attack without mercy.
To nullify or contain The Never-ending Arachne, one must first eliminate its Surge Anomalies. Then, The Never-ending Arachne will personally attack with nimble and elaborate dance steps. Even the music and lighting become its weapons. Those attacked must respond with equally exquisite footwork, dodging those deadly attacks and seizing any opportunities to counterattack. At the height of the battle, the arena will plunge into darkness, with only areas illuminated by "spotlights" clearly visible. Leaving the lit areas will cause one's movements to gradually slow. The target must complete a final duet with it under the spotlight. If they defeat The Never-ending Arachne during this process and deliver a spectacular performance, The Never-ending Arachne will "take its bow" and become an ordinary evening gown.

The Never-ending Arachne was born from human material desire, meant to satisfy envy and the urge to compete. Even as an Anomaly, it remains the eternal center of the ball, even if the "ball" and "eternity" were realized in unexpected ways. No matter how distinguished those aristocrats were, things have changed, and even "aristocracy" has become nothing more than a symbol in history books. For The Never-ending Arachne, there are no more endless balls left for it to conquer. Perhaps its best fate is to remain in a containment unit as a relic of that era.

Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly tempts witnesses to wear it and begins to activate when someone approaches with curiosity.
· This Anomaly forces those who approach to "dance" with it. Those who comply will dance continuously until they collapse from exhaustion.
· Refusing to dance with this Anomaly will result in it attacking. To nullify it, one must ultimately perform a grand "curtain call."

Anomaly Nexus
Perform a grand curtain call together.

Risk Assessment
Moderate hazard.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not in containment.

Containment Measures
Properly seal in a small, enclosed container.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1030_des:
"Amid the endless cycles, who can hear their cries?"

Anomaly Story
The Fogden-Wright is, by far, the most dangerous Derivative Anomaly in Fogden. Within a valley contained in the Hunt Zone, two participants encountered an Oddity that appeared similar to a giant serpent. It was described as "enormous, immensely strong, and with lightning-fast reflexes." At the bottom of the valley, the two participants found multiple remains of other Oddities, alongside a record log left behind by someone who had once defeated the Fogden-Wright. The record log describes the original individual as having a head that imitated the silhouette of a human face, sounds that are similar to those of a snake, scaled wings, a serpentine body, and eye-like markings spread all over its skin. Based on these descriptions, it's been inferred that the Fogden-Wright is not a naturally occurring creature, but a transformed, composite beast pieced together from the remains of previous participants. Following this transformation, none of the participants seem to retain their initial personalities or memories.

Characteristics
Form: A giant serpent-like entity over 65 feet long. Several halo-like rings surround its body.
Behavior: Attacks any living thing that enters its territory.

Anomaly Nexus
Defeated

Risk Assessment
Highly dangerous

Containment Status
Eradicated
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1024_des:
"All aboard!"

Anomaly Story:
In recent history, an Anomaly Metro calling itself the "Ghost Train" appeared and caused the Bureau of Anomaly Control a myriad of problems. The Ghost Train Anomaly was large and surprisingly mobile, therefore preventing direct contact and making observation increasingly difficult. Around the time that the BAC was to deem the Ghost Train mission a complete failure, a faint glow emanated from the train's conductor's cabin. Out flew an owl, alight with a blue sheen, and, from the loudspeaker on her chest, came a gentle, human voice: "Welcome aboard the Ghost Train! I'm Miss Levi, your conductor for this trip. It's my pleasure to welcome you all aboard!"
From a scientific standpoint, "Miss Levi" can be categorized as a Derivative Anomaly of the Ghost Train itself. On the other hand, some researchers claim that she may have been a fragment of the train that split off. Others claim she's a manifestation of the train's desire to be understood; a translator of sorts.
As the conductor, Miss Levi consistently plays pre-recorded announcements for anything pertaining to the train's daily upkeep. No one has ascertained where these pre-recorded announcements were acquired from. It's important to note that Miss Levi can also communicate through natural avian means, that is, owl sounds from her beak. Despite the difficulties that being a train-conducting owl might pose, Miss Levi firmly believes in doing her job well.
Though, few humans can interpret the language used by Oddities, which leads to Miss Levi often being left with only herself to communicate.

Characteristics:
· "Miss Levi" is an owl-like Oddity that dons a train conductor hat and a loudspeaker. Similar to the Anomaly she descended from, her body gives off a faint blue glow.
· Normally, Miss Levi works at the information desk of the Ghost Train's station. Whenever someone enters the station, she appears at the desk, ready to assist. She also seems to manage many other tasks within the station and the Anomalous Realm it's connected to. Miss Levi can manifest in several different stations, or in multiple places, at the same time.
· When the station is empty, Miss Levi is believed to disappear entirely.


Anomaly Nexus:
Access restricted.

Risk Assessment:
Miss Levi is extremely friendly toward humans. Her aggression is reserved primarily for unreasonable complaints.

Containment Status:
Guaranteed by the Bureau of Anomaly Control.

Containment Procedures:
No containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2025_des:
"Tonight, expect to see heavy rainfall with a chance of thunderstorms. For those that need to go out, be sure to prepare accordingly, and, please… be on the lookout for Rainmen."

Anomaly Story:
It's a late, rainy night. An exhausted white-collar worker, having finally escaped the office, begins to walk through the downpour. Though their clothes are soaked and their feet are numb, they continue walking—completely unaware of the dark, gloomy stare watching their every move. Thin tendrils begin to wrap around their throat…
Cut!
Well, if this were one of those horror flicks, the scene would've ended there. Unfortunately, this office worker wasn't so lucky.
Clad in black, holding a black umbrella, prowling the streets on rainy nights—the Rainman roams back and forth through obscure alleyways, waiting to ambush any poor souls who left their umbrellas at home. So, as long as you have your raingear, you're safe, right? Guess again.
Hypotheses like "the Rainman only manifests on rainy nights" or "the Rainman is a Bio Anomaly" are just that: hypotheses. Recent research on Rainmen has destroyed both assumptions. Even on a clear, sunny day, you might spot an "umbrella" in some back alley that gives off an uncanny vibe—potentially a Rainman in its "umbrella" form.
In reality, that neatly dressed figure in a business suit is nothing but a puppet: a human silhouette molded from long, dangling tentacles hanging down from the umbrella canopy. Its real form is the umbrella proper.
The Rainman is only openly hostile on rainy nights. However, that doesn't mean that their activity is strictly limited to certain times and weather patterns. Even in broad daylight, approaching an unclaimed umbrella could potentially lead a victim to the Rainman's domain: a grim, damp alleyway, with an aggressive Rainman waiting at the other end.
The reasons behind the Rainman's behavior are still insufficiently researched. The leading theory claims that, when under adverse weather conditions like a thunderstorm, the city resembles the Rainman's domain almost one-to-one, thus encouraging the Rainman's territorial instinct. If so, simulating an umbrella with a bag or jacket might be your barrier between life and death. Even so, for your safety and the safety of the public, please remember your umbrella.

Characteristics:
· The Rainman is not a "person", nor is it an Oddity. It is an Object Anomaly whose true form resembles a black umbrella.
· A Rainman does not have a preferred method of attack. Confrontations head-on or from behind are common. Because of this, the Rainman poses extreme danger to ordinary civilians.
· During periods of high Rainman activity, new Rainman sightings are reported consistently. As of right now, there has been no discernible correlation discovered between Rainman observation points and places with high humidity and rainfall.
Recently, some Anomaly Hunters have reported seeing Rainmen use Weather Vines to alter surrounding environments, therefore expanding their "territory". Whether Rainmen possess true intelligence and sentience remains to be confirmed by Zerogon Laboratory.

Anomaly Nexus:
Destroy the "umbrella".

Risk Assessment:
Extremely High Risk. Ordinary citizens who approach Rainmen recklessly face severe danger. During high-activity periods, it is recommended that the Bureau of Anomaly Control dispatch specialists to carry out focused purges of Rainmen.

Containment Status:
Four specimens are contained at the Celaeno Compound.

Containment Procedures:
Use rack‑shaped containment units to fold and store the "umbrella" form.

Experiment Record:
Experiment Objective:
To verify how umbrella‑like "cover structures" affect Rainman's targeting behavior and aggression.

Experiment Method:
In a district with a confirmed Rainman presence, three groups were sent in for a controlled test. All personnel were CSU members with professional Anomaly training.
Group A held umbrellas fully open over their heads, completely covering the top of their heads.
Group B held backpacks, coats, and similar items over their heads, forming an umbrella‑like cover.
Group C held open umbrellas at their sides, not covering their heads.
The three groups each approached a Rainman in their "umbrella" state, observing and synchronously recording its reactions.

Experiment Results:
All three groups triggered hostile behavior from the Rainmen. However, in Group A, only 20% of personnel were actually attacked; in Group B, 60% were attacked; in Group C, every single member was attacked. This indicates that "whether the umbrella‑shaped cover fully shields the head" is the key factor in how Rainmen choose their targets.

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2003_des:
"He will keep on laughing."

Anomaly Story
There was once a famous clown named Lar. Every show he appeared in was packed to the rafters, and audiences were always moved by his hilarious performances and witty jokes, laughing until they doubled over. However, after his final performance before retirement, he was found dead in the backstage dressing room. He sat quietly in his chair, as if he had simply fallen asleep. His mask had melted into a pool of black liquid, and his true face bore no comical smile, only the tired, pale features of an aging man… A subsequent investigation revealed that his life had been filled with countless misfortunes, so much so that he had long grown weary of living. Yet he persisted in performing, for the smiles of his audience were the only remedy for his bitter existence. That melted mask became the first Anomaly known as "Lar," a name given in memory of that performer.

N-0502(Ob) Lar is an Anomaly occasionally found backstage at comedy venues. It appears as a pool of viscous black liquid, with every instance of Lar measures exactly 502 milliliters. Lar can be stored in any sealed container that can hold it, though to avoid accidents, containers of at least 1 liter capacity are recommended. Gloves should be worn when handling Lar to avoid direct skin contact. Upon contact with human skin, Lar will climb from the point of contact and spread across the user's body, which can look somewhat alarming, though the process is harmless. Users may feel a slight tightness on their skin, but once Lar has fully covered the user, they can adjust their appearance, voice, and even alter their body shape and physical features through mental visualization. We strongly recommend using a mirror as an aid. Please do not go outside with a terrifying face. After approximately 2 hours, the Lar covering the user's skin will gradually peel off and return to its liquid state, and the disguise will disappear along with it.
Some users claim that using Lar has a subtle influence on the mind. Users may develop tendencies toward theatrical personalities, attention-seeking behavior, risk-taking, and uncontrollable actions, along with a reduced sense of shame. There is no proof that these effects are caused by Lar, but we have slightly raised its potential hazard rating and are monitoring the effects of long-term use.

Smile! Even a fake smile can be medicine for the soul.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Appears as a pool of 502 milliliters of viscous black liquid. Can be stored in any container.
· Forms a thin film covering the user's body upon skin contact. The user can adjust their appearance and body features.
· Gradually peels off after approximately 2 hours of use, and the disguise disappears.

Anomaly Nexus
Comes in contact with someone who has absolutely no worries, or someone who has absolutely no happiness. When used by the former, Lar evaporates and disperses. When used by the latter, Lar crumbles into fine sand and soon disappears. Neither outcome causes harm to the user.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Most specimens are contained at Celaeno Compound. Guarantees are permitted. A small number circulate among the public.

Containment Measures
When not in use, store in any sealed container with a capacity over 1 liter. Letting it bask in the sun occasionally can make it seem less gloomy, but this is not necessary.

Experiment Records
Research on the Potential Psychological Effects of the Anomaly Lar
Experiment 1: A patient with social anxiety was given Lar to use, allowing her to attend social events in an appearance she preferred.
Conclusion: Lar does not improve the user's social skills.

Experiment 2: An ordinary person with no acting experience was given Lar to use and participated in a stage play.
Conclusion: Lar does not improve the user's acting ability.

Experiment 3: An agent used Lar before confessing their feelings to someone they had secretly admired for a long time but never had the courage to approach.
Conclusion: Lar will not turn an introverted and gloomy person into someone bright and cheerful. Not one bit.
Note: I really need to do something about your habit of misusing safe anomalies. You three, come to my office tomorrow.

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3008_des:
"Reflects one thousand wants, and even more desires."

Anomaly Story
Humans are born trapped within the prison of an intangible concept: the "self". As both an anchor of survival and a curse from birth, the "self" is an integral part of human consciousness. Water, by nature, possesses the ability to "reflect" and "refract". People often hold the belief that water can reveal "realities", whether it be a "truth" that's been shrouded, or a deeply held desire. When the energies of self-deception, confusion, or destruction overflow, nearby bodies of water can potentially hatch an Anomaly: the "Mirror Wraith".
The "Mirror Wraith" is a "spirit" enslaved by humanity's own delusions. It has no face, no flesh, and no wants or thoughts. Instead, it's an inevitable byproduct of self-rejection. As a result, it utilizes water to construct a "projection" of a victim's ideal self, and continues to sustain itself by devouring and reshaping a human's consciousness.

Characteristics
A massive mimetic trap-type Anomaly that lurks in enclosed natural bodies of water. The surrounding ecosystem exhibits cognitive interference visible to the naked eye: the outer perimeter appears completely normal; upon entering a certain range, subjects first encounter a "sanity cleanse" phenomenon in the form of rainfall; upon reaching the Anomaly's core, the entire water surface and surrounding space enter a state of absolute stillness and dead silence.
This Anomaly can reveal a target's deepest delusions or desires through their reflection on the water's surface, then refract a watery illusion of the target's "ideal self". In ordinary victims, this induces intense self-loathing and yearning, luring them willingly into the center of the lake, where they quietly drown, unaware of their situation.
Against targets that resist it or even show hostility, the Mirror Wraith instantly drops its disguise. The absolutely still water hardens and shatters, gravity inverts, and intruders who refuse to merge are forcibly dragged beneath the surface into a "fragmented prison." At that point, the Anomaly materializes the intruder's inner fears as a dark Mirror Self, born from the same source as the target, to unleash a vicious counterattack.

Anomaly Nexus
- For individuals whose subconscious cannot be probed, or who harbor no delusions, its probing fails and cannot trigger any lure mechanism.
- The only way to nullify it is to personally shatter the "Mirror Self" formed from one's own "dark side."

Risk Assessment
Latent Hazard

Containment Status
Cannot be contained.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1002_des:
"A crowd united. A crowd that can melt gold. A crowd impossible to please. A crowd that ???. ???…"

Anomaly Story
Fleur the Storyteller is one of the Derivative Anomalies of the Silent Garden. Compared to the other wildly overgrown vegetation in the Silent Garden, Fleur is arguably the most gentle and harmless. This plant appears as a flower with deep blue petals blooming on its vines, but at the center lies a white porcelain-like mask wrapped in plant matter. Fleur can emit a type of "readable" pheromone that conveys fragmented information, producing a sensation similar to "hearing" in those who perceive it. For ease of understanding, this method of information transmission will be referred to as a form of "narration". Based on the gathered evidence, the stories told by Fleur seem to be anecdotes about the Serenetti family. Though the garden has fallen into ruin and the family head no longer exists, the invisible shackles of their strict discipline still remain. As a result, all narrations by Fleur maintain a vague and unclear tone. The muffled "voices," ambiguous stories, and deliberately embellished wording make these narrations seem rather unreliable. However, since so much time has passed, these scattered stories relayed by the Anomaly are the only knowledge we now have of that once prosperous family.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Tells visitors stories of the Serenetti family's past, though with questionable authenticity.

Anomaly Nexus
Bound to C-3624(Lo) Silent Garden.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Only appears when the Silent Garden is active; cannot be contained separately.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3009_des:
"Yet each man kills the thing he loves, by each let this be heard. Some do it with a bitter look, some with a flattering word. The coward does it with a kiss, the brave man with a sword!"

[Anomaly Story]
The Fog Coffin's contract bearer must complete the ritual to begin the Fogden Game. For the ritual, the contract bearer must offer three anomalies and turn in a handwritten letter of rules. Once the sacrifices and the letter are devoured by the Fog Coffin, it opens and the game begins. The portal stays open for about an hour. Whoever enters it during that time will enter the Fogden and become a participant in the Fogden Game.
(Exception: the Dimension Visitor was brought into the Fogden in her astrolabe form, and was not seen as a participant.)

Madam T, leader of the Scarlet Letter, became the Fog Coffin's contract bearer roughly two hundred years ago. From that point on, she held the Offering Right. Judging from information on past participants gathered inside the Fogden, Madam T has since successfully held at least two rounds of the game and won both.

Before the Scarlet Letter incident, Madam T operated in Hethereau under the identity of Inanna. She put effort into scouting participants, with a penchant for desperate outlaws with nowhere else to escape. She'd tell them about a game in which the winner can take one thing they want from the losers. Winning these people over gave her both enough resources to initiate the game and access to supplies beyond ordinary means. To make them believe the game was easy to win, she'd also drag in unwitting Espers and common folk who were relatively weak, exploiting them as "consumables."
The rules differ from each round and they are decided by the contract bearer. But one iron law holds true: in each round, the Fog Coffin allows only one person to survive.

However, the latest round was interrupted by the descent of Code Zero. After it destroyed the Fog Coffin Colossus, the rules fell apart. There was no winner, and the game was terminated. The Fogden collapsed, the Fog Coffin disintegrated, and the game was no more.

[Characteristics]
The Fogden Game begins with the awakening of the Fog Coffin. When a participant enters the Fogden, a Lumen Circle forms on their wrist.
The game has three phases:
The hunting phase: Participants compete for Lumen Circles. They must defeat other participants and collect up to ten of them to enter the next phase.
The fog-zone phase: Qualified participants enter the fog zone, where thick fog blankets everything, visibility is low, and communication and perception are disrupted. Participants must traverse the fog zone to reach the arena, putting themselves at risk of being ambushed by the Fogden-Wright.
The arena phase: Participants who reach the arena gather here. The Fog Coffin Colossus appears to oversee this final phase. The colossus will eliminate any participant who indiscriminately attacks others or attempts to sabotage the game.

The transfer and counting of Lumen Circles are carried out automatically by the Fogden, with no manual operation required. The number of Lumen Circles on a participant's wrist updates in real time.
After the winner signs a contract with the Fog Coffin, they receive the Offering Right to initiate the next game, along with a reward of their choice. From then on, the contract bearer holds the power to awaken the Fog Coffin.
The game setting of each round differs. The nature of the offerings impacts the details of the Fogden. The "blood moon" that appeared in the final round was brought about by the properties of that round's offerings, the Helm of Theseus, the Eternal Present, and the First Branch.

[Anomaly Nexus]
The game ends.

[Risk Assessment]
Highly dangerous: The Fogden itself has powerful oddities and can cause encroachment. Participants must follow the rules to win, or be eliminated by the colossus.

[Containment/Guarantee Status]
Nullified
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4005_des:
"You shall not pass."

Anomaly Story
Once upon a time, there was an ancient kingdom. Though not particularly powerful, it was led by a devout monarch and its people were loyal. The kingdom held great wealth earned through hard work, stored in a temple, where the kingdom prayed that the God they worshipped would protect their property. Even when enemies brought war to their lands, they still held onto this hope. The king prayed to the divine: since these enemies came for the kingdom's wealth, let them be buried here along with it. Soon after, the king fell to the blade, and the conquerors opened the temple gates, greedily filling their bags with gold, silver, and jewels. They excitedly prepared to leave the temple, only to find that the exit had vanished! The entire army had become trapped within a vast labyrinth. They marched with their expensive treasures, then grew hungry and thirsty. Inevitable infighting and slaughter followed, until finally, they fell silent alongside the treasures they could never take with them. Many years later, this city's ruins, buried in history, were discovered by an expedition sponsored by Ebisu Auction House…

The above is the Story of Nantanì, as told by Ebisu Auction House. Of course, everyone knows Ebisu has always been good at story marketing, otherwise they wouldn't have made such a splash in the auction industry. Back to the Anomaly itself: U-7006(Lo) Nantanì appears as a floating creature wearing a green, semi-transparent cloak, looking just like a ghost. As you are reading this profile, you might have probably noticed that Nantanì is classified as a Location Anomaly. That would be a good observation, as the truth is Nantanì's true nature is an area rather than a being. The Nantanì we see is more like an avatar the Anomaly created for easier communication.
Nantanì's ability is to establish entry and exit rules for the domain it influences. According to Ebisu Auction House's design, any attempt to remove collection items from their contained positions through illegitimate means violates Nantanì's rules. Once the rules are broken, the entire auction venue becomes affected by Nantanì's power and cannot be exited until the rules are satisfied again. Under the influence of Nantanì's rules, escape is meaningless. No matter how you try to flee, you will eventually return to where you started. Attacking Nantanì is also meaningless, since, as mentioned earlier, Nantanì's true nature is an area, and attacking the visible green spirit has no effect whatsoever. Stalling for time is even more pointless, because Ebisu's security personnel aren't fools. The moment Nantanì's rules are triggered, they're already on the move.
When theft occurs, Nantanì will appear before the violator shortly after its power takes effect, demanding they return the collection items. If an Anomaly that should be contained ascends past containment, Nantanì will also use its power to control the disaster and protect auction guests, while guiding those capable of re-containing the Anomaly to do so. Within Nantanì's domain, it has the ability to open teleport channels, allowing rapid movement across obstacles. This sounds like the perfect security measure… No wonder Ebisu Auction House trusts Nantanì so much.

Even with all these conveniences, Nantanì's power is not without flaws. Its target is an area rather than individuals, which means when its power activates, everyone gets trapped inside until the rules are satisfied again. What happens if the rules can't be satisfied? Well… my mind wanders to those enemy soldiers who starved to death in Nantanì's labyrinth in the story… Let's hope no one exploits this weakness to cause any trouble…

Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly's visible form is a green spirit wearing a cloak.
· This Anomaly has the ability to understand others but cannot communicate through general means.
· This Anomaly affects an area, treating it as its domain and establishing entry and exit rules. When rules are violated, the domain becomes impossible to leave. Anyone who attempts to leave will be brought back to their original position until the rules are satisfied again.
· This Anomaly has teleportation abilities within its own domain.

Anomaly Nexus
Currently unknown.

Risk Assessment
Harmless under general circumstances, but with potential high hazard. When its power is active, it is nearly impossible to break from the inside.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Guaranteed by Ebisu Auction House.

Containment Measures
When no auction is being held, Nantanì resides in a room Ebisu Auction House has prepared for it, commonly called the temple. Ebisu keeps the interior layout of the temple strictly confidential. It is said to be filled with numerous treasures discovered alongside Nantanì.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3002_des:
"A rain to end the world, flowing from a wound upon reality's skin."

Anomaly Story
The Hypervortex is a highly dangerous Anomaly that suddenly appeared in New Helios, archived under number N-0824(Ph). The Hypervortex appeared and underwent nullification very quickly, yet in that brief window, it caused devastating destruction, nearly obliterating all affected areas of New Helios and resulting in countless casualties and property losses.

The Hypervortex can be divided into three parts: the storm, the halo, and the core. Currently, we cannot confirm whether the Hypervortex's appearance created the storm, or whether it emerged from within the storm. The thick clouds during the New Helios incident was one of the reasons early warnings were not issued. Under the Hypervortex's influence, precipitation from the storm cloud causes physical laws within the rainfall area to fall into chaos. The rain erodes the material structure of anything it touches, and organisms that come into contact with the rain lose control of their bodies, compulsively staring up at the sky. Protective equipment used by JTF, including the Black Box Mask, can resist rain erosion to some degree, but cannot completely block its effects.
Those who look up at the sky under the rain's influence will inevitably see the Hypervortex's halo, and unfortunately… by that point, there is no turning back. Directly viewing the halo instantly destroys the minds of ordinary people. Of those rescued from the ruins of New Helios after the Hypervortex's nullification, many had suffered brain death or become vegetative. Those with milder symptoms still had severe cognitive disorders, amnesia, or other post-traumatic conditions. Survivors who were fortunate enough to avoid the rain and did not directly look at the halo mostly escaped direct harm from the Hypervortex. According to feedback from Espers who participated in rescue operations, Espers can briefly look at the halo without serious injury, but will only see chaotic, bizarre images and experience tremendous pain, as if their minds were being torn apart.
Ironically, despite being an Anomaly that "cannot be looked at," its Nexus is surprisingly fragile. The Hypervortex began undergoing natural nullification from the moment it appeared, and directly looking at its core greatly accelerates the nullification process. Strangely, looking at the Hypervortex's core is harmless. The core is protected by layers of halos and thick storm clouds. The core has no describable physical form. Only "■■■■■" and "■■" truly witnessed the Hypervortex's core. According to eyewitness accounts, it looked like a "rift," or even a "wound." The erroneous info overflowing from the rift conflicted with the physical laws of reality and common sense, thus producing the phenomena including the storm and the halo.
After the Hypervortex's nullification, the damage it caused did not disappear, and the danger of secondary disasters cannot be underestimated. Surge Anomalies, primarily Protocores, appeared in large numbers within the Hypervortex's area of influence, attacking everything around them. Even after the Hypervortex's nullification, these Surge Anomalies did not vanish. Contrary to initial predictions, the Hypervortex's nullification left behind more than just ruins and rubble. Floating buildings, trees growing in reverse, steel reinforcement bars slowly branching like limbs… The city displays a twisted form of "prosperity," yet is no longer suitable for human habitation. There are detailed plans on clearing the ruins and rebuilding the city, with enormous workforces and resources being committed to the cause.

There were many witnesses to the Hypervortex, but most of them only saw the halo. Even if they were lucky enough to survive, we cannot extract useful information from them. Researchers later speculated based on the core's nature that the Hypervortex is essentially some kind of… space, region, or something similar, originating from outside our world, which intersected with ours. That world operates on a completely different logic, and the conflict caused by the leaked erroneous info led to everything that followed. We know very little about that world, but this may be fortunate. Directly viewing that world would probably fry my brain. The Hypervortex's appearance also caused some disturbances within the Circle, though those were unrelated to the Hypervortex itself.
In this Anomaly disaster, we did not come away empty-handed. We discovered… Insufficient clearance. Unable to access.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Divided into three parts: storm, halo, and core.
· Rain from the storm cloud alters physical laws, erodes material structures, and causes those who contact the rain to look up at the Hypervortex.
· Those who look at the halo suffer severe mental damage. Espers have better resistance but are not immune to it.
· The core is a rift with no describable physical form. Looking at the core accelerates the Hypervortex's nullification process.

Anomaly Nexus
The core being directly observed by someone.

Risk Assessment
Extremely high hazard. Has the potential to destroy an entire city.

Containment/Guarantee Status
The only known individual has been nullified. No containment was performed.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2037_des:
"If She Stops Dreaming of You…"

Anomaly Story

A new circus had come to town. But Alice's mother wouldn't let her go see it, saying that the circus was a vulgar, low-class form of entertainment. Instead, Alice was made to stay in her room, practice the piano, learn math, and do all those tedious, boring things.
But Alice still wanted to see the circus. So she began to dream. In her dream, she tried to create a mirror that could transport her anywhere. She envisioned every detail, from the outside in: its wood-grain frame, its smooth and reflective surface, and so on. Alice locked herself in her room and stopped practicing the piano and studying math. She neither ate nor drank. She only dreamed. Before long, the mirror was complete in her dream. She studied it carefully, as if her reflection were studying her in return. Unable to contain her excitement, Alice climbed inside. She walked through a long, dark tunnel and emerged in the center of the circus amid a blinding flash of light.
It turned out that Mr. Rabbit had been performing a conjuring act, and Alice had appeared from an empty box. The audience erupted in applause and showered Alice onstage with flowers. Alice was overjoyed. She joined the circus and performed with the troupe.
Gradually, Alice stopped trying to wake up. All she did each day was dream. Each and every day, in her dreams, she traveled through the mirror to the circus and performed alongside the troupe.
Then one day, a familiar voice suddenly rang out from the audience, interrupting the performance. Everyone turned to look. Standing among the spectators was a girl identical to Alice, who also claimed to be Alice. The other Alice ran onto the stage and confronted the original, demanding to know why she wasn't practicing the piano or studying math.
Alice panicked and asked, "Why should I have to do such boring things?"
"Because," the other Alice claimed, "you're just another version of me that I dreamed up. I needed you to do those boring things in my dreams so I'd have time to come see the circus."
Alice froze. She realized that her body was beginning to dissolve, spilling into the pool on the stage. Alice disappeared, like a drop of water vanishing into an ocean.
"Since you can't do those boring things for me," the other Alice continued,
"I've decided to stop dreaming about you entirely."

Anomaly Characteristics
The mirror's surface produces a cloudy reflection that cannot render clear shapes.
It reflects very little light, which is one reason it cannot render clear shapes.
The mirror strongly absorbs light, presumably because of the space behind its surface.
The mirror itself cannot be shattered, and any cracks caused by damage quickly repair themselves.
The mirror's surface appears to be made of a nonlinear fluid. It becomes exceptionally hard when struck with great force, but feels like a viscous, adhesive fluid when touched lightly.

Anomaly Nexus
Find the mirror that serves as the exit

Risk Assessment
Stable

Containment Status
Following its risk assessment, the Bureau has guaranteed the anomaly for use as an amusement park attraction

Containment Measures
/
Experiment Record
To explore the Anomalous Realm behind the mirror, the researchers initiated the Ariadne Project. Portions of the plan are as follows:
Researchers wear specially designed orange protective suits and explore the space in teams of four.
Everyone must carry a "Red Thread," a device that leaves marks in the form of pheromone traces. Each "Red Thread" can operate for thirty minutes.
All researchers must return to the nearest station before the "Red Thread" runs out.
The food ration consists of one raisin cake to restore energy and a serving of black tea soda to recover their sanity.
Each exploration cycle lasts seven days. After seven days, all researchers who participated in that cycle must exit the project and undergo psychological evaluations lasting from one to six months.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4007_des:
"Everything on this land belongs to me."

[Anomaly Story]
The Fogden is a self-contained space anomaly opened with the awakening of the Fog Coffin. Once the Fog Coffin opens, a portal that leads to the Fogden appears.

The Fogden is not rebuilt each round. The belongings and remains of previous participants can be found all over the hunting grounds, which indicates that the Fogden carries over between different rounds, and it is in a dormant state when no games are in session. Each time a game begins, the Fogden takes on features of the properties of that round's offerings. The "blood moon" in the final round was generated by the properties of that round's offerings.

In the final round, Code Zero appeared in the Fogden and fought the Fog Coffin Colossus. Once the colossus was destroyed, the Fogden lost its rule enforcer, the realm collapsed, and it eventually faded away.

[Characteristics]
The Fog Coffin's portal opens up for about an hour. During this time, those who enter the portal find themselves in the Fogden.
The Fogden is completely cut off from the outside world. No means of communication work inside. Even Esper abilities with communication powers do not work.
The Fogden is divided into three zones, corresponding to the three phases of hunting, traversal, and battle royale. Anyone who fails to meet the current phase's objective cannot advance.
Participants eliminated in the Fogden are transformed into Bloomhost Effigies. In addition, the Fogden hosts a powerful derivative anomaly, the Fogden-Wright.

[Anomaly Nexus]
The Fogdame's rules no longer enforceabe; the Fogden's anomalous realm destroyed.

[Risk Assessment]
Highly dangerous: The Fogden itself has powerful oddities and can cause encroachment. Participants must follow the rules to win, or be eliminated by the colossus.

[Containment/Guarantee Status]
Nullified
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2012_des:
"Boots and cats! Chika-taka! Sway to the rhythm and blow up the crowd!"

Anomaly Story
Clement Music Corner was once a lively place. Every day after school, a rowdy group of students would gather at that modest public performance plaza to set the night ablaze with beats and movement. On center stage, the DJ's fingertips would glide across the turntables, sending wave after wave of sound crashing over the crowd. Music shakes hearts, and dance moves eyes. The upbeat rhythm spread like a tide through the students, drawing more and more people into this ocean of pulsing notes.
But as time passed, as those original students gradually grew up, graduated, and left, Clement Music Corner slowly grew quiet…
…Until "it" appeared.
"Why is it so loud in the middle of the night…" The security guard at Clement Academy's east gate rubbed his tired eyes and frowned in the direction of the Music Corner.
"…Is there a performance? Didn't those kids from the electronic music club all graduate years ago…?"
Upon arrival at the performance plaza, his flashlight didn't illuminate the lively scene from his memories. There was no DJ spinning tracks, no dancing crowd. Only a set of performance equipment floating in the center of the plaza, glowing with fluorescent light. The speakers, keyboards, and screens, all covered in graffiti bearing the electronic music club's logo, seemed to have formed some kind of living creature, automatically playing a deep yet tight drumbeat. A few curious and bold students were gathered around it. Fluorescent projections filled the plaza, forming a dance floor, and the volume bars on the screen jumped restlessly to the low-frequency beat, as if plotting a wild party.
Suddenly, the display lit up brilliantly, and incredibly intense music began to blare out! Wave after wave of "sound blasts" that materialized from the rhythm came crashing toward them, and the students could only try their best to dodge, awkwardly twisting their bodies on the dance floor. The tempo kept increasing, layer upon layer of sound waves rushing at them. Some started missing the beat and were hit directly by the sound waves, sent flying to the edge of the venue, collapsing with stars in their eyes. Yet the remaining young challengers grew more and more excited as they completed the Rhythm Challenge…
"Is this… an Anomaly? I need to contact the Bureau right away!" The security guard who witnessed this hurriedly pulled out his phone, only to see a green figure dash into the plaza like a gust of wind, leaping into the center of the stage.
"CSU-2, Mint, here to assist… Whoa, what is this thing?!"
Though a bit stiff at first, Mint dodged the increasingly dense sound waves released by the equipment. Gradually, she found some patterns in the rhythm and began handling things with ease while trying to rescue those poor souls on the ground, seeing stars and occasionally getting tossed into the air by sound waves before falling back down.
PERFECT! PERFECT! PERFECT! The fluorescent big screen in the plaza displayed perfect hit judgments one after another, as the crowd of onlookers only grew larger. The green figure swiftly weaved through the dense barrage of sonic attacks, carrying the unconscious students off the dance floor one by one… Once all the students were saved, the equipment struck the final note on its keyboard with force, emitted a burst of electrical static, and scattered across the ground, returning Clement Music Corner to hushed silence.
"Phew… What a troublesome Anomaly. I need to get these students to the hospital… Huh?!"
The crowd burst into applause and cheers. Mint looked up and realized the performance plaza was already packed with an audience.
"Not a single miss! That was amazing…"
"Can you do that again? I didn't get the whole thing on video!"
"That song sounds so familiar… Could it be that genius DJ?!"
…
The security guard smiled unconsciously among the cheering crowd and began clapping along.
It had been so long since things were this lively.

Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly consists of a set of electronic music production and performance equipment. This equipment can operate without being plugged in and can combine into specific forms to move autonomously.
· This Anomaly has states similar to being deactivated and activated. When deactivated, it appears as equipment lying on the plaza; once activated, the Anomaly will float and move autonomously, challenging people in the plaza.
· When a challenge starts, this Anomaly will play electronic music and form fluorescent projections indicating the volume within the plaza. The reason it initiates challenges has not yet been determined, but it is confirmed that the Anomaly attacks according to the music's rhythm, forcing the challenged party to move to the beat. If the challenged party makes a mistake, they will be hit by a powerful sound wave attack, which can cause unconsciousness in severe cases.
· This Anomaly is suspected to possess the ability to compose music autonomously. Its musical compositions have attracted the attention and love of many citizens.

Anomaly Nexus
Within its performance area, move according to the rhythm and attack in-between to defeat it.

Risk Assessment
Moderate hazard.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not contained.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2020_des:
"Create anything just by thinking about it? Is there really such a good deal!?"

Anomaly Story
The Imaginadough is an Anomaly Product released by DSD POP. After being shaped, it can take on the appearance of nearly any material imaginable based on the creator's thoughts alone! These materials include wood, metal, gem, ceramic, and more. It is widely used in Home Decor. Notably, regardless of what material Imaginadough is shaped into, only its appearance and texture change, but its physical properties remain that of a soft dough. When exposed to extreme temperatures, pH levels, or physical impact, Imaginadough loses its form and may gradually lose its Anomaly characteristics. Under the aforementioned conditions, or after repeated use, Imaginadough loses its Anomaly characteristics and transforms into a substance similar to normal dough, composed mainly of starch and various organic compounds that are harmless to humans.

When Imaginadough is shaped into a Bio Appearance, it does not exhibit biological characteristics, but signs of instability appear. In most cases, it eventually softens back into its original dough form. In a few unverified reports, shaped creatures were said to possess brief mobility. For personal safety and mental health considerations, such attempts are not recommended.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Can take on various colors and materials according to the user's thoughts.
· Regardless of the material it is shaped into, it remains essentially a soft dough. Under extreme conditions, it will lose its shape or even its Anomaly characteristics.
· Shows signs of instability when shaped into a Bio Appearance.

Anomaly Nexus
Even though it can be freely shaped into various materials, its essence remains as soft as dough. Under extreme temperatures, extreme pH levels, or after excessive repeated use, it gradually loses its characteristics and ultimately transforms into a harmless organic dough without Anomaly characteristics.

Risk Assessment
Guaranteed by DSD POP. Sold in public circulation.

Containment/Guarantee Status
/

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
1. Experiment: Placing Imaginadough in boiling water.
Result: Imaginadough melted immediately. After approximately 5 minutes, it lost its Anomaly characteristics. We obtained a bowl of thick starch soup.
2. Experiment: Placing Imaginadough in a flash freezing environment.
Result: After approximately 5 minutes, Imaginadough had lost its Anomaly characteristics and became a normal block of starch.
3. Experiment: Placing Imaginadough in strong acid solution and strong alkaline solution respectively.
Result: Upon contact, Imaginadough lost its Anomaly characteristics. The remaining organic matter reacted with the solutions.
4. Experiment: Using high pressure to flatten Imaginadough.
Result: Even when flattened into a thin sheet, Imaginadough could still recover and maintain its Anomaly characteristics. After exceeding a certain threshold, however, it lost its Anomaly characteristics.
5. Experiment: Using a blender to break apart Imaginadough.
Result: After being kneaded back together, Imaginadough maintained its Anomaly characteristics. After repeated blending for a period, its Anomaly characteristics weakened and the materials it presented became unrealistic. After continued blending for another period, it lost its Anomaly characteristics.

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1001_des:
"Scolding and defiance, ??? turns into absolute silence. A manor built on but a single word."

Anomaly Story
Serenetti is one of the Derivative Anomalies of the Silent Garden, serving as the embodiment of the Garden's will. It is a massive, pale plant composed of vines and flowers that bind the Gardener that triggers the Silent Garden's activation. Words siphoned from the Gardener's mind randomly manifest onto Serenetti's petals, though only those carrying negative emotions seem to do so. Based on observation and speculation, the Silent Garden's activation process originates from Serenetti, spreading throughout the entire Garden. It is connected to all plants within the Garden through some form of unseen bond.
Though other vegetation in the Garden may be hostile, Serenetti itself does not display strong aggression. It serves as the core of the Silent Garden's Derivative Anomalies, and as the executor of the Garden's will, it represents absolute control over "words." It strips the Gardener of speech, restricts that poor soul's actions. It proceeds to extract their life force, reshaping it into various plants that adorn the Garden, ensuring that not a single sound disturbs the space. Despite this, Serenetti also serves to protect the Gardener. Any act of offense toward the Gardener, or any attempt at rescue, will enrage Serenetti and trigger a ferocious counterattack.
In battle with Serenetti, "words" become its power. Or rather, the malice within words is somehow converted into physical violent attacks. During combat, one might observe certain text entities laden with negative emotions taking physical form. These words have been deliberately distorted and do not represent the true intentions of the one chosen as Gardener, yet their offensive capability bears a certain correlation to the Gardener's thoughts.
Even after rescuing the Gardener from Serenetti's control, the victim will bear permanent physical and psychological damage. There is no perfect solution. As the saying often goes… some wounds never heal.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Binds the Gardener, displaying words stripped from the Gardener on its petals.
· Does not initiate attacks, but will counter actions that attempt to harm, rescue, or anger the Gardener.
· Transforms words and malice into physical attacks.

Anomaly Nexus
Eliminate or rescue the Gardener, or have the Gardener break the Garden's silence through speech.

Risk Assessment
Moderate risk.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Only appears when the Silent Garden is active; cannot be contained separately.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1014_des:
"Huh, where did my wrench go?"

Anomaly Story
The Cheek Pouch came into existence far earlier than we might imagine. This adorable little creature, counting purely by how long it has existed, has probably been around longer than most of our careers, or even ages. Since its inception, the Cheek Pouch has served the Circle, primarily Yggash Court, and become an important companion. When first discovered, it had swallowed an entire warehouse full of construction materials meant for a new experimental facility. Can you imagine how absurd it was when security personnel rushed to the warehouse, only to find a burping hamster on the empty floor?

The Cheek Pouch appears as a hamster-like creature encased in a transparent bubble, that can swallow objects far larger than itself and regurgitate them when needed. This ability makes it an excellent portable storage helper. The storage space of a Cheek Pouch is theoretically immeasurable, but that vast space is controlled by a single "Mother." The individual Cheek Pouches we use are "branches" split off from the Mother. Branch Cheek Pouches have storage space that the Mother has actively partitioned off, so their capacity is limited. Each Cheek Pouch controls an independent space, and only its holder or those with authorized access can use the Cheek Pouch to store and retrieve items. If a Branch Cheek Pouch swallows an object that exceeds its storage limit, it will vomit, causing random items to be expelled. Extra caution is advised during use to not exceed this limit.
Cheek Pouches have mimicry abilities. The form they mimic seems to depend on the Cheek Pouch's impression of its holder. Only when storing or retrieving items must the Cheek Pouch return to its original hamster ball form, but even then, it remains invisible to non-Espers. This convenience and concealment ability make it extremely useful for Intel personnel.
The mechanism by which Cheek Pouches swallow and expel items resembles deconstruction and reassembly, allowing them to swallow objects larger than their mouths. However, note that when this process occurs with living creatures, it causes severe mental trauma, as such, living things should never be stored in a Cheek Pouch. Inside the Cheek Pouch's storage space, items will not spoil or deteriorate, but damage from external forces (such as a lit bomb) still poses risks and may harm the Cheek Pouch. We do not recommend anyone attempt this.
In its non-mimicry state, the Cheek Pouch exhibits certain biological instincts. It has the ability to eat, and items it truly "eats" will not be regurgitated. Instead, they convert into energy for its activities. This is not essential, as most of a Cheek Pouch's energy comes from the Mother. Different Cheek Pouches have different dietary preferences, including soda, cake, rusted iron, plastic heated to 35 degrees, and other bizarre things. However, most Cheek Pouches prefer to eat novel objects they haven't yet tasted, which may cause certain personal belongings of the holder to mysteriously disappear. (Please note: using a Cheek Pouch to fraudulently claim work expense reimbursements is a disciplinary violation!) When multiple Branch Cheek Pouches are in close proximity in their hamster forms and the surrounding environment is safe, they exhibit certain social behaviors. Cheek Pouches with larger capacity seem to hold higher status in this society, while those with similar capacity will chase and play with each other, attempting to swallow one another to establish hierarchy, though they cannot actually accomplish this. Cheek Pouches are more affectionate toward their holders and are friendly toward others with Cheek Pouch access, but they tend to be cautious and timid around Espers who do not possess a Cheek Pouch.
Additionally, Cheek Pouches have self-defense instincts, using any items in their storage to try to protect themselves or counterattack. Some large-capacity Cheek Pouches are specifically used to store mobile bases and can construct heavily fortified facilities within minutes.

That is all the information permitted for written records. As for the origin and true nature of the Cheek Pouch, I do not know either. This little creature is cute and useful, so for now, that is all we need to know.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Normally appears as a hamster encased in a bubble, but can mimic common objects.
· Most Cheek Pouches are Branches split from the Mother, with limited and independent storage space.
· Invisible to non-Espers.
· Objects swallowed by a Cheek Pouch will not naturally spoil or deteriorate, but living things cannot be stored.
· Cheek Pouches possess biological instincts such as eating, curiosity, and self-preservation. When Branch Cheek Pouches gather, they exhibit certain social behaviors.

Anomaly Nexus
Insufficient clearance. Currently inaccessible.

Risk Assessment
Essentially harmless. Occasionally causes the user's belongings to go missing, but considering its convenience, this loss is negligible.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Contained by the Circle.

Containment Measures
Insufficient clearance. Currently inaccessible.

Experiment Records
Experimental Report on the Anomaly Cheek Pouch and Its Branches (Abridged)
Experiment 4: Testing the Cheek Pouch's storage upper limit.
Conclusion: Testing halted. We cannot fill this bottomless pit.
…
Experiment 6: Testing the Cheek Pouch's storage lower limit and the effect of partitioning storage space on the Cheek Pouch's size.
Conclusion: Storage space has no significant effect on the Cheek Pouch's size. Its minimum storage space is approximately ■■■ and cannot be further partitioned.
…
Experiment 11: Testing the energy conversion efficiency when the Cheek Pouch consumes different substances.
Conclusion: The energy converted from items the Cheek Pouch consumes is unrelated to the item's composition and seems to depend solely on volume. This energy does not return to our world in any known form. If left to eat without restraint, the consequences could be extremely severe.
…

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_5001_des:
"Hey, you're watching too, aren't you?"

Anomaly Story
A product of ours that rose to prominence alongside the rapid development of the internet.
Surely many of us have had this experience: you just wanted to watch a quick video online to relax, but before you knew it, the whole night was gone in the blink of an eye! All the plans you had, everything you meant to get done, completely wasted by your newfound lack of energy.
Doomscroll often lurks among these rolls. Viewers have their attention captured in mere seconds, maintaining a state of complete focus until the video ends, usually never noticing anything unusual. They might not even realize they had just watched an Anomaly video! After all, losing two or three minutes to Doomscroll or rolls on Bagel doesn't seem like much of a loss. Everyone has plenty of time to spare.
However, Doomscroll has recently attracted attention and sparked heated discussion online. For unknown reasons, recently trending videos have become far longer than before, ranging from three to four hours on the short end to dozens of hours at most. Being locked in front of a screen by an Anomaly video for that long is hardly comfortable, and some have even missed important matters, resulting in severe consequences. Calls for the Bureau of Anomaly Control to step in and stop the spread of such videos have been growing louder.
The Bureau has reportedly begun addressing this issue, but due to troublemakers fanning the flames and secretly spreading these videos disguised as something else, completely eliminating Doomscroll's negative effects has proven far more difficult than expected. On a positive note, there has been some progress in solving the mystery of the sudden increase in video length. Evidence of deliberate editing and splicing has been found in the excessively long videos.
The Bureau of Anomaly Control urges everyone not to click on links of unknown origin, and to plan their daily screen time reasonably to reduce the chances of falling into the Doomscroll trap.


Anomaly Characteristics
· Refers to a series of inexplicable videos with unknown creators, varying lengths, and their diverse topics of content. Their common link is that these videos are extremely captivating.
· By captivating, we mean viewers often have their attention seized within mere seconds and become deeply absorbed. In the early stages of having attention captured by Doomscroll (generally within the first minute of watching), one can still break free through sheer willpower. Though, once absorbed for too long, one can no longer escape voluntarily. Absorbed viewers become oblivious to everything around them, watching with complete focus until the video ends. Viewers have described afterward that even though the video has finished playing, their consciousness feels as if it's still trapped in the virtual world on the other side of the screen, unable to escape that state of mind for quite some time.
· Every so often, new Doomscroll videos emerge on social media, spread widely, then quickly fade from attention, in an endless cycle.

Anomaly Nexus
The video itself. Currently, the only way to end the state of capture is to watch the complete video.

Risk Assessment
Requires case-by-case analysis. Since people have gradually grown accustomed to having their attention stolen by trending videos (not necessarily Doomscroll) from time to time, tolerance for Doomscroll's effects has been surprisingly high.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Cannot be contained.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2022_des:
Heehee… no need to be scared, I'm just a wee little kite…

Anomaly Story:
