That night, like always, I was on my rooftop, taking in Hethereau's skyline. Suddenly, an orange kite appeared, hanging midair, backlit by the city lights.
I thought to myself, "If I were that kite, I could probably see all of Hethereau from that height…"
The thought flitted through my mind, and before I even registered what I was doing, my body jumped off the edge of the roof: I didn't fall, however… I had actually grabbed onto the kite in midair. The kite maneuvered through the sky as if I were as light as a feather.
"Hethereau really is breathtaking…" I whispered to myself.
At that moment, something lightly brushed my shoulder. I turned my head to look; it turned out to be the streamer trailing behind the kite—at some point, it had gotten tangled in the wind. Lit up by the city's neon lights, I noticed two dark spots and a twisted arc that had, at some point, emerged on the kite's fabric. It bore an uncanny resemblance to a human face. Straight after, the tip of the kite's streamer clutched onto my shoulder, like a pseudo-hand, with brutal force. The markings on the kite began to warp and stretch, forming a bizarre face that cackled hideously: "Heehee!"
"H-help… Help me!" 
Without thinking straight, I let go of the kite, forgetting I was still thousands of feet in the sky. Just as I braced myself to become a contemporary art piece on the pavement, there was a violent tug on my wrist. That same streamer that had initially gripped my shoulder was now tightly wrapped around my wrist. Fearing the worst, I grabbed onto the streamer and held on for dear life. At that moment, something even crazier occurred: The eerie face and behavior of the kite were wiped away entirely. Its maniacal laughter also stopped. Instead, the gentle sound of the wind was all that filled my ears. The kite no longer flew erratically or tried to scare me. Rather, it continued to softly glide through the sky.
"Can… can you take me back?" I asked tentatively.
The kite fluttered tenderly, as if nodding its head. Following my guidance, the kite wove through the towering buildings and high-rises before finally bringing me safely back to the rooftop I was standing on previously. The moment my feet touched solid ground, the kite streamer lingered in my hand, as if reluctant to let go. Eventually, it slipped away from my palm and flew off. I turned my head to watch it gradually fly off into the distance. For a fleeting moment, I had believed that the kite was entirely ordinary, nothing more.

The above constitutes an oral testimony of an anonymous passerby who encountered R-4205(Ob) Ghostly Kite.
Perhaps the Ghostly Kite isn't as evil as previously believed. Its frightening facial expressions and gestures were, maybe, a clumsy way of seeking attention. When its streamers were held tightly by human hands, it might have felt a subtle feeling of human connection. In that "connected" state, the Ghostly Kite might actually serve as a reliable air transport vehicle.

Characteristics:
· An Anomaly that tends to partake in mischief and trickery. Typically, it disguises itself as an ordinary kite, but once a human gets close, the kite's "face" distorts into a mocking expression, letting out a high-pitched cackle.
· The tail streamers seemingly possess tremendous strength. Observers have claimed that it has extreme dexterity and strength, and the ability to fly through the air at high speeds.
· However, if physical contact is made with a human, all mischievous or aggressive behavior immediately ceases, and the kite instead becomes obedient and compliant.

Anomaly Nexus:
Initiate physical contact to establish a "connection" with the kite.

Risk Assessment:
Low Risk.

Containment Status:
Currently, several specimens are contained within the Celaeno Compound. There are a few privately contained in the city, and their appearance has served as inspiration for glider designs.

Containment Procedures:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2005_des:
"The old school building you thought you'd never return to appears before you once more."

Anomaly Story
If only the school building could mysteriously vanish, then there would be no need for school to start! Surely many of us had such daydreams during our student days. But… what if this was more than just a daydream?
Many students from Clement Academy's Class of ■■■ still remember that day at the start of the semester. Everyone dragged their reluctant feet to the school gates, only to have their jaws drop at the sight before them: their grand and beautiful school building had vanished without a trace! There was nothing but a massive crater of staggering proportions in its wake… The entirety of Building D, which housed the library, had mysteriously vanished into thin air.
Recently, it was discovered that the mysterious school building connected through the Anomaly known as the Red Door bears a striking resemblance to Building D in its layout and furnishings. According to an Anomaly Hunter who visited the site, he found homework from his childhood in one of the classrooms, half finished and half torn up. This confirms that the space beyond the Red Door is indeed Clement Academy's missing school building. However, the halls no longer echo with the sounds of students reading aloud… Only the gentle sound of dust settling can be heard.
Why did the school building disappear? Why does the Red Door connect our world to this building? These questions remain unsolved mysteries, but one theory seems to have gained widespread acceptance among graduates: the building returned to this world because of our longing and nostalgia for our school days. Despite this, it exists only as a place for reminiscence and visitation, never to be truly used as it once was. No matter how much you wish to stay, you cannot stop the space from gradually crumbling, collapsing, and ultimately vanishing before your eyes. Inevitably, everything dissolves into nothingness once more, as if it never truly existed.
Some say the red color of the Red Door carries strong metaphorical meaning, and that the space beyond the red is the true reality. For details, see the film ■■■■. This theory has no factual basis, and is noted here only for reference.

The blackboard you were too lazy to erase that day. The failed test you deliberately "forgot" in your desk drawer. The little notes filled with the secrets of teenage boys and girls… Do you still remember?


Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly is a door of an unusually bright and vivid red color. It typically appears on a wall composed of common objects such as trash cans, vending machines, and similar fixtures. The objects forming the wall usually depend on the miscellaneous items near the location where it manifests, including but not limited to trash cans, abandoned furniture, manhole covers, and other items.
· The Red Door appears in an open state. The Anomalous Realm connected to the Red Door bears a strong resemblance to the missing Building D of Clement Academy in Hethereau. Some claim this space is Building D itself.
· The specific and location patterns governing the appearance of the Red Door have not yet been determined.

Anomaly Nexus
The Red Door itself. Grasping the door handle allows one to leave the Anomalous Realm.

Risk Assessment
There is minor Surge Anomaly activity within the Anomalous Realm, which exhibits aggression.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Cannot be contained.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2019_des:
"Revenge, revenge… Teehee hee!!!"

Anomaly Story
The childhood companion Anomaly "Huggy Bear" could not accept the fact that its child had grown up and no longer needed it… or worse, had forgotten about it. Instead of naturally fading away through nullification, it transformed into a more dangerous and cunning Anomaly: the "Teehee Bear."
As a branching Anomaly derived from "Huggy Bear," the "Teehee Bear" is considerably rarer.
These anomalies believe that an abandoned and forgotten bear is a coward if it does not seek revenge! After all, those little brats say things like "I love you the most!" but after a period, they just toss whatever they have to the wayside… No matter how innocent or pitiful it looks, it will never receive another glance from its former "companion." As such, the Teehee Bear will use every means necessary to make those hateful children taste the terror of being utterly alone. Whatever the children love, it becomes to lure them in. Whatever the children fear, it makes them witness… Truly terrifying.

Anomaly Characteristics
Unlike "Saddy Teddy," another branching Anomaly of "Huggy Bear" that hates all adults, the Teehee Bear hates all children. They appear as plush toy Oddities that easily win children's affection, leading them astray and even destroying them.
Childhood companion anomalies that transform into this branch are extremely difficult to deal with. They excel at appearing harmless and endearing. Each one tailors its appearance to the specific child it targets, making it often impossible to identify the Anomaly's true name.
It possesses three forms:
(1) A cute appearance used for deception (appears different to each child)
(2) A harmless version seen by adults (a teddy bear plush)
(3) An evil version revealing its true nature (the malevolent core that tears through the plush exterior, a chaotic Anomaly fusing different species)

Anomaly Nexus
Find the child who originally forgot or abandoned it, and have the child apologize to the Teehee Bear.

Risk Assessment
Hazard level is uncontrollable. Nullification should be carried out as soon as possible upon discovery.

Containment/Guarantee Status
No Containment method has been discovered. Cannot be guaranteed.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1009_des:
"The sea is bleeding."

Anomaly Story
According to the final voyage report, the Pequod had been chasing a whale for forty days. Supplies were nearly exhausted and the crew was at their mental limit, but the whale they pursued was also on its last legs. Harpoon strikes had caused the great beast to bleed, leaving a red trail across the open ocean. The whale was heading towards a field of packed ice, perhaps hoping to force the Pequod to abandon pursuit. Shortly after, both the whale and the Pequod vanished into the packed ice. No one ever saw them again, until we encountered the Sea Prisoner.

R-1851(Or) Sea Prisoner is a large Bio Anomaly resembling a whale-like creature. According to citizen reports, when traversing the undersea tunnels, one can occasionally hear "strange singing." Continuing forward leads into the Sea Prisoner's Anomalous Realm, which resembles packed ice interspersed with shipwrecks and abandoned structures. Inside this Anomalous Realm, water becomes "walkable." The surface remains liquid, but attempting to go below the surface meets resistance. The water composition is similar to seawater, but a period after the Anomalous Realm forms, it turns a vivid blood red. Though harmless to humans, its appearance is gruesome and terrifying leading frightened drivers to abandon their vehicles and flee. Those who do so soon find themselves exiting the Anomalous Realm, back in the undersea tunnel.
The Sea Prisoner appears unable to leave its Anomalous Realm. Based on certain physical characteristics, the Sea Prisoner shares similarities with the whale the Pequod was tracking, but the Sea Prisoner has many additional growths on its body. Some appear to be characteristics of other marine creatures, while others are scars from healed wounds. A massive harpoon is lodged in the Sea Prisoner's back. It is a common whaling cannon model, but far larger than any standard harpoon. The missing Pequod was equipped with the same model, but we have no way to determine whether this particular harpoon belonged to the Pequod. Nevertheless, after confirming it as a Derivative Anomaly of R-1851(Or), we still gave it the name Pequod.
The Sea Prisoner shows no active aggression, and according to those who have encountered it, the Sea Prisoner initially is friendly and seems inclined to communicate. Unfortunately, no one can understand the Sea Prisoner's singing, so what it is trying to express remained unknown for a long time. After entering the Anomalous Realm, the water eventually turns red and the Sea Prisoner exhibits extreme pain, struggling to dislodge the harpoon deeply embedded in its back. Even without malicious intent, the Sea Prisoner's massive size causes tremendous destruction when it thrashes. After being driven mad by agony, the Sea Prisoner begins attacking everything around it indiscriminately.
Those who have encountered the Sea Prisoner generally report sensing that it is suffering gravely. Having Anomalized, it cannot die, and the harpoon on its back will torment it forever. It appears to draw others into its Anomalous Realm as a cry for help, longing for someone to end its pain. After leaving the Anomalous Realm, those who have encountered the Sea Prisoner generally express concern for its condition. A small number develop obsessive symptoms regarding "helping the Sea Prisoner," but we cannot verify whether these changes stem from post-traumatic stress after witnessing its suffering, or whether the Anomalous Realm exerted influence on their minds.

In nearly all ancient beliefs, the sea was a personified deity: generous yet capricious, an embodiment of abundance and disaster alike. Majestic creatures like whales were also imbued with much mythological significance. Yet now, as reverence for the sea has been replaced by a hunger for resources, few stop to ask: What must we give in return? Will endless plundering one day invite the sea's fury?

Anomaly Characteristics
· The Sea Prisoner is a Bio Anomaly resembling a whale, with characteristics of multiple marine creatures fused together.
· A massive harpoon is lodged in its back, which is a Derivative Anomaly.
· It continuously emits singing of unknown meaning.
· It has no malicious intent, but when affected by the harpoon, it loses reason and attacks everything around it.
· No records exist of it being observed outside its Anomalous Realm, and it is unclear whether this is due to inability or lack of intention.

Anomaly Nexus
The harpoon embedded in the Anomaly's body.

Risk Assessment
Potentially high destructive power, but only within the Anomalous Realm. After entering the Anomalous Realm, getting off the vehicle immediately allows one to leave.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not in containment. Cannot be guaranteed.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
R-1851-1(Ob) Pequod
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1022_des:
"Stars reflected on the ocean's surface can be seen, but remain out of reach."

Anomaly Story:
On clear, cloudless nights, twinkling stars will be reflected onto the ocean's surface. However, observers may notice that any alteration in the sky that veils the stars will not be similarly reflected in the water's surface. Instead, the 'stars' in the ocean mirroring those in the sky may not be 'stars' at all.
Once night falls, you might occasionally spot tiny "starlings" drifting up and down on a water's surface, giving off a faint, blue glow. This phenomenon is actually a Bio Anomaly of near microscopic scale. These Bio Anomalies only become clearly visible when clustered together on the surface of a body of water. Typically, the relative positions and luminosity of these clusters align perfectly with the night sky's constellations overhead, forming something akin to a star chart on the water's surface. Because of this, the Anomaly has been deemed: "Aqua Astra".
The lifespan of a single Aqua Astra is incredibly short, often only lasting one night before undergoing natural nullification.
When the moon sets and the sun begins to rise, the glow of the Aqua Astra begins to fade. Observation and documentation suggest that Aqua Astra does not affect any other lifeforms in the same body of water it inhabits. As of right now, the only noted effect of Aqua Astra is to reflect the night sky on a surface of water.

Characteristics:
· Aqua Astra is an aquatic Bio Anomaly, with sightings recorded across multiple natural bodies of water of various sizes. As of now, Aqua Astra has not been observed in small artificial pools such as open-air swimming pools or storage tanks.
· A single Aqua Astra persists for only one night before undergoing spontaneous nullification.
· Each Aqua Astra cluster imitates a different constellation. There has been no noted documentation on how these clusters determine which constellation to replicate.

Anomaly Nexus:
Automatically nullifies after sunrise.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
Since Aqua Astra will nullify itself after a set period, no method has been found to fully contain it or trigger early nullification.

Containment Procedures:
No containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2035_des:
"Take good care of your ticket."

Anomaly Story

Kapanela rose from the icy river, soaked from head to toe and shivering in the evening wind. All he wanted to do was return home to the warmth of the stove and a dinner made by his loving mother. When he staggered to the bus stop, he realized he had missed the last bus.
"Just my luck…" he muttered, wondering about the route he would take home.
Just then, a bus pulled over by the roadside. He had never seen this bus before, and it looked nothing like any bus he had ever ridden. When the driver opened the door, Kapanela was shocked to see Xiaomin—the little dog he had once raised, who had died before he started middle school. Xiaomin had both paws on the steering wheel and wore a driver's cap.
Xiaomin honked the horn. "Hop on, Kapanela!"
"You can talk?!" Kapanela exclaimed. "I haven't seen you in so long, Xiaomin! I've missed you so much!"
Kapanela eagerly boarded the bus. As he watched the scenery pass by, he told Xiaomin about everything that had happened over the years, pouring out all his troubles about school.
The bus soon stopped at the next station, and a Frizzle climbed aboard.
"Want to try some of my French fries?" the Frizzle asked warmly. "I've never seen a human on this bus before!"
Kapanela picked up a fry from the Frizzle and put it in his mouth. It was crisp and well-salted, with the rich flavor of potato spreading across his tongue.
"It's delicious!" Kapanela cried. "Can we be friends? Then I'll have endless fries!"
"Of course! We can be best friends forever!"
The bus soon reached the next stop, where two Danzaburou climbed aboard. They appeared to be arguing, and almost looked ready to scuffle. Kapanela hurried to mediate between the two, and learned in turn that they were actually friends who were blaming each other for waking up late and nearly missing the bus! Thanks to Kapanela's mediation, they were able to agree and let the issue drop.
"Do you always mediate arguments between your friends at school, too?" one of the Danzaburou asked.
"No… I don't have any friends at school," Kapanela said. "They always bully me. One time, they even threw my homework into the river, so I had to go into the water to retrieve it. It's not so bad, though… It's not like anyone talks to me anyway. If they stopped bullying me, no one would pay attention to me at all."
"We'll be friends from now on, then."
Kapanela was overjoyed. In such a short time, he had somehow made many, many friends.
The bus stopped again, and a Mysty climbed aboard. It looked around the bus and quickly spotted the conspicuous Kapanela.
"Hey! What is a human doing here?" the Mysty demanded. "Get off, quick! We're almost at the Terminal Station. Once we get there, you won't be able to leave."
"What's at the Terminal Station?" Kapanela asked.
"I don't know. I've never been there either. They say that whether you're human or an Oddity, you only get one chance in your life to reach the Terminal Station."
"Please let me go with you, then. You're all my friends, and I've never had this many friends before. I'm having more fun on this bus than I've ever had in my life!"
Seeing that Kapanela could not be persuaded, the Mysty said nothing more.
After the bus had traveled for a while longer, Xiaomin suddenly spoke up. "Everyone, we've entered the Terminal Station. Please, look out the windows on both sides of the vehicle."
Kapanela pressed himself up against the window and glanced outside. The scenery of Hethereau was gone, replaced by a sky full of stars. More precisely, he was surrounded by stars, floating in outer space. Red, yellow, blue… Stars of every color glittered like sugar crystals. Kapanela gradually forgot the past, where he came from, his parents, the way home, and, eventually, who he was. Gazing at the vast, dazzling starscape, he exclaimed from the bottom of his heart—
"Oh my gosh, there are only stars from here on out…"

Anomaly Characteristics
In appearance, the Wayward Line has no significant differences from any other bus. Its overall body is only slightly larger.
The Anomaly has a unique ability to attract Oddities, especially low-level Oddities.
The time required for the Wayward Line to complete its entire route varies, usually depending on the number of Oddities that board at each stop.
The Anomaly can maintain a nearly constant speed while traveling. Its maximum speed ranges from roughly 40 to 45 miles per hour.
The Anomaly itself has no independent consciousness and does not respond to interference from the driver. This means the bus can easily be operated by unaffected humans or Oddities, which is one of the main reasons it is classified as an object.

Anomaly Nexus
Return the Anomaly to containment

Risk Assessment
Stable

Containment Status
Contained, with the Bureau of Anomaly Control acting as Guarantor, and operated under supervision.

Containment Measures
/
Experiment Record
The following experiments were conducted on the Anomalous Realm entered by the Wayward Line when it traveled to the Terminal Station under its own power:
Cameras and audio recorders were installed inside the bus. After it entered the Anomalous Realm, the video showed radial static, while the audio consisted of irregular low-frequency noise. The devices disconnected after a dozen seconds.
A tracked robot carrying cameras and collection equipment was used. After it entered the Anomalous Realm, its signal rapidly degraded and was lost within 5 to 8 seconds.
A low-level Oddity was used as a carrier for experimental equipment, with its behavior controlled through simple bioelectric neural stimulation. Its signal was lost instantly upon entering the Anomalous Realm.
Inference: The speed at which the Anomalous Realm blocks signals appears to correlate positively with the intelligence of those entering it. The more intelligent an object is determined to be, the sooner its connection with the outside world is lost.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1008_des:
"Lucky, Lucky… Please come back to me."

Anomaly Story
In an apartment somewhere in Hethereau, a dog named Lucky once lived with its owner, an employee of the Bureau of Anomaly Control. Lucky remembered it clearly: during that period, Anomaly cases were frequent and staff was short, so its owner had to work overtime almost every day until very, very late. Lucky, left waiting at home for its owner, felt like the loneliest little dog in the world… The owner noticed of this too, so during work, they secretly connected to the home computer's video feed. When Lucky saw its owner appear on one of the screens at home, it happily pounced forward, only to bump its nose unexpectedly. Seeing Lucky's awkward state, the owner couldn't help but laugh. Basking in the owner's smile, Lucky felt the pain in its nose fade away and stuck out its tongue, laughing along. "Once work is done, I'll come back to Lucky." Lucky remembered those words and understood that the only thing between them was this hard piece of glass that must be called "work." If only I could do "work" too, Lucky told itself, gazing at its owner hunched over the desk on the other side of the screen. If work finished sooner, the two would be reunited sooner…
Later, on one ordinary rainy night, Lucky watched its owner through the screen as usual. It noticed the owner had gotten thinner, and the dark circles under their eyes were more obvious, but the dedication to work had never changed. Lucky barked twice, trying to convey the deepest concern a little dog could imagine: Owner, you should rest! Work can be slower, Lucky isn't afraid of being lonely! Just being able to watch the owner like this is enough!
Suddenly, the screen emitted a blinding light that illuminated the entire apartment, and Lucky instinctively closed its eyes. As the light gradually dimmed and Lucky opened its eyes again, all it saw was darkness. Unable to sense its owner, Lucky frantically barked, scratched at the door, and paced around the room anxiously until it collapsed on the floor, exhausted. Lucky tried to comfort itself, thinking: The owner must be on the way home! It dragged its tired body to crouch by the door, waiting anxiously. One hour passed, two hours passed, one day passed, two days passed, but the familiar footsteps never came from outside the door again.
"Am I abandoned?" This possibility never even crossed Lucky's mind… After all, the owner said that once all the work was done, they would come back to Lucky!
A few more days passed. Lucky stared blankly at the dark computer screen, missing its owner deeply. Maybe… maybe now is the time when the owner needs me! This thought suddenly appeared in Lucky's mind. I can't just sit around doing nothing anymore. Lucky took a deep breath and opened the door.
Opened… the door…?
Lucky looked down in astonishment and found itself standing on its two hind legs, having just opened the door with its front paws, just like its owner. After a period of surprise, Lucky quickly adapted to its new body. Thinking about finding its owner filled it with strength.
A dog walking upright naturally caused quite a commotion in Hethereau. The Bureau of Anomaly Control soon received the message and, after determining it was an unregistered Bio Anomaly, dispatched two staff members to view the situation. When Lucky saw people wearing the same uniform as its owner, it happily ran up to them. Just as one of the staff was about to pull the trigger on a tranquilizer gun, the other recognized Lucky. "Aren't you Lucky? That kid in the office was always insisting on showing us photos of you!" he said, and brought Lucky to the Bureau of Anomaly Control.
The moment Lucky entered the Bureau's doors, a long-missed scent hit its nose! Following the scent, Lucky found a desk piled high with documents, with a photo framed at the corner of the desk of the owner and Lucky together. So the owner hadn't come home to be with Lucky because "work" wasn't finished! Lucky finally relaxed and grinned. It wagged its tail, wiped the dust off the photo, and then did something that shocked everyone: it began working, as naturally as could be.
The Lieutenant of ETD-4, who had rushed over upon hearing the news, stared with awe at the scene. He seemed to completely understand Lucky's feelings. This understanding Lieutenant exchanged a few words with the nearby staff, abandoned the original plan to contain Lucky. From then on, Lucky stayed at the Bureau of Anomaly Control, and was even given an official title: Agent.LUCK.
It must be said that Agent.LUCK's ability and energy amazed almost everyone. Unfinished work was like enemy number one in LUCK's eyes. As its work scope expanded, LUCK even revealed a new ability: rapidly teleporting between two lit computer screens. With this ability, LUCK could efficiently handle work from other departments.
The Bureau of Anomaly Control's search and rescue for the mysteriously vanished employee continues, but LUCK no longer worries. Deep in this dog's heart, it firmly believes that its owner is watching it work from somewhere, just as LUCK once watched its owner work through that little screen. "Once work is done, LUCK will come back to me." It seems the owner's gentle voice still echoes in its ears from time to time. So LUCK buries its head deeper in work… This is how the owner felt back then, faster, even faster! Once all the work is done, Agent.LUCK… no, Lucky will return to its owner's side, and they'll never be apart again.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Like a little dog, it has endless energy, but LUCK seems to devote all of it to work, to an astonishingly dedicated degree.
· LUCK can teleport through lit computer screens within the Bureau of Anomaly Control, helping handle work from various departments.

Anomaly Nexus
While the Anomaly is teleporting through screens, simultaneously turn off the power to both screens.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly, guaranteed by the Bureau of Anomaly Control

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2026_des:
"If you're on the train, but suddenly can't remember where you're headed, do yourself a favor—get off."

Anomaly Story:
Sometime ago, a train pulled into an underground station that had suddenly appeared out of nowhere on the outskirts of the city. Its model matched an old railcar series Hethereau retired years ago, but it had no train number, and its interior designs were unlike anything that had been produced prior. The most noticeable detail of the train was its eerie blue glow, which inevitably led to its name: the "Ghost Train".
For the most part, the Ghost Train is entirely harmless. In fact, it was ignored entirely when it first appeared. However, this changed when a famous urban explorer, Karen Wilde, launched a campaign named the "Ghost Train Dare", encouraging young daredevils and thrillseekers to camp in the station overnight to prove their fearlessness. Eventually, one young explorer attempted to board the train. His friends watched as the conductorless railcar suddenly awakened, rolled out of the station, and then, a while later, returned—noticeably without the young explorer it had left with initially. That single disappearance was enough to kick the BAC into action, leading to the lockdown of the "Ghost Train Station".
When the Bureau began studying the Ghost Train's characteristics, an owl-shaped Oddity suddenly fluttered out of the empty conductor's cab. According to this Oddity, otherwise known as Miss Levi, the Ghost Train wants something very simple: a desire to deliver passengers to their destination. After a full round of tests, experiments, and verification, the Bureau of Anomaly Control reached a conclusion: the Ghost Train did indeed wish to resemble the common metro.
After extensive safety measures were placed, the BAC eventually decided to open the Ghost Train to the public. Alongside the Zerogon Laboratory and the Ghost Train (represented by Miss Levi, the Conductor), the BAC drafted the Passenger Manual to ensure passenger safety. Any traveler who wishes to take the Ghost Train must adhere to and fully understand the Passenger Manual and pass the Ghost Train Qualification Exam at the Bureau.
The Ghost Train does not discriminate when allowing passengers aboard. It runs diligently around the clock, and always arrives almost instantaneously at the station whenever a passenger steps onto the platform. Since the train runs through the Anomalous Realm, it will sometimes mistakenly appear at the wrong station, dropping bewildered passengers off at places swarming with Surge Anomalies, which is the probable reason for the many earlier disappearances.
Miss Levi does not condone any behavior from Anomaly Hunters purposefully trying to arrive at the wrong station, and, out of a deep respect for professionalism, assists any passengers who "accidentally" end up in the wrong place. All in all, the safety of the Ghost Train, due to the BAC's efforts, has been increased considerably. Nowadays, the Ghost Train can be considered a fast, uncrowded method of traveling around the city.

Characteristics:
· The Ghost Train is a retro railcar, with its entire body shrouded in a blue glow. It doesn't require any physical tracks; instead, it opens an Anomalous Realm and travels within it.
Because of this, the Ghost Train may occasionally drop passengers off at the wrong station.
· Surprisingly, the Ghost Train exhibits both determined and stubborn behavior patterns. Records show it refusing to assist passengers who violate the Passenger Manual.
· Whenever a Wednesday lands on the same day as a full moon, the train will suspend all service for maintenance.
· Possibly due to the Train Conductor being a bird-type Oddity, the Ghost Train tends to avoid any cat-like passengers.
Therefore, as a rule, all feline animals, Oddities, or Espers with feline traits are advised not to board.

Anomaly Nexus:
Access denied.

Risk Assessment:
As long as the Passenger Manual is followed and the train is used normally, the Ghost Train is harmless.

Containment Status:
Guaranteed by the Bureau of Anomaly Control. As an officially certified anomalous transit service, it is open for public use to all citizens of Hethereau.

Containment Procedures:
No containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
To verify the accuracy of the Ghost Train Passenger Manual, Zerogon Laboratory designed targeted experiments for each rule. Only a small excerpt is recorded in this log. To access the full log, please submit a request to Zerogon Laboratory.

……
Experiment 17
Corresponding rule: Section 6 of the Ghost Train Passenger Manual: "Except on suspension days, whenever a passenger is waiting on the platform, the Ghost Train will arrive within one minute".

Objective: Verify how the Ghost Train responds to waiting passenger behavior.

Method:
On a non-suspension day, multiple test groups were arranged on the same platform for comparison:
· Group I: 1 Passenger, normally waiting on the platform;
· Group II: no humans, only a humanoid dummy placed in a waiting posture;
· Group III: 1 Passenger present, but instead of waiting at a fixed point, they walk repeatedly around the station;
· Group IV: 1 Passenger in a waiting posture on the platform, but silently and repeatedly thinking negative phrases such as "I don't need to ride" and "The train isn't coming."
The observers recorded whether the Ghost Train arrived, its arrival time, and whether the doors opened.

Results:
With test subjects from Groups I, III, and IV present, the train arrived within one minute;
Group II did not trigger any response;
In Group IV, although the train arrived, its doors never opened.

Conclusion:
The Ghost Train's judgment of "a passenger is waiting" is based on the passenger's actual presence and a recognized intention to board. Whether that intention is valid has nothing to do with outward behavior. The exact method by which the Ghost Train confirms a Passenger's intent still requires further study.
……

Derivative Anomaly:
U-5972-1(Or) Miss Levi
U-5972-2(Lo) Ghost Station
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1021_des:
"If you look down on me, I'm just gonna flat-out leave."

Anomaly Story:
Flatty is a relatively common Bio Anomaly. It looks like a flat, soft-bodied creature. It is primarily timid, gentle, and completely non-aggressive. When startled by outside stimuli, it will prioritize escape. As of right now, there have been no documented cases of aggression from a Flatty. In the occasion that a Flatty cannot escape an unfavorable situation, it will enter a catatonic state, spreading onto the ground in a puddle-like shape.
Due to its lack of aggression, a Flatty is an Oddity highly recommended as a common household pet.

Characteristics:
· Appears as a flat, soft-bodied creature with no offensive capability. When hurt or frightened, it will either feign unconsciousness or attempt to escape.

Anomaly Nexus:
Can be nullified through sufficient physical force.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
A number of Flatties are contained at the Celaeno Compound and Anomaly sanctuary, "Sunward Island". Qualified individuals may apply as Guarantors.

Containment Procedures:
No containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_5004_des:
"If we acknowledge that an individual with absolute power can abuse it against their opponents, why should we not acknowledge that the majority can do the same?"

Anomaly Story
In the narrowest sense, a "witch hunt" is a collective effort to seek evidence of witchcraft, and accuse and judge alleged "witches"; in a broader sense, it is the act of targeting or even eliminating dissenters within a group under the pretext of exposing evil during a moral crisis, a crisis of faith, or a survival crisis. The judges participating in a witch hunt may become the judged at any moment. Only by tacitly directing their attacks at a minority can they avoid bringing misfortune upon themselves. In such an environment, abnormal emotions begin to grow among the crowd: frenzy, suspicion, blind obedience… When these emotions accumulate to a certain point, the Anomaly known as "Witch Hunt" may be born.

"Witch Hunt" is an invisible Meme Anomaly. Those affected by it fall into a state of frenzy and blind faith, their consciences temporarily suppressed while their darker thoughts are amplified. In this state, people can easily lose their reason, turn resentment toward others into concrete action, and begin an actual trial and execution. Yet the crises people face do not change because of a single witch trial. After a brief period of confusion, they continue to judge the next innocent victim—Witch Hunt can even cloud its victims' minds, making them believe they are guilty.
Witch Hunt is rooted in human thought, and spreads through it as well. After coming into contact with people affected by Witch Hunt, ordinary people gradually become influenced by it, growing fervent and blindly faithful. Those who firmly refuse to participate in the witch hunt often face the fate of being judged as witches or witch co-conspirators. Only when its source—the "crisis" threatening people's daily lives—is eliminated will people end the witch hunt, causing Witch Hunt to undergo Nullification. Before long, however, witch hunts arise elsewhere, and Witch Hunt appears alongside them. This unique characteristic made Witch Hunt impossible to deal with for a long period of time.

A turning point came after a trial that affected a wide area. Because of its devastating consequences, people began to reflect on what the so-called "witches" truly were and what the witch-hunt movement actually meant. As these doubts gradually spread, the frequency of witch-hunting anomaly manifestations declined, and the scale of their influence diminished considerably. With advances in knowledge and technology, people gained more ways to access information and solve problems. They no longer relied on barbaric methods such as witch trials, and the soil that sustained the witch-hunt diminished greatly. It could no longer trigger large-scale crises.
But this does not mean Witch Hunt has disappeared from our era entirely. When the existence of Espers became public knowledge several decades ago, anti-Esper groups emerged in various places, and witch-hunting anomalies began to manifest frequently once more. Trust between humans is fragile. Whenever they encounter changes that existing knowledge cannot explain, and frenzy and blind faith once again become the norm, Witch Hunt will rise again from the depths of human thought.

Anomaly Characteristics
Born from the frenzy and blind faith of crowds, and further intensifies those emotions;
Suppresses the consciences of those affected, making them more likely to turn minor malice into action;
Spreads through interpersonal relationships and is difficult to eradicate.

Anomaly Nexus
The crisis that triggered the initial witch-hunt movement is eliminated, or the people themselves begin to question the movement's true nature.

Risk Assessment
High risk; prone to spreading through crowds.

Containment Status
Cannot currently be contained; its emergence can only be prevented.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2031_des:
"If only I could cuddle it forever…"

Anomaly Story
When a "Cuddly Bear" is no longer needed by its owner and is cast aside, it has the potential to transform into the Derivative Anomaly "Saddy Teddy."
A Saddy Teddy takes the form of a large, worn—if not damaged—plush bear. Common features include a cape and a weapon. The original discarded doll, the Anomaly "Cuddly Bear," is stuffed into the place its heart would be if the bear was a real creature. The Saddy Teddy is known to collect other abandoned toys that met a similar fate of abandonment, repeatedly tearing open its own heart to stuff them inside.
Children's picture book-like patterns sometimes appear in the area surrounding a Saddy Teddy, and can often serve as an early warning sign of its presence. According to multiple investigations, Saddy Teddies are highly hostile and aggressive towards others. Some unverified reports claim that Saddy Teddies do not attack children.
Although Saddy Teddies are hostile towards people, many eyewitness records show that they are open to cooperation with other Anomalies—to a certain extent.

Characteristics
- Appears as a worn, damaged plush bear;
- Has stitched marks over the heart area;
- Continuously collects discarded toys;
- Highly aggressive.

Anomaly Nexus
Destroy the toy(s) in its heart.

Risk Assessment
Low risk.

Containment Status
The Celaeno Compound currently contains one Saddy Teddy. Guaranteeing this Anomaly is currently prohibited.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3005_des:
"Ashes to ashes, dust to dust."

Anomaly Story:
When Dolores Constantine broke the ultimate taboo of life and death, bringing the dead back to life and avoiding her own death entirely, the "Debt Collector" manifested. To drag what should have remained dead back to the afterlife, the Debt Collector mercilessly hunted down the lives of Dolores and her machinations. Though the Constantine family managed to dodge fate once, they were unable to do so again. In the end, the Debt Collector drove the bygone Constantine family straight into ruin.

The Debt Collector is the embodiment of a Rule Anomaly with a single, crystal‑clear purpose: erase any consequences caused by those attempting to defy the natural order. In every case recorded, the Debt Collector's appearance is closely linked to the last matriarch of the Constantine family—Dolores Constantine. After Dolores used her Esper Ability to transfer the embers of her remaining life into a puppet, her drained lifespan should've ended then and there. But the Anomaly she held, "Eternal Present," shielded her life. That perverse act—the reversal of life and death, the theft of time—triggered the manifestation of the Debt Collector, which went on to relentlessly pursue the Constantine family. It's believed that the Debt Collector's ongoing attacks on its "Debtors" are its way of forcing the world back into its proper, natural timeline.
The Debt Collector itself appears as a humanoid figure wrapped in a dark cloak, with one hand replaced by a large glaive, and the other substituted with a heavy chain. Only the "Debtor" themselves, along with other Espers, can perceive the Debt Collector. It manifests at the same time every day to attack its Debtor. These attacks are usually not physical, but instead, metaphysical. That isn't to say it cannot also cause serious physical harm—if anyone interferes with the Debt Collector's collection process, it will utilize the blade and chains it is equipped with till the very end. Once suffering sufficient damage, or its given attack window closes, the Debt Collector temporarily vanishes. Current theory suggests that only by fulfilling its "Rule" and fully clearing any outstanding debt can the Debt Collector finally be nullified.



Characteristics:
· The Debt Collector appears as a humanoid entity draped in a dark cloak.
· It attacks "Debtors" who committed the highest sin: reversal of the natural order.
· Only the Debtor and other Espers can see this Anomaly.
· It cannot be entirely destroyed, only temporarily repelled.

Anomaly Nexus:
The Debt recorded in the "Tally of Ages" is fully cleared.

Risk Assessment:
Difficult to measure accurately. As a Rule Anomaly, it is almost impossible to eliminate via normal means, and can only be temporarily banished, making it extremely dangerous for the victim. On the other hand, it almost never poses a threat to anyone other than the Debtor.

Containment Status:
Not contained.

Containment Procedures:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
C-0312-1(Ob) Tally of Ages
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2016_des:
"Right here… the Ghost of art."

Anomaly Story
T-1881(Ob) Scarlet Phantom is an Anomaly that occasionally appears in performance venues such as concert halls, theaters, or cinemas. It takes the form of evening gowns in black and white, with female and male styles appearing in pairs. Though no one wears them, they float in midair, dancing gracefully together. Since Scarlet Phantoms are drawn to grand performances and naturally undergo nullification when the performance ends, they are often considered harmless. However, any attempt to disrupt the performance or stop the Scarlet Phantom's dance will provoke retaliation. When attacking, the Anomaly transforms dance steps into attacks. Though not particularly threatening to experienced Anomaly Hunters, Scarlet Phantoms often appear in groups, which significantly increases their danger level.
Some artists consider the appearance of Scarlet Phantoms a sign of success. This notion is not entirely wrong, as these entities are actually quite picky about their tastes. However, given the danger they pose to ordinary people, it would be best to notify the Bureau of Anomaly Control as soon as they are spotted, wouldn't it?

Anomaly Characteristics
· Drawn to grand performances; Attacks anyone who attempts to stop the performance using their dance.

Anomaly Nexus
The performance that drew them ends, or their dance disrupted by external force.

Risk Assessment
Low hazard. When appearing in groups, hazard level may increase to moderate.

Containment/Guarantee Status
A small number are contained at the Celaeno Compound.

Containment Measures
The containment unit should provide sufficient space for dancing. Since this Anomaly naturally undergoes nullification when the performance that attracted them ends, a large screen continuously playing classic performances that have previously attracted Scarlet Phantoms is sufficient. The playlist should be updated according to their appearance records.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2032_des:
"A relic of the past."

Anomaly Story
T-1881 (Ob) Scarlet Phantom is an Anomaly that occasionally appears at performance venues, such as concert halls, theaters, cinemas, and so on. It often manifests as black-and-white evening wear, with men's and women's outfits always appearing in pairs. The pairs of clothing will float in midair and engage in ballroom or other styles of dancing. Because Scarlet Phantom is drawn to ostentatious performances and is subsequently nullified following their ending, this Anomaly is typically considered harmless. However, disrupting a performance, or inhibiting Scarlet Phantom's dance, will trigger an aggressive response from the Anomaly. When attacking, what were once moves dedicated to dancing transform into moves for combat. For experienced Anomaly Hunters, Scarlet Phantom poses little to no threat. However, Scarlet Phantoms are known to appear in groups, thereby greatly increasing their danger to the public.
Some performers regard the appearance of Scarlet Phantoms as a sign of a spectacular performance. This belief isn't entirely unfounded, considering that Scarlet Phantoms have distinct tastes. However, it is always ideal to remain conscious of their threat levels, and notify the Bureau of any Anomaly appearances.

Characteristics
- Drawn to grand performances, they attack anyone who tries to hinder their performance.
- Recent reports indicate that when an object, imbued with intense human obsession, is present in the environment, the underlying nullification rules are severely disrupted, and a corresponding performance stage is constructed according to said obsession.

Anomaly Nexus
When the performance that attracts them ends, or when their dance steps are disrupted by an external force.
When Scarlet Phantoms are in a state where their underlying nullification logic has been disrupted, active intervention in the stage they have constructed is required, and the core entity within the area must be defeated to force the performance to conclude.

Risk Assessment
Low hazard. When they appear in groups, the hazard level may rise to moderate.

Containment Status
A small number are contained at Celaeno Compound.

Containment Measures
The Containment Units must provide enough space for dancing. Since this Anomaly is naturally nullified when the performance ends, the Containment Units should continuously play classic performances that have previously attracted Scarlet Phantoms on a large screen, and the playback list should be updated according to appearance records.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2029_des:
"Once upon a time…"

[Anomaly Story]
999 Nights is a Pop Toy type of anomaly product released by DSD. It is a board game that allows participants to step inside and experience unique adventure stories. Depending on the choices made by the participants, 999 Nights can generate completely different environments and stories, giving players a different experience every time. To be precise, the stories created by 999 Nights come from a vast collection of stories, and if all the stories were played through, 999 Nights would be nullified. However, given the immense number of stories collected, this is almost impossible. That said, physical destruction of the board game itself would also result in nullification.
DSD POP currently offers different versions of 999 Nights. Aside from variations in accessories and merch, the central anomaly board itself doesn't vary much between versions. DSD also added a wider story collection to the deluxe edition, but even the standard edition has more than enough stories to keep players exploring for a long time.

[Characteristics]
It takes the appearance of a board game. Each time players begin, the game randomly creates a customized adventure experience based on the participants.

[Anomaly Nexus]
Experience each and every story collected in 999 Nights.

[Risk Assessment]
Harmless.

[Containment/Guarantor Status]
No need to contain.

[Containment]
/

[Experiment Record]
/

[Derivative Anomaly]
/

[More Information]
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1015_des:
"Those it accepts may enter its happy little world."

Anomaly Story
Anomalies often possess some kind of extraordinary ability, and some can even rewrite reality. Morphix is one such Anomaly. We know very little about Morphix's origin, but it has likely been hiding in human society for quite some time. Had it not used its ability during the Pawn Moonlight incident and been witnessed by an Anomaly Hunter, we likely would still be unaware of its existence.

Morphix can construct a unique Anomalous Realm and set conditions for entry and exit, completely refusing entry or trapping individuals who enter it. It can freely restructure the form of its Anomalous Realm, creating complex labyrinths. For us, this would require immense spatial imagination, but for Morphix, constructing such spatial structures seems to be an ordinary instinctive ability. For any outsider who enters the Anomalous Realm, overcoming a Morphix with its home-field advantage would be a long and difficult process.
According to investigations, Morphix's appearance primarily depends on what Morphix wants to show, but it also varies based on the observer. Morphix has two most commonly seen forms: in most people's eyes, Morphix appears as a fluffy white canine creature that looks completely harmless. However, within its own Anomalous Realm, Morphix may appear as a massive white wolf with wings on its back. This is presumably Morphix's true form.

Many Anomalies can generate Anomalous Realms, but most have obvious connections and constraints between themselves and the realm they create. These Anomalies typically have only a limited ability to interfere with their own Anomalous Realm. Anomalies like Morphix, which can actively control their own Anomalous Realm, are uncommon. However, its ability to alter its own appearance is even more intriguing. This external transformation appears to result from the combined effect of its subjective intentions and the observer's objective perspective. Can it read the observer's thoughts? Why does it choose to appear harmless? When did it start hiding among human society? Is this connected to its origin?

The Pawn Moonlight incident was successfully resolved with the assistance of an Anomaly Hunter. During this incident, Morphix's identity as an Anomaly was exposed. Shortly afterward, Morphix's current Guarantor promptly applied for guardianship. This Anomaly's abilities carry significant potential risk, so the Bureau of Anomaly Control strictly reviewed the circumstances of both Morphix and its Guarantor. During the review process, Staff from the Bureau of Anomaly Control evaluated Morphix as "just an ordinary pet dog." Considering this Anomaly's high level of intelligence, lack of intent to harm others, and the fact that the Guarantor (or rather, "owner") had already proven capable of taking care of it through their prior cohabitation, the Bureau ultimately approved the application.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Morphix appears differently to different observers. Most of the time, it looks like a white, harmless canine creature.
· It can create an independent Anomalous Realm and set conditions for entry and exit.
· Within its own Anomalous Realm, it can freely alter the spatial structure.

Anomaly Nexus
Unknown. Subduing this Anomaly by force is presumed to be the most effective method.

Risk Assessment
High risk. Given this Anomaly's high level of intelligence, it is recommended to prioritize maintaining good relations with it and meeting its living needs, while closely monitoring both the Guarantor and the Anomaly itself.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Guaranteed by the individual "Boomboom."

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3007_des:
"The winds of change still blow through Hethereau." 

Anomaly Story:
Long before its delegation as an Anomaly, the "Windbringer" was revered as a manifestation of divine will. This phenomenon has been well documented by people all over the world: Overnight, a myriad of flowers will blossom simultaneously, transforming vast meadows into floral paradises. This effect can occur even in the dead of winter, when most plants have already withered. True to its name, the "Windbringer" is akin to a small breeze, leaving blooming flowers in its wake.
Across various civilizations, bearing witness to a sea of flowers brought about by the Windbringer was considered a divine gift. In recent times, many have sought to host weddings, anniversaries, or celebrations amidst the Windbringer's flowers. As a result, there have been task forces dedicated to tracking down the elusive Windbringer phenomenon. However, there remains no means to accurately predict the time and location of the Windbringer, nor a method to contain it. Consequently, many scams surround the "Windbringer Market", so caution is advised.
 Some researchers theorize that it may be a Bio Anomaly invisible to the naked eye, or an Object Anomaly that operates beneath the ground, rather than a Phenomenon Anomaly that shares striking similarities to wind. Others believe that the name "Windbringer" has encouraged numerous public misconceptions, and have put forth efforts to have the phenomenon renamed. However, the widespread and common usage of "Windbringer" has deterred this movement. To this day, many people still use this phrase when making a wish: "May the path before us be graced with strong winds and brilliant petals." 

Characteristics:
· Upon manifestation, the Windbringer will remain in a fixed location for twenty-four hours, after which it will naturally dissipate. The flowering lasts for one week, after which the plants naturally wither or bear fruit.

Anomaly Nexus:
Unknown.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
No viable method of containment has been discovered.

Containment Procedures:
None at present.

Experiment Record:
Due to the short duration of the Windbringer's appearance and no discernible method of tracking or locating the anomaly, no experiments have taken place. Based on existing observational data, the Windbringer has no visible effect on the growth of non-flowering plants. For plants induced to bloom by the Windbringer, the subsequent processes of wilting and fruting proceed in a manner restricted to natural growth entirely. Likewise, resulting seeds and fruits are indistinguishable from natural plants unaffected by the Windbringer.

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4003_des:
"May we all have a wonderful tomorrow!"

Anomaly Story
Once upon a time, there was an ordinary tree stood among many equally ordinary trees. Back then, where it grew was still a dense forest with rugged terrain, with many ferocious beasts roaming about. Residents of the nearby villages made their living from logging, and woodcutters and hunters had no choice but to venture into the forest to gather resources and hunt. One day, someone passing by this tree tied a strip of cloth to one of its branches, both to mark the path and to wish for a safe return home. Gradually, more and more people grew accustomed to leaving something under the tree, wishing for blessings for themselves and their families. This practice gave way to tradition, and as humans expanded their farmland and cleared the forest, this unique tree was preserved and given its name: Fortune Shades.
Ages passed, and towering buildings rose from the ground. Those villages of old no longer exist, having long been replaced by a metropolis called Hethereau. And yet, Fortune Shades, having weathered the years, has grown into a magnificent tree. It still watches over each person who comes to make a wish, quietly waiting for their wishes to take root and flourish. The accumulated wishes have granted it the ability to bestow happiness to a certain degree, making it a unique Anomaly. This is the origin of Fortune Shades.

Wishing under the Fortune Shades produces a sapling. When the sapling is placed at Fortune Shades' roots, it is absorbed by the tree, and people's wishes are absorbed along with it, becoming nourishment for its growth. In return, Fortune Shades provides some form of small blessing to those who make their wishes. Sometimes it's winning a free drink. Sometimes it's nearly tripping but just happening to catch a nearby tree for support. Such small strokes of luck often brighten someone's entire day. As for wishes that are harder to fulfill, such as curing a family member's illness or performing exceptionally well in an entrance exam, even if they do come true, it's difficult to credit Fortune Shades.

Based on existing evidence, Fortune Shades shares certain characteristics with ordinary trees. Fortune Shades needs to absorb people's wishes as nourishment, and to ensure people continue coming to make wishes, it offers small blessings in return. This is much like how plants reward birds with delicious fruit, so that they may carry away their seeds. However, the nourishment each person can provide is very limited, so Fortune Shades can only bring people good fortune within an even smaller scope.
For most people who wish, the act of wishing is itself a form of psychological comfort. Often, the act of wishing matters far more than actually receiving anything in return. From the days when we ate raw meat and tilled the land with fire, to today's age of towering skyscrapers… wishing has always carried humanity's hopes for a better tomorrow. It is the determination to pursue happiness and the courage to overcome hardship. Fortune Shades watches over those who work hard for a better tomorrow day and night, drawing nourishment from their pursuit of happiness, and giving each person who tries their best its own small gift.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Wishing under Fortune Shades produces a sapling. Returning it to the roots allows Fortune Shades to absorb both the sapling and the wish.
· Pure and sincere wishes will receive blessings from Fortune Shades.

Anomaly Nexus
Extended periods without wishes, causing accumulated power to be depleted.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Given Fortune Shades' fame, difficulty of relocation, and symbolic significance, on-site containment measures have been adopted. It is supervised by the Bureau of Anomaly Control, with maintenance handled by the Hethereau Municipality.

Containment Measures
Early plans called for transplant containment measures, relocating Fortune Shades to Celaeno Compound for containment. However, Fortune Shades loses its power upon leaving its original coordinates and recovers only upon returning. Considering the difficulty of containment, safety, and symbolic significance, on-site containment measures were adopted for Fortune Shades, supervised by the Bureau of Anomaly Control with maintenance by the Hethereau Municipality. After the failed transplant attempt, Yggash Court classified Fortune Shades as a Location Anomaly.

Experiment Records
1. Experiment: Removing a sapling from Fortune Shades.
Result: The sapling disappeared after leaving Fortune Shades.
2. Experiment: After wishing, not placing the sapling at Fortune Shades' roots.
Result: After 300 seconds, the sapling disappeared.
3. Experiment: Wishing at the Fortune Shades to see the deceased ■■■ once more.
Result: The wish was not fulfilled.
Note: The one who made the wish was Researcher ■■■, who did not complete the required application and registration before conducting the experiment. Researcher ■■■ claimed they visited in a personal capacity and did not need to follow procedures. They have been formally reprimanded.
Note 2: Researcher ■■■ claimed to have seen the deceased ■■■ in a dream and said their final goodbye. There is no evidence linking this event to Fortune Shades.

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2008_des:
"We poked a small hole between reality and illusion, and a torrent of wild imagination came flooding through."

Anomaly Story
There once existed an avant-garde art collective composed of extraordinarily talented writers. They organized a creative technique exchange, with this collision of ideas flowing from their pens as ink. Ideas converged into the invisible current of thought that gave birth to countless magnificent imaginary worlds and unforgettable stories. As time passed, the participants in this creative endeavor felt their obsession grow, as if enchanted by the words they wrote, rushed forwards by this torrent of thought to ink the next stroke to paper. One day, they all gathered together, claiming they would explore "the ultimate nature of consciousness," then entered a mansion together and shut themselves away from the world.
At first, people assumed this was merely an ordinary creative retreat. For eccentric and talented writers, this was nothing unusual. But from the day they entered the mansion, its doors never opened again… Their servants, friends, and family members visited out of concern, yet not one of them could pry open the mansion's doors. Several weeks later, the mansion doors suddenly creaked opened on their own. However, what emerged was not the writers, but a true torrent of consciousness. Every area it touched was transformed into a bizarre and surreal scene! By then, that door had become an Anomaly passage connecting reality to the "World Beyond the Door," spreading out of control. Fortunately, it was contained by an independent Anomaly Hunter group before its influence could spread further. After changing hands several times, it is currently held by the Ebisu Auction House.

Outside the Inner Door, designated R-3407(Ob), appears as a door composed of stained glass panels. The other world it opens to, which we call the World Beyond the Door, is a chaotic space formed from its creators' wild imaginings. When this Anomaly is opened, a surging "torrent of consciousness" flows out in an instant, sweeping through the area. Everywhere it extends through gradually becomes part of the World Beyond the Door, eroded by maddened consciousness. It becomes a zone where gravity acts abnormal, space becomes fragmented and twisted, and creatures that should not exist in reality manifest freely. The range of this Anomaly expands rapidly, and historical observation records show no limit to its expansion. If left unchecked, the World Beyond the Door will become large enough to devour an entire city in approximately eight to nine months.
Once opened, due to spatial displacement, Outside the Inner Door manifests as multiple doors as its area of influence expands. Only one of these doors, the final one, is the true form of this Anomaly. The doors are connected by the "torrent of consciousness," which also serves as the primary means of movement between the fragmented spaces of the World Beyond the Door. As long as all the doors are closed, Outside the Inner Door will maintain the appearance of an ordinary door. Therefore, in theory, following the "torrent of consciousness" and closing each door one by one should allow for the containment of this Anomaly. However, it should be noted that the essence of the "torrent of consciousness" is a maddened consciousness. Anyone submerged in it will inevitably be affected, experiencing visual and auditory hallucinations, or developing more severe mental issues. During the containment process, one must watch for another relatively inconspicuous substance in the World Beyond the Door: the "droplets of reason." Like the "torrent of consciousness," these appear to be liquid in form, but unlike the ceaselessly surging torrent, they are often stationary spheres of water. Touching the "droplets of reason" will reduce the mental contamination suffered during the containment process, and also stabilize the surrounding "torrent of consciousness" to some degree, allowing passage with less risk to one's sanity.
Touching the "droplets of reason" is not without a price, however. Outside the Inner Door was born from the wild imaginings of writers, and reason is like poison to them. Touching the "droplets of reason" will provoke retaliation from the Anomaly. This retaliation is sometimes in the form of Surge Anomaly attacks, sometimes sudden hallucinations, or attacks fabricated by the consciousness within the unstable "torrent of consciousness"… The longer you take, the more difficult this Anomaly becomes to resolve.

Every era has great minds that attempt to transcend their limits. Some are called geniuses; others are dismissed as madmen. Their ideas may seem too bizarre to ordinary people, even touching the edge of madness, but they are equally captivating. Their wildest ideas may never normally become reality, but Anomalies have the power to make the impossible possible. Outside the Inner Door gives us an opportunity to glimpse a corner of their unknowable minds.

Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly appears as a large door made of stained glass panels. Behind the door is a World Beyond the Door that does not follow the rules of reality.
· When this Anomaly is opened, a water-like "torrent of consciousness" surges forth. Everywhere it passes is eroded by the World Beyond the Door and becomes disordered. The erosion range expands over time.
· Multiple doors appear within the affected area of the World Beyond the Door, interconnected by the "torrent of consciousness." One can move through the "torrent of consciousness."
· Immersion in the "torrent of consciousness" causes hallucinations and mental issues. Touching the spherical "droplets of reason" can alleviate symptoms but will also provoke hostility from the Anomaly.

Anomaly Nexus
Close all doors connecting reality to the World Beyond the Door.

Risk Assessment
Medium.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Guaranteed by the Ebisu Auction House.

Containment Measures
The closed Outside the Inner Door can be stored in any space large enough to accommodate it. Considering that opening the door is the trigger for an breach, it is recommended to lay it flat on a solid surface.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1017_des:
"We have a way to punch through any communication barrier—the phone? Nah, I'm talking about Chuppa."

Anomaly Story:
The Bureau of Anomaly Control has a myriad of tools at its disposal, and U-0734(Or) Chuppa is easily one of the more common ones. How this Bio Anomaly, which resembles a long-eared flying squirrel, manifested is strictly confidential. Compared to the Bureau's large workforce, usage rights for Chuppa are reserved for a small subset of personnel—aside from a few key staff in each department. Typically, Chuppa usage is limited to field agents like the Containment Strike Unit and the Enforcement Tactical Division, who work extensively with Anomalous Realms.
Normally, an Anomalous Realm blocks all regular communication signals. Chuppas, however, cut straight through any interference. When cleared to use Chuppa, you can summon it nearby at any time. Through the Chuppa, tone, voice, and cadence can all be replicated and transferred, with slight distortion occasionally occurring. Those who do not have personal access to a Chuppa can still interact with one summoned by someone else.
Regardless of when or where it's summoned, the Chuppa itself remains the same. Once dismissed, it disappears entirely. The science behind this phenomenon is deeply complex and an unnecessary tangent. Although classified as a Bio Anomaly, Chuppa behaves more like an Object Anomaly—it does not need food, has no fear, and works without complaint—to the point that it's rumored to be a BAC surveillance tool.

Characteristics:
· A Bio Anomaly resembling the common pteromyini, otherwise known as a flying squirrel.
· Can negate communication interference in most Anomalous Realms.
· Appears when called upon by any user with clearance.

Anomaly Nexus:
Information restricted due to insufficient clearance.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
Secured by the Bureau of Anomaly Control.

Containment Procedures:
Information restricted due to insufficient clearance.

Experiment Record:
"Abridged Research on Communication Capabilities of Anomaly: 'Chuppa' in Various Anomalous Realms"
……
Based on multiple experiments conducted on Chuppa's communication abilities in several Class V and lower Anomalous Realms, our conclusions are:
1. Chuppa can establish communication within the vast majority of known Anomalous Realms. However, in higher-level Anomalous Realms, the Chuppa's "signal" is subject to stronger interference, affecting both the quality and speed of its communication.
2. Despite being a Bio Anomaly, Chuppa exhibits almost no instinctive biological behavior. Even in Anomalous Realms that negatively affect biological beings, the Chuppa remains unaffected.
3. There are dedicated usage hours for the Chuppa: during business hours, casual Chuppa usage is strictly prohibited.

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1020_des:
"Two-headed, Two-faced."

Anomaly Story:
N-6174(Or) Divergent Flower is a newly discovered Anomaly. It is presumed to have originated somewhere outside Hethereau, and has only been sighted in Hethereau relatively recently.

Divergent Flower displays a hybrid of plant and animal traits. It possesses limited intelligence but has unique spatial awareness and is primarily driven by its instinctive nature. A Divergent Flower sprouts two separate heads. The Divergent Flower is primarily carnivorous and must eat consistently to survive. The heads of the Divergent Flower are seemingly two separate entities, and will attack and provoke each other occasionally. In extreme cases, aggression between the two heads can lead to critical injury, and sometimes, nullification.
When attacking, the Divergent Flower will utilize its limbs, tails, and heads as weapons. Additionally, the Divergent Flower can produce and expel hallucinogenic pollen. Any ingestion of a Divergent Flower's pollen can cause brief hallucinations and a disruption in judgment.

Of the few records on Divergent Flower, it is indicated that its lifecycle is similar to that of a regular plant. When a Divergent Flower reaches the end of its life, it will rapidly wither and become inert, leaving behind two seeds from each head, which can potentially grow into a new Divergent Flower.

Characteristics:
· A two-headed Bio Anomaly, half flora and half fauna.
· Highly aggressive;
· Capable of expelling hallucinogenic pollen.

Anomaly Nexus:
Can be nullified through both natural and unnatural death.

Risk Assessment:
Low Risk. Long-term observation is required to determine an increase in risk level.

Containment Status:
Not contained.

Containment Procedures:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2034_des:
"I hear you—your resentment, your anger, your cries of anguish… Pray to me, and I shall grant you supreme happiness."

Anomaly Story
Throughout history, with the emergence of the witch-hunt anomaly, victims who fell prey to human malice would crystallize into blood-red stones that radiate a crimson glow. Their souls, filled with resentment and unwillingness to accept their fate, would be imprisoned within, suffering endless torment and crying out day and night. If they are fortunate enough to be purified, those aggrieved souls will return to their original bodies, given a chance to rekindle the flame of life. But if they fail to receive timely purification, the bloody radiance of Oracle Stones will gradually fade, until it is completely consumed by the black taint of resentment.
At present, the only known way to purify Oracle Stones is through the power of the anomaly Blackbird. For more than five hundred years, Blackbird has diligently purified countless Oracle Stones scattered across the world since the witch-hunt era. However, most of those Oracle Stones are black, and no matter how much they are purified, the souls within can no longer return to the ranks of the living. All Blackbird can do is drive away the nightmares that have haunted them for centuries and pray that the souls who have endured centuries of suffering may finally sink into a peaceful slumber.
In the world of today, there is no longer any place for the witch-hunt anomaly to exist, and as civilization has advanced, the number of Oracle Stones has consequently dwindled. As the anomaly's power has weakened, Oracle Stones no longer carry the weight they once did. The Oracle Stones we encounter today are more often crystallizations of the malice within people's hearts. Yet Blackbird's work remains unchanged. Black birds still bring her glittering stones from all corners of the world, and she continues to purify them with the same devotion and diligence as she once did, until pure light envelops the Oracle Stones and one more trace of malice is erased from the world.

Characteristics
Throughout history, the souls of victims who fell prey to human malice would crystallize into Oracle Stones that radiate a blood-red glow.
If a red Oracle Stone is purified in time, the soul within will return to the world of the living. If it is not purified, the Oracle Stone will gradually be consumed by black taint, and the soul will never be able to return to life.
At present, the only known way to purify Oracle Stones is through the power of the anomaly Blackbird.
Oracle Stones have lost their original significance in the modern world, and the Oracle Stones we encounter today are more often crystallizations of the malice within people's hearts.

Anomaly Nexus
Being purified by the anomaly Blackbird.

Risk Assessment
No risk.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not in containment.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2036_des:
"My entire life has been utterly, utterly ordinary."

Anomaly Story
Several monkeys were placed in an experimental enclosure, with food suspended above their heads. At first, every monkey desperately reached out for the food. But whenever one of them touched it, they were all visibly punished.
Gradually, the monkeys realized the pattern. Therefore, they all chose to stop reaching for the food.
Then, a new monkey was placed in the enclosure. Instinctively, it reached for the food, but the moment it tried, the other monkeys prevented it from doing so. Before long, the new monkey stopped thinking about the food above its head entirely.
Every monkey introduced afterward went through the same procedure. Eventually, even after all the original monkeys had left the enclosure, the remaining monkeys still refused to touch the food above them. Some of them may never have tried to touch it, even if they were never punished for doing so in the first place. Or perhaps the original rule—that touching the food would result in punishment—had ceased to exist long ago. None of the monkeys would ever know, however.
…
Although this is an Anomaly Profile, I still wanted to preserve the thought experiment above. We live in an orderly society, where many of the rules have no clear origin—much like the later-generation monkeys, who did not know why they could not touch the food above them. As ordinary people, we cannot afford the cost of defying the rules. All we can do is comply.
The Anomaly "Dreamaway Pillow" presents us with a similar Dreamscape: all you need to do is follow the crowd, hide in the shadows, and do what you are "supposed" to do. Deviant behavior is not permitted. As long as you follow everyone's choice and remain an ordinary person, you can obtain stable happiness for next to nothing.
The concept of a "pillow" has existed since ancient times, while the "Dreamaway Pillow" evolved from the modern soft pillow. This does not mean that such ideas only began to emerge in the modern era. Perhaps it is only now that we have the opportunity to rationally observe our own behavior—and that of the group as a whole.

Anomaly Characteristics
The "Dreamaway Pillow" appears to be an ordinary soft cotton pillow. When unused, it does not affect its surroundings. If someone uses the Anomaly pillow to fall asleep and enter a dream, the dream manifests as several consecutive, bizarre rooms, with indescribable monsters circling overhead, as if constantly monitoring the dreamer's every move.
