This Anomaly only affects the images presented in people's dreams. It does not create a real Anomalous Realm.
Once someone uses the Anomaly to enter a dream, everyone else within a certain range will continue having separate dreams within the same environment until the Anomaly undergoes Nullification. The affected range varies, and it is currently believed that the number of affected people is capped, though at what number remains unknown. When the surrounding population is more dense, the affected range becomes significantly smaller.
The affected range moves as the user moves through space. In other words, if the user leaves the original area and enters another, the original area will no longer be affected by the Anomaly.
Most people will unconsciously perform the same actions as those around them in the dream. A small number of people have reported waking up within the dream and voluntarily leaving the crowd, only to be attacked by the monsters overhead. They immediately wake up and are unable to enter a dream again until the Anomaly undergoes Nullification.
Studies indicate that the Anomaly generally does not affect sleep quality. Some subjects reported feeling more relaxed upon waking after following the crowd and performing the same actions in their dreams.
The Anomaly's effects are automatically lifted when the pillow's user leaves the "room" in the dream. Users who leave the room cannot use the Anomaly to enter a dream again.

Anomaly Nexus
The user successfully leaves the room in the dream

Risk Assessment
No Risk

Containment Status
Uncontained
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4002_des:
"The justice we represent must be justice for all."

Anomaly Story
Long before Hethereau's justice system was as well developed as it is today, the mysterious and powerful Anomaly known as Justice Executioner had already been officially registered. According to existing records, this Anomaly is normally invisible, believed to lurk beneath the city's roads. It resides somewhere deeper than the darkest sewers, in a place that cannot be observed or reached… Notably, Justice Executioner is not a single entity, but an entire forest of steel traffic lights. It is said that this forest listens to the pulse of every road in the city, and when a perpetrator whose crimes have reached an extreme appears, it randomly selects a car near the offender. A giant traffic light tree then bursts from the ground and takes control of the vehicle, temporarily utilizing it as a vessel for executing punishment. Perhaps from this, one can speculate that the Anomaly originally emerged from citizens' frustration with frequent traffic chaos and their strong desire for just law enforcement. In reality, very few people have actually seen Justice Executioner, since troublemakers can be handled by Security Officers and Officer Whiskers nowadays. Only the rare few thugs that even the Security Office struggles to deal with will disturb this dormant Anomaly, and they usually collapse before they even realize what terrifying colossus stands before them. Put simply, they faint from sheer fright… What kind of punishment Justice Executioner inflicts upon these people, how it hands criminals over to the Security Office for official processing, and why almost everyone refuses to speak of those encounters remains unknown to us.
Due to its rare appearances, Justice Executioner has gradually become regarded as one of Hethereau's many urban legends, though it carries a certain deterrent power that ordinary rumors lack. Some parents embellish stories about Justice Executioner to tell their children, using them to teach obedience to the law. For example: "Stay close to adults when crossing the street and don't run around, or the monster hiding underground will take away naughty children." "You can't just take other people's things. That monster who loves children the most will come catch you if it finds out." "Those bullies who always pick on others will definitely be defeated by that justice-enforcing Anomaly no matter where they run!" And so on… As you can see, the duties Justice Executioner has taken on in folklore have exceeded its actual responsibilities, having become a symbol of absolute justice. For ordinary citizens, its existence is like a blade lurking in the shadows, ignored most of the time. But once an uncontrollable situation occurs, it will exercise its authority and eliminate all threats to peace.
As mentioned earlier, Justice Executioner is an entire forest of traffic lights. Interestingly, Officer Whiskers are said to live within this tangled jungle of branches, forming a peculiar symbiotic relationship between these anomalies. Therefore, some anomaly researchers speculate that the Whiskers help maintain and repair Justice Executioner's traffic light branches. In return, Justice Executioner provides the Officer Whiskers with a place to rest and train. Whatever the true situation may be, their cooperation has remained remarkably stable and harmonious to this day.
As a member of ETD-6 once claimed: "Justice delayed is justice denied." This powerful Anomaly seems to share this view, rising from the ground when the Security Office is overwhelmed and extinguishing all violence within its Anomalous Realm in a timely manner. With such powerful and decisive methods, Justice Executioner serves as the Security Office's most formidable secret weapon, safeguarding this city's peace and tranquility.

Anomaly Characteristics
· An extraordinarily powerful Anomaly that only appears when city crime reaches a certain level, pulling perpetrators into its Anomalous Realm.
· Not a single entity, but an entire forest of traffic lights. Officer Whiskers are said to reside within it.

Anomaly Nexus
Insufficient permissions. Currently unable to access.

Risk Assessment
Extremely high hazard. Does not normally appear. Only manifests when major criminal incidents occur.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly. Guaranteed by the Security Office.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1019_des:
"Those who dream, stay dreaming. This is deemed the First Law of Somnodynamics."

Anomaly Story:
Wakeybee is an Anomaly that has extensive documentation. Scattered records of its presence show up all throughout history, with a primary focus on the unique honey it produces. There is written evidence of Wakeybee honey being utilized in historical battles, assassinations, and so on.
The Wakeybee has the appearance of a common honeybee, though far larger in size. When flying, their wings produce almost no sound. As a result, Wakeybees can approach drowsy individuals and siphon their "sleepiness". Those that are siphoned by the Wakeybee often claim that they were not aware of the siphoning itself, but that they felt incredibly energized post-siphoning. Individuals experiencing severe sleep deprivation have a higher chance of attracting a Wakeybee.
The Wakeybee has the unique ability to utilize siphoned fatigue, drowsiness, and exhaustion, and transform it into Somnosweet—the Wakeybee's distinctive honey product. When ingested, Somnosweet can be used as a sleep aid. However, excessive ingestion of Somnosweet can result in extreme mental fatigue and can even be fatal.

Somnosweet is primarily used by those who need assistance with adjusting their sleep schedules. This can be due to a change in routine, a malfunctioning circadian rhythm, or individuals suffering from extreme insomnia. However, it's imperative to note that Somnosweet is only a temporary solution for the challenges previously listed. Getting proper, natural rest takes precedence over any Somnosweet-induced respite.

Characteristics:
· A larger version of the common honeybee.
· Primarily survives through the siphoning of fatigued individuals.
· Absorbed fatigue can be converted into Somnosweet by the Wakeybee.

Anomaly Nexus:
Nullification occurs if absorbed fatigue is insufficient over long intervals.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
A certain number are contained at the Celaeno Compound and the Anomaly sanctuary, "Sunward Island". Qualified individuals may act as Guarantors, but no Guarantor may keep more than one Wakeybee, and any Somnosweet obtained may not be privately traded or gifted.

Containment Procedures:
No special containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
"Preliminary Study on Anomaly 'Wakeybee' and Its Honey Production"
Case Overview: The limits of Wakeybee in resisting drowsiness.
Wakeybees exclusively siphon from human subjects; thus, no research can currently be conducted on Wakeybee siphoning for ethical reasons. As a result, we must observe historical usages of the Wakeybee. Based on recorded history, the longest documented duration a human remained awake due to Wakeybee siphoning is 140 hours. Disclaimer: We do not condone nor encourage the usage of Somnosweet or the Wakeybee to remain awake for extended periods of time. The effect of the Wakeybee's siphoning only gives the illusion of fatigue removal. The body and mind will still suffer from sleep deprivation, which can lead to serious health problems.
Below are some related case records:
……

Clinical Trial: Safe Dosage of Wakeybee Honey
Test subject ■■■ volunteered to test Wakeybee honey effects, while explicitly under the protection of an Anomaly capable of forced mental stimulation. For this trial, we served the subject different dosage amounts at fixed times during the day to observe the effects of dosage amount. When a single dose exceeded 50g, the subject stopped responding to most conventional waking methods. When a single dose exceeded 80g, the subject's breathing and heartbeat were both significantly suppressed—suppression that lifted immediately upon waking.
We recommend that the daily intake of Wakeybee honey not exceed 15g, and that continuous use be heavily limited and monitored. Relevant experiment records are as follows:
……

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2015_des:
"Home is the source of our strength."

Anomaly Story
Long, long ago, a count signed a contract with the devil, gaining all the world's riches and glory, and in exchange becoming a vampire who sustained eternal youth by drinking human blood. As the price, he could never leave his own domain. The count soon grew weary of the familiar flora and fauna, birds and beasts, fish and insects on his land. Even the blood offered by his trembling subjects became difficult to swallow down. He devised a solution: using soil from his domain, he crafted a perfect miniature castle model, then used magic to shrink himself down and live inside it. This way, as long as he carried his "castle" with him, he could venture anywhere beyond the walls he had long been confined to. Four hundred years later, he chanced upon a beautiful lady…
These Legendary tales are of course fabricated by later generations, but the castle at the root of this legend, the "Hospitable House," does exist. Records and legends about the "Hospitable House" date back centuries. Very few Anomalies can persist across such a long span of time without undergoing nullification. The origins of the "Hospitable House" can no longer be traced. It has continuously changed hands among collectors, and currently belongs to the collection of the antique shop "Eibon."

The Hospitable House appears to be a miniature castle model. Its interior is exquisitely decorated with complete sets of furniture. Setting aside its size, it is practically a fully livable castle. The appearance and decor of the Hospitable House change slightly with the times, making it impossible to deduce its era of origin from its architectural design or interior decoration style. Today's Hospitable House has complete water, electricity, and lighting facilities for "guests" who enter to use freely. How these facilities operate without any actual utility connections remains an unsolved mystery.
After opening the door to the Hospitable House, humans within a certain range (as well as certain Oddities) are recognized as "guests" by the Hospitable House. "Guests" are shrunk to a size matching the Hospitable House and can temporarily enter for a tour. During this process, the guests' personal items are also shrunk along with them and continue to function normally. The shrinking effect lasts for 7 minutes, after which "guests" are teleported outside the Hospitable House and restored to their original size. Opening the door again allows another tour, but each visit is limited to 7 minutes. This has caused no end of frustration for directors hoping to use the Hospitable House's interior for filming.
The shrinking limit does not apply to those the Hospitable House recognizes as "masters" or "enemies." These individuals do not automatically return to normal size after shrinking, and only the "master" knows how to restore them. The Hospitable House is as sturdy as a real castle, allowing this otherwise harmless Anomaly to protect its "master" or trap "enemies" when necessary. Once, a thief accidentally touched the door of the Hospitable House and remained shrunk for an entire night. Only after swearing to the Hospitable House's "master" that he would turn over a new leaf, he was restored to his original size.

The Hospitable House's long existence without nullification has piqued the curiosity of some scholars: what is its Nexus? One theory, drawing from the legend, suggests that the Hospitable House's Nexus is its "homeland," the place where it was first born. Though unverifiable, the Hospitable House's "homeland" is likely a settlement that still exists. Until that place is destroyed, the Hospitable House will continue to exist. This also explains why the Hospitable House's decor and facilities keep up with the times. The development of its homeland is reflected in the Hospitable House, and it delights in showing visitors the progress of its hometown.
This theory has not been confirmed, but in this writer's opinion, it is quite romantic. For an Anomaly with many legends that is safe and harmless, maintaining its mystique and leaving room for imagination may be the best outcome.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Appears as an exquisite miniature castle model.
· After opening the door to the Hospitable House, humans within a certain range (as well as certain Oddities) are recognized as "guests" by the Hospitable House and shrunk to a size that allows them to tour the castle.
· The shrinking effect lasts for 7 minutes. Playing the pipe organ inside the Hospitable House can end the tour early and restore visitors to their original size.
· The 7-minute time limit does not apply to those the Hospitable House recognizes as "masters" or "enemies." Only the "master" of the Hospitable House knows how to restore them.

Anomaly Nexus
Unknown

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Given that the Hospitable House does not move on its own and poses no danger, it was decided after evaluation not to contain it. Currently part of the Eibon Antique Shop Collection.

Containment Measures
No special containment measures required.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2027_des:
"If this world holds only sorrow, then rest here awhile."

Anomaly Story
R-4321[Ob] "Dimension Visitor" is, in essence, an ancient nautical astrolabe. Beyond locating physical directions such as north, south, east, and west, as well as the positions of stars in the cosmos, it possesses a strange ability: it can point toward where the heart belongs, the path to hidden treasure, those with potential, and more. The ancient astrolabe was kept in an equally ancient hidden village. The villagers used it and worshiped it, yet they never spoke of it to outsiders, nor did they use its power for immoral ends. Grateful for their kindness, it formed a contract with the villagers and granted them long lives.
Those peaceful days lasted until word of the "long-lived village" eventually reached the outside world. Rumors grew and spread until the villagers were forced to leave their home and become trapped in a cruel "game." Tragically, the village's already scarce bloodline was completely extinguished in that game, and the organizers were disappointed to discover that they truly were only ordinary people who lived a little longer. Realizing that everything they had done had been meaningless, the powerful complained and walked away. Dimension Visitor was left adrift amid this undeserved chaos. Yet to the very end, everyone still prayed to it and protected their shared secret. Dimension Visitor felt confusion, bewilderment, and endless loneliness. But how was it supposed to process emotions that "should have belonged to humans"? Unfortunately, the astrolabe could not point the way to its own future. Thus, it developed a desire to "escape," giving birth to the Anomalous Realm known as the Corridor of Echoes.
Taking on the appearance of its last contract bearer, Dimension Visitor has wandered for ages at the entrance to the Corridor of Echoes, fulfilling the astrolabe's original purpose: speaking with every visitor likewise drowned in the past and guiding them toward "escape." The present no longer exists, and even the future will someday become the past. Perhaps in this way, it can forever keep the contractors it once knew, and the kind people who live on in its memories.

Characteristics
Its true form is an ancient nautical astrolabe with a strange ability to form contracts with people and grant them long life.
After all of its contract bearers passed away, the astrolabe was left adrift. It eventually took on the appearance of its final contractor and began wandering the entrance to the Corridor of Echoes, an Anomalous Realm born from its will.
It speaks with every visitor similarly lost in the past and guides them toward "escape."

Anomaly Nexus
Insufficient clearance. Currently inaccessible.

Risk Assessment
Low risk.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly. Not currently contained.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1026_des:
"Through rain and shine, the vines live on."

Anomaly Story
.Roughly a dozen years ago, a forest fire broke out in the mountains near Hethereau. The flames spread with alarming speed, making the situation extremely difficult to control. At the same time, abnormal fluctuations in the Wertheimer Index were detected within the fire zone, making any reckless entry potentially dangerous. Just as the firefighters found themselves unable to advance or retreat, they saw a giant vine rise from the center of the burning area. What followed was a localized downpour that lasted more than ten hours. The fire was extinguished in time, but the rain was so heavy that the forest became marshland. After extensive experiments and research, scholars determined that the giant vine had been formed by many smaller vines of the same kind winding together and expanding. The vine-like Anomaly that had rendered such great service during the fire was therefore collectively named R-2340[Or], also known as "Weather Vine."
As its name suggests, Weather Vine can alter the weather in a small area according to its own condition. The fastest way to distinguish it from ordinary vines is to check whether one or more drop-shaped blue "Vine Pearls" grow on its tendrils. When it senses a lack of water, Weather Vine disregards the local geography and causes rain to fall in the surrounding area to water itself. Researchers found that the plant rapidly expands when burned by flame, increasing the range over which it can alter the weather. However, this behavior is undoubtedly devastating to Weather Vine itself. After the forest fire mentioned above, the giant Weather Vine gradually returned to its original size, but the exhausted plants permanently lost their Vine Pearls and became no different from ordinary vines. Some even withered away. Around those dried vines, however, people found new plants quietly taking root. This clever Anomaly had used cooperation to withstand disaster and protect the seeds of its group.
Weather Vine's remarkable ability allows it to survive almost anywhere it can take root. Even in barren places where living creatures are rarely seen, traces of its green can still be found. For this reason, Weather Vine has become a top choice for beginners interested in growing potted plants. After all, who wouldn't want a few evergreen plants on their balcony that never need watering? However, before raising one, be sure to report it to the local Bureau of Anomaly Control office and the fire department.

Characteristics
·Weather Vine is a vine-like Anomaly that can alter the weather in a small area based on its own condition. Its tendrils grow one or more drop-shaped blue "Vine Pearls." When it senses a lack of water, it disregards the local geography and causes rain to fall nearby.
When burned by flame, it rapidly expands to increase the range of rainfall. However, if the rain lasts too long, Weather Vine will lose its "Vine Pearls" afterward and become no different from an ordinary vine.

Anomaly Nexus
Continuous burning by flame.

Risk Assessment
Basically harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Three specimens are contained at the Celaeno Compound.

Containment Measures
Plant Weather Vine in a containment unit with ample soil and sunlight.

Experiment Record
Experiment 1:
Researchers cut off a Weather Vine tendril bearing a "Vine Pearl," then burned both the section with the "Vine Pearl" and the remaining section. The section with the "Vine Pearl" could still produce rain in its surroundings, while the other showed no response. Conclusion: the "Vine Pearl" is the key organ that allows Weather Vine to alter the weather.

Experiment 2:
Researchers attempted to separate the "Vine Pearl" from the main body. However, once removed from the vine, the "Vine Pearl" immediately evaporated, making further experiments impossible for now.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3006_des:
"A warm and snuggly hug."

Anomaly Story:
Kids love cuddling their stuffed animals. Plenty of children grow up with at least one plush, bear-shaped friend. That bear is a diehard partner in crime, right up until the kid matures and the stuffed animal gets left behind in a closet or on a shelf somewhere.

The Phenomenon Anomaly, "Cuddly Bear", only manifests in toys adored by children. Its arrival seems to be visible to children only. Once affected, the toy becomes "alive" in the eyes of a child, while apparently remaining a normal stuffed animal to adults. Despite the name "Cuddly Bear", the toy's actual form depends on the child's preferences, and isn't limited specifically to bears.
From the moment a Cuddly Bear is born, it is dedicated towards one objective—to stay by its owner's side, grow up with them, listen to their troubles, and make sure they never feel alone. As the child grows and gradually becomes more independent, they stop needing their stuffed animal. When that time comes, the Cuddly Bear naturally undergoes nullification and reverts to being an ordinary toy.
Aside from providing emotional support, Cuddly Bears have no other effects. When the time for nullification arrives, most Cuddly Bears accept their fate with grace. However, there are always exceptions. Some refuse to disappear, causing their host toys to gain physical mobility and sentience, thus transforming into Derivative Anomalies. Those who are saddened by the "adults" who no longer need them become "Saddy Teddies", while those who harbor resentment toward the "child" who abandoned them become "Teehee Bears". Driven by grudges and animosity, a Cuddly Bear that has turned into a Derivative Anomaly will actively threaten the target of its anger.

In general, a person will encounter their very own Cuddly Bear once in a lifetime. So far, there are no recorded cases of a new Cuddly Bear manifesting on the same child's toys after the previous one has undergone nullification. However, "maturing" does not seem to be an absolute requirement for Cuddly Bear nullification. In a select few cases, there have been Cuddly Bear owners who, even as adults, still can't part with their Cuddly Bear. In such cases, the Cuddly Bear's duration of existence far exceeds the norm.

Characteristics:
· When an ordinary toy is affected by this Anomaly, it moves and acts—within the child's perception—in whatever way the child desires.
· It has no real physical capabilities and only serves to provide emotional value to the child.

Anomaly Nexus:
As the child matures, and the Cuddly Bear is no longer needed and is gradually forgotten, the Anomaly undergoes nullification—typically resulting in the Cuddly Bear returning to its initial stuffed animal state.

Risk Assessment:
Low Risk.

Containment Status:
Due to its unique Nexus, no Cuddly Bear has been contained to date.

Containment Procedures:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
C-3091-1(Ob) Teehee Bear
C-3091-2(Ob) Saddy Teddy
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1032_des:
"Tyranny takes root in the soil of absolute power."

Anomaly Story
St. Arbor is a place name that no longer appears on modern maps. According to historical records, the town was destroyed during a "witch trial," and the Inquisitor, who presided over the trial, disappeared. The historical records surrounding the incident are riddled with inconsistencies, with different versions of the chronicles even contradicting one another on certain points. However, they all agree that the incident marked a major turning point in the surrounding regions' attitudes toward the witch-hunt. Following the incident, witch trials in the surrounding areas gradually declined until they disappeared altogether.
What no one could have expected was that the Inquisitor, who disappeared during the trial, would return to the world in the form of an anomaly.

Anomaly C-8782-6-2[Or], the Inquisitor, was once a human named Cotton. He later became the host of Inquisitor the oddity, and this anomaly is preliminarily identified as one of the derivative anomalies of the anomaly Witch-Hunt. In the unenlightened age when the Inquisitor first emerged, witch trials were commonplace, and people generally attributed their misfortunes to witches. It was in this environment that the unprecedentedly powerful witch-hunt anomaly came into being. Under the influence of the witch-hunt anomaly, those who traveled from place to place in the name of faith, putting witches on trial, were humans who wielded the authority of judgment. Not all of these people became hosts of the anomaly. Most were merely apostles who spread the witch-hunt anomaly among the populace. The trial that took place in St. Arbor, however, not only implicated a great many people but was also disrupted by a "special circumstance," causing the human Cotton to suffer severe Encroachment and become the host of the Inquisitor.
The Inquisitor is the embodiment of humanity's obsession with "judging witches." It can also draw nourishment from people's accusations and attacks, growing ever stronger. It possesses the ability to control flames and uses them to burn those it deems witches. No ordinary human can withstand the Inquisitor's flames, meaning its judgment can continue without end.
The Inquisitor, born in St. Arbor, was imprisoned by the power of ■■■■ and was therefore recorded as missing. Inquisitor recently broke free of its imprisonment and appeared in the real world, bringing the witch-hunt anomaly of that era back with it. However, times have changed, and modern society no longer provides the conditions necessary for the Inquisitor to survive. After the Anomalous Realm was broken, Inquisitor also weakened and was ultimately nullified.

Power breeds desire, and even the exercise of power itself can become a form of desire. Unlike the masses influenced by the witch-hunt anomaly, judges did not have to fear becoming the targets of judgment themselves. Instead, they possessed the power to decide whether ordinary people should live or die. They were not corrupt from the outset. Many genuinely believed that they could protect the people by putting witches on trial. But such beliefs were twisted and exploited by the witch-hunt anomaly, until eventually, the trials themselves became the objective.

Editor's Note: Yggash Court has reviewed and redacted sensitive information.

Characteristics
Possesses both human and non-human biological forms.
Possesses the ability to control flames.
As a derivative of the witch-hunt anomaly, it takes physical form and incites the negative emotions within people.

Anomaly Nexus
Weakens after the witch-hunt anomaly is nullified, and defeating it will lead to its nullification.

Risk Assessment
Moderate risk.

Contain/Guarantee Status
Already Nullified.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_5003_des:
"The Greatest Evil Spirit of All Time!"

Anomaly Story
About thirty years ago, a horror movie became a sensation. In it, an evil spirit used telephones and TVs as mediums to cause a series of terrifying incidents. The movie was highly innovative for its time and caused quite a stir. Many viewers consequently developed a fear of telephones and TVs, worrying that a real evil spirit might appear and possess them.
After the movie became a major hit, people began claiming that their home phones would ring at midnight, their TVs would turn on by themselves for no apparent reason, and that they could even hear something resembling a woman's laughter echoing throughout their homes. Since no actual physical harm had occurred, these incidents were dismissed as pranks or products of the witnesses' imaginations and received little to no attention.
As the movie's popularity waned and old-fashioned telephones and TVs were gradually replaced, reports of such anomalous phenomena also declined sharply, nearly disappearing altogether. In a retrospective investigation, the Bureau determined that the movie's popularity may have given rise to an Anomaly closely resembling the evil spirit depicted in the film, but assumed that it had naturally undergone Nullification as the movie's influence faded.
However, that was not the case.
During an Anomaly crime, an Esper criminal broke into an office building and attempted to attack people, only to be dragged into an Anomalous Realm. Although he eventually escaped, he was critically injured and captured by members of ETD-6.
During the ensuing investigation, several employees of the office building claimed that a mysterious "Ghost Lady" had long haunted the building. She was described as a girl with long hair and side-swept bangs who wore a white dress. She mainly appeared on TVs and computer screens at night, enjoyed playing pranks, and often crawled out of computer screens late at night to frighten employees working overtime. She even caused considerable panic for a while. Aside from frightening people and playing pranks, however, the "Ghost Lady" had never genuinely harmed anyone. Employees who regularly worked late gradually grew used to her presence, and some even talked to her and confided in her about the stress of their work. Not long afterward, an Anomaly incident occurred at the company. One of its senior executives returned to the office late at night for a surprise inspection and inadvertently entered an Anomalous Realm he described as being "filled with TVs playing horror movies." After being thoroughly frightened, he insisted that the company was completely haunted at night. The company's late-night overtime decreased significantly after that, and although there was no evidence directly linking the incident to the "Ghost Lady," the employees were all grateful to her.
However, no one reported seeing the "Ghost Girl" again after the criminal incident. We, therefore, believe that the "Ghost Lady" described by the employees is closely connected to the Anomaly individual known as "Xiaozhen" below, and may even be the same individual.

Anomaly T-5550(Me), named "Xiaozhen" at the Guarantor's request, resides inside an old TV that had been left unused somewhere in the office building where the aforementioned criminal incident occurred.
Xiaozhen can condense energy into physical forms for battle, and can also drag other people into an Anomalous Realm under her control, matching the office employees' description of the "Ghost Girl" fighting the Esper criminal. However, Xiaozhen is a small ghost with the apparent age and stature of a little girl, differing in build and appearance from the white-dressed girl described by the employees, though they do share some similarities. In addition, the Anomaly does not remember what she experienced inside the Anomalous Realm during this incident, which is presumed to have resulted from being injured and weakened in the battle.
Xiaozhen was initially classified as a Bio Anomaly. Only after she was linked to the supernatural phenomena from thirty years ago was she reclassified as a Meme Anomaly. She possesses full intelligence and the ability to communicate. Although she enjoys playing pranks, she has shown no inclination to deliberately harm others. Perhaps because of the circumstances behind the Meme Anomaly's formation, Xiaozhen is extremely committed to playing the role of a "terrifying evil spirit," but… her appearance and personality make it very difficult for anyone to find her frightening. According to Xiaozhen, she was once a "powerful evil spirit," but lost most of her power over time and became what she is today. This also largely matches the Bureau's assessment.
A "concerned citizen" recovered the TV in which Xiaozhen resided from the crime scene. This person is now Xiaozhen's Guarantor and has joined the Prohibition Mobile Unit.

Note 1: For investigative purposes, we dutifully watched the entire series of movies related to this Anomaly. As expected, every sequel after the first was terrible.
Note 2: Employees at the office building described in this file have reportedly been holding regular séances in an attempt to summon the "Ghost Girl." They should be discouraged from doing so to prevent panic or the formation of a new Anomaly.

Anomaly Characteristics
Appears as the ghost of a little girl, enjoys playing pranks, and displays no obvious malice;
Resides in a TV and can float and fly around after leaving it;
Can shape energy into physical forms for battle and temporarily trap other people in her Anomalous Realm;
Must replenish any energy consumed in battle by resting inside the TV.

Anomaly Nexus
Leaving the TV in which she resides consumes her energy. She undergoes Nullification when her energy is depleted.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment Status
Guarantor status granted.

Containment Measures
The Guarantor is responsible for her.
Supplementary Note: The Anomaly resides in an old TV and cannot remain outside it for extended periods of time. If necessary, the Anomaly can be contained by containing the TV itself.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3004_des:
"A carp emerges from the chasm of heaven, the tide flows back through the mortal realm. The Dragon Gate stands tall and timeless, ever awaiting the return of shimmering scales."

Anomaly Story
As one of the oldest anomalies, Tidal Ascension has existed in this world long before paper and pens. Whenever it manifests, it is accompanied by gentle rain falling from the sky and all vegetation sprouting forth into spring. Even the most barren and desolate lands are revitalized. Thus, in an age when every blade of grass was sacred, Tidal Ascension was regarded as an auspicious blessing from the heavens. Simple folk would hold feasts and celebrations of song and dance, commemorating this phenomenon through various ceremonial traditions. Yet one ritual was performed everywhere without exception: the leaping of the Dragon Gate.
When the ritual began, people would construct a towering Dragon Gate. The Skyfish Banners that migrated along with the Tidal Ascension phenomenon would then compete to leap over it, while skilled performers would cleverly maneuver against them, preventing them from crossing the Dragon Gate. Yes, I said preventing, not assisting. This has been the custom since ancient times, and even though the reasons for it have long since faded into obscurity, later generations have continued to follow it strictly. Needless to say, such a fantastical and grand performance won the adoration of all children, and so Tidal Ascension took on another layer of meaning: to fulfill childhood dreams together with the youth, so that they would carry a heart that never loses its innocence.
The ethereal colorful carps have no physical form and cannot actually be harmed or blocked, but they respond to their opponents' actions accordingly. Stopping them is not difficult, as if this spectacle itself deliberately cooperates with humans to present the Dragon Gate trial more romantically to the eyes of eager children. When encountering obstacles, the carp blow bubbles, trapping those who block them from leaping over the Dragon Gate. These light bubbles carry the people inside up into the air before gently floating back down, and so children eagerly join in. Weighing less, children often fly higher, high enough to vanish amidst the clouds and glimpse the homeland of the carp. Such rituals would eventually transform into joyful games, and the carp would complete their Dragon Gate trial amidst laughter. The translucent colorful carp that failed to leap over the Dragon Gate would wave their tails and ascend like fireworks, gradually vanishing into the distant sky. Thus the celebration would come to a perfect close, and the children would continue to grow while cherishing the beautiful memories of that day.
This celebration continued until a certain ceremony in a certain place in a certain year. In retrospect, it was likely that some curious young people deliberately allowed the carp to successfully leap over the Dragon Gate…
A witness once told their children and grandchildren what happened that day: it was an extraordinarily magnificent dragon, rising from the Faraway land. "A great dragon made of countless colorful carp! It circled round and round in the sky, with fish constantly swimming into its body from all directions. Then a river in the sky descended to meet it, and the dragon followed that heavenly stream back into the clouds."
It was not until several days later, when the last of the fish had scattered and vanished, that people discovered everyone who had participated in the ceremony at that place had disappeared. Where the village once stood was now silent, yet the vegetation had grown astonishingly lush… Even the tallest chimney was covered in countless flowers. Some said they were punished for angering the spirits with their irreverence toward the ritual. Others said they were chosen by the dragon formed from fish and taken to the heavens, becoming new colorful carp awaiting the next migration.
However, all we can confirm is that this Anomaly may cause extraordinary consequences after evolving, that is, after successfully leaping over the Dragon Gate. From every perspective, we should do our utmost to avoid repeating this mistake. As recorded in ancient texts restored by archaeologists: "…The shimmering scales came from the nine heavens in great numbers, seeking to cross the Dragon Gate. Wherever they passed, sweet rain fell upon the world and all vegetation was revived. All people celebrated, and this became an established custom, passed down through generations… To prevent disaster, there is but one rule: they must not be allowed to cross the Dragon Gate."
Regrettably, after more and more people learned the truth, it became impossible to approach this phenomenon with the same pure innocence as before. The ritual of leaping the Dragon Gate has gradually become an ancient ceremony only found in history books… The children of yesteryear have long been swallowed by the river of time, remembered by none… Only the colorful carp still return to the human world, and again.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Accompanying that slender river from the heavens, the translucent fish shadows that migrate here seek the trial of leaping over the Dragon Gate.
· Ignores geographic conditions. Able to revitalize the surrounding area.
· Failed trials result in a 'return to the sky', while successful ones cause the Anomaly to evolve.

Anomaly Nexus
Help the Skyfish Banner complete the challenge of leaping over the Dragon Gate, regardless of whether they succeed or fail.

Risk Assessment
Generally does not attack proactively. Can serve as city scenery.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Cannot be contained.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
Skyfish Banner
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2006_des:
"A weapon to kill the sea."

Anomaly Story
Some say the harpoon is humanity's weapon of defiance against the sea. It is used to hunt majestic creatures like panicked boars in a common hunting ground. R-1851-1(Ob) Pequod may well be the very embodiment of humanity's will to conquer the sea, encompassing ambition and courage, but also greed and arrogance alike. It appears as a massively oversized version of a common whaling harpoon, covered in bloodstains and rust, lodged in the back of the Anomaly Sea Prisoner. Aside from causing the Sea Prisoner immense pain, no other special properties have been observed.

In earlier times, whaling was a thriving industry driven by commercial demand. Even today, such hunts are still ongoing, though not commonplace. Harpooners were highly respected aboard whaling ships, considering that they were the key to a successful hunt. They would approach beasts a hundred times their size in small boats, drive harpoons into their flesh to draw blood, then begin the long chase, tethered by a simple rope. Some whalers died in this process, claimed by storms, by the thrashing of the great beasts, or perhaps by three too many swigs of rum… But most of the time, the whales lacked the tenacity to outlast the humans. These giants would be hoisted up and dismantled. Useless flesh would be cast into the sea as a feast for scavenger fish, while the blubber was rendered in pots until dry and fed into furnaces as fuel. In the end, only thick oil and white bones remained.
From the accounts of some sailors, we know this "process" left a thick stench of blood and burning on the ship, like the smell of hell itself. It follows that the harpoon must be a weapon from hell, then. The dying songs of those ocean giants were so sorrowful… so profoundly moving… The conflict between the demands of industrial development in the past and the natural world is difficult to judge as right or wrong, but now that we no longer need to sacrifice their flesh as fuel for industry, may these creatures of the sea never again become victims of mere greed and ignorance…

Anomaly Characteristics
· Causes immense pain to the Anomaly Sea Prisoner and provokes its aggression.

Anomaly Nexus
Undergoes nullification together with the Sea Prisoner.

Risk Assessment
Low hazard. However, under its stimulation, the Sea Prisoner exhibits heightened aggression.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not contained. Guarantee not permitted.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
…
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4008_des:
"Welcome to my castle."

Anomaly Story
Edward D. always believed that a true haunted house should do more than simply scare people. Rather than relying on ghosts that suddenly emerge from the darkness or skeletons planted around corners, he wanted visitors to truly "enter" an exciting story. So, while still an employee of the Puka Group, he drew on his extensive experience with supernatural fiction and his fondness for vampire stories to design a "Medieval Castle" haunted-house attraction for Pukaland.
The castle had a master of its own, while visitors were guests who had wandered in by mistake. They would push open the heavy front door and explore the dim corridors until they reached "The Count's" room at the very end.
Unfortunately, the project was never completed as scheduled. During the prolonged pause, Edward D. also left the Puka Group, leaving his design unrealized.
When the Puka Group finally had the time and resources to resume the haunted-house project, they discovered that the structure left behind had quietly changed. Beginning with the appearance of a door that was not on the blueprints, it was no longer an unfinished haunted-house attraction, but a newly born Anomaly. It seemed to have inherited the designer's will, and its challenges within felt even more natural than the artificial stages initially laid out in the project plans. These newfound changes had the potential to make it a more competitive commercial venture for the Puka Group, so they actively cooperated with the Bureau's experiments and monitoring. After confirming that the haunted house, now deemed "Spooky Cookies," was stable and harmless, they agreed to guarantee it for use as a theme-park attraction. From then on, every visitor to Pukaland had the chance to experience a special, spooky adventure.
Spooky Cookies has always welcomed every guest. Perhaps, it might also be quietly waiting for the day Edward D. returns as one of its many guests.

Anomaly Characteristics
Spooky Cookies treats everyone who enters as a "visitor" and seeks to provide a deeply immersive haunted-house experience. Visitors must follow the applicable rules.

Anomaly Nexus
Clear Spooky Cookies.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment Status
Following the risk assessment, the Puka Group agreed to guarantee it for use as a theme-park attraction.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Record
1. Experiment: Refuse to follow the applicable rules, including but not limited to forcing entry without paying Fons, hiding inside Spooky Cookies instead of continuing the experience, and attempting to bypass The Count and open the door directly.
Result: Subjects were unable to successfully enter or leave Spooky Cookies.
2. Experiment: Deliberately become excessively frightened without using a flashlight.
Result: Upon reaching a certain psychological threshold, the subject briefly lost consciousness and awoke at the entrance to Spooky Cookies.
3. Experiment: Remove an item from Spooky Cookies.
Result: The item disappeared when the subject left Spooky Cookies.
Note: The frightened subject was Researcher ■■■. A subsequent medical examination found no abnormalities.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2033_des:
"The dead dance with the dead, and the ashes spin with the ashes."

[Anomaly Story]

"First Confirmation"
During the Scarlet Letter incident, Bureau personnel observed for the first time a massive, pitch-black coffin whose appearance matched no known anomaly. The only confirmable information mainly comes from the testimony of the Dimension Visitor. Roughly two hundred years ago, as a bystander, she witnessed the elimination process of the Fogden Game. From all the participants, only one woman, Inanna, survived to the end. As the victor, Inanna entered into a contract with a black coffin. The black coffin described by the Dimension Visitor matches the object discovered in this operation in both looks and traits. On this basis, we believe that the black coffin discovered in this operation is the same anomaly, the Fog Coffin, she witnessed two hundred years ago.

During this incident, the Fog Coffin was ritually awakened by Madam T, the leader of the Scarlet Letter. Madam T is the "Inanna" mentioned in the Dimension Visitor's testimony; she won the Fogden game two hundred years ago and entered into a contract with the coffin, which gives her the Offering Right to awaken the coffin. The ritual was carried out in the underground space of an abandoned building. Madam T offered up three anomalies: the Helm of Theseus, the Eternal Present, and the First Branch, and submitted her handwritten rules. Once the offerings and the rules were taken in by the Fog Coffin, the coffin door opened, presenting a portal to the Fogden. The portal stayed open for about an hour. Anyone who entered during that time automatically became a participant.

During this round of the game, several participants witnessed ■■■■ appear in the Fogden. The Fog Coffin's avatar and enforcer, the Fog Coffin Colossus, designated ■■■■ as its primary target and fought it, yet was ultimately destroyed by ■■■■. With the enforcer gone, the Fogden's Anomalous Realm began to collapse. At the same time, the Fog Coffin, which was still in the real world, crumbled into black dust before everyone.

Henceforth, it has been determined that the Fog Coffin has been nullified.

"The Initial Game"
In subsequent investigations, Madam T's surviving private records, together with statements from members of the Scarlet Letter, gradually pieced together the Fog Coffin's origins. This account did not come from official documentation, but from fragments Madam T herself privately gathered over many years. She called it "The Initial Game."
According to the records, the Fog Coffin first appeared on a nameless, isolated island. The island once held a lighthouse and was guarded by generations of keepers. They made a promise to the villagers on the shore: as long as the light stayed lit, no ship would lose its way. In return, the villagers regularly sent supplies.
Though remote, the coast was still caught in war. Surviving villagers gradually forgot their pact with the lighthouse keepers. No more provisions came, and the lighthouse had long since dimmed.
Until one day, a pitch-black coffin was swept ashore.
No one knew where it came from, or how long it took to arrive. The keeper opened the coffin but found nothing inside, except for a sentence carved into the coffin inside:
"Everyone, let's play a game."

[Characteristics]
It appeared as a massive, pitch-black coffin, with no inscriptions, no ornaments, and no markings. Its material was unknown, and it looked like it was in perfect condition.
When dormant, it remains asleep, and can only be awakened through a specific offering ritual. Awakening requires all of the following conditions to be met:
First, a contract bearer who is qualified to make an offering. The qualification must come from being a previous winner of the Fogden Game and having had formed a contract with the Fog Coffin.
Second, three anomaly artifacts offered by the contract bearer.
Third, written rules submitted in physical form, handwritten by the contractor, its contents being the rules of this Fogden game.
Once awakened, the Fog Coffin opens, revealing a portal leading to the Fogden, which itself is a confined Anomalous Realm. The portal stays open for about an hour. Once it closes, the coffin seals shut again, and it returns back to a dormant state, awaiting the next awakening.

[Anomaly Nexus]
The Fogdame's rules no longer enforceabe; the Fogden's anomalous realm destroyed.

[Risk Assessment]
In its dormancy, the coffin poses no danger. During the ritual, it devours the offerings chosen by the contractor. Once the coffin opens, there is almost zero possibility of survival.

[Containment/Guarantee Status]
Nullified
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1029_des:
"Let the dead sleep, and let their dreams serve as seeds."

Anomaly Story
Bloomhost Effigies are Anomalies formed from players being eliminated in the game, "Fogden". The items they once carried remain perfectly intact and usable. Instead, their flesh turns to stone, and small buds begin to sprout from their skin, blooming into blue flowers.

Characteristics
Bloomhost Effigies are scattered throughout Fogden's Hunt Zone.
The effigies themselves are inert. The only components considered "alive" are the clusters of small blue flowers sprouting from their body.


Anomaly Nexus
The Fogden Game's rules were broken; Fogden Space was destroyed.

Risk Assessment
No danger

Containment Status
Vanished alongside Fogden's collapse. No containment required.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2023_des:
"Every grain of sand, lost to time." 

Anomaly Story:
The "Tally of Ages", also known as the "Register", is the Derivative Anomaly of Anomaly C-0312 (Or), the Debt Collector. The "debtors" who are hunted by the Debt Collector, along with the "debts" they owe, are recorded within the Tally of Ages. When a debt has been cleared, the debtor vanishes along with it.

Characteristics:
· A Derivative Anomaly of the Debt Collector", which records debt victims and their debt owed.

Anomaly Nexus:
Nullified together with the Debt Collector.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
Not Contained.

Containment:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4006_des:
"Without day and without night, it's but a dead sea drowning in the past."

[Anomaly Story]
The Corridor of Echoes is an enclosed space materialized from the desire to escape. At first, it was just a vast, boundless sea, inhabited only by Twisties born from the water. Later, a whirlpool appeared at the center, spiraling inward endlessly, as if yearning to draw something in. The outside world answered the whirlpool's call. People who shared the same mindset as the space's creator were drawn here, becoming its new residents. And so this stretch of sea was no longer just a sea, land and rooms for its residents emerged in response.
The Ferrier brings guests to this place, where the streams ultimately converge into the sea. A haven for new arrivals and those who linger, celebrating their arrival.

Countless orbs of light drift across the Corridor's sky and sea, each representing the escapism and obsession cast off by visitors, who can only become part of this place by shedding a piece of their soul.
The colossal statue at the center is the creator's projection. It's silent, accepting, and gives off the stale scent of old wounds left behind by long solitude. Perhaps it was this very loneliness that summoned a crowd of people to keep it company.

This anomaly's entrance can only be activated by a specific kind of person. Those with escapist tendencies, unable to face their present selves, develop the urge to shut themselves away, which makes them eligible to enter this space. In terms of the real world, they vanish briefly before returning unharmed. Outsiders call this phenomenon "spirited away." Though they appear unharmed, those close to the missing person often notice something off: their personalities shifted; things they obsessed over seemed forgotten; problems bothering them just days ago suddenly don't matter. They've lost their pain and their struggles, but they've also lost their hopes and their drive. Indifferent, detached, unbothered, like gentle puppets stripped of their souls. These people are no longer who they once were. They are just shells, or rather, duplicates, of their former selves.
As for whether anyone ever managed to leave with their soul intact… we do not know.


[Characteristics]
- Within a fixed area, the entrance and exit to the space appear at random. After remaining in place for some time, they shift to new locations.
- The anomalies created within feed on the past dreams of visitors. They could become aggressive If the visitors don't have dreams they can feed on.
- The space creates a customized space based on the visitor's past. Most visitors gradually fall into slumbers since they cannot maintain consciousness of their present timeline.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1006_des:
"Bathtubs have boundaries. Lakes have boundaries. So where, then, are the boundaries of the world?"

Anomaly Story
In modern times, a cargo ship transporting rubber ducks suffered an accidental spill. Rubber ducks intended to spin around in bathtubs poured into the ocean, embarking on a legendary voyage. Led by a giant leader duck, they drifted around the globe for decades.
Interestingly, the leader duck was not from the cargo ship, but rather, it was an Anomaly that happened to be passing by. Its name was Rubbaduck, also known the big yellow duck, with the ability to attract nearby floating objects to follow it. Due to this, the flock of ducks that fell into the sea rarely lost their way. However, as people developed a keen interest in the drifting rubber ducks, many were plucked from the flock as they floated about. Eventually, very few remained, and the voyage came to an end. Rubbaduck's main body was acquired by a certain exhibition company and is displayed to the public from time to time.
The exhibitions brought this Anomaly into the public eye, simultaneously sparking more mysteries surrounding it. Some people claim they can communicate with the big yellow duck, believing that the ducky knows everything in the world. Apparently, all kinds of information these people have received from it has been verified as true… This phenomenon has yet to be reasonably explained.
It is worth noting that records of Rubbaduck existed long before humans invented the rubber duck, and it was explicitly recorded as a living creature. Anomalies are things that should not exist, therefore, it is understandable that this big yellow duck is considered a life form that should not exist.

Anomaly Characteristics
All bodies of water in the world are one and the same to it. It tours all bodies of water in the world according to a certain pattern.
The body of water it recognizes is defined as a water volume of 520L or more. Therefore, when coming into contact with 520L or more of water, it can directly drift to another body of water through this water, unhindered by spatial barriers. As a result, it is often seen suddenly disappearing and suddenly reappearing.
It has a pull effect on floating objects within the same body of water. Other floating objects on the water surface will gather around it, drifting along with it. This pull effect is not strong and cannot attract floating objects from far away.

Anomaly Nexus
Puncture its surface and submerge it in water. It will achieve nullification on its own and reappear at the submersion site after 24 hours.

Risk Assessment
The main body is harmless, but attention should be paid to the abnormal gathering of floating objects in the water where it resides.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Currently owned by an exhibition company. This company regularly holds public exhibitions for it.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
Experiment 1
Liquid water was continuously added to the containment unit. When the water volume reached 520L, the Anomaly disappeared and was later found in a nearby lake.

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2018_des:
"Lights out."

Anomaly Story
The story begins in an abandoned ancient castle. No one knows its exact history anymore, but residents of the nearby villages all agree that the castle was "haunted." Light sources in the hands of anyone who entered would unnaturally extinguish, and those who remained in the castle's darkness for too long would be taken away by ghosts, never to return. This rumor spread among niche paranormal enthusiasts, and a group of curious young people gathered together to explore the castle, only to vanish without a trace… Their parents hired an Anomaly Hunter skilled at operating in darkness to search the castle for the missing persons, but in the end, that Anomaly Hunter never located the missing people. They only retrieved the culprit behind everything: a lamp.

Anomaly U-2016(Ob) is a lamp we call "After Lights Out." Its craftsmanship bears traces of different eras. It has no power cord, yet it can still be switched on. When illuminated, it appears no different from a common lamp. However, after being lit for a period, it gradually begins to flicker and eventually goes out. Afterward, within a certain radius centered on it, all light sources gradually extinguish, forming an unnatural "dark zone." Such a zone is its Anomalous Realm, within which, the brightness of all light sources is severely limited and will extinguish after a short time. From outside the dark zone, it is nearly impossible to see what is happening inside. After entering the dark zone, a person will unknowingly transform into a blurry "Shadow" creature. Only by relighting After Lights Out can the surroundings return to brightness and the Shadows be restored to their original human forms. However, if someone remains in Shadow form within the dark zone for too long, when the lamp is relit and the dark zone disappears, the Shadow will disappear along with it… Those poor souls are forever lost in the realm of Shadows.

Fear of the dark is instinctive, as is curiosity about the unknown. Whether to prove we are fearless or to discover what truly hides in the darkness, we are always driven by instinct to step into the dark. After Lights Out is like an anglerfish with an extinguished lure, lying in wait for the next batch of curious explorers…

Anomaly Characteristics
· Appears as a Common lamp.
· After extinguishing, the surroundings are gradually devoured by darkness, and light sources within range go out one by one.
· People in the dark zone transform into Shadows, only being restored after After Lights Out is relit. Those who remain in Shadow form for too long may be unable to recover.

Anomaly Nexus
Light the lamp. This is not a permanent nullification method; it can only eliminate its effects. However, unless Ebisu agrees, we cannot forcibly nullify it.

Risk Assessment
Moderate hazard.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Guaranteed by the Ebisu Auction House.

Containment Measures
Maintain surveillance on this Anomaly. When it begins to flicker, immediately pull the switch to relight it.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2009_des:
"Yet not a single gaze lingers upon it."

Anomaly Story
Outstanding paintings, due to the artist's fame and the work's rarity, may pass through the hands of untold numbers of collectors throughout history. Even when temporarily obscured by personal taste and era-specific preferences, they are bound to reappear thanks to their inherent artistic value. However, the frames that have accompanied these masterpieces and endured the trials of history are often replaced according to their new owners' tastes.
Every viewer who admires a masterpiece will certainly see the frame, but when people eagerly discuss the painting's colors, composition, and meaning, not one word is spared for it. The more fervently people pursue masterpieces, the more they consider the frame, which serves to protect and display, as merely a dispensable decoration, some even believing it diminishes the painting's refined taste.
If freed from the constraints of paintings, could a frame earn even a single word of praise? Perhaps it was this obsession that allowed the frame, considered a mere accessory to masterpieces, to develop the power to protest its unjust treatment, becoming the Anomaly Picture Frame.

Creating bizarre spaces and attacking by splashing paint, Picture Frame's abilities still seem closely related to the paintings it once framed… If Picture Frame has consciousness, such a reality must be quite disheartening for it, right?
Perhaps this very frustration led to Picture Frame's aggressive nature. From another perspective, its motivation for creating Anomalous Realms might be to seek attention, whereas its attacks on those caught in Anomalous Realm might seem more tantrum-like…? For those swept into the Anomalous Realm, marveling at the ever-changing, beautiful "world within paintings," might be percieved as mocking Picture Frame's own mediocrity… provoking its retaliation.
Such behavior sounds somewhat childish, but for an Anomaly with such powerful abilities, even throwing a tantrum can cause immense damage to its surroundings.

Can a frame separated from its painting still be called a "frame"? Or rather, there are things in this world which always serve as accessories, dependent on primary entities, right? Frames used to frame paintings, or even paintings used as house decorations… Do all these things have the potential to become anomalies? Or did Picture Frame happen to possess some special quality?
…Such questions are better left for scholars. Perhaps next time I visit the Gold Apple Collection Hall, I should pay my respects to the display cases…? Would that count as an effective measure to prevent Anomaly formation?

Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly suddenly manifested during a public art exhibition. The specific cause of formation is unknown. Multiple audience members were injured before the Bureau of Anomaly Control arrived.
· In its normal state, it appears as a common picture frame. After transformation, its main body becomes a hexagram-shaped object. The entire hexagram's outer surface is covered with oil paint, with layered textural depths that continuously undulate.
· Bureau of Anomaly Control members responsible for containing this Anomaly described in their reports that it can fly and rotate at low altitudes, possesses aggressive tendencies, sprays paint to attack its surroundings, and changes appearance according to battle conditions.
· This Anomaly appears to have the ability to transcend spatial limitations. When its powers activate, it can independently create a small Anomalous Realm and manifest real elemental scenes within the space. Based on speculation, the Anomaly's abilities may be related to paintings it once framed. Due to audience imagination (and perhaps over-interpretation) of paintings, layered, patchwork, and otherwise unconventional scenes appear in the spaces this Anomaly creates.
· Words of praise for Picture Frame, even if not heartfelt, seem able to pacify the Anomaly and significantly reduce its destructiveness.

Anomaly Nexus
Receiving genuine praise and recognition.

Risk Assessment
Due to its ability to trigger Anomalous Realm phenomena and active aggressiveness, Picture Frame poses a considerable threat to civilians accidentally caught in its effects. For Bureau of Anomaly Control professionals and experienced Anomaly Hunters, however, danger is not particularly great. Given that it breached the Bureau of Anomaly Control's Temporary containment measures, its potential risk may be higher, but considering this Anomaly has undergone nullification, no further speculation will be made.

Containment/Guarantee Status
After temporary containment by the Bureau of Anomaly Control resulted in breach, it was jointly nullified by Bureau of Anomaly Control, CSU-2 member Mint, and an Anomaly Hunter.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1013_des:
"Race, win, swing the scythe."

Anomaly Story
Rumors of the Headless Rider initially only circulated among street racing gangs: "If you race at speeds over 200 kilometers per hour at midnight, you'll summon a rider clad in black motorcycle gear, with cold flames burning eternally beneath his helmet. He comes to judge the street racers and will invite you to a chase you cannot refuse… where the loser forfeits their soul!" The origin of this legend is lost to time, and most who heard it simply laughed it off, never taking it seriously. One night, a gang of street racers were tearing through the empty streets on their motorcycles as usual, when they began to discuss the legend. "Ha! You don't actually believe that guy exists, do you?" The gang leader doubled over with laughter after hearing the story. "Even if he were real, why would I be scared of him?" Laughing away, he mounted his motorcycle and floored the throttle, shooting straight past 200 km/h. Just as he lost himself in the rush of speed, the streetlights began to flicker. A piercing shriek suddenly sounded out, and a rider clad in black atop a motorcycle as dark as the night itself came roaring up from behind. After locking onto his target, the rider's motorcycle spewed blue flames, speeding ahead at a provocatively fast pace. The gang leader refused to back down. He floored the throttle again and fearlessly accepted the challenge.
According to the gang members' later accounts, that night, the roar of two engines echoed across half the city. In this chase, their leader ultimately failed to overtake the motorcycle shrouded in black mist… When the other members caught up, they were horrified to see the rider remove his helmet. In the eerie glow of blue flames flickering at his neck, he swung a terrifying black scythe, mercilessly slashing the loser before him. The blade flashed cold, and the gang leader, unharmed, stood before his motorcycle cleaved in two, reduced to scrap. By the time everyone came to their senses, the headless rider had vanished swiftly into the dark night. From that night on, the leader quit the gang and swore never to race again. That black scythe, destroying his beloved bike, seemed to have taken his "racing spirit" as well.
After this incident, the Headless Rider became the hottest topic in Hethereau for a time. The road was completely closed off, and it remained sealed for a long while before reopening. According to this writer's investigation, if a race with the Headless Rider drags on too long, he will pull his opponent into a mysterious Anomalous Realm… No one knows what happens inside, but for street racers, this danger is precisely what makes him so alluring.
Thus, despite knowing they will pay a heavy price, people continue to seek out and challenge the Headless Rider. "Defeating the Headless Rider" has become the ultimate dream and goal for many racing enthusiasts. Over time, the Headless Rider has somehow become the spiritual leader of these street racers, now known as Garuda, emblazoned proudly on their crew jackets as their symbol. In the eyes of these worshippers, a "judge" like the Headless Rider stands at the top of the food chain and is therefore worth following. The Headless Rider also provides "fuel" to the members through Garuda's core leaders, the "Four Kings." This "fuel" consists of the "racing spirits" of those defeated in midnight races. Rumor has it this "fuel" greatly enhances members' prowess, making them unstoppable. But for the Headless Rider himself, his purpose seems to be simply to race, win, then swing his scythe. The reasons for an Anomaly born to judge instead assisting Garuda remains a baffling mystery.
Incidentally, official records also document several cases of speeding drivers encountering the Headless Rider. However, when the drivers fled in terror, the rider seemed to lose interest in continuing the race. Since the Headless Rider's appearance, the frequency of illegal speeding on the roads has dropped significantly. In that sense, this headless rider has inadvertently made quite a contribution to the city's traffic safety, which the Security Office finds itself rather thankful for.

Anomaly Characteristics
· A headless rider clad in black motorcycle gear, atop a black motorcycle.
· Born to judge street racers. At night, he challenges vehicles that illegally exceed speed limits to a race. Losing reportedly results in both vehicle and 'racing spirit' being severed.
· His weapon is a massive scythe formed from condensed black mist.

Anomaly Nexus
Defeat the Headless Rider in a chase.

Risk Assessment
High Hazard. Generally, driving during the day or not illegally speeding will not attract the Headless Rider's attention.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly. Not in containment.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Record
/

Derivative Anomaly
T-8467-1(Ob) Soul-Cleaving Motorcycle: The Headless Rider's treasured bike. Entirely deep black, it spews blue flames from its exhaust pipe while in motion.
ST_Manual.NounManual_2_1_des:
One of the Circle's five major public authority organizations.
Primarily responsible for the Containment and Nullification of Anomalies, handling criminal cases involving Anomalies or Esper Abilities, and suppressing disasters caused by Anomalies or Esper Abilities.
Headquarters are located in Hethereau, with branch offices established in various locations.
ST_Manual.NounManual_1_15_des:
A member of the Circle who is not part of any public authority but carries out Anomaly investigation, containment, and nullification work—tacitly approved by public authorities—as a private enterprise for individuals or groups.
Compensation comes from various sources, including guilds and private commissioners.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_5002_des:
"Tomato jelly, evidence! Destroy everything!"

Anomaly Story
Lacrimosa, a member of ETD-4, encountered a vending machine malfunction while purchasing her favorite Tomato 100. Lacking common sense, she lifted the entire machine in an attempt to pour the tomato jelly out. This senseless behavior drew a crowd, and many photos were posted on Bagel. Thanks to ETD-4 Lieutenant Skia's timely intervention and Lacrimosa's proper apology, the incident was initially just an amusing story. After all, you don't see a girl with monstrous strength lifting a vending machine every day. However, as someone dug up Lacrimosa's identity as an ETD member, unfavorable public opinion began to form… More and more people believed that Lacrimosa, as an ETD member, had committed an unforgivable act by damaging public property. Baseless claims like "destruction maniac," "abuse of privilege," and "robbery" spread everywhere. This wave of public opinion ultimately brought the fabricated "destructive Lacrimosa" into reality, giving birth to the Anomaly known as Tomato Devil.

C-6957(Me) Tomato Devil is a Meme Anomaly born from nothing. Its appearance is that of a humanoid girl with features nearly identical to Lacrimosa, but its body is composed of a red jelly-like substance similar to Tomato 100. This Anomaly appears near vending machines that sell Tomato 100, robbing and destroying them. When bystanders witnessed this and uploaded rolls to Bagel, it only caused more rumors to spread, further strengthening Tomato Devil's power. As the public's attitude toward Lacrimosa grew worse, Tomato Devil's behavior became increasingly extreme, forming a vicious cycle.
Tomato Devil's fighting style resembles Lacrimosa's. It can form various weapons from tomato jelly to fight and possesses the ability to fly. Compared to Lacrimosa herself, Tomato Devil relies more heavily on close combat, likely influenced by the impression of her as a "monstrous strength girl." Since this memetic anomaly was born from online public opinion, she lacks a complete mind. What drives her actions is a pure desire to destroy tomato jelly vending machines.
The Bureau's PR experts initially proposed a minimization strategy: keeping Lacrimosa out of the public eye for a period. As public attention shifted to new topics, discussions about Lacrimosa would gradually die down, and the Tomato Devil born from them would naturally undergo nullification. This would normally take a period, but in reality, public interest faded far faster than initially expected. On one hand, Lacrimosa's friends took action that partially turned around her reputation on Bagel. On the other hand, some breaking news redirected attention from this matter, causing the controversy to cool down earlier than expected. Ultimately, having lost the public opinion that was its reason for existence, Tomato Devil underwent natural nullification.

Info becomes distorted during transmission, and people will inevitably fill in the gaps with imagination. When more and more "I heard that…" replaces the original info, the "truth" the public puts faith in becomes completely opposite to the facts. The further from the source the rumors spread, the more severe the distortion becomes. We happen to live in an era where information transmission is incredibly convenient, so rumors and gossip are a given. Lacrimosa merely lacked common sense, yet after spreading through Bagel, people fabricated a real Tomato Devil… Simple words, just like that, transformed into actual destructive power. Even if the Tomato Devil underwent nullification following the minimization strategy, wouldn't people continue to misunderstand Lacrimosa in the future? From this perspective, the malice carried by rumors is actually more harmful than the memetic anomaly itself.

Anomaly Characteristics
· A humanoid Anomaly composed of tomato jelly with the ability to fly. Able to control tomato jelly to form various objects to attack.
· Has features identical to Lacrimosa from ETD-4, but lacks consciousness.
· Will rob and destroy Tomato 100 vending machines. If externally interfered with, the interferer will also become a target to attack.

Anomaly Nexus
Born from online public opinion about Lacrimosa, it will naturally undergo nullification when public opinion dies down.

Risk Assessment
Moderate hazard.

Containment/Guarantee Status
The only known individual has undergone nullification. No containment was performed.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2021_des:
"The paper planes from childhood… in the end, they never do fly back."

Anomaly Story:
R-9843(Ob) Paper Squadron is an Anomaly consisting of multiple paper planes. Typically, this anomaly will nest in the mailboxes of suburban homes. If startled, they'll swarm and repeatedly circle in the sky.

"Reporting to the Captain! Lightwing is prepped and ready, requesting takeoff!"
"Request received, Lightwing. You're cleared for takeoff!"
The child on the rooftop blew onto the paper plane in his hands, throwing the plane towards the sky with all his might. The paper plane made a soft arc in the air before finally fluttering down into the yard. "Lightwing, you did your best! Skywing can handle the rest." The child grabbed another paper plane, preparing for its next "sortie".
His mother yells from the house down below, "Come and clean up your toys from the yard!"
"Okay, Mom! Paper Squadron, listen up! Today's mission was a complete success—begin your orderly return to base!" The kid dashed downstairs, picking up each paper plane one by one, carefully dusting off their wings. He began to delicately put them back in a cardboard box labeled, "Fleet's Secret Hangar".

As time progressed, the child continued to grow, eventually attending school and beyond. The Paper Squadron was launched less and less. Instead, they remained in base, patiently waiting for their Captain's orders.
One day, the child, now a grown man, discovered a box caked in dust while clearing out the attic. Inside, he found the paper planes that had loyally followed his every order as a child. He noticed that the paper was no longer crisp white, but instead a creased yellow. Their markings had faded, and he could no longer distinguish one plane from the other. In hopes of captaining one more flight, the man dragged the box out to the yard and tossed one of the planes into the air. Far from its prime, the plane wobbled for a few moments in the air before dropping entirely. The man stared at the paper plane on the ground. Silently, he picked it up, dusted it off, and placed it back within the box.

Before leaving his childhood home, the man climbed to the roof and tried to send the paper plane into the air for the last time. He blew on it gently and, with a flick of his wrist, sent the plane flying. However, instead of its usual flight pattern, the paper plane caught wind and actually began to… hover. The man was frozen in shock. He quickly grabbed another plane and repeated his previous action.
