The second plane replicated the same behavior, soaring into the air before hovering, as if awaiting an order. The man finally understood: his childhood Paper Plane Fleet had awakened. Only, he was no longer qualified to be their Captain. A strong gust of wind swept across the rooftop, catching the paper planes and carrying them off onto the horizon.

From that moment on, the Paper Squadron lost its Captain—leaving only a flock of paper planes, forever flying with no direction nor commands in mind.

Characteristics:
· An Anomaly comprised of multiple paper planes, collectively referred to as the "Paper Plane Fleet".
· Under normal circumstances, the Anomaly shows no active hostility. However, if their flight path is interfered with, there is a chance they will initiate a counterattack.


Anomaly Nexus:
Forcing the fleet to ground itself will result in nullification.

Risk Assessment:
Low Risk.

Containment Status:
Not contained.

Containment Procedures:
/

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2004_des:
"Smile, hold still… Don't move! Don't blink!"

Anomaly Story
N-0683(Ob), commonly known as "Cheese," is an Anomaly that occasionally appears in places with a high concentration of photography equipment, such as camera shops, film sets, or large conventions. It blends in with ordinary photography gear, posing as a camera. When a scene catches its fancy, Cheese takes a photo on its own. Click! Then, everything within the frame falls into a state of stasis, unable to move. The duration of this effect varies from person to person, ranging from a few minutes to several dozen minutes. However, those who recover from the stasis seem to have no memory of what happened during that, and show no other abnormalities. By then, Cheese has already undergone nullification, satisfied with the photo it captured.
If you discover a camera that turns out to be Cheese, you can call yourself a "Photographer," which allows you to direct Cheese to capture what you want. Cheese will not include the Photographer in the frame when shooting, however, if none of the photos turn out to its satisfaction, it will turn around and freeze the Photographer before undergoing nullification on its own.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Appears similar to an ordinary camera.
· When taking a photo, everything within a certain range in front of the lens enters a state of stasis.
· The duration of stasis varies by individual, ranging from a few minutes to several dozen minutes. The effect on Espers is relatively weaker.
· Claiming to be a "Photographer" to Cheese allows control over what Cheese photographs.

Anomaly Nexus
Undergoes nullification after capturing a satisfying photo.

Risk Assessment
Low hazard.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Celaeno Compound has a certain quantity in containment. Public guarantees are permitted.

Containment Measures
Contain in a darkroom, ensuring the lens' field of view is completely dark.

Experiment Records
Research on the Duration of the Stasis Effect of the Anomaly Cheese
Experiment 1: Have the same person photographed by Cheese in different environments.
Conclusion: Significant variation in stasis duration.

Experiment 2: Photograph different people with Cheese in the same environment.
Conclusion: Significant variation in stasis duration.

Experiment 3: Photograph the same person with different instances of Cheese in the same environment.
Conclusion: Significant variation in stasis duration.
Note: That's it. I'm not falling for this again. You're not doing this for research at all. You're just trying to draw on my face while I'm frozen.

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4004_des:
"Though there is but one moon, the stars that belong to each of us still hang high in the night sky, shining brightly."

Anomaly Story
If you want to make a name for yourself in music but feel you lack a stage to showcase your talents, then Night of Moondog is the perfect venue. The earliest records of this Anomaly date back to ████, describing the same phenomenon that still appears periodically today: a stage and accompanying audience seating floating in the night sky, all staff being ordinary small dogs, a small dog giving each performer a score after their performance, and a stage that may change based on the content of the performance. Night of Moondog follows a format similar to a talent show, where after registering through special rules, performers can take the stage. Since it was deemed harmless and opened to the public, Night of Moondog has gradually become a periodic music celebration.

Although theaters that utilize anomalies to enhance stage effects aren't uncommon nowadays, the experience that Night of Moondog can provide as a complete Anomaly far exceeds human imagination. Among fans of Night of Moondog, the phenomenon where the stage changes according to the performer is called Resonance, and witnessing Resonance is what these audience members yearn to see: the so-called unpredictable stage. During Night of Moondog, all staff share a kind of hive mind, working together under the coordination of this Location Anomaly's self-awareness, Moondog, to ensure the smooth running of performances. Resonance can be seen as a phenomenon that occurs when Moondog is moved by a performer, though this phenomenon does not only occur with performers. The most talked-about Resonance among longtime Night of Moondog audiences actually started from the audience seating: Hethereau's famous landmark, Hethereau Skytower, emerged from the bottom of the stands and connected to the stage. An audience member then leaped onto the stage via the Skytower and completed the performance together with the solo performer on stage.

Without a doubt, Night of Moondog possesses self-awareness, and the existence of Resonance also shows that Moondog has preferences. Yet its scoring is recognized by the vast majority of audiences and music critics as completely objective evaluations based purely on performance quality. A performer who receives the highest score at Night of Moondog may not have given the most spectacular performance, but it will certainly be the most skillful. For this reason, some talent agencies and music schools closely follow each Night of Moondog, hoping to discover talented performers.

If one's inner emotions are strong enough, they can deliver an incredibly brilliant performance with Moondog's approval. If one's skills are refined enough, Night of Moondog will award an admirably high score. With both Resonance and scoring coexisting, every performer can find their own moment to shine at Night of Moondog.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Approximately two weeks before Night of Moondog appears, posters will appear on nearby bulletin boards. The posters will change as the performance date approaches.
· Tearing off a poster that has changed once allows the holder to participate in Night of Moondog on performance day. The torn poster will reappear.
· All Staff at Night of Moondog are common small dogs.
· Under special circumstances, Night of Moondog will resonate with people in the Anomalous Realm, causing the space to change.

Anomaly Nexus
Receiving a perfect score from Moondog, or natural nullification after all participants have finished performing.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
The Bureau of Anomaly Control will be responsible for the maintenance whenever Night of Moondog appears.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2030_des:
"Old soldiers never retire, they merely lie in wait."

Anomaly Story
The fairy-tale play, "The Brave Tin Soldier," written by playwright Cassandra, tells the following story: A child once bought a box of tin soldiers to play games with. Some of the Tin Soldiers are wounded in fierce "battles", while others are awarded plastic "medals". As time progresses, however, these fine soldiers are soon left behind and forgotten. Once the child grew older and finally moved away, the Tin Soldiers were packed up and abandoned, stuck in a lone box soaked by the rain. Thus, the once highly-decorated regiment is disbanded, and left wondering: "What now?"

The soldiers in the tale never found the answer. In reality, however, the "Tin Soldiers" did: they created "Bubble Cans." While some Tin Soldiers venture out to gather materials, others handle the processing and guarding of the Bubble Can Factory. The cans themselves are able to, somehow, seal away fragments of Cassandra's fairy tales.
Some believe that Cassandra's play itself created the "Tin Soldiers". Others believe that the Tin Soldiers were inspired by Cassandra's writing, and thus manifested existence and purpose for themselves. This debate has yet to be resolved, unless someone is willing to ask the author themself.
Nowadays, Tin Soldiers are an uncommon, though not rare, Anomaly. Most remain at the Bubble Can Factory, but those who are sent out to accumulate resources have been encountered. If left unthreatened, these Anomalies will avoid onlookers or passersby.

Characteristics
They appear as brightly painted tin can soldiers, but their physical durability far exceeds what tin should be capable of;
 They often appear in groups;
The toy weapons they carry are as powerful as normal weapons, if not more so.

Anomaly Nexus
Remove the military cap and pull the tab on top of the Tin Soldier's head. If they are not defeated, they will continue aggressive behavior.

Risk Assessment
Low risk.

Containment Status
Four Tin Soldiers are currently contained at the Celaeno Compound. No guarantee is permitted at this time.

Containment Measures
Tin Soldiers can be restrained with sufficiently strong restraining devices. Standard methods include custom handcuffs and leg irons fixed to the floor with electromagnets. As long as they are prevented from using their weapons, they can be safely contained.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_3010_des:
"The chosen one is but the chosen marionette."

[Anomaly Story]
The Fog Coffin Colossus is the physical embodiment of the Fogden's rules. It is not an independently existing being, but the manifestation of the rules within the Fogden. It stands towering and motionless within the Fogden, present from the start of the game to the end.

The colossus begins to announce the rules when the remaining participants reach the arena. Like the mask the participants encountered before, the announcement is not read in a human language, but sent to their minds.
Once the announcement is complete, the colossus begins overseeing the game, watching the participants slaughter one another, eliminating anyone who attempts to sabotage the game, until the last one standing wins. When the game ends, the colossus forms a contract with the winner.

During this incident, Madam T took part in the game as the contract bearer. Before the descent of Code Zero, the colossus showed signs of protecting Madam T, presumably tied to the terms of the previous contract. Once Code Zero appeared, the colossus designated it as the highest-priority and attacked, no longer carrying out its original oversight function, and ceased protecting Madam T. The colossus was ultimately destroyed by Code Zero, vanishing together with the Fogden.

[Characteristics]
Form: The colossus consists of tangled, thorny branches, humanoid in shape, adorned with a mask and a skirt of hanging-branches.
Location: Once the game begins, the colossus remains in the Fogden.
Function: Announces rules to participants in every phase. In the arena, the colossus oversees the game and enforces the rules.

[Anomaly Nexus]
The game ends.

[Risk Assessment]
In the final phase, anyone who avoids attacking others for some time will be attacked by the colossus until they die.

[Containment/Guarantee Status]
Nullified
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1010_des:
"Could it be that she was merely indulging in the role of mother, intoxicated by self-satisfaction?"

Anomaly Story

"The children will soon hatch, and Mommy has prepared everything."
"Brocade and velvet line the bed, a red silk dreamcatcher keeps nightmares away."
"The children will soon be born, and Mommy has practiced over and over."
"Silver bells go jingle jangle, gentle whispers lull you to sleep."

…

Humming the lullaby over and over, the Mother Bird had waited far, far too long for the day her children would be born. She wished to dote upon them, granting them all the beautiful things in the world. With her mind made up, the Mother Bird spread her wings and left the nest. She journeyed around the world before her eggs hatched, gathering countless treasures. She could see it clearly now: when her children are born, their tender faces would be illuminated by the shimmer of gold and silver filling the nest.
That was the very best a mother could prepare for her children. The Mother Bird was certain of this.
And she, too, would be the very best mother.
Whenever she closed her eyes, her heart was filled with visions of nestling with her hatchlings in a nest woven with golden thread and red silk. She dreamed of gently feeding them, watching them grow up healthy and hearty.

But such a scene would never come to pass.
The Mother Bird, so full of anticipation, never got to become a mother.
When she returned to the nest with a gem-studded mask in her beak, she was devastated to find only shattered eggshells. Her children were nowhere to be found.

Who stole my children!!!
Broke their shells and stole them from their mother!!!
It is said the shrill cries from the nest continued for three days and three nights without end.

From that day on, the Mother Bird ceased to exist. Only a bird-like creature wearing a mask with an expression neither smiling nor crying, the Nestbound Bird, remained there, guarding an eggshell with its cracks mended by red thread.
Any living being in this world could be my stolen child, so I shall be the mother of any living being in this world.
My stolen, lost children. Come back to me. Come back to this beautifully decorated nest.
Mommy promises no one will ever separate us again.
Look at these Plumettes sewn from my bones, my feathers, my flesh. They will forever guard this nest.
Come back. Please, call me Mommy.

Children who grew up in Hethereau have mostly heard this story. When lost, never heed the gentle and loving female voice calling your name from who knows where. If you answer that earnest call, you will be taken back to the Nestbound Bird's nest and raised as its child. If you listen to it and call it "Mommy," you will forget yourself forever, destined to become lost in the nest.

Who exactly stole her children? This question seems destined to remain unanswered, or perhaps the Mother Bird knew the answer all along…
The Mother Bird, so blinded by decorating a comfortable nest for her children, neglected to actually care for and accompany them. The newly hatched chicks could not find their mother and, driven by hunger, had no choice but to leave the nest. Their whereabouts remain unknown.
What does it matter if the truth is simple and clear? The Mother Bird no longer exists.
Only the Nestbound Bird's earnest calls for her children continue to echo.


Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly resembles a giant bird-like creature with its face concealed by a human-faced mask. It generally dwells in an Anomalous Realm it calls its "nest."
· It calls out to lost children in a gentle, loving female voice, then abducts the entranced children to its nest.
· After the Nestbound Bird succeeds, it hangs a mask at the archway of the "nest" entrance, signifying its protection over the abducted child.

Anomaly Nexus
"The identity of mother"

Risk Assessment
Critical risk.

Containment/Guarantee Status
/

Containment Measures
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1018_des:
"Season it, salt it—solve it."

Anomaly Story:
In certain parts of the world, there are people who seek out a "Garlicbeak" to resolve their arguments, disagreements, and conflicts. The process of summoning a Garlicbeak is as follows: each person acquires one feather from a Garlicbeak, and recites the phrase, "Season it, salt it—solve it". Once the Garlicbeak manifests, the initial conflict between the two parties is forgotten entirely.
At a glance, the Garlicbeak looks like a common bird. However, upon closer inspection, it's revealed that the Garlicbeak's 'feathers' are instead individual garlic slices. Garlicbeaks are primarily drawn towards loud noises. As a result, verbal arguments, screaming, and yelling attract their attention. Garlicbeak feathers are, in fact, edible and taste like garlic. Garlicbeak feathers are known to have a soothing effect when ingested and are commonly used as a relaxant for those suffering from anxiety, conflict, or unease.
However, the calming effect of Garlicbeak feathers is limited to superficial struggles. They cannot be used to solve severe emotional distress. Overindulgence in Garlicbeak feathers can cause a pungent garlic smell to be emitted from the consumer's body. Garlicbeaks can regrow their feathers, unless they experience heavy feather loss in a short amount of time, in which they undergo nullification.

Characteristics:
· A Bio Anomaly resembling the common bird with garlic slices for feathers.
· Feathers can be ingested and utilized as a relaxant.

Anomaly Nexus:
Undergoes nullification when experiencing extreme feather loss in a short amount of time.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
A certain number of Garlicbeak are contained at the Celaeno Compound and the Anomaly sanctuary "Sunward Island"; eligible individuals may act as Guarantors.

Containment Procedures:
No special containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
"Study on the Regeneration Rate of Bio Anomaly, Garlicbeak, and Its Feathers"
……
Conclusion: The regeneration speed of a Garlicbeak's feathers shows an exponential positive correlation with the number of feathers lost. When one feather is lost, studies approximate 12 hours for full feather regeneration. After losing 100 feathers, the Garlicbeak displays clear signs of fatigue, but will recover fully in roughly 7 days.
Note: All Garlicbeak feathers collected in this experiment have been destroyed in accordance with Bio Anomaly waste-disposal standards. The cafeteria's proposal to use Garlicbeak feathers to develop new menu items has been rejected.

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1011_des:
"Though it has a big head, there's nothing inside."

Anomaly Story
Hello, nice to meet you. I'm… who am I? Hello, who are you?
Huh, why am I swimming around here…? Oh, oh, I guess this is the only place that I can swim around.
Hello, who are you?
What can you possibly remember in seven seconds… What's your name again?

Mhm! I'm guessing that's what goes through some Bonzitas' heads!
Actually, most goldfish can retain memories for over a month, but the saying "goldfish only have seven-second memories" spread so widely that fat-headed fish Oddities that actually only have seven-second memories appeared: the Bonzita.
This harmless Bio Anomaly is pretty common. You can find them in aquariums, pet markets, Bio Anomaly shelters… I actually keep one myself, and it's super cute! Too bad I can't go into detail in an official profile. What a shame!

Anomaly Characteristics
· Most have no worries, since they can't remember what they were worried about anyway.
· Sizes vary.
· They swim freely in water. Their greatest hobby is blowing bubbles, which can become exceptionally large and last exceptionally long, even longer than their memories.
· Occasionally, some individuals become withdrawn due to their poor memory. "Why can't I ever make friends?" "There's something I should remember, isn't there?"… Things like that. They're the "deep thinkers" of the species: forgetful philosophers.

Anomaly Nexus
Make it remember at least one thing within seven seconds.

Risk Assessment
Harmless.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Contained in large numbers at Bio Anomaly shelters; widely guaranteed by civilians.

Containment Measures
Containment unit consists of a fish tank.
No special measures required. Regular feeding is sufficient.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_4001_des:
"This brutal ??? shall end in ???."

Anomaly Story
The garden of the Serenetti family was once a place of elegance and solemnity, and like the rest of the family, was shrouded in the patriarch's strict rules. These rules regulated every aspect of his children's behavior, molding them into tools for the family's glory who appeared harmonious on the surface but harbored no true affection for one another. In his later years, the patriarch was bedridden with illness. His children returned to the garden, not to visit him, but to quarrel endlessly over their inheritance. The aging, powerless patriarch had lost control over his family, as siblings turned against each other, making a mockery of the once orderly family. Sharp words and underhanded schemes shattered the garden's silence. They made no effort to hide their disgust and resentment toward their powerless father, who had oppressed them their entire lives. The elderly patriarch was heartbroken, and a dark thought began to take root:
"If only these kids could be as quiet and dignified as plants and flowers."
And so, silence once again descended upon the garden. The venomous words fell silent, but the malice did not cease. Instead, it nourished the greenery within the garden. The patriarch had hoped these plants would help his children understand the beauty of order and obedience, but this was merely wishful thinking. That endless malice was transformed, becoming sharp thorns, toxic pollen, and twisted vines. The children imprisoned in this garden their whole lives continued their silent attacks on one another, while also turning their new weapons against the one responsible for it all: their father. In the end, the patriarch died from pollen poisoning, and his children fell silent one by one. The peace he had longed for his entire life returned to his garden in a way he never imagined.

The Silent Garden is a Location Anomaly that has taken over the former site of the Serenetti garden. Since its emergence, the Serenetti garden has effectively been abandoned. Although ownership still passes among the family's few remaining descendants, no one is willing to return to claim this cursed land. The garden is overrun by wildly spreading vegetation, and for most of the time, the Silent Garden remains dormant. However, when a creature capable of speech becomes the Gardener, the entire Anomaly activates. Within the Silent Garden, the Gardener's words are erased and muffled, and the garden responds to the erased words by growing various plants to decorate itself.
The plants in the Silent Garden share many similarities with normal plants. For example, they are drawn to sunlight and can perform photosynthesis, though none of the nutrients produced ever benefit the Gardener in the slightest. The plants in the garden become more active and aggressive during the day, thriving in the abundant sunlight. Therefore, investigations and patrols of the Silent Garden should be conducted at night whenever possible. When the garden is active, precautionary measures should also be taken after nightfall.
The creation of a Gardener does not seem to be entirely related to the individual's will. Those who wish to control the garden may find their efforts in vain, but curious passersby may be unwittingly captured by the garden. The Silent Garden does not act according to the Gardener's wishes, disregarding the Gardener's original intentions, as plants that grow will always possess a malicious nature. When outsiders disturb the silence of this land, these plants will attack to drive away intruders. At the same time, these plants drain the Gardener's life away, converting it into nourishment for themselves. It is like a reenactment of that absurd scene from years ago: the head of the family bound by the rules he obsessed over his entire life, while his children did as they pleased, coveting his inheritance, ultimately taking his life.
These plants will strip the Gardener of their ability to speak, aiming to keep the garden eternally silent. However, if the Gardener overcomes the restraints through sheer willpower and breaks the garden's silence with their voice, the garden is likely to become dormant once more. Yet under the garden's powerful restraints, with the Gardener's life dwindling by the day, how can they possibly find their voice?

If you bury seeds of belladonna and aconite in the soil, no matter how carefully you tend them, no matter how beautiful the plants that grow, you cannot change the deadly poison in their nature. The one who started it all suppressed speech in this silent garden, demanded etiquette, grounded down individuality, and treated family members as mere garden ornaments, stubbornly believing this would make the family a model for others. But the peace and harmony he pursued his entire life ultimately shrouded the garden in eternal silence, leaving behind only abandonment, disorder, and oblivion…

Anomaly Characteristics
· Usually dormant. Becomes active when a creature capable of speech becomes the Gardener.
· When active, it strips the Gardener of their speech and vitality, converting them into aggressive plants within the garden.
· Plants in the garden prioritize enforcing the rule of silence and driving away noisy intruders.
· Plants in the garden are drawn to light like normal plants. Nighttime is relatively safer.

Anomaly Nexus
Eliminate or rescue the Gardener, or the Gardener breaks the garden's silence with words. Note that even if the Silent Garden enters dormancy as a result, it may reactivate if a new Gardener emerges.

Risk Assessment
Harmless in dormant state. Poses a moderate threat when activated by a Gardener. Threat range is limited to the area around the garden.

Containment/Guarantee Status
The garden is private property belonging to the descendants of the Serenetti family. Containment or demolition cannot be implemented due to this. Currently, only regular patrols are maintained.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
C-3624-1(Or) Serenetti
C-3624-2(Or) Fleur the Storyteller
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1023_des:
"The wheel of fortune spins on forevermore."

Anomaly Story:
Fate had decided upon a pair of twin goldfish—one gold and one silver, scooping them up and dropping them in the same tank, thus transforming them into the "Temporal Fish".
The owner of the pair of goldfish claimed that, on one random morning, they had stumbled upon their pet goldfish swimming in circles repeatedly. Though panicked at the time, the owner said that the fish eventually separated and resumed their normal behavior. However, over the next few days, the odd behavior returned. Over time, the owner noticed that, on the days the fish swam clockwise, his business would pull a profit. On the contrary, when the fish swam counterclockwise, the business suffered. After contacting the Bureau of Anomaly Control, it was confirmed that these two otherwise unremarkable goldfish had awakened as an Anomaly: the "Temporal Fish".
Whether the Temporal Fish can actually predict the future, or swim in certain directions by sheer coincidence, cannot be determined. Nevertheless, the Temporal Fish's popularity has grown amongst the public in recent years, causing uproar amongst those who wish to obtain them. There have even been recorded incidents of radical action, such as an attempted assassination of the business owner, to acquire the Temporal Fish.

Characteristics:
· A pair of goldfish, one with golden scales and one with silver, that assume regular goldfish behavior. However, every day at exactly 6:00 AM, the pair links head to tail and swim in a ring for fifteen minutes before returning to normal. It's been said that when swimming clockwise, good fortune is sure to follow. When counter-clockwise, vice versa.

Anomaly Nexus:
It's hypothesized that the separation of the two fish may result in nullification.

Risk Assessment:
Harmless.

Containment Status:
Privately owned.

Containment Procedures:
No containment procedures required.

Experiment Record:
/

Derivative Anomaly:
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1003_des:
Before the black cat came, we had nothing. After the black cat came, we had everything.

Anomaly Story
Mammon came into existence long ago, when ancient tribes first began fighting over treasure and territory. The Anomaly's true form is that of a massive black beast, yet it chooses to appear before people as a black cat with golden eyes, adorned with lavish jewelry. It is a omen of desire, with a keen nose that can sniff out the scent of greed. This elegant black cat prowls near wars sparked by avarice, seizing desires to satisfy its bottomless appetite. Besides desire, Mammon also loves to devour money. After all, for thousands of years, humanity has never given up its pursuit and possession of wealth, so the greed attached to coin is often the richest and purest.
In the modern times, conflicts have all but ceased. Once people's basic needs are largely met, the little desire they retain isn't even enough to serve as a snack for Mammon. As the hungry black cat was searching for food, its gaze fell upon the wealthiest family in Hethereau, the Dvořák family, and the Anomaly that could bring infinite wealth, Ladon. Thus, Pink Paws Bank and Gold Apple Collection Hall became the two locations Mammon frequents most. Predictably, the deplorable act of devouring gold coins is absolutely intolerable to Ladon, who views Mammon as a natural enemy. The moment Mammon's trail appears nearby, Ladon will mercilessly drive it away, refusing to stop until Mammon is nullified. To humans, the conflict between these two Anomalies appears to be nothing more than two bad-tempered cats fighting. Before long, their "guardians", representatives of the Dvořák family and members of ETD, will arrive with dried fish and balls of yarn to mediate. This is a common sight to see. Apart from Fons being swallowed by Mammon, their disputes have not caused any real harm to other people or buildings. But from the perspective of the Anomalies, every time they roll up their sleeves and prepare to give the other a good thrashing, some meddlesome humans always show up to watch or break up the fight… This must give both cats quite the headache.
In truth, Mammon may have arrived in this city much earlier than people realize. Several decades ago, a massive and violent beast-type Anomaly suddenly appeared in the central area of Hethereau and attacked nearby residents, causing a great panic. The Bureau of Anomaly Control was urgently dispatched to contain this unknown Anomaly, but it fled after its defeat and its whereabouts became unknown. Personnel involved in the containment conducted a carpet search of the surrounding area but found nothing, with no trace of this monster surfacing again. According to reliable sources, that Anomaly was actually Mammon's true form. After being defeated, it did not leave, choosing instead to wander the streets in the guise of a stray cat. For unknown reasons, its Wertheimer Index fluctuations are extremely low, so the Bureau of Anomaly Control never detected its presence. No one would connect the Fons thief currently running rampant in Hethereau with the black beast that once caused so much trouble… But what brought Mammon to this city in the first place? Why does it truly linger here? The secrets hidden behind those golden eyes may only be uncovered by those who come after…
In my opinion, even if Mammon were to devour the entire Dvořák family's fortune- no, all the wealth in Hethereau, or even the entire world, it would only temporarily appease its insatiable heart. Desire itself can never be truly satisfied. One needs only look back at history: no matter how much desire is fulfilled, new desires will continue to emerge endlessly. Perhaps it is under this powerful catalyst that the wheels of our society keep rolling forward, never ceasing.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Its true form is a massive black beast. Under normal circumstances, it appears as a black cat with golden eyes.
· Feeds on human greed and money. Seems to possess the ability to amplify human desires.

Anomaly Nexus
Giving Mammon what it craves will achieve temporary nullification.

Risk Assessment
Moderate risk. Generally harmless to humans, but since it is impossible to predict when it might go berserk, cautious contact is advised.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly. Not in containment.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
/
ST_Manual.NounManual_3_3_des:

These Modules are split into two categories based on their roles: Core Modules and Common Modules. Common Modules are available in four types—Type I, II, III, and IV—with higher-grade Modules offering better advantages.

The Arc features a non-0° arc degree as its unique identifier and must be rotated to the correct degree for use. ST_Manual.ManualVision_1012_des:
Anomaly Story

"We'll sweep the rain away! Then the sun will come out soon!"

Rain-Sweeping Maid is an Anomaly with a long and storied history. Documented sightings can be traced back hundreds of years: "On a rainy day, my broom suddenly ran outside to sweep away the water!"
Yes, in the earliest written records, they were spirits shaped like brooms or mops. When they dozed off with their eyes closed, they looked no different from ordinary cleaning tools. As brooms and mops were gradually phased out of households in favor of robotic vacuums and floor washers, Rain-Sweeping Maids' forms seemed to adapt to this change, taking on more… modern technological features. Perhaps this made them more efficient at cleaning?
No matter how times have changed, the Rain-Sweeping Maids has always been a Bio Anomaly with a drive to sweep away rainwater. On sunny days, they appear relaxed and sluggish, but the second it rains, they rush outdoors to "clean" the rain, absorbing it into their bodies for temporary storage, firmly believing this will make the rainy weather pass more quickly… It is said a single Rain-Sweeping Maid can absorb up to several swimming pools worth of water, and will keep working until the entire rainy season ends. After the rain clears, they seek out rivers to discharge the rainwater stored inside them.
In the past, people believed the Rain-Sweeping Maid was likely an Anomaly born from humanity's wish for the rain to stop and the sun to shine. Hundreds of years ago, people often paid them respect or offered prayers, sometimes tying ribbons to their seemingly sentient mop handles to thank them for their help to humanity… But today, very few people appreciate this Anomaly. Now, you hardly ever see a Rain-Sweeping Maid with human tributes on her vacuum hose. If you ask city residents what they think of them… some will even exclaim in half-exasperated, half-annoyed tones: "These Oddities are ridiculously stupid!"
In ancient times, the Rain-Sweeping Maids' behavior of temporarily storing rainwater like sponges and acting as a buffer layer could indeed alleviate flooding in villages that lacked drainage systems. But in modern cities with complete drainage infrastructure, their endless absorbing and discharging of water serves virtually no practical purpose.
Worse still, perhaps because modern rainwater contains far more chemical pollutants than in the past, Rain-Sweeping Maids that have absorbed excessive contaminated water may begin to exhibit chaotic, violent behavior. The Rain-Sweeping Maid who always used to smile are now covered in black, their faces often twisted in expressions of pain. The polluted water accumulating inside them causes corrosion, causing constant burning agony. Driven by their nature and unable to stop absorbing rainwater, the Rain-Sweeping Maids affected by pollution are no longer able to discharge water properly. They end up crashing around like balloons, spewing rainwater erratically, even attacking humans who walk into their rain curtain… With the climate becoming increasingly extreme and unpredictable, a Rain-Sweeping Maid might encounter a sudden cold snap before she can empty her stored rainwater. This causes the rainwater she discharges to freeze into sleet, hail, or even snow, triggering a severe blizzard in localized areas. These are situations that never would have happened before.
An ancient, gentle, and stable Anomaly species has undergone a fundamental change due to shifts in era and environment… As a prime example of an Anomaly transformed by the human social environment, the Rain-Sweeping Maid holds considerable research value. If atmospheric pollution and extreme weather can be brought under control in the future, those Oddities who always smiled happily while quietly waiting for the sun to shine might return to our side once again…

Anomaly Characteristics

· In the past, Rain-Sweeping Maids resembled brooms or mops with a wooden pole standing upright on their heads, but the crisscrossing 'apple pie'-like cloth strips below were their actual bodies. The wooden pole was merely decorative. As times changed, the broom and mop-like wooden poles gradually "evolved" into flexible hose tails resembling vacuum cleaners or floor washers, and the way Rain-Sweeping Maids absorb rainwater changed accordingly. The formerly decorative tail developed the function of absorbing rainwater, while their main body became a water storage container.
· Rain-Sweeping Maids love sunny days and dislike rainy days, but they do not complain about the weather they dislike. Instead, they become more active and attempt to change the situation, which is why rainy days gets them up and about.
· They are stronger than they appear, and as such, being struck by their rainwater-filled tail is quite painful. They have sharp teeth on their "suction nozzle," but rarely use them for attacking. Although Rain-Sweeping Maids can overcome the weight of their tails and hover steadily in the air, they usually keep their tails pressed close to the ground and "crawl" forward when sweeping up rainwater, like an unmanned upright vacuum cleaner.
· After absorbing large amounts of rainwater, their body will visibly swell. If polluted water is absorbed, their body turns black or develops oily stains.
· During the process of discharging and reabsorbing rainwater, if the surrounding temperature drops sharply, the "black rain" in their water circulation system undergoes a phase change and continues to circulate in solid ice form.
· Out-of-Control Rain-Sweeping Maids discharge and reabsorb rainwater repeatedly, causing a "black rain reflux" phenomenon in a small radius. If someone wanders into the rain curtain's range, they may be attacked by the Rain-Sweeping Maid. If you can help them release the polluted water and restore them to a dry state, they can be easily contained or subjected to nullification.

Anomaly Nexus

Drain all the rainwater stored in its body.

Risk Assessment

Friendly to humans when dry, but will attack humans who wander into its rain curtain range when it is filled with rainwater.

Containment/Guarantee Status

The Celaeno Compound currently contains one Rain-Sweeping Maid that still retains the original form with a wooden pole on its head.

Containment Measures

Purify or drain the polluted water inside its body to contain it.

Experiment Records

Experiment Objective: Verify the Rain-Sweeping Maid's behavioral criteria.
Experiment Process: Research personnel placed the same Rain-Sweeping Maid successively in four environments: natural rainfall, artificial rainfall, beneath a waterfall, and an indoor rain curtain Landscaping installation. They observed its reactions to "water falling from above" in different situations.
Experiment Results: In both natural and artificial rainfall environments, the Rain-Sweeping Maid showed clear reactions and immediately began absorbing rainwater. However, beneath the waterfall and in the indoor rain curtain landscaping installation, the specimen showed no reaction whatsoever. It is therefore hypothesized that the Rain-Sweeping Maid has a specific identification mechanism for determining what constitutes a "rain."


Derivative Anomaly
/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2001_des:
Anomaly Story

"A banquet that abducts but not invites is destined to welcome only reluctant guests."

There are many legends about the origin of Anomaly C-1704, commonly known as the "Expired Invitation." The following is the most widely circulated:

Long, long ago, as a wealthy merchant was nearing the end of his life, he reflected on his years: mountains of wealth, countless honors, and though he had no children, he was always surrounded by people wherever he went. The merchant was quite satisfied. "I have no regrets in this life," he thought.
Just then, laughter drifted in from outside his enormous floor-to-ceiling window. He struggled to sit up and peered through, spotting a family was holding a party across the street. Children chased each other, laughing and playing. When they grew tired, they climbed onto their elders' laps to beg for sweets. The dishes on the table were modest, but the flickering candlelight looked so warm and bright… Meanwhile, in the vast bedroom where the merchant lay, how cold the light from the crystal chandelier seemed!
The merchant's banquet hall had once been packed with guests, but none of those gatherings had ever felt so warm. Every wine glass held invisible interests, exchanged with each gentle clink of the rim. Yes, the merchant thought: I want to hold a "true banquet."
And so, he ordered countless invitations to be sent out. The next day, the merchant forced himself out of his sickbed, changed into a loose evening suit, and had his Butler wheel him to the banquet hall. But when he opened the doors, not a soul was in attendance…
The merchant refused to believe that perhaps he was not as beloved as he had imagined. That night, he tossed and turned, making a silent promise: If anyone comes to my banquet tomorrow, I will open my mansion, my gardens, and my treasury to them, and let them choose any gift they should so desire.
Still, not one soul came.
On the second night, the merchant thought: If anyone comes to my banquet tomorrow, I will give them my most precious thing… my wealth!
Still, no one came.
On the third night, the merchant thought: If anyone comes to my banquet tomorrow, I will do everything in my power to grant all their seemingly impossible wishes!
Still, the halls were empty.

Time passed, and the merchant's illness worsened in his solitude. At last, he no longer had the strength to rise from bed. Hearing the footsteps of death's approach, he felt regret, rage, and resentment churn and swell within his cooling body. With his final breath before dawn, the merchant uttered a curse: Whoever opens my invitation shall never leave my "banquet."


The truth of this legend remains unknown as I record this profile. What we can confirm is this: the merchant's dying curse may be one of the most destructive "curses" in human history, so much so that even when people use it as a swear, they cannot help but feel a twinge of dread.
Now, although the gardens of eternal spring have long fallen to ruin and the magnificent mansion has changed hands, those expired invitations still bear the merchant's curse. They appear to be nothing more than an oversized golden wax seal, unremarkable aside from their size… but the moment someone accidentally touches one, they are forced to become an "invitee" of the Expired Invitation and "visit" a dim courtyard constructed entirely of cardboard.
The cardboard castle folded within the invitation dutifully despises every guest, unfurling a malicious red carpet eager to devour all that approach, simultaneously raising weapons fit for a siege. The tardy guests flee in panic, barely escaping with their lives. The bell announcing the end of the banquet should be its Nexus, but as if to punish these late arrivals, it too is always fashionably late. Beyond that, unless the entire Anomaly is violently subjected to nullification, nothing can stop it from toying with the next passerby who is forcibly invited.
In recent years, thanks to the joint efforts of the Circle and Anomaly Hunters, the quantity of Expired Invitations has been greatly reduced. However, some may still lurk in streets and alleyways… Since the total number cannot be determined, we have no way of knowing how long this prolonged vengeance will continue, nor whether new invitations might be born should another host somewhere harbor similar resentments toward guests who refused to attend.
Perhaps the way these invitations come into being has never been truly understood. A long-told story may simply be repeated to perpetuate itself. The more I study, the more I realize how little humanity knows about anomalies.
However, at least one thing is certain: when you go for a walk, remember to watch your step.

Anomaly Characteristics

· Appears as a large golden wax seal, typically found on flat ground.
· Humans who directly touch the wax seal are drawn into a pop-up book-style Anomalous Realm, forced to attend an "expired banquet."
· The seemingly fairytale-like Anomalous Realm is actually hostile toward intruders. Once inside, visitors will certainly be attacked by the cardboard castle and the cardboard red carpet.
· The total quantity is unknown, the locations are unknown, and the duration after triggering is unknown. After a guest escapes the Anomalous Realm, it folds back into the form of a wax seal. The Anomaly can be triggered multiples.
· After nullification, the wax seal burns itself out completely, leaving behind a treasure chest in its place. This is perhaps the party favor originally prepared for guests.

Anomaly Nexus

The bell announcing "the end of the banquet"

Risk Assessment

Before Activation: Stable. After Activation: Highly aggressive toward humans who enter the Anomalous Realm.

Containment/Guarantee Status

5 specimens in long-term containment at Celaeno Compound.

Containment Measures

No special measures required. Simply ensure containment in an environment where ordinary people cannot make contact and the Anomaly cannot be accidentally triggered.

Experiment Records

Experiment 1
Dispatched one test subject with sufficient supplies into the Expired Invitation's space to observe the time required for the Anomaly to naturally undergo nullification.
After 119 hours, the experiment was terminated out of concern for the test subject's physical and mental endurance. The Expired Invitation showed zero signs of natural nullification.

Experiment 2
Test subject entered the space carrying multiple timing devices, playing bell sounds and announcing "the banquet is over" at different intervals to observe the Anomalous Realm's response.
The Expired Invitation did not respond to any of the sounds. Preliminary assessment: objective changes in and external announcements cannot trigger nullification of the Expired Invitation.

Derivative Anomaly

/
ST_Manual.ManualVision_1025_des:
Anomaly Story
"Behave yourselves. These little ones are gentle, as warnings go. Get carried away, and something far worse may come next…"

An Anomaly group that appeared in Hethereau around the same time as "Justice Executioner." From the very beginning, they seemed intimately familiar with Hethereau Public Safety Ordinance, including every amendment and annotation. Not long after arriving uninvited, they brazenly attempted to blend in with the city's officers. Having already witnessed the oppressive presence of Justice Executioner, the Bureau did not let its guard down around these Anomalies. For a long time, they were treated as Anomalies associated with Justice Executioner and monitored with caution. During that period, "Officer Whisker" clumsily tried to act as street vigilantes while also enduring the Bureau's hasty containment attempts. This is not meant as criticism of those colleagues who are also members of the Circle.
Eventually, the Anomaly won the affection of most citizens and indirectly became an important turning point in Hethereau's acceptance of Anomalies after the Fifth Calamity. The Bureau was also forced to admit that Officer Whisker's motivation was truly simple: to keep Hethereau's public order at a high standard. Nothing more. Later, the Anomaly was officially incorporated into the public security office and received gear and uniforms designed specifically for them.

Although these Anomalies show great enthusiasm and endless patience for routine public security patrols, their appearance alone makes one thing clear: these small, rodent-like Anomalies are not built to intimidate potential criminals. Their combat ability is not especially impressive, either. Even so, Officer Whisker responds to every dispatch with extraordinary enthusiasm and accompanies other officers to the scene as quickly as possible.
Within this Anomaly group are three populations distinguished by body color: red, yellow, and green. Research from Zerogon Laboratory notes that the most commonly sighted "yellow" individuals seem to intentionally create a relaxed, easygoing atmosphere, which can reduce traffic accidents or violent conflicts caused by heightened emotions in the surrounding area. This population is also regarded as the most senior among Officer Whisker, and only they participate in handling incidents they consider "high-risk," such as traffic violations or public disturbances. Individuals from the "red" population show a strong fixation on maintaining current order. When they appear in public, nearby citizens may be affected by a level ▊ psychological suggestion, slightly increasing their respect for laws and regulations. The traits of the "green" population remain comparatively unclear, though they may be related to granting vitality or various positive emotions to others. Zerogon Laboratory has not disclosed the exact strength of these traits. Regardless, these traits do not change the fact that Officer Whisker has become an iconic symbol of the Hethereau Public Security Office, thanks to its ability to maintain officer morale and improve the office's image among citizens.

Their peculiar connection to Justice Executioner is another trait of Officer Whisker that warrants deeper investigation. For example, the oddly distinctive vehicles often noticed by observers are not provided by the public security office. Like the other tools they use, these vehicles appear to be cobbled together from materials gathered in Justice Executioner's Forest of Traffic Lights. How these absurd little pieces of equipment function, and where Officer Whisker acquired the knowledge to make them, remain unsolved mysteries.
Despite the impression given by their gentle, harmless appearance, Yggash Court has yet to record any credible report of their nullification. It should be noted that excessive attention to methods of nullifying Officer Whisker may be regarded as an act of hostility toward the entire city of Hethereau. When facing a single Officer Whisker, most adult citizens are capable of subduing it, and Esper criminals can easily repel groups of vehicle-riding Officer Whisker. However, records show that individuals who disappear after being defeated are not actually nullified. Instead, they retreat to the steel jungle where Justice Executioner resides to recover, then reappear after varying periods of time. In one observed case, an individual disappeared after being fed an excessive number of doughnuts by citizens. It has been confirmed that this, too, was not the corresponding Nexus of Officer Whisker. Rather, it appears that Justice Executioner interpreted "obesity caused by excessive sugar and fat intake" as a condition that made continued duty impossible, then recalled the overweight individual for mandatory exercise and weight loss.

There has long been a view within Yggash Court: while the intimidating rumors surrounding Justice Executioner continue to grow and spread, Officer Whisker is also softening the city's atmosphere in its own way. Deterring potential criminals is certainly important, but isn't it even more vital to give law-abiding citizens lasting confidence that their lives can remain peaceful? It is hard not to see this as an extremely sophisticated method of governance. Yet this raises an even more fundamental question: have people misunderstood which side is truly central to this symbiotic relationship? Which side was it that actively established this marvelous cooperation?

Characteristics
They often appear alongside Security Officers in armed form during unlawful incidents, but can also be seen patrolling the streets in a more relaxed manner.
·They carry a variety of nonlethal weapons and tools of uncertain origin, which they use to stop and pursue citizens who violate the law.
·They come in red, yellow, and green populations, with subtle differences in personality and appearance even among individuals of the same population.
·They appear to have some kind of symbiotic relationship with the unique Anomaly "Justice Executioner." Attacking Officer Whisker seems to greatly increase a criminal's so-called "Evil Index" in Justice Executioner's eyes.
·They are unquestionably closer to squirrels than hamsters. I will continue to stand by this view.

Anomaly Nexus
Insufficient clearance. Currently inaccessible.

Risk Assessment
Basically harmless. This Anomaly's behavior follows known fixed patterns. Officer Whisker will only stop citizens who are clearly caught committing unlawful acts, and their attacks are highly restrained and nonlethal. The only exception occurs when an offender causes excessive harm to an individual of this Anomaly. In such cases, the subsequent risk assessment must be raised by at least ▊ levels, and the consequences should be borne by the offender.

Containment/Guarantee Status
All are guaranteed by the Hethereau Security Office. At present, ▊▊▊▊ Officer Whisker individuals are active within Hethereau. This number fluctuates slightly, but all newly appearing individuals voluntarily report to Security Office headquarters for registration. No individuals have yet been observed outside the office's jurisdiction.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Record
Test: Intervene in random street disputes; station yellow-population Officer Whisker individuals at specific accident-prone road sections; request increased Security Office patrols in certain blocks with yellow-population individuals participating.
Result: Confrontational states eased in ▊▊% of observed subjects. Conflict-related dangerous driving incidents on the test road section decreased by ▊▊% compared with the control group. Crimes of passion in the test block are still being counted, but the overall trend is downward.
Note: A small increase in unlawful incidents appears to have occurred around the test block due to the transfer of yellow-population individuals for the test. The Security Office has now filed a formal protest with the laboratory.

Test: Simulate various extremely minor violations in daily situations. Invite red-population Officer Whisker individuals to participate and randomly place them in darkrooms near the experimental group sites.
Conclusion: The effect is equivalent to a level ▊ psychological suggestion. The number of test personnel showing clear resistance to unlawful behavior increased by ▊▊% compared with the control group, though this influence is largely ineffective on those who already lack reverence for authority.
Note: Site supervisors are advised to pay closer attention to members who displayed a challenging attitude toward authority during this experiment.

Test: Invite green-population Officer Whisker individuals to remain along the commuting route of staff at laboratory site ▊▊. Randomly select subjects at the start of work, at the end of work, and during sudden overtime, then assess their physical and mental vitality.
Result: The phenomenon's effect is approximately ▊‰... After further confirmation, observed subjects generally stated that their "mood improved slightly." However, it is difficult to determine whether this was due to the Anomaly traits of this population or simply because the Anomaly's appearance is endearing.
Note: After the experiment concluded, the participating green-population individual fell into a rather dejected state. Yellow-population Officer Whisker in the waiting area immediately expressed dissatisfaction toward the researchers. The test subject then began displaying behavior resembling mutual encouragement, and its mood improved again.

Test: Borrow individual No. ▊▊▊▊ from the Security Office. After obtaining its consent, attempt to reproduce the recovery-return process used by Officer Whisker and verify the principle behind it.
Result: The experiment triggered a reaction from Justice Executioner within site ▊▊. A total of ▊▊ personnel were injured, and the experiment was terminated.
Note: This project may only be restarted with joint authorization from more than ▊ site-supervisor-level personnel from Zerogon Laboratory, the Bureau of Anomaly Control, and Yggash Court.
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2007_des:
Anomaly Story
The Eternal Lamp is an Anomaly that emerged with the invention of electric lighting, having transformed from discarded light bulbs.
In the earliest records, the Eternal Lamp looked very different from its current form, appearing as an ordinary small light bulb. Its unique ability was being able to glow continuously without any attached power supply. Research revealed that the Eternal Lamp was actually siphoning electricity from other light bulbs to do so. Within a one-kilometer radius, all other bulbs would dim noticeably.
As technology advanced and new types of electric lights replaced old bulbs, the Eternal Lamp gradually completed its evolution: no longer limited to stealing power from lights alone, it began stealing all forms of electricity. Its appearance also became larger and more aggressive.
The survival pressure on the Eternal Lamp drove its evolution, and the abundance of electricity of the new era provided the perfect source of energy for this transformation. Under these favorable conditions, the Eternal Lamp completed its metamorphosis from a mere light bulb to its current form. It seems anomalies are not static after their creation, but can adapt and change over time.

Anomaly Characteristics
This Anomaly commonly appears in groups in alleyways at night, plunging the surrounding area into power outages accompanied by spreading black fog. Entire blocks succumb into darkness, severely disrupting residents' daily lives.
Additionally, its stealing behavior damages the circuit boards of power facilities. After charging itself to full capacity, the anomaly enters a satiated state and gradually grows stronger, requiring ever more electricity.
This Anomaly appears extremely stingy with its stored power, strictly controlling electricity usage with each attack. Attempting to drain its power externally will provoke intense resistance.
After the yellow core battery is destroyed, the Eternal Lamp will collapse. If other active Eternal Lamps are nearby, they will move to recharge their fallen companion, bringing it back into the battle. Therefore, all Eternal Lamps in the area must be defeated simultaneously to achieve nullification.
After this Anomaly undergoes nullification, the power it siphoned will return, any damage caused will restore itself, and the surrounding fog will dissipate.

Anomaly Nexus
A single Eternal Lamp becomes paralyzed once its yellow core battery is destroyed. Complete nullification requires defeating all Eternal Lamps in the area simultaneously.

Risk Assessment
Its behavior disrupts residents' normal lives and poses an explosion risk. Prompt nullification upon discovery is recommended.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Containment costs are too high and research value too low. Containment is not recommended. Standard protocol is nullification.

Containment Measures
Requires continuous power supply to the containment unit.

Experiment Records
Experiment 1
Drained electricity from an Eternal Lamp individual. The subject exhibited intense aggressive behavior. After complete power extraction, the subject self-destructed.
Experiment 2
Attempted to continuously supply sufficient electricity to an Eternal Lamp. Power was continuously absorbed until the experiment was terminated due to a small-scale laboratory blackout.
Conclusion: Containment costs for this Anomaly are too high and research value too low. Containment is not recommended.

Derivative Anomaly
None

Extended Info
None
ST_Manual.ManualVision_2013_des:
Anomaly Story
You and your kind were invented by humans. Humans said you were their greatest invention, manufacturing you in all shapes and forms to send into every household… Yet many, many years later, they declared that you were humanity's worst invention. You polluted the world. You should disappear from this planet.
You know that many of your kind are indeed causing enormous trouble in the oceans, but after all, right now you are just a small, quiet, blue, plastic basin…
You feel angry about being blamed for things you did not do, and want to see what the oceans really look like now. You don't realize that as an anomalous plastic basin, you are connected to a different ocean, one residing in the void…
"So this is an angry plastic basin?"
"Correction: an angry plastic basin that does not know how to express itself, though I think it might not be so angry anymore. Now it is treated like a treasure, with lines of people waiting to borrow the reflections in this basin to find guidance. It is no longer one of those pollutants."
"So, what this basin is connected to is actually that…"
"Yes, that place… Let us not put it in the profile."

Anomaly Characteristics
· When not filled with water, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary washbasin.
· When filled with water, if one observes their own reflection on the water's surface, they will see a strange vision about themselves, including but not limited to fantasies, futures, etc. The content and accuracy of these visions has not yet been accurately determined.
· Each individual can only see a strange vision once. On any subsequent observations, they will only see a normal reflection.
· Does not apply to living things other than humans.
· No aging phenomena have been observed in this plastic washbasin so far.

Anomaly Nexus
When this Anomaly is placed into a plastic bag, it will undergo nullification on its own. After a period, it will reappear near the location of its last nullification.

Risk Assessment
Harmless, but due to its special properties, continuous observation is required.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Currently privately owned.

Containment Measures
/

Experiment Records
Experiment 1
Various liquids were poured into the basin. Regardless of the type, color, or density of the liquid, visions could be observed.
Since all members involved in this experiment have already observed the visions, further testing cannot continue. Experiment suspended.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Kiroumaru has no sense of satiation, and any object that enters its field of vision may be treated as food.
· Objects swallowed by Kiroumaru are either intact or vanish. The whereabouts of disappeared objects are currently unknown.
Considering the Anomaly's past experiences, Kiroumaru may still possess characteristics that have yet to manifest. Close monitoring is required.

Characteristics

This anomaly is an unusual individual and may possess other traits that have yet to manifest. Close monitoring is required.

Anomaly Nexus

ST_Manual.ManualVision_3003_des:
Anomaly Story
Picture this: a group of expressionless people ascending or descending through the open air. Sounds creepy and funny at the same time, right? But that's exactly what's happening in every elevator out there.
The earliest elevators weren't so enclosed. You could see the gaps between floors from inside them. Only later, for safety or whatever reason, did elevators become fully sealed. The doors open, people walk in, doors close, and when they open again, the world outside has become completely different. For those inside, once the doors close, the outside world becomes a complete unknown.
Most people trust elevators, believing this machine will dutifully deliver them to their destination. A pitiful few, both imaginative and insecure, feel it's dangerous to be locked in an enclosed space and left at the mercy of machinery, fearing the unknown that lies beyond their line of sight. Even after being delivered to the correct floor nine hundred and ninety-nine times, they still fear that on the thousandth ride, when the doors open, they'll be greeted by a terrifying scene…
One such poor wretch's imagination actually came true. When the elevator doors opened before him, lights flickered, eerie sounds persisted, and unfamiliar dark water flowed into the elevator. This was how Level Proliferation was first discovered. Fortunately, this poor wretch already worked in Anomaly-related fields and didn't pass out from the sudden abnormality, so he can still sit here now, writing the profile for this obliging Anomaly.

Anomaly Characteristics
· An Anomaly that may occur in elevators with enclosed views in buildings of three floors or higher. This Anomaly will not appear in elevators where the outside can be observed from inside, such as transparent sightseeing elevators.
· Manifests as an elevator malfunction where the elevator cannot reach its original floors and has a high probability of connecting to random Anomalous Realms. Additionally, announcements or music occasionally appear out of nowhere inside the elevator.
· Its nature resembles a peculiar elevator malfunction that forcibly connects random elevators to strange floors, while stairs in the same building are completely unaffected.
· Destroying the malfunctioning elevator and replacing it with a new one will eliminate this phenomenon.
· Dismantling the connected Anomalous Realm will cause the elevator to automatically repair itself ahead of schedule, meaning the problem to solve is not the elevator itself, but the other anomalies outside it.

Anomaly Nexus
Insist on not using the malfunctioning elevator and taking the stairs for at least one year (exact required varies). The elevator will repair itself back to a normal elevator as if healing on its own.

Risk Assessment
Hazard level fluctuates depending on the Anomalous Realm the elevator connects to, with an extreme range between upper and lower limits. For ordinary people and Anomaly Hunters without sufficient preparation, the best advice is: just take the stairs until the elevator is fixed. Think of it as exercise, what's wrong with that?

Containment/Guarantee Status

ST_Manual.ManualVision_3001_des:
Anomaly Story
Did I lock the door? Did I turn off the lights? Did I turn off the faucet? These questions pile up minutes after you leave home. You keep replaying the details in your memory: the twist of the handle, the feel of the switch… but memories aren't entirely reliable. You want to run back and check again, just to feel at ease.
This is a form of compulsive doubt, and only a lucky few aren't troubled by it. Those who are, however, are tormented by it again and again. Did I lock the door? What if I didn't? Won't my home get robbed? Did I turn off the faucet? What if I didn't? The water will keep flowing and flowing until it floods the room, then the hallway, then the stairwell, then the entire building… These increasingly catastrophic imaginings spread through the mind, and from them, the "Faucet Left Running" was born. It is the embodiment of baseless fear, thus, the water that flows out appears dark and muddy, sometimes takes the form of monsters. After all, how could catastrophic imaginings exist without monsters?

Anomaly Characteristics
· Manifests as a sink with a faucet. The faucet is in the open position, with dark water continuously flowing from it.
· The dark water flowing from the faucet is not affected by gravity and can spread in any direction. In most cases, the water does not spread directly into the real world, but expands through other means that connect to the Anomalous Realm.
· Occasionally, highly aggressive entities appear within the dark water.
· Once the faucet is turned off, the sink and water will disappear.

Anomaly Nexus
Find the faucet, turn it off.

Risk Assessment
The water exhibits aggressive behavior and is a threat. Prompt nullification is required.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not contained.
