ST_UI_GYJ.BidKing_GameplayDescription:
<title>"Going, Going, Gone!" Rules</>

<title>How to Play</>
1. This mode uses a special auction currency: <orange>Gold Shells</>.
2. Before entering an auction, you can freely choose your <orange>Auction Assistant</> and <orange>Device Set</>. There are 3 auction tiers, each with different lots and entry requirements.
3. Each match features a randomly selected auction container and set of auction rules. Check the rules and adjust your strategy accordingly.
4. After the auction begins, you will have 5 rounds to place bids. In each round, estimate the total value of the lots within the time limit and submit your bid. Your selected Auction Assistant and items can provide intel to help you appraise the lots.
5. If you meet one of the following conditions, you can immediately win all current lots and end the auction:
<orange>Round 1</>: Bid more than <orange>2×</> the 2nd-highest bid.
<orange>Round 2</>: Bid more than <orange>1.6×</> the 2nd-highest bid.
<orange>Round 3</>: Bid more than <orange>1.3×</> the 2nd-highest bid.
<orange>Round 4</>: Bid more than <orange>1.1×</> the 2nd-highest bid.
<orange>Round 5</>: <orange>The highest bidder</> wins all lots.
6. If players are tied in Round 5, the auction enters Round 6. Only players tied in Round 5 advance to the final bid. Their Round 6 bids must match or exceed their previous bids, and the highest bidder wins all lots. If players are tied again in Round 6, the auction ends with no sale.
7. If the winning bidder ends the settlement phase at a loss, each of the other three players receives a bonus equal to 10% of the loss.
8. Any collectibles you win are automatically added to your Collection. You can sell them or put them on display to earn Gold Shells and Fons over time. Fons earnings are capped at <orange>350,000</> per collection.
9. Display Collectibles in the Collection Showcase. Once you meet the requirements, you can exchange them for the corresponding furniture.
10. Enabling Anonymous Mode hides all players' nicknames during matches, but only on your screen.

Players reported for unfair teaming, intentionally going AFK, or using cheats are subject to bans. Help us keep the game fair for everyone!
Your goal is to earn more Gold Shells and win the most valuable auction pieces. The Treasure Ship Auction starts now!
ST_UI_GYJ.BidkingEffectRule_Desc:
<title>Court Conditions</>
After matchmaking, each auction is assigned one Court Condition. The selection rates vary by Auction Hall. There are 8 Court Conditions in total:
1. Blackout: Hides all players' <orange>exact bids</> each round, showing only their <orange>bid rankings</>.
2. Insider Intel: Provides <orange>one extra</> piece of public intel from the auctioneer in Rounds 1 and 3.
3. Double Up!: Doubles the value of all <orange>Purple-rarity</> Collectibles during this auction.
4. Super Rush: Doubles the value of all <orange>Gold-rarity</> Collectibles during this auction.
5. Gemheart: Converts all Collectibles that occupy <orange>1×1</> slots into random Gem Collectibles that also occupy <orange>1×1</> slots at the start of the auction.
6. Bonus Bonanza: Increases the Bonus Fund earning rate to <orange>30%</> at the end of the auction.
7. Time Crunch: Reduces the bidding time to 20s per round for the rest of this game.
8. By the Book: Runs this auction under standard rules.

ST_UI_GYJ.BPUI_OpMotorboatCollectMain_Description:
<title>Shipwreck Salvage Guide</>
1. Take a specially modified Jet Ski into the designated waters and salvage Floating Cargo.
2. Aim the Harpoon Gun at Floating Cargo and fire to retrieve it. Cargo that exceeds the Harpoon Gun's towing capacity cannot be salvaged. Return to the landing point with your cargo before your energy runs out to turn it in.
3. Some Floating Cargo contains Motor Oil, which can be used to upgrade your Jet Ski and Harpoon Gun, allowing you to venture into deeper waters and salvage heavier, more valuable cargo.
4. Salvaged cargo is automatically converted into an equivalent amount of Drifting Bottles, which can be exchanged for rewards in the Salvage Shop.

ST_UI_hpy.MangHe_summer_01_Des_rule:
<Black>Draw Method</>
There are 15 Mystery Boxes in total. For each single draw, you may spend either Annulith or Fons. The required amount of Annulith or Fons varies by draw, and the cost increases with each draw.
<Black>Weight Details</>
As draws are made and items are removed from the prize pool, each reward's probability is calculated in real time based on its weight. The formula is as follows:
Chance to obtain a specific reward = remaining quantity of that reward × that reward's weight / sum of (remaining quantity of each item in the prize pool × that item's weight)
<Black>Reward Delivery</>
Rewards obtained from draws are sent directly to your Inventory. Please check your Inventory to view them.
<Black>Notes</>
<Orange>Tide</>, <Orange>Sunny Surf</>, Cloudless Summer, Saltwater Taffy and Endless Summer are available for a limited time in the Lucent Tides event. After this limited-time Gacha ends, there are currently no other ways to obtain them.
<Black>Example</>
After 5 draws, if you have obtained "Beetle Coin ×100,000" ×2, "Elite Hunter Guide ×10" ×2, and "Dreamless Seed ×10," the chance of getting "Tide" on the 6th draw is:
= 1 * 1 / (1 * 1 + 1 * 3 + 1 * 5 * 2 + 1 * 10 * 2 + 1 * 99 * 4) = 0.23%
After 12 draws, if only "Tide," "Sunny Surf," and "Cloudless Summer" remain undrawn, the chance of getting "Tide" on the 13th draw is:
= 1 * 1 / (1 * 1 + 1 * 3 + 1 * 5) = 11.11%
As draws continue, the probabilities of all items fluctuate in real time.

ST_UI_hpy.Netfishing_17:
<title>Event Rules</>
1. You begin the event with the Harpoon. The Fishing Net unlocks at Fishing Level 3, and the Bomb unlocks at Fishing Level 5.
2. Each fishing tool has its own range and effect. Choose the best tool based on the location of the fish.
3. Fish have different amounts of HP depending on their rarity. Higher-rarity fish take multiple hits to catch.
<title>Fish Rules</>
1. The fishing area starts with 400 fish on the first day of the event.
2. Beginning on Day 2, 100 new fish are added each day: Green-rarity Fish ×60, Blue-rarity Fish ×34, Purple-rarity Fish ×5, and Orange-rarity Fish ×1.
3. No new fish will be added after Day 12. A total of 1,500 fish will be added throughout the event.
<title>Reward Rules</>
1. Catch fish to obtain them and earn additional rewards.
2. Reach new Fishing Levels to claim level rewards.
ST_UI_hpy.MultiCItyGameplay_2:
<title>Event Rules</>
1. During the event, designated Hethereau Hobbies events consume City Stamina at double efficiency.
2. The efficiency multiplier may vary by event. Check the event screen for details.

ST_VisionArchives.BusStop_Record_2:
1104-RC Recording: Hey, everyone! I'm Darren, and I'm really into paranormal adventures! Today, I'm here with a few buddies to check out the Ghost Bus everyone's been talking about online! We've made it to one of the stops on the rumored Route 137. What's going to happen next? Let's wait and see! Don't forget to Like, Share, and Follow!
1105-RC Recording:
"Hey, it's here! It's really here!"
"No way, it's real?!"
"Hey, are we seriously getting on this thing?"
"You're getting cold feet now? Come on, let's go."
1107-RC Recording:
"Hey, everyone, we're really on the bus. I'd better keep my voice down. Look there—some passengers just got on. They don't look human."
"They're Anomalies, right? I heard this bus specifically picks up Anomalies."
"So those Wooden Men are Anomalies? They're kind of creepy."
1108-RC Recording:
"Hey, Darren. Let's get off at the next stop, okay?"
"What? Why? Aren't you coming all the way to the Terminal Station?"
"No… Didn't you hear? They say anyone who rides to the Terminal Station disappears, along with the Anomalies."
"That's exactly why we're going to the Terminal Station—to see what's really going on! No way, seriously? You're getting scared? Fine, fine. Get off if you want. I'm going to the Terminal Station."
1110-RC Recording:
"Okay… My two buddies have already chickened out and gotten off. And me… Hang on, let me check the time… We're entering the Terminal Station in five minutes. I want to see what the Terminal Station is really like, and whether it's as creepy as the rumors say. Just now… We passed another stop, and the last group of passengers got on."
1111-RC Recording:
"Okay, everyone, I've made it to the Terminal Station. It looks… kind of dark. All those Wooden Men have finally gotten off. I'm still hiding on the bus. Outside… There's something out there, I think. I'm going to stick my head out and take a look…"
"…"
"I see something… It's ■■… flickering ■■■■"
"It's ■■! I can see ■■! ■■■■■■"
"■■■■■■■■■■"
"…………"
ST_VisionArchives.SadBear02_Record_2:
XX/XX Mission Log
Got the mission notice and went to handle the Anomalies "Saddy Teddy" and "Tin Soldiers."
There were a few hiccups along the way… but it was managed in the end.

I had initially thought to focus on the bigger enemy, so I charged straight at the bear. An old gentleman was sitting nearby, however, and I was worried for his safety—so I turned my focus to the Tin Soldiers. After I realized the Tin Soldiers' focus was primarily on me, I shifted my target back to the bear.
Luckily, Dally was there and helped me get rid of the Tin Soldiers so I could put my full focus on this "Saddy Teddy".
Honestly, the whole thing was no big deal.
ST_VisionArchives.PaperCastle_RecordBefore_1:
"…Uh, do I have to fill this part out too? Alright then…
So here's what happened. I'm an artist, and I usually dabble in street art. But lately, the Bopp been causing quite a ruckus. They've taken over all the graffiti walls I usually go to! You know how it is, the Bopp aren't as reasonable as human artists. They're really aggressive! Anyone who dares to paint over their masterpieces is gonna get beaten up! I'm getting off track here… Anyway, I really had nowhere to express my creativity, so I had a bright idea to find some manholes on the street to beautify. Wouldn't get in anyone's way, wouldn't mess up the city's appearance, and the Security Office probably wouldn't mind… right?
I thought I was a genius, so I grabbed my paint and went looking for manholes. But as soon as I got to the street, I saw something round and golden in the distance that looked like a patterned manhole cover. I thought maybe a fellow artist had the same idea, so I got closer to take a better look… Suddenly, fog started rising all around… when it cleared, the sky had turned a sickly yellow color. There were trees and streetlights made of cardboard everywhere… and this castle that looked like a stage prop from a play.
Even then, I still thought it was some installation art by that fellow artist, so I wasn't scared at all. While I was trying to figure it out, that castle sprung to life! First it shot out some streamers, then it set up a bunch of machine guns and cannons and started firing at me. I got so scared I couldn't think about anything else and just ran… I ran really far, and when I looked back, everything was gone. When I looked up at the sky, it was blue again, like it was all just a dream.
I'm not saying I miss it or anything! Thank goodness that creepy thing didn't chase after me… Though, I have to admit, that pop-up book design was actually pretty creative and really sparked my imagination… I'm just saying, next time, I'm definitely going to stick to finding empty walls for graffiti. No more bright ideas!"
ST_VisionArchives.BuildingDrawing_Record_2:
"Interview me? Heh heh… I didn't realize The Coluccis' reputation had spread so far already! Huh? T-that's not what this is about?
Oh… you mean that building? I did wander over there last week and ran into this annoying Anomaly… Right! The one you mentioned, that pile of messy papers!
I'd just finished some super crispy mackerel at Noetic Bridge and wanted to find a building for some 360 parkour! Perfect for digesting while enjoying the scenery! So I set my sights on that construction site… Hey, don't worry about how I got in…! Anyway, I just wandered around the building for a bit, and when I reached the rooftop that's when I bumped into that Anomaly.
At first, I thought it was something like a Chatterflyer, so I wanted to see what was written on the paper. Before I could get a good look, it suddenly lunged at me and pulled me into the Anomalous Realm! Hmph! No manners at all!
What was it like inside? Just a similar building… Oh! I remember now, doing parkour in that building inside the Anomalous Realm was way more interesting than outside! Its exterior walls had all sorts of weird stuff on them, like obstacles set up just for me! As the Ichi-daime of The Coluccis, how could I refuse a challenge after receiving such an invitation!
Uh… well, I did run into a little trouble… I finally managed to climb to the rooftop, but apparently that didn't count! I had to collect all the blueprints that thing had scattered around. But when I got them, I couldn't understand what was drawn on them at all. They did chatter on about something, but I couldn't make heads or tails of it…
A-anyway! I eventually got sent out of that Anomalous Realm! Which proves I completed the challenge… Right! That's exactly what happened!"
ST_VisionArchives.SpookyHouse_Record_3:
Excerpt from "Pukaland Haunted House Themed Facility Project Proposal"
…
II. Project Concept
Unlike traditional haunted houses, which rely on established scare points and sudden NPC jump-scares to deliver an exciting atmosphere, this project will center its core experience on "immersive exploration." Through setting design, lighting and sound effects, level design, route planning, and character interactions, the project will make visitors feel as if they're really there.
The attraction's overall theme is tentatively set as "Midnight's Medieval Castle," with the Count as the main character, inspired by classic vampire works. He can do more than just scare people. He can also interact with visitors as the master of the castle.
…
Excerpt from "Work Log"
…
The project's main construction is now basically complete. The main structure and entrances/exits have passed inspection and are largely in line with the intent of the original design. Per the initial plan, the next stage would formally move into scene setup and interior decoration.
However, regrettably, due to recent unforeseen circumstances, the project is temporarily on pause, with the exact time for resuming work remaining unclear. I'll be leaving Puka Group soon as well. The handover is complete, and the project should be picked up by my other colleagues going forward.
Honestly, I still can't quite let the project go. From the very first spark of the idea, through one meeting after another, to the proposal being approved and the project kickoff, I invested all I had into it. Even after the outside structure was finished, I was still working on the Count's character design, up to the 27th draft, hoping to make it as polished and perfect as possible. In hindsight, I suppose it just wasn't meant to be.
I hope I get to see the day it truly opens, if ever.
…
ST_VisionArchives.Dancer_RecordBefore_1:
"Mountain Patrol Log: Forest Area Anomaly Report"
Submitted by: Sicilian - Resident Forest Ranger
Date: Wednesday, 03:30; Weather: Overcast, with rain

…I've reported this many times already, but even now no one has come to deal with the problem. I need to submit another request to the Bureau, and especially request that a specialist come to handle the Anomaly in this forest immediately.
Before he retired, my mentor warned me about the dangers of these parts of the woods. He said that, ever since he was a young ranger, he would repeatedly run into two sets of empty clothes dancing endlessly in the middle of the forest.
Back then, most had considered it some sort of mirage created by the mountain fog—but my mentor had spent the better part of his life patrolling these paths, and had seen those two dancing regularly.
I've been in charge of this area for almost a year now, and those two have yet to stop! This is no natural phenomenon, I assure you. It's some weird Anomaly! If the Bureau won't do anything, who knows how much trouble it'll cause.
ST_VisionArchives.Dancer_RecordBefore_2:
"Citizen Affairs Liaison Letter: Application to Clear the Deep Forest Anomaly"
Applicant: Aurelia
Affiliation: Tamamochi Street Resident Association

Concerning the assaults on citizens camping within our jurisdiction, I hereby submit this supplementary statement:
Last Saturday, several residents went camping in the forest outside the city. According to the incident reports and medical records, the campers discovered an old violin and ring inside a "Phantom Ballroom" while exploring the woods.
The statements noted that one of the individuals tried to pick up the ring. This immediately triggered an extreme response from the nearby male-form "Scarlet Phantom", which began to attack the individual responsible. The residents then proceeded to abandon their camping equipment and fled beyond the illusory stage. The individuals are currently recovering at the local clinic from minor injuries and shock, and none are in life-threatening condition.
Although the incident resulted in no serious injuries, our association remains concerned for public safety. Without prompt intervention, there's a high risk that an incident like this could be repeated. On behalf of the public, I hereby submit a formal application to the Bureau and respectfully request that Specialists be dispatched as soon as possible to quell the "Scarlet Phantom" roaming the woods.
ST_VisionArchives.BusStop_VisionDescBefore:
The "Wayward Line" was originally nothing more than an ordinary bus. Initially, its owner, while still alive, was a bus driver responsible for transporting passengers. The term "while still alive" is used in this context since the driver disappeared in an accident, and after years of fruitless searching, the police were ultimately forced to declare him dead. During his lifetime, the driver transported various passengers along the routes designated by the transit company. The accident occurred when he was driving back to the terminal after finishing his routes for the day. The bus, which should have naturally been driven by the driver, surprisingly returned empty. The vehicle had no autonomous driving functions, yet the driver himself was nowhere to be found.
On days of heavy fog, the "Wayward Line" runs along the driver's original route, picking up passengers at various stops all the while. Nowadays, however, it no longer carries ordinary passengers, but instead all kinds of Anomalies.
The "Wayward Line" appears to have a unique pull on Low Threat Anomalies, drawing them inside akin to a Venus flytrap. The bus's interior can suppress Anomaly abilities, therefore trapping any Anomalies who enter. To some extent, then, the vehicle can be used to transport Low Threat Anomalies under containment.
As long as its route is not interfered with, the bus will disappear at its last stop, Terminal Station, and enter an undetectable Anomalous Realm. The Anomalies riding as passengers disappear along with it, just like that missing driver so long ago.

When the Anomaly's behavior is analyzed thoroughly, it is difficult not to conclude that it possesses intelligence resembling that of a living organism. Loading Low Threat Oddities into the vehicle as Passengers and transporting them to a unique Anomalous Realm can be roughly compared to predatory behavior in living organisms.
However, classifying the Anomaly as a Bio Anomaly on this basis would clearly be insufficient. The "Wayward Line" does not act autonomously. For example, the vehicle can be controlled by human means—and even diverted from its original route—without encountering any resistance from the Anomaly itself. Put simply, the "Wayward Line" behaves more like a preset program than an autonomous behavior.
There are two possible explanations: either, through some effect of an Esper Ability, the Anomaly "remembered" the driver's habits and memories from while he was alive, or someone tampered with the Anomaly itself, implanting something like "code" that made it operate according to a predetermined program.
After considering all the factors, the former possibility is considered more likely. The Bureau has intervened in the investigation of this incident.
ST_VisionArchives.Mirror_CusConmment_3_Dis_Player:
The "Mirror Wraith" is not some indescribable supernatural force, but instead a mimicry-based trap Anomaly. Like an alligator, it lurks beneath the water's surface, impossible to detect. For those who peer into the lake, the Anomaly peers back, probing into the deepest memories of the onlooker. It will transform the strongest regrets and desires in the human heart into a "pseudo-nectar", luring those consumed by obsession across the lake's threshold and into the depths willingly.
However, if its prey are aware of the trap, the Anomaly will tear away its disguise and "snap" shut. In these situations, the Anomaly will materialize the onlooker's deepest fears into tangible reflections. To cause nullification, one must personally shatter "themself" within the elusive cage it constructs.
A feeding method such as this is downright repulsive. The victims die believing they've attained their ideal form: glorious or redeemed. This Anomaly treats a human's inner weakness and ego as nothing more than cheap bait.

ST_VisionArchives.Dancer_RecordAfter_3:
"Excerpt from a Performing Arts Weekly Interview: Between the Final Act and the Void"
Interviewee: Karls, renowned film director, and "Former Artistic Director of the Municipal Theater"

A:…The new film is coming along swell. The lead actress has a solid camera presence. However, if we're truly discussing the artistic standard, then, frankly… Well, ever since the decline of classical stages and the pivot into cinema, I've only grown more convinced that today's actresses are far too protective of their images. It's been a difficult transition for everyone. Bringing that unique theater-style intensity in front of the camera isn't really…
Q: Are you referring to Alicia Solon?
A: I'm surprised anyone still remembers her. She was a ballet prodigy, gifted to the point of genius. Her talent and discipline were unmatched, but her body was far too fragile. She burned through her potential early in her career, sadly. When she was declared banned from performing, she could no longer handle the situation and disappeared from the public sphere entirely.
Fortunately, she had a choreographer with resolute faith in her ability, to which she eventually responded in kind. Y'know, young people love to take a story and just run with it, throwing around words like "coercion" or "consent", but in my view, nothing of the sort existed between them.
I read through the notebook that the choreographer left behind. Nowadays, people just queue a recording over speakers for rehearsal. He despised that method entirely. Once the company musicians were off the clock, he'd pick up that little violin of his, that never left his side, mind you, and would personally accompany her, one-on-one, to the practice room. Her rehearsal didn't stop until the music did.
He would play continuously just to fix a mere half-second mistake in her dance, even if her joints were completely swollen.
Alicia, during these times, never once uttered a single "no" to his methods. If the pain made her muscles seize up, rigid straps were used to lock the angle in by force. If blood soaked her shoes, she'd immediately swap them for a fresh pair and begin anew.
Outsiders were desperate to judge her with their black-and-white worldview, even going so far as to assume she was being coerced. But those who truly have a passion for their crafts saw the truth: two souls starving for perfection, desperate to give their all.
So, when that cold, hard hospital bed tried to strip her of her spotlight, that choreographer made a choice. He took his violin, along with her, and led them both out of the public's eye. He went to the woods, desiring to finish that final performance with no audience—and thus, froze Alicia forever at her zenith…
Q: What an inspirational story. So then, Director, what kind of camera work can we, the audience, expect in your upcoming new film?
A: Haha, look at me—once I start talking, I can't ever stop. Let's get back on track. As for the camera movement, staging, and art design in this movie's ballroom climax, we've specially brought in…
ST_VisionArchives.ColorsMerge_RecordBefore_2:
"Turns out these Inspiration Terminators don't just swipe a single idea. They go after the whole network of connected thoughts.
I learned this the hard way, and honestly? It's mortifying. Here's how it went down:
I'd just sent my latest manuscript to my editor and was finally ready to breathe, but my brain wouldn't quit. Figuring I should use the momentum, I started sketching out spinoff ideas… and that's when it hit me.
One second, my thoughts were flowing fast and clear. The next? It felt like slamming into a brick wall. Total mental gridlock! The worst part? It wasn't just the spinoffs that vanished… When my editor called to discuss revisions, my mind went completely blank on my own book! I just stammered like an idiot, and all I could think was, "Why did I write it that way? What was I even thinking?"
The fog didn't lift until I got an Anomaly Hunter to deal with the Terminator. Suddenly, the stack of blank pages on my desk was my manuscript again. Looking back, it makes sense. Those spinoffs were tangled up with the world and themes of the main story. The Terminator didn't just steal the idea I was working on; it blocked everything tied to it.
Yeah, you can bet I'm stocking up on industrial-strength bug spray before my next writing session."
ST_VisionArchives.Dancer_CusComment_2_Dis_Player:
"Scarlet Phantom" is widely believed to be drawn to world-class performances and undergoes natural nullification once the curtains close. Typically, the appearance of a "Scarlet Phantom" poses little to no threat and is often regarded as complementary to the artists.
However, this Anomaly can be easily influenced by objects imbued with human "obsession". Depending on the nature of that obsession, the "Scarlet Phantom" will construct a corresponding stage for itself, therefore causing natural nullification to no longer be possible.
To then nullify this Anomaly, the executor must enter the stage's illusion and utilize physical force to destroy the Core entity—thus bringing the performance to an end. This will then satisfy the Anomaly's underlying rules and lead to its natural nullification.
Whether this rumor consisted of two obsessive performers who admired each other, or a choreographer's biased control over a dancer, no one can verify. Regardless of the situation, the performer who was victimized initially—therefore trapped in an endless cycle of dance—had, perhaps, begun to look forward to the day the curtain finally fell.

ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_RecordBefore_3:
"First bell rings.
When I rushed into the school building this morning with bread in my mouth, I absolutely never imagined I'd be performing slapstick comedy in the hallway. I face-planted on flat ground, and when I grimaced and crawled back up, the bread in my mouth had already been smashed into a desperate mask of pain when I used my face to soften my fall…
Fifth bell rings.
I'm out of time! When I rushed to the second floor corner, something even weirder happened. My backpack strap was suddenly yanked by some mysterious force, making me feel like a puppet pinned in place. An invisible force was blocking my progress! Though when I turned around, all I could see was the fire extinguisher door swaying slightly. The classroom was clearly right in front of me, yet I felt like I couldn't move an inch—like that powerless feeling when you're running in a dream, where a one-meter distance stretches into an endless abyss of helplessness…
Eighth bell rings.
Haha, I'm already about to be late anyway, might as well take my time… The hall monitor at the end of the corridor is already writing down my name. He adjusted his glasses and asked why I wouldn't enter the classroom, why I was standing in the middle of the hallway confronting him. Dude… it's not that I don't want to walk, I feel like there's a massive weight on my feet. It's not super glue stuck to them! It's not a leg cramp either! I swear there's some invisible guy pulling on me. The hall monitor adjusted his glasses again, saying he'd heard this kind of excuse plenty of times, and he stopped believing me from the first word I said.
Ninth bell rings.
The hall monitor walks toward me…
Tenth bell rings.
The hall monitor rolls toward me…
Twelfth bell rings.
Someone save me and the hall monitor—we've been bounced around the hallway like two rubber balls by some invisible force!!
Thirteenth bell rings.
Thankfully, I finally made it into the classroom. Though not through the front door… I crashed through the wall.
Hey, hall monitor, don't worry about whether anything's broken. Your right hand still works, right? Cross my name off that list! I got in before the thirteenth bell, so it doesn't count as being late, right?"
ST_VisionArchives.SadBear02_Record_1:
Sorry, I can't really recall when this bunch first showed up. I'd just finished testing a new motorboat when I turned around and saw a bear attacking a bunch of Tin Soldiers. It was quite entertaining, so I watched for a while. Their formation was bizarre, though—kind of painful to watch, frankly. Still, the Tin Soldiers were constructed with impressive precision, and the way they marched was mesmerizing.
Not long after that, some random guy suddenly rushed in and started fighting the bear! The Tin Soldiers swarmed him, so he ended up chasing them instead. Halfway through, it seemed as if he couldn't decide who to fight. After he took care of the Tin Soldiers, the bear went wild. The guy managed to take care of the bear, too.
Curious why I was just watching? I don't have any Esper ability, so I figured I was better off just watching.
—Oh, so you're actually that young guy! I couldn't recognize you after you changed your clothes. Kudos to you!
Oh, and those Tin Soldiers looked pretty interesting. I wonder what they were made of. If we run into them again, mind if I touch them?
ST_VisionArchives.ZhangYuChe_RecordBefore_3:
From a battle perspective, this thing isn't too tough. You just need to watch out for its frontal charge while keeping an eye on sneak attacks from its tentacles. The high danger rating is mostly based on its destructive power, and honestly, its destructive power lives up to that rating. It's fine when it's not in battle mode, but once it enters battle mode, everything standing nearby is probably going to get smashed.
By the way, you should still be careful when fighting it. After all, nobody can tell if its tentacles retreating into the truck means it's scared or if it's been hit with Nullification. What if you let your guard down and it suddenly sticks out a tentacle to grab you and lift you up? These are all lessons learned from others' blood and tears… I'm getting off track. So, it's best to consider the octopus part separating from the truck as the signal of victory. That's the safest choice.
That's all for my experience sharing. Hope it helps any Anomaly Hunters looking to deal with this Anomaly. Ahem, I'll stay anonymous this time…

ST_VisionArchives.Mirror_Record_1:
Guys, night fishing at Tearlake is a total no-go! I just ran from there, and even left my rod behind! 
 
I know you'd never believe this, but I went there in the middle of the night to fish, and sure, I wasn't getting any bites or whatever…. But I swear something was wrong with the water!
It gets really windy at night, so you'd think the water would at least have ripples, right? Wrong! Dead still. I couldn't believe my eyes, so I took out a flashlight and shined it at the water, thinking that something might've been affecting the water from below. Instead, the second I turned the flashlight on, I saw a person standing upright, about a couple feet below the water's surface at the center of the lake! I almost screamed in terror, scrambling back to shore.
 I swear that I'm telling the truth. A person was standing there in the middle of the lake! The freakiest part was when I actually shined a light on that… "person" the face on it looked eerily similar to my own. My hands are still shaking while typing this. THAT WAS DEFINITELY A WATER GHOST!!!
I'm posting this as a warning to my fellow anglers: don't fish at that damn lake at night!
Seriously!
ST_VisionArchives.ZhangYuChe_VisionDescAfter:
An oddity with decent camouflage abilities that occasionally appears on roads throughout Hethereau in the form of an old trailer truck with octopus tentacles. Under normal circumstances, Octowpus will try its best to follow traffic rules to blend into its surroundings, but there are also cases where Octowpus attacks nearby pedestrians and facilities. Since it's impossible to predict when it will attack, citizens are advised to keep their distance once they spot Octowpus. For Anomaly Hunters, Octowpus is highly sensitive to threats in its vicinity. Once you enter its alert range, it will immediately drop its disguise and prepare for battle, destroying the surrounding environment and blocking traffic to create a favorable battle zone for itself.
Until Octowpus is nullified or leaves on its own, any moving object that enters the battle area will be considered an enemy and attacked. Therefore, blocked traffic can only be restored after Octowpus disappears.
ST_VisionArchives.Mirror_VisionDescAfter:
So long as barriers are erected, and all entrances are firmly blocked, the threat level of this body of water can, theoretically, be reduced to low. The "Mirror Wraith" is not an actively expanding disaster, but a localized environmental Anomaly limited to natural bodies of water.
 Its primary manifestations are as follows: within specific areas of the water, the surface tension is manipulated into a state of complete stillness. Based on perimeter surveys and search-and-rescue reports, this phenomenon is believed to induce severe cognitive hazards in its victims. Susceptible individuals will experience visual and auditory hallucinations after observing the water's surface, typically resulting in drowning incidents. *Note: All known victims have been found suspended upright beneath the water's surface, with no liquid found in their respiratory tracts.
Preventing an Anomaly of this caliber should be simple. Physical isolation should render it dormant… However, in reality, individuals are often drawn to this Anomaly, even going so far as to risk their livelihoods to come into contact with it. Considering the number of recent disappearances has crossed the normally accepted threshold—and thus indirectly triggered a public panic—the Bureau has no choice but to carry out an investigation.
Civilians have demanded the complete removal of this body of water's luring capabilities.
Direct contact has confirmed that this Anomaly is a mimetic Anomaly driven by a human's "self-perception". It can capture the observer's exemplary self, and mimic that "self" beneath the water's surface, causing the observer to abandon their physical body to merge with the idealized version. To nullify this Anomaly, an operator with exceptional mental fortitude must encounter and reject the Anomaly's mimic, and therefore provoke a rejection response. As a result, the Anomaly will instantly tear away its disguise and enter a highly aggressive defense state.
In short, a purge operation's main objective is to shatter the "Mirror Wraith's" domain and shatter the reflection borne of the same source.

Oh! You like that haunted house too? Then we're really on the same wavelength—
Huh? This is just an interview? Okay…
The first time I went to Spooky Cookies, my dad brought me. He said he wanted to find some inspiration, but after we ran into Grandpa Butler, he said he had to use the bathroom and left early, so I stayed in there playing by myself for a long time… Who's Grandpa Butler? He's a really kind old man. He talked with me for ages, and was super kind and welcoming… Oh, sorry, I suppose I should say "ghost".
The Count's laugh sounds awful, but he's actually pretty nice too. Back when I used to come here, he'd see I was still little, so every time we'd settle it with rock-paper-scissors and then he'd just leave me alone. After I joined ETD and came back with Xiaozhen, though, it was no longer just rock-paper-scissors. Instead, I had to go toe-to-toe with him… But his moves are easy to remember, so Xiaozhen and I break our speedrun record every time we return~
Hm? Oh, Xiaozhen… She really doesn't like coming here, because Grandpa Butler and the Count both call her "little ghost," and she finds that super embarrassing. I told them that Xiaozhen is the strongest, cutest ghost in all of Hethereau, and Grandpa Butler started coughing up a storm while the Count kept apologizing and laughing super loud, so after that Xiaozhen wasn't interested in coming back… Now whenever she sees those two, she hides in the TV and won't come out.
Spooky Cookies' frequency? Hmm… If I had to describe it, it's like an old record, all squeaky and a little warped. If nobody goes there, its melody even starts to sound kind of desolate… Oh, right! I've also noticed a really strange frequency in Spooky Cookies before, totally different from the norm. It sounded bright and cheerful, like every instrument in an entire symphony joyously harmonizing. Just hearing one note filled you with giddiness, but I have no idea where it came from… I asked Grandpa Butler and the Count about it before, and they both looked genuinely surprised. They kept exchanging looks for a while, and in the end they got all cryptic and would only say it was an old special "friend" of theirs who stops by once in a blue moon. They even told me to keep the whole thing hush-hush. So weird… I wonder who it could be?
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_CusConmment_2_Dis_Player:
They're truly afraid of being alone.
Clumsily designing games, carefully adjusting the difficulty, all just to make participants stay a little longer. They desperately hope that those who leave might return due to various coincidences—whether it's forgotten keys, sudden downpours, or simply thinking the game wasn't half bad…
"Want to play another round?" When they see returning participants, they'll quietly ask with heads down, though inside they're already bursting with joy.
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_VisionDescAfter:
Regarding the strange behaviors exhibited by the Wandering Puppets, all witnesses describe a sense of "being deliberately guided to participate in games." This may suggest they possess a need for companionship.
When participants actively propose "performance invitations" to the dolls, all abnormal activities immediately cease and transform into courteous interactions. The musical doll will voluntarily give up the piano bench and turn pages for the participant during their performance; beneath the baking doll's cup lies delicious sweets carefully prepared for the participant; the running doll prefers to jog shoulder-to-shoulder with participants rather than compete for speed, aimlessly circling the playground together while enjoying the evening breeze.
Once the dolls sense kind responses from participants, their loneliness dissipates. They'll then return to the art room on their own, remaining inactive for the following week.
It is recommended to maintain monthly "Social Gatherings" as this is currently the most effective containment measure. They never wanted to win the games—they just wanted friends.

Bureau of Anomaly Control Internal Document

Clearance: Internal Public
Department: Containment Unit 2
Submitted by: Mint

Review Report on Failed Containment of Expired Invitation

An incident occurred during today's containment of Anomaly C-1704 Expired Invitation, and it's all Mint's fault… After receiving a citizen's distress call, Mint's team immediately arrived on scene and entered the Expired Invitation's Anomalous Realm. We prioritized ensuring the safety of the trapped citizen, then prepared to contain the Anomaly according to protocol. Following the New Containment Safety Protocol, we had prepared the containment vessel in advance, but while weakening the Anomaly, Mint saw those two paper streamers swaying back and forth, and suddenly felt this irresistible urge and lunged at them… By the time Mint came to her senses, those two streamers were already torn down, and the Anomaly was directly nullified… We had no choice but to bring back the treasure chest it left behind to the Bureau. It's currently placed in Temporary Containment, scheduled to be processed separately as an anomalous derivative later. Looking back, it's still really strange. Why did that happen? Could this Anomaly also have had mental control abilities? Mint definitely wasn't asleep when reviewing the materials…

Anyway! Mint feels deeply guilty about this mistake and formally apologize to the other team members. Mint is sorry! My teammates operated completely according to protocol during this containment operation. Mint requests that only my salary be docked! T T

Team Member Opinion 1: The salary is a minor issue, but next time let's not assign Mint to containment quests for Anomalies with… colorful dangling objects.
Team Member Opinion 2: Also try not to assign her to quests with yarn balls…
ST_VisionArchives.PaperCastle_RecordBefore_2:
"I'm not here asking you to deal with Anomalies. I'm an Anomaly Hunter myself! Don't let my current appearance fool you, I've got several rookies under me… Sure, they're pretty green, but for this level of Anomaly, why would I need to ask the Bureau for help?
You've heard of the Expired Invitation Anomaly, right? I first encountered it about four or five years ago. I was new to the business back then, and my luck wasn't great. I'd gone several days without any work. My account was nearly empty, and I was about to go hungry when I saw Hyelp post a new commission. I didn't even think twice before accepting it. When I got to the quest location, I realized this thing was incredibly tough to deal with. My skill level back then wasn't nearly enough to handle it. After getting beaten and having to flee embarrassingly several times, it actually sparked my competitive spirit. Luckily, this commission had no time limit, so every day I'd take down a few small fry to earn meal money, then spend the rest of my time studying the Expired Invitation. After messing around with it for over half a month, I finally discovered the true purpose of the Expired Invitation.
Think about it: touch it and you enter the Anomalous Realm, enter the Realm and you get swarmed. Escaping isn't that hard though, so there's no real risk. After you escape, it turns back into a wax seal… but the next time you go there, it triggers again. Isn't that just an indestructible, self-repairing target dummy? Perfect for practice! Once I figured this out, I managed to convince the original client to let me keep it and rent it out to rookie Anomaly Hunters as a training tool. Business was booming! The Fons it earned me far exceeded the original commission fee. Every day, rookies would come to rent this 'Expired Invitation' from me. Sure, they'd always tease me saying 'If there really are demons in this world, every demon would have your tattoo on them'… but I was really broke! Wanting to make money isn't shameful!
…So, my request? Uh, didn't I already say? I don't want to nullify the Anomaly. I just want to ask around and see if you know where there might be other Expired Invitations. A couple days ago, some rookie accidentally nullified the one I was renting out… Now everyone can't use such a versitile and cheap practice tool. So I… Hey, I wasn't finished talking yet!"
ST_VisionArchives.SpookyHouse_Record_1:
The first one to notice something was off was a coworker of mine who was helping renovate the amusement park. He kept telling me Spooky Cookies had its lights on at night, with weird noises coming from the inside. That project had been shut down for ages, though, so how was I supposed to know he wasn't just drunk and freaking himself out! When he saw I didn't believe a word he said, he insisted on making a bet, so after work one day, we went to check it out. Once we got there, the door just wouldn't open! I argued with him for a bit, but then the door opened suddenly. (I only realized later that I'd dropped my wallet while we were arguing. Was the thing really after my lousy few Fons?)
Spooky Cookies looked nothing like it had when the project was shut down! It had turned into this huge medieval castle. We were scared out of our minds and had no idea how to get out. Luckily, we found a flashlight pretty quickly. We wanted to go back, but the door wouldn't budge, so we had no choice but to keep going.
At some point my coworker and I got separated. He's a total scaredy-cat, so who knows—maybe he passed out somewhere and hid. It was way too dark in there, and my flashlight battery kept draining, so there was no way to find him. I just had to keep pushing forward. I also ran into a whole bunch of ghosts on the way. I don't know what the things actually were, but they sure looked like ghosts!!! Whenever I shined my flashlight on them, they seemed to back off. Maybe I was just seeing things after all?
God, I kept thinking that maybe I was imagining the whole thing, but the second I saw a vampire, I knew deep in my bones that everything was real! I think I accidentally wandered into an Anomalous Realm… That vampire called himself "The Count" and claimed that if I beat him, I could leave. He kept standing there doing that creepy "heh-heh-heh" laugh, but he didn't seem to actually have any malice toward me, so I went along with it. I never thought I'd actually make it out alive!!
Thankfully, I found my coworker outside Spooky Cookies. He said the moment he opened his eyes, he was already outside and had no idea what had happened. He totally refused to believe anything I said! It wasn't until I reported it to the Bureau and Spooky Cookies was officially classified as an Anomaly that he finally stopped arguing with me!!

Hethereau Transit reminds you: For your comfort and that of other passengers, please comply with the Hethereau Bus Code:
1. To prevent dense fog from entering the vehicle, all doors and windows will lock automatically while the vehicle is in motion. Do not stick your head or any body parts out of the windows. If you accidentally inhale the fog, please report it to a bus attendant immediately.
2. The vehicle will not stop for any reason while in motion. It will stop only at the next station. This service is for boarding only; passengers may not get off at any stop other than the Terminal Station.
3. Do not interfere with the driver while the vehicle is in motion. If the driver is disturbed and their ability to drive safely is affected, the driver may use any means to protect themselves and ensure the vehicle continues operating normally.
4. On Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, please board through the front door. On Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays, please board through the rear door. Passengers must comply strictly. Do not board through the wrong door at any time.
5. Only one passenger may occupy each odd-numbered row. Even-numbered rows may be filled to capacity. If no seats are available, hold on to the handrails to avoid injury.
6. If another passenger speaks to you, answer only with "Yes" or "No." All other forms of response are prohibited. Likewise, when speaking to another passenger, limit yourself to no more than three sentences to avoid disturbing the driver.
7. The full route takes one hour and thirty-seven minutes. If you are wearing any device that displays the time, synchronize it with the time displayed on the vehicle. Once every minute, raise your arm high at the 42-second mark to ensure that you have not fallen asleep.

"It's not exactly a troublesome Anomaly. Usually you just rush in and clean house. But even so, every time we get this kind of commission, everyone in our team becomes extremely polite and courteous. They decline and defer to each other until we have to draw lots to see which poor soul gets to 'hit the jackpot.'
You know how Inspiration Terminators create Anomalous Realms based on exaggerated versions of the inspiration they absorb, right? Basically, it becomes a massive theme park of materialized ideas. Just by standing there, you know exactly what the person whose idea got stolen was thinking.
This is… definitely not fun. Let me put it this way: I once got a commission from the manga artist I admire. If I didn't help solve her big problem, the ending of her series would be… Anyway, with the devout and anxious feeling of being able to help my idol, I stepped into the Anomalous Realm, only to discover it was generated from her inspiration for the final chapter! Completely caught off guard, I got thoroughly spoiled… All the anticipation from following the series, the excitement of discussing plot threads with others, all the satisfaction that belonged to this work… it was all shattered so carelessly and hastily. I should have… I should have celebrated with my friends as it reached its final chapter, reading through this story slowly with both happiness and reluctance…
Ahem, I'm getting off track. Anyway, these Anomalous Realms generated from people's inspiration are even more complex than those created by other Anomalies. If the inspiration owner is a horror film director, congratulations on earning an unforgettably terrifying experience. A colleague of mine almost got lost in a mystery novelist's inspiration space, which really gave everyone quite a scare. Does PTSD count as a work injury?
Oh, and here's the most important point. Usually we're required to sign confidentiality agreements and whatnot. After all, we're the only ones besides the client who know about these ideas. While I can understand it, all those rules and regulations are just so annoying! The commission fee isn't that high, but there's no shortage of restrictions! It's no wonder nobody wants to take these jobs…"
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_VisionDescBefore:
This Anomaly appears as standard artist mannequins commonly found in art classrooms, with articulated joints that allow them to mimic human limb movements. Their current numbers remain unknown. The dolls lack any sense of privacy or shame and show no interest in wearing clothing. Since they only appear during nighttime (20:00–06:00), they effectively avoid violating the school's dress code policies.
Early on, the Wandering Puppets attempted daytime activities, including substituting for a student suffering from Delayed Sleep Phase Syndrome (a condition common among teenagers and night owls). When the teacher called the student's name during attendance, the doll's inability to produce normal vocal sounds led to the teacher publicly criticizing it with "Are you made of wood?" This comment proved prophetic, causing the teacher to suffer a heart condition from excessive shock. The substitute doll was subsequently dismantled and permanently stored in the storage room.
Currently, dolls with detectable activity within the school grounds include Welcome-type, Sprint-type, Shell Game-type, Performance-type, and Hide-and-Seek-type variants. All exhibit strong social needs and actively initiate "games" to gain companionship and interaction from human targets. When the dolls sense declining attention, they may develop punitive attitudes toward their game partners. It is recommended to respect the dolls' game rules—refusing to play equals voluntary surrender. They never punish rule-breakers… but the games will continue forever.
ST_VisionArchives.ColorsMerge_VisionDescAfter:
"This Bio Anomaly resembles flies and other insects in appearance. It typically attaches to the victim's head and absorbs inspiration through its mouthparts. After obtaining a considerable amount of inspiration, it constructs an Anomalous Realm to hide in. Nullifying an Inspiration Terminator requires entering the Anomalous Realm and reaching its hideout. Since the Anomalous Realm is composed of inspiration consumed by the Terminator, its content is often complex, variable, and irregular. Anomaly Hunters must adapt on the fly and respond flexibly.
After reclaiming the stolen inspiration, the Anomalous Realm will change accordingly. It should be noted that the rules within Anomalous Realms often follow specific logic. Understanding these rules will be very helpful for nullification work."
ST_VisionArchives.SpookyHouse_VisionDescAfter:
Located within Pukaland, the Spooky Cookies Anomaly is generally considered harmless, manifesting only as an indoor haunted house attraction that remains perpetually "open for business." Based on what we know, this Anomaly is believed to have originally been an unfinished Puka Group amusement-park project that developed into a Location Anomaly while construction was stalled. Its exterior still retains its original form—a small dark house shaped like a bat with spread wings—but inside is a deep medieval castle-like space that does not match the outside structure of the real building.
Before entering Spooky Cookies, people will rarely sense any unusual fluctuations. Once inside, however, they are automatically identified by Spooky Cookies as "visitors," which triggers its operating state. To have any chance of leaving safely, entrants must pay a set amount of Fons, collect a few items, and follow the stated rules. Naturally, Spooky Cookies itself and the "Ghost Butler" entities that emerge within it are not hostile toward visitors. Although they actively pursue visitors, they show no real intent to attack. Instead, they resemble dedicated haunted house actors to enhance each visitor's experience.
After a visitor leaves safely, Spooky Cookies enters a temporary dormant state. It will not reactivate until a new "visitor" arrives.
The specific rules to be observed inside Spooky Cookies are as follows: First, entry is permitted only after paying Fons. Visitors then receive a flashlight. Second, during the attraction, visitors must search for keys, evade pursuit from the many different forms of the "Ghost Butler," and, once all keys have been collected, defeat "The Count" in order to leave successfully. Both "The Count" and the "Ghost Butler" are suspected to be remnants of the will of former designers and construction workers. They seem especially devoted to preserving the fun of the experience—and genuinely enjoy doing so. Finally, after leaving, visitors will receive rewards based on their performance—supposedly one of "The Count's" many clever ploys to attract repeat customers.
Spooky Cookies operates with an almost obsessive level of perfectionism. Because it is otherwise stable and harmless, Spooky Cookies is regarded as one of Pukaland's unique attractions.

"Everyone says Inspiration Terminators are creators' mortal enemies. Wherever they show up, it's like a swarm of locusts passing through, not a single good idea is left behind. But I need to set the record straight about these annoying little pests: they're picky eaters.
That's right, I actually saw one feeding. It wobbled down, fluttering weakly before crash-landing on its victim's head. You could tell it hadn't eaten in ages, it was so hungry it could barely stay airborne.
Unfortunately, the guy's thick hair blocked my view, so I couldn't see just how it sucked out the inspiration. All I could make out from a distance was a tiny dot starting to glow in that mess of hair. I figured it had done its thing, I grabbed my fly swatter, held my breath, and waited…
But then? That glowing dot floated back up, flickering erratically. Suddenly, it convulsed and spat out a dull, grayish orb of light. The orb drifted right back to its owner, while the Inspiration Terminator just hung there, dazed. Seizing my chance, I swatted the Terminator out of the air.
The guy at the desk had no clue what happened. He just stayed hunched over, scribbling away like mad. Makes you wonder… what kind of "inspiration" did he get back? Clearly, the Terminator found it so disgusting it'd rather starve than keep it down."
ST_VisionArchives.BusStop_Record_3:
Breaking News: Hethereau City Bus Driver Missing, Whereabouts Unknown. Driverless Bus Returns to Station on Its Own.
Our reporter now brings you the latest details:
A disappearance has been reported in Hethereau. The missing person is the bus driver of Hethereau Route 137. After finishing work, the driver failed to return to the main terminal. The operations manager contacted the driver's family, who confirmed that he had not returned home either.
The manager and the family subsequently contacted the police. After more than twenty-four hours of searching, the police classified the case as a missing-person incident.
Here are the details of the case:
At 21:13 last night, after completing his final run, the bus driver began returning to the main bus terminal along the designated route. He was expected to arrive at 21:55.
The bus arrived at the terminal at 22:02. However, the driver, who should have been in the driver's seat, was nowhere to be found. Instead, the bus had returned "on its own." According to a statement from the operations manager, vehicles in this series are not equipped with any autonomous-driving capabilities.
After reviewing surveillance footage from along the route, investigators found that the vehicle passed through a mountain tunnel at 21:42. Footage taken before it entered the tunnel showed the driver still in the driver's seat, with no other passengers on board. However, footage of the vehicle exiting the tunnel showed that the driver had disappeared. The bus had also spent longer than usual traveling through the tunnel, leading investigators to suspect that it had stopped inside.
As there are no surveillance cameras installed inside the tunnel, the police sealed it off and began searching the area. No results have been found as of this evening.
We will continue to bring you further updates on the case. Please stay tuned.
ST_VisionArchives.Sadbear_RecordBefore_3:
#MyChildhoodFriends
Thanks for the invitation. When I came across this topic, I happened to be cleaning up at home and stumbled upon my childhood diary, one of those expensive password journals from the corner store back then. I couldn't remember the password anymore, but since so much time had passed, the plastic casing of the lock had become very brittle and I pried it open easily. Even though I was 100% sure it was my own diary, the unfamiliar handwriting and events I had no memory of made it feel like I was peeking into someone else's diary.
Maybe I'm setting this up too much, but anyway… I found some pretty interesting stuff, so I wanted to record it on Bagel.
"Why can't Mommy and Daddy see Nini? Nini is sitting right there on the bench, her white dress is so pretty, I want a dress just like hers too, but Mommy won't buy it for me."
"Amai said he couldn't see Nini either, so I told him Nini has two braids and wears a really pretty white dress, and she's as tall as me, then Amai could see Nini too. I also told Linlin and Songzi, and they could all see Nini. Only the grown-ups can't see her, oh well, I guess grown-ups don't know everything after all."
"Linlin said his friend is really strong, and it's true, he can lift a chair with one hand. Amai's friend is a bit shy, but he's willing to play with us too. Songzi's friend is a white little dog, and we all got to pet it. This is our secret."
"Nini is a bad person, I hate her."
"Nini gave me her little bear toy, and we made up."
…
"Linlin can't see Nini anymore, I told him Nini is right next to me, and he said I was lying, he doesn't want to play with me anymore. But Amai and Songzi can still see her, so I don't want to play with Linlin anymore either."
…
"Amai's friend disappeared, and Songzi's little dog is gone too. I asked Songzi where his white little dog was, and Songzi said he never had any white little dog, all their friends are gone."
"Now only I can see Nini."
…
"Why can't they all see her? They all say I'm lying, that I'm making it all up… But I'm not lying, Nini is right here."
"Amai doesn't want to play with me anymore either, so I lied, I said I couldn't see Nini anymore too. Then I could play with Amai and the others again, but I still like playing with Nini the most."
…
After that, "Nini" never appeared again. I messaged my parents to ask, and they said I never had a friend named Nini when I was little. They did buy me a few teddy bears though, but they don't know where those went either. Kids really are so imaginative.
The rest of the diary wasn't very interesting, so I'm planning to organize all this stuff and throw it out as recyclables. No follow-up.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss08_Record_1:
Recording

I saw Swallowtail on my way to the cinema. A large butterfly of vibrant colors, wanting to soar high but weighed down by the paper scraps on its body, left dreaming of escaping the world. It had no idea that even if it really flew up into the sky, it would still be tied down to this world. There's no escape. No one can escape.
3 seconds of silence
She was terrified of fire. She was afraid those ticket stubs would burn. She loved watching movies. She felt that compared to real life, movies were more worthwhile. Everything dormant would be stirred awake, everything unresolved would be promised an ending. Unlike real life, which is always a chaotic mess… In life, she was a fly bumping around aimlessly. Outside of life, she could be a butterfly, one that was uniquely magnificent and beautiful. She never watched theater, because she felt the wall between the stage and the audience was too flimsy. She couldn't convince herself to believe in it. So, it was only ever movies.
(Another voice: Excuse me, you don't seem to be talking about Swallowtail. Who are you talking about?)
It's always been Swallowtail. I haven't been talking about anyone else.
(Another voice: But it sounds like… you "knew" it.)
Hearty laughter
Yes. I knew her.

Recording Ends
ST_VisionArchives.C-7111Ob_RecordBeforeContent_2:
(Background noise)

…Who are you? What do you want? I don't do interviews.
(Another voice: We're not from the media.)
Hm? With all that equipment… Oh, is this about what happened before?

(Prolonged silence)

Come in, then. Don't just stand at the doorway.
(Another voice: Thanks for letting us in.)
What do you want to know?
(Another voice: Just tell us what happened.)
It was nothing special. On my way home from work, I was attacked by a vending machine that suddenly came to life. I was scared out of my wits when the president of the society appeared out of nowhere and effortlessly turned the vending machine into a Puka Sweet Dreams Marshmallow. I thought he was just a kind Esper passing by. When I thanked him, he told me it wasn't an Esper Ability. It was "magic." Espers can only nullify anomalies, but magic can do so much more. And he was just an ordinary person like me. As long as you study magic seriously, even ordinary people can do seemingly impossible things.
(Another voice: So you believed him?)
I was skeptical at first. But after following him to the society, I witnessed miracle after miracle.
(Another voice: "Miracles"?)
You might have other words for it. To me, they were miracles. At every gathering, he would present anomalies that had hurt people or nearly hurt people, and announce he would purify them with the power of magic. He'd draw a magic circle on the ground, and then the ground would glow. Those struggling anomalies would instantly transform into the most ordinary objects. He said this was the power of the Black Tome. The president of the society would casually perform these miracles like they were nothing, telling us that with enough practice, anyone could have this power… He was a bit odd, always muttering strange things, but he was easygoing. No matter when someone asked him about magic, he would set aside whatever he was doing and answer seriously. He reminded you of that friendly top student, or the helpful class representative… Anyway, he wasn't like what outsiders say.
(Another voice: Have you seen the Black Tome? What's written in it?)
I've seen it from a distance, but I've never read what's inside. Only the President could read that book. He said only "the chosen ones" could touch the tome, and it would be dangerous for anyone else to do so. Some people did try to steal the Black Tome when he wasn't paying attention. But I don't know why they all gave up in the end. The President often held that book and recited strange sentences, saying they were incantations. I copied down a few of them and practiced often.
(Another voice: Did the practice work?)
No. Of course not.

(Brief silence)

You've got the wrong person. I was just an ordinary follower of the Black Tome and the President. I never got close to either of them, and I didn't lose anything from this experience. During that incident… when the Black Tome went berserk and anomalies out of control took over the building, I wasn't hurt either.
To me, that time was like a dream. Every day I'd listen to the President talk about magic, then go home and give some serious practice. Every time I recited an incantation, nothing happened, but it never discouraged me. I just thought I wasn't skilled enough. If I had tried a little harder and became someone chosen by the Black Tome, I could've learned magic too. I really believed that.
I don't blame the President. Who goes through life without ever being deceived? "Everyone is unique and special"… Isn't that society's biggest lie?
…You should go. I have nothing more to say.

(Silence continues until the end of the recording)

ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_VisionDescBefore:
R-1851(Or) is a large Bio Anomaly with an appearance similar to cetaceans, featuring ribbon-like flesh fins and tentacle-like aberrant organs on its surface, possibly a fusion of multiple marine organism characteristics. This Anomaly cannot be observed in real space, but instead operates within an Anomalous Realm whose entrance randomly appears near the undersea tunnel. All witnesses share the experience of suddenly entering the Anomalous Realm while driving through the undersea tunnel, and consistently report hearing complex calls resembling whale songs.
According to witness descriptions, this Anomalous Realm is a frozen wasteland connected to seas of blood, featuring surreal landscapes such as chains in the sky and giant ship anchors. Most witnesses chose to hide or exit their vehicles within the Anomalous Realm and were safely teleported back to the undersea tunnel. A very small number claim to have followed R-1851(Or) to the depths of the Anomalous Realm and were attacked by R-1851(Or). Historical records indicate that some Anomaly Hunter team disappearances may be connected to this Anomaly. Please handle with caution.
It is noteworthy that all interviewees, including those who encountered attacks, expressed varying degrees of concern and sympathy for R-1851(Or). It remains unclear whether this is due to the Anomaly's special abilities, the Anomalous Realm's influence on human emotions, or other reasons.
ST_VisionArchives.Lamp_RecordBefore_3:
XX/XX
Today I carried out an Eternal Lamp containment mission. Everything was going smoothly at first, and the containment was completed quickly. But for some reason, I had a momentary lapse in judgment and thought that draining the electricity from the lamp might be safer…
It exploded. Good thing there was more than one specimen…

XX/XX
I heard that an Eternal Lamp escaped from Zerogon Laboratory because of a small-scale power outage at the lab, which temporarily disabled its containment measures. I thought the lab's management was supposed to be really strict? In theory, there shouldn't be any power outages, right?
I asked a friend at the lab about the situation, and apparently it was because the Eternal Lamp consumed too much electricity that the lab couldn't pay the electric bill in time, which caused the blackout… Maybe it deliberately got itself caught just to enjoy the lab's free electricity?
I'm glad that re-containment quest wasn't assigned to me, I really have trauma from dealing with it…

XX/XX
Huh? I have to contain an Eternal Lamp again? Me? Wasn't it assigned to someone else before? Did that mission fail? Alright then…
ST_VisionArchives.PillowDreams_RecordBeforeContent_3:
XX/XX
I dreamt about my childhood again. Back then, I didn't know what it meant to "cut in line". I walked right up to the front of a line and got scolded for it. After that, I stuck to trailing behind everyone else. I was at fault, yes, but no one had ever taught me such a thing. No one was at fault.

XX/XX
I dreamed about my school days. Back then, everyone looked more or less the same. Now and then, one or two students would deviate from the norm and stand out. I hated them, yet I envied them, too. The truth is, they never directly bothered me, so I can't say exactly what about them I hated or envied, but they were the kind of students who wouldn't pursue further education.
I've been sick lately. My cough's getting worse.

XX/XX
My condition has declined. The doctor said there was nothing more he could do.

XX/XX
I've realized there's something strange about the pillow I've used all my life. Whenever I fall asleep, I'm sent back to some moment in my life, and I am once again reminded how utterly unremarkable I am in a crowd. Looking back on my life, I never wished to be ordinary, yet I was powerless to change. Is the pillow trying to warn me? But what meaning is there in warning someone who's about to die?

XX/XX
The pillow is nowhere to be found. It doesn't matter anymore. I don't have long left.
